title: Restore the latest browser Draft on Web startup
description: The packaged Web Edition successfully autosaves Browser Drafts, but a hard reload constructs a fresh Design Session and returns to the welcome screen because no production caller invokes openDraft. The website integration guide requires reload recovery, and the current UI intentionally has no visible Draft list, leaving persisted Designs unreachable after reload. Restore the newest valid Draft automatically when WebApp mounts with no active Design, without replacing an already active Design or exposing storage policy in the shell.
design: Keep latest-Draft selection and replacement inside BrowserDesignSessionController. Add a single restoreLatestDraft entry point that is inert when a Design is already active, selects the store's newest normalized Draft summary, and delegates the existing replacement path so Design/canvas authority and autosave semantics remain unchanged. WebApp invokes it from its lifecycle effect before installing autosave and logs bounded startup failures through the existing Web command error path. Add controller and WebApp integration regressions, then repeat packaged root-browser recovery with an isolated profile.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh WebApp controller with valid Drafts restores the newest Draft on mount; an existing active Design is never replaced; empty/corrupt Draft state remains on the welcome screen without crashing; restored Designs use the existing replacement/finalization path and remain downloadable; focused controller/shell tests, TypeScript, full frontend suite, both edition builds, browser-boundary scan, and isolated packaged reload smoke pass; release task can rebuild commit-stamped Web archives.
notes: Reproduced against the packaged 1.2.0 root artifact in a fresh Chrome profile: New Design, real-catalog search for oak, Favorites, canvas placement, panels/keyboard/resize, and .canopi download worked, but hard reload returned to the welcome screen. Added controller-owned restoreLatestDraft and WebApp startup invocation with docs. Red focused run: 3 expected failures (missing controller method and no mount restore). Green: 98 focused Browser Design Session/App Shell/App Data/Canvas Workspace tests; full frontend 250 files and 2309 tests; check:types; check:editions with 1151 Desktop and 1168 Web modules plus boundary scan. Rebuilt the real-catalog root package in the same isolated profile: hard reload restored Untitled Design, Oak/Quercus favorite, one placed Quercus, derived consortium, and a fresh 1906-byte .canopi download. Headless Chrome emitted only software-WebGL/GPU diagnostic warnings. User profile, Downloads, Designs, settings, and existing port 1420 process were untouched.
close_reason: Restored the newest valid Browser Draft automatically at Web startup through the existing Design Session replacement seam, preserved active Designs, added regression coverage and operating-guide ownership, and verified the original packaged hard-reload failure red/green with an isolated real-catalog Chrome session. Focused 98 tests, full 2309 frontend tests, TypeScript/generated/gallery checks, both edition builds, and browser-boundary scan passed.

title: Fix Linux WebKitGTK WebGL startup freeze
description:
## Slice Summary
Linux desktop launches should configure WebKitGTK early enough that WebGL-backed map surfaces do not freeze when a Design has a saved Location and visible map layers.

## User Value
Linux users can open saved-location Designs without the desktop app freezing, and developers can run the normal local desktop command without remembering an external environment variable.

## Out of Scope
Do not rewrite MapLibre, change map provider behavior, add a non-WebGL map renderer, or alter macOS/Windows startup behavior.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Prevent Linux WebKitGTK WebGL context creation from freezing map-backed desktop surfaces.

**Current behavior:**
On affected Linux desktop runs, WebKitGTK freezes when a WebGL context is requested. MapLibre requires WebGL, so opening a Design with a saved Location and a visible map layer freezes the app with an empty map. Developers can work around the issue by launching with `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1`, but the normal local desktop command and packaged app launches do not apply that environment.

**Desired behavior:**
Linux desktop startup configures WebKitGTK before the webview or WebKit child processes initialize so WebGL context creation succeeds by default. The normal local desktop command and packaged Linux app launches should no longer require users or developers to set an environment variable manually. The behavior should be Linux-only and should not change macOS or Windows startup.

**Key interfaces:**
- Desktop process startup before Tauri/WebKit initialization
- Linux WebKitGTK renderer environment
- MapLibre/WebGL map activation for saved Location Designs
- Agent documentation for local desktop launch and MapLibre/Linux gotchas

**Out of scope:**
- Replacing MapLibre or adding a non-WebGL map renderer
- Changing map provider, tile source, Location Workbench, or Canvas Map Surface behavior
- Applying the Linux renderer workaround to macOS or Windows
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Linux desktop startup sets `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1` before Tauri/WebKit initializes, without requiring a shell wrapper.
- [ ] The workaround is scoped to Linux and does not change macOS or Windows startup behavior.
- [ ] A comment or nearby documentation explains why the environment must be set before WebKit child processes start.
- [ ] Agent docs mention the Linux WebKitGTK/WebGL renderer workaround and keep `cargo tauri dev` as the normal local desktop command.
- [ ] Manual verification on Linux shows a fresh `canvas.getContext("webgl")` probe returns without freezing when launched via plain `cargo tauri dev`.
- [ ] Manual verification on Linux opens a `.canopi` Design with saved Location and visible map layers without freezing.
- [ ] Relevant Rust formatting/check commands for the touched desktop startup code pass, or any skipped gate is recorded with the reason.
close_reason: Fixed Linux desktop startup by setting WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 before Tauri/WebKitGTK initialization; scoped to Linux; added focused Rust regression coverage and agent docs. Verified plain cargo tauri dev WebGL probe returned webgl=true, saved-location .canopi opened with mapActive=true and MapLibre canvas, and nav.location Location panel loaded with MapLibre canvas. Gates: cargo fmt --all -- --check; CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo check --workspace; CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace.

title: Windows in-app update reopens a Design whose path has a space as two files
description: Found by CI round 4 (gate-logs/phase-0/ci-triage-pr76-r4.md T1). Canopi starts the NSIS installer with /ARGS "<path>"; NSIS GetOptions strips the outer quotes and nsis_tauri_utils RunAsUser passes the bare path, so the relaunched app gets the path split at the space and fails to open it (no data loss: the edit is saved before the installer). Fix: backtick-wrap the escaped args in launch::installer_command; round-trip test through ports of GetOptions and Windows argv parsing. Upstream (tauri-plugin-updater escape_nsis_current_exe_arg + bundler installer.nsi) has the same flaw: report upstream after the fix (user's call, outward-facing).

title: Vite 8's minifier unquotes a non-ASCII key; WebKitGTK rejects the raster worker and GeoTIFFs never draw
description: Found by F0b's live check on the production build (a9e164e2b). geotiff-geokeys-to-proj4/index.js has the quoted key "\u088f"; the Oxc minifier writes it as a bare identifier, which this WebKitGTK (Safari 605 UA) rejects: SyntaxError Invalid character '\u088f' in assets/worker-*.js; the same table sits in cog-tiler-*.js (Web too). The worker error reaches no console or log; the imported GeoTIFF is listed in Site data and never drawn. Playwright's newer WebKit parses it, so e2e passed. Fix in F0b before its PR merges, with a build check over every emitted chunk and worker.

design:
# Story maps in Canopi: implementation plan

Status: agreed (2026-09-26). Nothing is implemented beyond the parked `ux-views` branch.
Beads: canopi-5ys2.3 (epic) · .1 saved views · .2 Stories panel · .3 present · .4 export.
Mockups: design canvas boards StoryAuthor, StoryPresent, StoryPhone.

## 1. What users get

- **Save a view** of the map: where it looks, which background and site data are shown, which species or objects are highlighted, an optional title and text. View › Saved views lists them; Go to view moves the camera only.
- **Build a story** in a Stories panel beside the live map: steps are saved views with a title, formatted text and optional images; add the current view as a step, reorder with drag or Alt ↑/↓, edit text in place, "Use the current map view" to update a step, "Go to this view" to check it.
- **Present** full-window inside Canopi (Desktop and Web, and on phones): a text card beside the map, Previous/Next, step dots, keyboard (← → Space Esc), the map moves between steps (a jump when reduced motion is on), highlighted plants ringed.
- **Export** later: a self-contained web page and a PDF, one step per page.

## 2. What already exists (parked branch `ux-views`, commit b2ee529b, not merged)

- `common-types/src/views.rs`: `SavedView` (camera lon/lat/zoom/bearing, visible layers: background, terrain, scene layers, site-data ids; highlight: species names and typed object refs; title; rich text), `Story`, `StoryStep` (view id, title, rich text, images), `RichTextBlock` (paragraph, bullets) with spans (bold, italic, link — http, https, mailto only), `StoryImage` (https URL or data URI), `validate_views_and_stories`.
- `.canopi` format v8 with `views` and `stories`; v7 refused (ADR 0003); generated TS bindings; Design Edit commands; `view.saveCurrentView` / `view.goToView`; a Save view dialog; camera fly in `maplibre/workspace-camera.ts`; i18n in 11 locales; guide updates. Gates had not been run to completion when the session limit hit.

Recommendation: keep this model and finish it as bead .1, after the decisions below (images and export affect it).

## 3. Architecture

- **Authority.** Views and stories are Design data owned by Design Edit (`app/design-edit/`), saved through the document session like budget and timeline. They are not part of scene undo (consistent with the architecture page); edits get an Undo toast for destructive actions (delete view, delete story, remove step).
- **Referential integrity.** A step references a view by id. Deleting a view used by steps asks first and names the stories; renaming is free. The validator refuses dangling references on load.
- **Applying a view** is session state, never a Design edit: camera through the workspace camera (fly or jump), background and terrain through the map layer store as a temporary presentation override (restored when leaving the step or presentation), scene layer and site-data visibility through presentation overrides (not the Design's own visibility), highlight through the existing species-focus / highlight seam. Leaving presentation restores the user's own state exactly.
- **Presentation mode** is a workspace mode owned by one controller (`app/story-presentation/`): it hides editing chrome, blocks editing commands and single-key tool shortcuts, traps focus in the story card, and disposes its overrides on exit, on Design switch and on HMR (resource-ownership rule).
- **Rich text.** A small editor over `RichTextBlock` (bold, italic, bullets, links, images) built on `contenteditable` with a strict schema: paste is sanitised to the block model; no raw HTML persists. Rendering is one pure function shared by panel, presenter and export.
- **Images.** See decision D1.
- **Web edition** has the same features (views and stories are plain Design data); export may differ (D3).

## 4. UI (per the mockups)

- Panel rail: Stories (Ctrl 9). Panel: story selector, New story; step list (thumbnail, number, title, first line of text, reorder handle, More: Duplicate, Move, Delete); Add the current view as a step; step editor (title, text toolbar, "This step shows" tags, Use the current map view, Go to this view); footer Export…, Present.
- Thumbnails: small map snapshots captured when a view is saved or updated, stored as session cache (or in the file, see D1) — never recomputed on every render.
- Presenter: floating text card (420 px, left), progress dots as buttons, Previous/Next, "Step n of m", full screen toggle, Leave (Esc). Phone: bottom card, swipe, 44 px targets, safe areas.
- View menu: Saved views ▸ list, Save current view…, Manage views… (a small dialog to rename/delete).

## 5. Export (bead .4)

- **Web page:** one HTML file with inline CSS, the story text, images and one map snapshot per step (PNG/WebP), attribution per snapshot. Static snapshots are reliable, offline and respect imagery terms better than embedding live Google tiles in a page outside Canopi (D3).
- **PDF:** reuse the PDF pipeline (ADR 0008) with one page per step: snapshot on top, title and text below.
- **Snapshot capture** needs a short spike: render each step's view off-screen at a fixed size (MapLibre canvas plus the Pixi scene layer) and read pixels after the frame settles (`preserveDrawingBuffer` or a read in the render callback), with tiles loaded or a timeout and a "some tiles missing" note.

## 6. Accessibility and languages

Presenter is a dialog-like region with a heading per step, live announcement of "Step n of m: title", keyboard and screen-reader navigation, visible focus, reduced-motion jumps, text scaling without clipping; step text keeps its authored language (`lang` per story, defaulting to the UI locale); all UI strings in 11 locales.

## 7. Tests

Format round-trip and refusal of v7; validator (dangling view ids, camera ranges, link schemes, image sources); Design Edit commands and undo toasts; applying a view never dirties the Design and restores state on exit; presenter keyboard and focus trap; rich-text paste sanitisation; snapshot capture fallback; export produces valid HTML and PDF with attribution; Web parity.

## 8. Beads and order

1. **.1 Saved views** — finish the parked branch: rebase on the new frame, run gates, add Manage views dialog and thumbnails cache. (M)
2. **Snapshot spike** — capture a map + scene snapshot reliably on Desktop and Web. (S)
3. **.2 Stories panel** — panel, step list, reorder, rich-text editor with sanitised paste, images per D1. (L)
4. **.3 Present** — presentation controller, overrides and restore, presenter card, phone layout, full screen. (M)
5. **.4 Export** — HTML and PDF. (M)

## 9. Decisions (2026-09-26: the user adopted the recommendations)

- **D1 Images:** (a) embedded in the `.canopi` as compressed data (single portable file; cap 1 MB per image, 10 MB per Design) — recommended; (b) links only (small files, breaks offline); (c) files beside the Design (breaks single-file sharing).
- **D2 Step ↔ view:** a step points to a saved view (one view can serve several stories; editing it updates all) — recommended; or each step owns a private copy.
- **D3 Export map:** static snapshots (recommended) vs an interactive web map (needs online tiles; Google imagery cannot be embedded outside Canopi, so it would fall back to OpenFreeMap).
- **D4 Scope for v2.0:** saved views, the Stories panel and presenting in v2.0, export after. Reason: the `.canopi` format change must land before v2.0, because a later bump would refuse every v2.0 Design (ADR 0003).

title: Extension seams for future analyses and story maps
description: Decided 2026-09-26 (user follows the recommendation): (1) Analyze is a registry of analyses declaring inputs, parameters and output types; the dialog is generated from it; slope, hillshade, contours become registry entries. (2) Every derived result records provenance: source item, tool, parameters, tool version, so results can be re-run or refreshed and a processing history is possible. (3) Site-data and library items are typed (raster now; room for point cloud and vector results such as streams or detected trees) instead of assuming elevation rasters. Record in the design ADR; build only the seams, not new analyses.
design:
# ADR 0011 implementation plan: analysis registry, typed items with provenance, hydrology

Research date 2026-09-26. Sources:
- Canopi worktree `.rq-scratch/wt-v2`, branch `feature/geolibre-adoption`.
- `geolibre-rust` at the pinned `aac2b743`; the checkout HEAD is that commit.
- `geolibre-src` at `e9df9e24`.
- Pinned CLI binary `.rq-scratch/s4-bin/geolibre` (`geolibre-cli 1.5.3`).

Every tool id and parameter below was checked with `geolibre manifest <id>` on that binary. The research agent ran the hydrology chains end to end on a synthetic EPSG:2154 Float32 DEM.

Beads:
- Seams: `canopi-h90p.9` (P1).
- Hydrology: `canopi-5ys2.1` (P3, depends on h90p.9).
- Where the UI lives in Layers: `canopi-h90p.2`.

---

## 0. Headline findings

1. **Slope is hard-wired end to end.**
   - `LidarAnalysisKind::Slope` is the only kind.
   - Rust side: `LidarAnalysisParameters`, `LidarAnalysisSummary.slope_unit` (required), `LidarAnalysisMethod::GeolibreProjectedSlopeV1`, `LidarLibrarySnapshot.slope_engine`, `SlopeRecipe`, `analysis::capability`, `inspection::result_units` and `paths::slope_scratch_dir`.
   - TS side: `lidarDisplayStyle` treats every `Analysis` as slope.
   - §1.4 lists every site.
2. **Hydrology cannot use the 1024² window lane.**
   - Fill/breach, pointers, accumulation, streams, basins, watershed and TWI are all global.
   - The guide currently forbids a whole-extent buffer ("no union raster … no whole-extent buffer").
   - Plan: add a bounded **global lane**:
     - Stream the composed collection into one scratch GeoTIFF, window by window.
     - Run the CLI on that file.
     - Read the results back window by window into the existing sparse chunk store.
   - A new admission limit caps the number of extent cells.
3. **Lane: GeoLibre CLI sidecar, not WASM.**
   - The CLI Canopi already pins has every tool needed: 1060 tools in total, from `wbtools_oss` in `opengeos/whitebox-wasm` @ `9c0ff4f`.
   - The WASM route (`geolibre-cli.wasm` via `npm/tools.mjs`) is the same catalogue running inside the WebView. It has these drawbacks:
     - It is limited by wasm32 memory.
     - It puts a raster engine in the frontend, which goes against the Web/Desktop boundary.
     - It is slower.
     - It adds nothing offline, because the sidecar also runs offline.
   - Recommend correcting bead `canopi-5ys2.1`, whose text says "bundled Whitebox WASM catalog", and the ADR's lane list. This is a user decision (§7).
4. **Licence (act now).**
   - The CLI binary statically links `wbspatialstats` (`license = "AGPL-3.0-or-later"`, John Lindsay / Whitebox Geospatial).
   - It comes in through `wbtools_oss` with no feature gate; the kriging and spatial-statistics tools use it.
   - `desktop/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:18-22` describes the sidecar as MIT with an MIT-or-Apache tool registry, which is incomplete.
   - Canopi is `AGPL-3.0-only`, and AGPL-3.0-or-later is compatible with that. Still:
     - The notice must name the AGPL component.
     - Releases must offer the sidecar's Corresponding Source: geolibre-rust `aac2b743` plus whitebox-wasm `9c0ff4f`.
   - `wbcore` and `wbtools_oss` declare no `license` field; only the repo-level MIT/Apache files cover them.
   - File this as its own bead now. This is not legal advice.
5. **The thread cap does not hold for hydrology.**
   - The hydrology and flow tools call `thread::available_parallelism()` directly:
     - `wbtools_oss/src/tools/hydrology/mod.rs:1966,2196,4771,10053`
     - `flow_algorithms/mod.rs:339,796,844,1307,2063,2197`
   - So `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2` is ignored.
   - The library-wide heavy lease already means only one heavy job runs at a time. Add a lower child-process priority and file an upstream issue.
6. **ADR 0011 changes three data-library contract lines.**
   - "A published result is never recalculated in place."
   - "A slope job has no stale or superseded outcome."
   - "No … automatic analysis refresh" (ADR 0002).
   - Refresh stays user-initiated, never automatic, so ADR 0002 still holds. The guide's section on the result lifecycle gets rewritten (§3.6).

## 2. Hydrology through GeoLibre

### 2.1 Where the tools are

**Location**
- None of these tools are in `crates/geolibre-*`.
- They come from `wbtools_oss`, a git dependency on `opengeos/whitebox-wasm` @ `9c0ff4fdf351` (`geolibre-rust/Cargo.lock:3697-3720`).
- `geolibre-cli/src/main.rs:40 build_registry()` registers them (`register_default_tools` plus `geolibre_tools::geolibre_tools()`).

**CLI grammar** (`main.rs:321-460`)
- Commands: `list`, `manifests` (JSON), `manifest <id>`, `version` (prints `geolibre-cli 1.5.3`).
- Tools run as `<tool_id> --k=v ...`; values are inferred as bool, i64, f64 or string.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 tool error (message on stderr), 2 usage error.

**Output and progress**
- The last stdout line is an outputs JSON (`{"path":"..."}`).
- Earlier lines are free-text `info` messages.
- Percent progress is compiled out (`EMIT_PROGRESS=false`, `main.rs:466`).

**Cancellation**
- There is no cancellation API: `ToolContext` has only progress and capabilities.
- Cancel means kill, which Canopi's runner already does.
- Outputs are written directly to the target path, so keep writing to scratch and publishing afterwards.

### 2.2 Tools at the pinned revision

All of these are present, and HEAD equals the pin. \* = required parameter.

**Conditioning, routing and accumulation**
- **Breach:** `breach_depressions_least_cost`
  - Parameters: `dem`\*, `output`, `max_dist` (integer, **cells**, default 100), `fill_deps` (false), `max_cost`, `flat_increment`, `minimize_dist`.
  - Output: Float64 raster. Global.
- **Fill:** `fill_depressions`
  - Parameters: `dem`\*, `output`, `fix_flats` (true), `flat_increment` (1e-4), `flat_resolution` (`garbrecht_martz` or `natural`), `max_depth`.
  - Output: Float64. Global.
- **D8 pointer:** `d8_pointer`
  - Parameters: `dem`\*, `output`, `esri_pntr` (false).
  - Output: Int16, NoData -32768, values 0..128. Mostly global.
- **Accumulation:** `d8_flow_accum`
  - Parameters: `input`\*, `input_is_pointer`, `out_type` (`cells`, `ca` or `sca`; default `sca`), `log_transform`, `output`.
  - Output: Float32, NoData -32768. Global.

**Streams**
- **Extract streams:** `extract_streams`
  - Parameters: `flow_accumulation`\*, `threshold` (same units as the accumulation raster; default 0), `zero_background` (false), `output`.
  - Output: Int16. Local on the accumulation raster.
- **Stream order:** `strahler_stream_order`
  - Parameters: `d8_pntr`\*, `streams`\*, `zero_background`, `output`.
  - Output: Int32. Global.
- **Streams to lines:** `raster_streams_to_vector`
  - Parameters: `d8_pntr`\*, `streams_raster`\*, `all_vertices`, `output` (line vector).
  - Output: lines with `FID` and `STRM_VAL`. Global.

**Catchments**
- **Snap outlets:** `snap_pour_points`
  - Parameters: `flow_accum`\*, `pour_pts`\* (point vector), `snap_dist` (**map units**; 0 means one cell), `output`.
  - Output: points. Local.
- **Watershed:** `watershed`
  - Parameters: `d8_pntr`\*, `pour_pts`\*, `output`.
  - Output: Int32, NoData -32768. Global.
- **Raster to polygons:** `raster_to_vector_polygons`
  - Parameters: `input`\*, `output`.
  - Output: polygons with `FID` and `VALUE`. Global.

**Wetness and ponding**
- **Wetness index (TWI):** `wetness_index`
  - Parameters: `sca`\*, `slope`\* (**degrees**), `output`.
  - Output: Float32, NoData -32768. Local on its inputs.
- **Ponding depth:** `depth_in_sink`
  - Parameters: `dem`\*, `zero_background` (false), `output`.
  - Output: raster in metres. Global.

**Later candidates**
- **Height above stream (HAND):** `elevation_above_stream` (`dem`\*, `streams`\*, `output`); raster in metres; global.
- **Flow length:** `downslope_flowpath_length` and `max_upslope_flowpath_length`; rasters; global. In testing, `downslope_flowpath_length` rejected pointers from a DEM with NoData corners, so defer it.
- **Basins:** `basins`, `subbasins`, `isobasins` (`d8_pntr`\*, plus `streams` for subbasins); Int32; global.

**Terrain entries**
- **Slope (used today):** `slope`
  - Parameters: `input`\*, `units` (`degrees`, `radians` or `percent`), `z_factor`.
  - Output: Float32, NoData -9999. 5×5 local stencil, windowed.
- **Hillshade:** `hillshade` / `multidirectional_hillshade`
  - Parameters: `input`\*, `z_factor`, `altitude` (30), `azimuth` (315); the multidirectional tool adds `full_360_mode`.
  - Output: Float32 with values up to about 32 684, not 0–255. Local; halo to be verified.
- **Contours:** `contours_from_raster`
  - Parameters: `input`\*, `output`\*, `interval` (10), `base` (0), `smooth` (9, odd), `tolerance` (10°).
  - Output: lines with `HEIGHT`. Vector; run it in the global lane.

**Vector formats and CRS**
- The vector writer picks the format from the file extension; `.geojson`, `.gpkg` and `.shp` were verified.
- GeoJSON output is written in WGS84 lon/lat, even when the input raster is Lambert-93.
- GeoJSON pour points are read as WGS84 and reprojected to the raster CRS. GeoJSON with projected coordinates fails with "latitude out of range".
- This matches principle 2 exactly: Canopi stores and exchanges vectors in lon/lat.

**Measured on a 3000×3000 Float32 DEM**

| Tool | Time | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|
| breach with fill | 4.3 s | 473 MB (about 50 B/cell) |
| fill | 5.0 s | 393 MB |
| `d8_flow_accum` from the DEM | 3.3 s | 358 MB |
| `d8_pointer` | 2.3 s | 225 MB |
| `slope` | 3.3 s | 258 MB |

Outputs are tiled 512×512. Breach and fill outputs are Float64.

### 2.3 Lane recommendation

**Use the GeoLibre CLI sidecar for every entry**
- Two modes: windowed (slope, hillshade) and the new global mode (contours, hydrology).
- One binary, one pin (`GEOLIBRE_REVISION`), one discovery path, one provenance string, one bounded runner, kill on cancel.

**Not Whitebox WASM**
- `geolibre-wasm` exports no hydrology; its `analysis.rs` has only `convex_hull` and `morans_i`.
- The WASI CLI path would run raster engines in the WebView.
- It is bounded by wasm32 memory (about 4 GiB), while global rasters need about 50 B/cell.
- It duplicates the native lane.
- The Web edition has no library to analyse anyway.

**Threads and priority**
- Keep `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2`; it still bounds slope.
- For global tools, accept that they use all cores. The library-wide heavy lease means only one such job runs at a time.
- Start the child at below-normal priority: `setpriority` in `pre_exec` on Unix, `BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS` on Windows.
- Upstream issue: make `wbtools_oss` hydrology respect `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` or accept a `--threads` flag.

**Licences**
- geolibre-rust: MIT (Qiusheng Wu).
- whitebox-wasm crates: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (Lindsay / Whitebox Geospatial), except `wbspatialstats`, which is AGPL-3.0-or-later and linked into the CLI.
- Actions:
  - Fix `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `third-party-notices.test.ts`.
  - Offer the sidecar's Corresponding Source.
  - Upstream issue: put `wbspatialstats` behind a feature so a hydrology-only CLI build is MIT/Apache.

## 3. Design

### 3.1 Registry: authored JSON contract, generated Rust and TS, handwritten executors

This follows the `plant-filter-fields.json` pattern: `bindings-gen/src/plant_filter.rs` renders TS and Rust, driven by `npm run gen:types` and `check:types`.

- **Authored:** `common-types/analysis-registry.json`. It holds ids, versions, inputs, params, outputs, lane and i18n keys. It says *what* an analysis is; the argv it runs stays in Rust.
- **Generated:**
  - Rust: `desktop/src/services/lidar/analysis_registry_generated.rs`, a static `&[AnalysisDefinition]`.
  - TS: `desktop/web/src/generated/analysis-registry.ts`, a typed const array.
  - New renderer: `bindings-gen/src/analysis_registry.rs`.
- **Rust executors:**
  - Files: `services/lidar/analyses/{mod.rs, windowed.rs, global.rs, terrain.rs, hydrology.rs}`.
  - `mod.rs` holds `fn executor(id) -> Option<&'static dyn AnalysisExecutor>`.
  - A test asserts a one-to-one match between registry entries and executors: no entry without an executor, no executor without an entry.

Registry types (Rust names; TS mirrors them through generation):

```rust
pub struct AnalysisDefinition {
    pub id: &'static str,              // "terrain.slope", "hydrology.water-flow"
    pub version: u32,                  // recipe version; bump when the method changes
    pub group: AnalysisGroup,          // Terrain | Water | Vegetation
    pub title_key: &'static str,       // "analyses.terrain.slope.title"
    pub summary_key: &'static str,
    pub lane: AnalysisLane,            // GeolibreWindowed { halo: u32 } | GeolibreGlobal
    pub inputs: &'static [AnalysisInputSpec],
    pub params: &'static [AnalysisParamSpec],
    pub outputs: &'static [AnalysisOutputSpec],
}
pub struct AnalysisInputSpec {
    pub key: &'static str,             // "dem"
    pub accepts: &'static [ItemTypePattern],   // Raster{GroundElevation}
    pub requires: &'static [GridRequirement],  // ProjectedMetreGrid, MetreValues
}
pub enum AnalysisParamType {
    Choice { options: &'static [&'static str] },
    Number { min: f64, max: f64, step: f64, unit: ParamUnit }, // Metre | SquareMetre | Degree
    Integer { min: i64, max: i64 },
    Boolean,
    Points { min: u32, max: u32 },     // lon/lat picked on the map
}
pub struct AnalysisParamSpec {
```

### 3.4 Execution

**Create**
- Command: `lidar_create_analysis(request: AnalysisRequest) -> AnalysisReceipt {definition_id, job_id, item_ids}`, on the `UserData` executor.
- Request shape: `AnalysisRequest {analysis_id, inputs: [{key, item_id}], parameters: [AnalysisParamValue], outputs: [String], name: Option<String>}`.
- Steps:
  1. Look the analysis up in the registry.
  2. `registry::validate`:
     - types, ranges, choices and required fields;
     - points inside the input's bounds;
     - at least one output selected;
     - inputs match `accepts`.
  3. Recheck the offer (engine present, grid facts, extent).
  4. In one transaction, insert the definition, its inputs, the derived items (units resolved from `OutputUnits`) and a job pinned to the current input heads.
  5. Spawn `run_analysis`.

**Run**
- `run_analysis` is generic and replaces `run_slope_job`:
  1. Wait for the heavy lease.
  2. On the `Local` executor, call `executor(analysis_id).run(ctx)`.
     - `ctx` provides the pinned inputs, parsed params, scratch dir `prepared/scratch-analysis-<job>`, cancel flag and engine.
     - It returns one `StagedOutput` per output key: raster chunk rows or a vector asset.
  3. Publish in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction:
     - check that the job is still preparing, each input's head still equals its pinned generation, and the definition still exists;
     - insert every output's generation, publish the chunks and **upsert** the heads;
     - record `tool_provenance` and `finished_at`, and complete the job;
     - delete the superseded generations' chunk and vector rows (the existing unreferenced-asset sweep removes the files).
- All outputs publish, or none do.

**Windowed lane** (`analyses/windowed.rs`)
- Generalises today's `compute_slope_block` over `(tool_id, args, halo, output_nodata_rule, quality: StencilValid | None)`.
- Slope keeps its 5×5 stencil (halo 2) and its quality mask.
- Hillshade gets halo 1, but only after an acceptance test proves its stencil and NoData handling across a chunk seam. The model is the existing `geolibre_slope_matches_the_analytic_surface_across_a_chunk_seam`.

**Global lane** (`analyses/global.rs`)
1. **Admission** (`admission.rs`):
   - `MAX_GLOBAL_ANALYSIS_CELLS` is charged on the lattice extent (width × height), because the tool allocates the whole bounding box, not just valid cells.
   - Proposed limit: 25 000 000 cells (5000²). That is about 1.25 GB peak in the tool, 25 km² at 1 m, or 6.25 km² at 0.5 m.
   - Free space must cover about 40 B/cell of scratch plus the 256 MiB floor.
   - Over the limit, the job is refused by name, and the offer reports `ExtentTooLarge` before the user starts. This is a safety limit, not a performance claim.
2. **Materialise the input:**
   - For each occupied 1024² chunk, read it with `generation::resolve_window` (sources) or `GenerationChunkReader` (derived inputs).
   - Write its rows at their offsets in a pre-sized raw Float32 file (`pwrite`; never a whole-extent buffer in memory). Invalid cells get the -2^127 sentinel.
   - Convert with `raw_to_tif` and tag NoData.
   - Check cancel and free space between windows.
3. **Run the tool chain** through a generic `GeolibreEngine::run(tool_id, args, env)`, which replaces `slope()`:
   - one bounded child per step, below-normal priority;
   - make the deadline configurable per step instead of the fixed 600 s;
   - parse the final stdout JSON line to confirm each output path.
4. **Read raster results back** window by window, using `gdal_translate -srcwin` into raw Float32 (a windowed `raw_f32_bytes`):
   - Map the tool's NoData (per output) and any non-finite values to invalid.
   - Force invalid wherever the input cell was invalid.
   - Write chunk COGs only for occupied chunks.
   - Write no quality chunks. The details view shows a caveat that catchments crossing the item's edge are truncated.
5. **Vectors** (the tool writes WGS84 GeoJSON). Canonicalise in Rust within a bound:
   - At most 64 MiB and 200 000 features; otherwise refuse by name ("raise the stream area threshold").
   - Keep only whitelisted properties, renamed to a stable schema: streams `{order}`, catchments `{outlet, area_m2}`, contours `{elevation_m}`.
   - Round coordinates to 1e-7°.
   - Reject coordinates outside the item's WGS84 bounds plus a tolerance.
   - Hash the file and admit it to `assets/<sha256>/features.geojson`. Files first, then catalogue rows, as today.

**Recipes**
- **`terrain.slope@1`** (windowed): `slope --units=<degrees|percent> --z_factor=1`, halo 2. Same science as today, renumbered under the new id.
- **`terrain.hillshade@1`** (windowed): `hillshade --altitude --azimuth --z_factor=1` (or `multidirectional_hillshade`), halo 1 to be verified. Displayed in gray over its value range.
- **`terrain.contours@1`** (global, vector): `contours_from_raster --input=dem.tif --interval=<m, default 1> --base=0 --smooth=9 --tolerance=10 --output=contours.geojson`. `smooth` and `tolerance` are advanced parameters.
- **`hydrology.water-flow@1`** (global):
  1. Condition the DEM, using either:
     - `breach_depressions_least_cost --dem=dem.tif --output=cond.tif --max_dist=<ceil(max_breach_m/pixel)> --fill_deps=true`, or
     - `fill_depressions --dem=dem.tif --output=cond.tif --fix_flats=true`.
  2. `d8_pointer --dem=cond.tif --output=d8.tif`.
  3. `d8_flow_accum --input=d8.tif --input_is_pointer=true --out_type=ca --output=area.tif`, which gives upslope area in m².
  4. Streams:
     - `extract_streams --flow_accumulation=area.tif --threshold=<stream_area_m2> --output=streams.tif`
     - `strahler_stream_order --d8_pntr=d8.tif --streams=streams.tif --output=order.tif`
     - `raster_streams_to_vector --d8_pntr=d8.tif --streams_raster=order.tif --output=streams.geojson` (lines with `order`)
  5. Wetness (flat cells become invalid):
     - `d8_flow_accum --input=d8.tif --input_is_pointer=true --out_type=sca --output=sca.tif`
     - `slope --input=cond.tif --units=degrees --output=slope.tif`
     - `wetness_index --sca=sca.tif --slope=slope.tif --output=twi.tif`
  6. Ponding: `depth_in_sink --dem=dem.tif --zero_background=false --output=sink.tif`. Depth in metres; non-sink cells are NoData and draw as transparent.

  Only the selected outputs' steps run, and the tool ids that actually ran go into `ToolProvenance.tools`.
- **`hydrology.catchment@1`** (global, vector):
  - Input: `dem` (ground elevation).
  - Parameters:
    - `outlets`: `Points{1..16}`, lon/lat picked on the map.
    - `snap_m`: default 5.
    - The same `depressions` / `max_breach_m` as water flow; the dialog prefills them from an existing water-flow run on the same DEM.
  - Steps:
    1. Conditioning, then `d8_pointer`, then `d8_flow_accum --out_type=ca`.
    2. Write `outlets.geojson` in WGS84.
    3. `snap_pour_points --flow_accum=area.tif --pour_pts=outlets.geojson --snap_dist=<m> --output=snapped.geojson`.
    4. `watershed --d8_pntr=d8.tif --pour_pts=snapped.geojson --output=ws.tif`.
    5. `raster_to_vector_polygons --input=ws.tif --output=catchments.geojson`.
    6. `area_m2` = per-value cell counts × cell area.
  - Recomputing the pointer from the immutable DEM takes seconds. It avoids storing a flow-direction item and avoids a result-to-result chain in v1.

**Rerun and refresh**
- `lidar_rerun_analysis(definition_id) -> AnalysisReceipt` (`UserData`) replaces `lidar_retry_analysis`.
- Rules:
  - Refused while a job is preparing.
  - The stored parameters are revalidated against the current registry version. If they no longer validate: "settings no longer valid; run a new analysis".
  - Inputs are pinned to their current heads.
- One command covers both cases: Retry (no head yet) and Refresh (a head exists).
- Heads are upserted:
  - Designs keep the same item ids and show the new generation.
  - Display descriptor keys include the generation, so no stale URL is drawn.
  - Inspection returns `StaleGeneration` and re-aims, as today.
- "Run again with changes" is different: it opens the Analyze dialog prefilled from the provenance and creates a new definition with new items.

**Stale detection** (in the snapshot builder, catalogue reads only). For each derived head, compare with its job:
- `input_generations_json[key]` differs from the input item's current head → `InputUpdated`.
- `job.recipe_version` differs from the registry's version → `RecipeUpdated`.
- `job.tool_provenance` differs from the cached current discovery → `ToolUpdated` (a soft reason: new build of the same method).
- One topological pass then marks dependents of stale items as `InputStale`.

Sources are immutable, so in v2 `InputUpdated` only happens for derived inputs that were refreshed (chains, Computree) or after a GeoLibre version bump. The mechanism is generic and cheap.

**Processing history**
- `lidar_processing_history(definition_id, cursor) -> ProcessingHistoryPage`:
  - `runs`: a list of `ProcessingRun {job_id, state, message, recipe_version, tool, inputs, started_at, finished_at, outputs: [{item_id, generation_id, coverage_cells | feature_count}]}`;
  - `next_cursor`.
- `UserData` executor, bounded pages (for example 50 runs).
- The bytes of superseded generations are deleted at publish; there is no restore.
- This keeps ADR 0002's "no dataset history" for the data itself, while giving ADR 0011's processing history as a log of runs.

**Other commands**
- `lidar_rename_item` and `lidar_delete_item` replace the separate layer and analysis versions.
- Delete behaviour:
  - Refused while `lidar_analysis_inputs` references the item; the error gives the dependent count, as today.
  - Removes a derived item's generations and head.
  - Removes the definition when its last item is deleted.
- `lidar_delete_impact` is generalised to items.
- `lidar_cancel_analysis_job` stays on the sync allowlist.
- Every new command lands together with its `invoke` call site; removed commands go with their helpers (the policy test enforces both).
- Restart recovery and the startup sweeps switch from `scratch-slope-` to `scratch-analysis-`.

**Display and inspection (native)**
- `display_cog.rs` already reads result chunks generically; only its entity lookup moves to derived items.
- Vector items get a display descriptor too:
  - the asset is copied, staged and then renamed, into `$APPDATA/lidar/display-vector/<sha>.geojson`;
  - the Tauri asset scope gains exactly `$APPDATA/lidar/display-vector/*.geojson`.
- `inspection.rs` reports the derived item's stored `units`, and `result_units` is deleted. Vector items are not sampled natively.

### 3.6 Docs to rewrite in the same changes

- **`docs/guides/data-library.md`**:
  - "Calculate slope" becomes "Analyze": registry, offers, create, rerun, stale, history.
  - Storage: v21 tables, derived items, vector assets, pruning of superseded generations.
  - Scientific invariants:
    - slope recipe renumbered;
    - global lane admission and materialisation;
    - hydrology NoData handling and the edge caveat.
  - Map display: vector descriptors, asset scope, styles by quantity.
  - Native execution: new commands; global-lane threads and priority.
  - Frontend state; gates (new tests and ignored lanes).
- Replace "A published result is never recalculated in place" and "A slope job therefore has no stale or superseded outcome" with the refresh model. ADR 0002's "no … automatic analysis refresh" stays true, because refresh is explicit.
- Also update:
  - `docs/architecture.md`: registry boundary, new module.
  - `docs/guides/native-and-release.md`: command list, `Local` jobs.
  - `desktop/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`: licence fix.
  - `AGENTS.md` quality gates: registry generation and check.

---

## 4. Beads and order

**L. Correct the GeoLibre CLI licence notice** (AGPL-3.0-or-later `wbspatialstats`). Standalone, P1.
- Content:
  - `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `third-party-notices.test.ts`;
  - a release note for Corresponding Source;
  - an upstream issue to feature-gate the crate.
- Gates: frontend tests, docs.

**1. Registry contract, typed items and provenance (slope only).** Parent h90p.9.
- Rust and contracts:
  - `analysis-registry.json` and its bindings-gen renderer;
  - `common-types/src/library.rs` and catalogue v21;
  - generic create, run, rerun, history, rename and delete;
  - offers and stale detection;
  - the generalised windowed lane, with slope as `terrain.slope@1`.
- Frontend:
  - the kind table;
  - the generated Analyze dialog replacing `CalculateSlopeForm`;
  - the stale badge with Refresh, and history;
  - i18n.
- Docs.
- Gates: all Rust gates, native policy, shared contracts, frontend plus coverage, `check:ui` and both builds, docs, the `lidar-native` lane.

**2. Hillshade entry.** Parent h90p.9.
- Content: windowed `hillshade`, the seam acceptance test, gray style.
- Gates: Rust, frontend, lidar lane.

**3. Contours entry: global lane and vector items.** Parent h90p.9, or a new bead.
- Content:
  - materialisation and global admission;
  - the vector asset store and display descriptors;
  - the vector adapter and vector inspection.
- Gates: full set.

**4. Hydrology: water flow.** Parent 5ys2.1.
- Content:
  - the `hydrology.water-flow` recipe;
  - styles for upslope area, streams, wetness index and sink depth;
  - child priority.
- Gates: full set plus ignored lanes.

**5. Hydrology: catchment from outlets.** Parent 5ys2.1.
- Content: the `points` parameter with map picking, and `hydrology.catchment`.
- Gates: full set plus ignored lanes.

**U. Upstream issues** in geolibre-rust and whitebox-wasm (external, no gates):
- respect the thread cap in hydrology;
- feature-gate `wbspatialstats`;
- optional percent progress.

**F. Later follow-ups** under 5ys2.1: height above stream, flow length, subbasins.

Doing contours before hydrology keeps each review small. Bead 3 proves the global lane and the vector kind with a single tool; bead 4 is then only recipes and styles.

## 5. Tests (write first)

**Rust unit tests (no engine)**
- Registry:
  - registry ↔ executor one-to-one;
  - registry JSON validation: unique ids and keys, defaults within ranges, `visible_when` targets exist, well-formed i18n keys.
- `validate(request)` refusals by name:
  - unknown id, wrong input type;
  - out-of-range number, missing required choice;
  - points outside bounds, no outputs.
- Offers per item: ground vs surface elevation, geographic grid, non-metre units, extent over the limit, engine missing.
- Catalogue versions: a v20 library is deleted; a v22 catalogue is refused.
- Lifecycle:
  - create inserts the definition, inputs, items and pinned job in one transaction;
  - multi-output publish is atomic: cancelling after the first output publishes nothing and cleans scratch;
  - rerun upserts heads, prunes superseded chunks and keeps the job history.
- Stale reasons: input head moved, recipe bump, tool change, transitive.
- Delete is refused for items used as inputs.
- Restart recovery for `scratch-analysis-`.
- Vector canonicalisation: property whitelist, rounding, out-of-bounds refusal, size cap.
- Global lane:
  - admission refusal and free-space checks;
  - materialisation never allocates a whole-extent buffer (peak live bytes bounded, measured like the `prepared_raster` counters).

**Ignored `lidar-native` lane** (pinned CLI, analytic surfaces in Lambert-93)
- Slope unchanged across a seam; hillshade across a seam.
- Contours on a tilted plane:
  - straight and parallel lines;
  - spacing equals interval ÷ gradient;
  - WGS84 coordinates inside the bounds.
- Water flow:
  - V-shaped valley: the stream follows the valley floor, order increases downstream, and upslope area grows linearly along it.
  - Bowl: sink depth equals the analytic depth; fill and breach differ as expected.
  - TWI is finite on slopes and invalid on flats.
- Catchment: an outlet on a two-valley surface covers one valley, and `area_m2` equals cell count × cell area.
- Cancelling mid-chain kills the child and publishes nothing.
- The real-fixture e2e lane gains `e2e_water_flow_on_ign_mnt`.

**Frontend tests**
- The dialog generated from a registry fixture: every parameter type, advanced disclosure, `visible_when`, optional outputs.
- Unavailable reasons shown by name, including NeedsDesktop and AlreadyInLayers.
- Point picking, including the keyboard path and Escape.
- `runAnalysis`, `rerunAnalysis` and `settleResultAttachments` fenced to their Design session.
- Stale badge and Refresh.
- Kind-table styles and legends (log stretch, gray, blues).
- Vector adapter lifecycle: create, sync, teardown, HMR.
- Vector inspection readout.
- i18n completeness across 11 locales.
- The Web build boundary still excludes raster engines.

## 6. Risks and constraints

- **Memory:** the global lane is bounded by the extent cap, not by the tool. Keep the cap conservative, and name it in the offer so users crop or import fewer tiles.
- **Edge effects:** catchments and accumulation are truncated at the edge of the item's coverage. State this in the details view and the guide.
- **Disk:** Float64 intermediates double the scratch size, and admission counts them.
- **Tool quirks:**
  - Hillshade's scale (about 0–32 767) comes from the value range; do not assume 0–255.
  - `downslope_flowpath_length` fails with NoData corners and is excluded until reproduced upstream.
- **Timeouts:** 600 s per child is ample at the proposed cap (breach on 9M cells took 4.3 s). Still, make the deadline per step and scale it with cell count.
- **Stdout:** only the last line is JSON. Parse it defensively, and treat a missing output file as failure (the current slope rule).
- **Native policy test:** it fails on any new command without an `invoke` call site, or with state access outside the executor. Land each command with its TS caller.

## 7. Decisions for the user

1. **Lane:** use the GeoLibre CLI sidecar for hydrology instead of "bundled Whitebox WASM". That means editing bead `canopi-5ys2.1`, and optionally changing ADR 0011's lane list to "GeoLibre CLI or native".
2. **Licence:** either ship the AGPL-3.0-or-later component in the sidecar with a corrected notice and Corresponding Source, or pursue an upstream feature gate first.
3. **Extent cap** for the global lane: 25M cells is proposed.
4. **Refresh semantics:**
   - Option A: refresh updates the item in place. Every Design that references it sees the new result, the old bytes are deleted, and the run stays in history.
   - Option B: refresh creates a new sibling item instead.
5. **Catchment in v1:** it recomputes routing from the DEM, so there is no flow-direction item and no chain.
6. **Order:** hillshade and contours as h90p.9 follow-ups before hydrology, or fold contours into hydrology bead 4.

title: Qualify exact batched Plant presentation
description:
Outcome: run one bounded experiment for an exact batched Plant presentation path that attacks the remaining per-Plant assignment/draw and Pixi submission cost in the production shared workspace, then accept it only if representative botanical correctness and lifecycle remain exact and measured reference-hardware evidence improves.

Trigger: canopi-ltck.26 reduced representative Graphics.clear p50 from 2,461 to 260 and dense 10,000 from 7,023 to 282, but final shared navigation still missed the fixed 16.7 ms frame reference. The final profiled dense run spent median 26.1 ms in Plant draw/assignment and 13.1 ms in Pixi submission; unprofiled dense navigation p95 was 66.8/83.4 ms and input proxy p95 173.0/263.6 ms. This continues to block Phase E qualification.

Non-goals: no threshold change, clustering, symbol/radius/colour quantization, label suppression, changed hit testing or editing/history, renderer replacement, new runtime dependency, second camera/context, LiDAR/terrain algorithm work, real-tile qualification, or release publication.
design:
Prototype behind the existing Pixi presentation seam and production capacity harness. Preserve the retained Scene graph and exact appearance key while reducing the one-Graphics-per-visible-Plant update/submission path, using Pixi v8 public APIs already installed. Measure one representative prototype before broad implementation. Keep one explicit owner for every buffer/context/listener and prove removal, Design replacement, fallback, and disposal.

Compare instrumentation off/on/off on the pinned representative fixture, then dense and dispersed temporary 10,000-Plant derivatives only after exact representative rendering, interaction, and lifecycle tests pass. Report synchronous CPU stages, Pixi submission, browser frame proxies, memory, GPU/native/raster unavailable fields, and fixture receipt separately. Reject and roll back the prototype if it changes botanical appearance/interaction or fails to improve the bounded bottleneck; record the failed experiment rather than expanding scope.

One implementation writer owns the Pixi Plant presentation module and focused tests. The lead owns harness/evidence, independent graphics review, bead/git integration, full gates, and push. Escalate after two failed implementation attempts or before changing public renderer/runtime ownership APIs.
acceptance_criteria: The representative 2,201-Plant Design preserves exact symbols, colours, radii, stacking, labels, selection, edit/history, semantic order, one camera/context, fallback and teardown; the pinned source hash remains unchanged. An accepted batching path has explicit bounded resource ownership and improves the measured Plant assignment/draw and Pixi submission bottleneck without threshold changes. Dense and dispersed temporary 10,000-Plant derivatives pass the same correctness/lifecycle gates and are removed. Record identical serial reference-hardware proxy evidence against 16.7 ms, below-50 ms and sustained-stall targets; failed targets remain failed and block downstream work. Pass focused tests, TypeScript, full frontend/UI/build gates, independent graphics review, diff hygiene, agent-doc updates, and measured effort reporting.
notes:
Rejected bounded batching candidates (2026-09-16):
- Measured wall effort was 22 minutes from claim at 15:54Z through final decision review at 16:16Z; token and monetary usage were unavailable.
- Delegation used one Sol high architecture/final decision review and one Terra high implementation/prototype pass; lead owned matched real runs, rejection decisions, evidence, bead and git integration.
- Forced public Pixi GraphicsContext batch mode preserved vector recipes but moved representative medians only slightly (shared layer 31.4→30.6 ms, Pixi 11.5→10.5 ms, Plant draw 11.0→11.0 ms). Two consecutive dense 10,000-Plant runs failed at the harness interaction stage with no cleanup failure while matched automatic batching passed. Cause remains unresolved; the control was fully rolled back after the second failure.
- A disposable exact-size atlas/ParticleContainer prototype covered all 16 symbols, dot/round, recipe/edge thresholds, close colours, focus opacity, interaction rings, cutouts, fractional positions, overlap/order, translucent layers and DPR 1/2. Its raster was nonidentical: DPR1 33,824 changed pixels, 22,502 delta>4, 1,079>32, max72; DPR2 80,775 changed, 38,090>4, 3,454>32, max79. Nominal RGBA atlas pixel storage was 2.5/10 MiB; one generation measured 29.6/47.9 ms before Plant updates. Appearance equivalence was unproven and steady-state p95 was not claimed. Cleanup left zero canvases; the throwaway prototype was deleted.
- Architecture review rejected Pixi internal tessellation APIs and a custom instanced vector renderer as outside this bounded bead. Neither evaluated candidate qualified; this is not an impossibility proof for separately scoped renderer work.
- Final tree has no renderer/test/harness changes relative to accepted canopi-ltck.26. Final validation was docs-only: git diff --check and fixture SHA-256 verification passed; code gates were not repeated. Temporary control validation passed 25 focused tests and npx tsc --noEmit before rollback; prototype passed DPR1/2 real WebGL execution, node --check and cleanup.
- Agent docs did not need changes because no production behavior changed. The v2 capacity evidence record was updated. Phase E and release publication remain blocked by the unchanged performance gate.
close_reason: Evaluated and rolled back forced vector batching after two dense interaction failures; rejected the atlas candidate because appearance equivalence remained unproven and setup cost was substantial. Recorded the bounded evidence with no production renderer change; Phase E remains blocked.

title: Optimize shared workspace navigation at botanical capacity
description:
Outcome: profile and reduce the measured production shared-workspace navigation bottleneck so the real 2,201-Plant Design and the supported 10,000-Plant capacity layouts are evaluated against the unchanged reference-hardware targets.

Measured trigger on headed Chrome 150, NVIDIA GTX 1080 Ti, i7-6700K, 1200x800, DPR 1: the representative shared scenario passed correctness but produced navigation frame-opportunity p95 100 ms, input-to-second-RAF p95 69.9 ms, and sustained intervals above 100 ms. The dense 10,000-Plant shared scenario passed correctness but produced navigation p95 150.1 ms and input proxy p95 219.4 ms. These fail the v2 plan targets and block Phase E qualification.

Non-goals: no threshold change, clustering that erases botanical styling, speculative renderer rewrite, LiDAR algorithm changes, native certification, real-tile qualification, or release publication.
design:
Use the accepted production harness and existing shared-layer diagnostics to separate camera/map scheduling, CPU scene projection/presentation work, Pixi submission, GPU/browser frame opportunity, hit testing, and memory. Add development-only observation only where existing diagnostics cannot be reached; do not broaden application ownership APIs.

First reproduce serially on the pinned representative fixture with identical headed hardware/method, then profile one bounded bottleneck. Prefer incremental viewport-only work, cached geometry/presentation, bounded label admission, culling with neighbour/footprint margins, or batching based on measurements. Preserve all Plant symbols/colours, Zones, guides, annotations, selection and edit/history behavior. Run the dense and dispersed temporary 10,000-Plant derivatives after representative regression checks. Report CPU submission, map/GPU proxy, memory and unavailable fields separately.

Escalate before adding a runtime dependency, changing SceneStore authority, replacing Pixi, changing camera ownership, weakening semantic appearance/correctness, or expanding into raster analysis/tile qualification.
acceptance_criteria: Representative and dense/dispersed 10,000-Plant scenarios preserve exact correctness, single-owner lifecycle and fixture integrity. On declared reference hardware, rerun identical serial evidence and classify p95 presented-frame proxy near 16.7 ms, p95 input-to-visible proxy below 50 ms, and sustained stalls above 100 ms without changing thresholds. Record any remaining miss as a failed gate with measured CPU/map/GPU/raster limits; pass focused/full frontend gates and independent graphics review.
notes:
Accepted bounded optimization and failed-gate evidence (2026-09-16):
- Measured wall effort was 72 minutes from claim at 14:39Z through final qualification and review at 15:51Z; token and monetary usage were unavailable.
- Delegation used one Terra implementation/profiling pass and one Sol architecture/review pass; lead owned integration, two real-render rejection decisions, lifecycle repair, gates, beads and git.
- Exact shared GraphicsContext reuse cut representative Graphics.clear p50 2,461→260 and Pixi submission p50 17.1→11.1 ms; dense 7,023→282 and 42.0→13.1 ms. A stable-context mutation experiment and a 64-Plant context-sharding experiment regressed measured work and were rolled back.
- Final two headed all-scenario runs passed exact pan/zoom/select/edit/undo, semantic order, single-canvas ownership, fallback, disposal/listener cleanup, derivative cleanup, and fixture integrity. Performance remained failed: representative shared navigation p95 66.7/66.7 ms and input proxy 53.7/100.0; dense 66.8/83.4 and 173.0/263.6; dispersed 100.1/133.3 and 308.8/236.6. Native/GPU completion, full-scene traversal, real tiles and raster/LiDAR workload remained unavailable.
- Sol found external Pixi context listener retention and unused per-Plant contexts; both were repaired and independently re-reviewed with no remaining blocking correctness/lifecycle defect.
- Validation: 9 Node harness tests; 49 focused Vitest tests; actual Pixi listener check; npx tsc --noEmit; full npm test; npm run check:ui; npm run build; npm run build:web; git diff --check.
- Agent docs updated: canvas performance, MapLibre shared-layer behavior, and the v2 capacity evidence record. canopi-ltck.27 owns the next exact batching experiment; Phase E remains blocked by the unchanged performance gate.
close_reason: Shipped bounded production-workspace profiling plus exact Pixi geometry reuse, bounded caches, redundant viewport-sync avoidance and lifecycle-safe context ownership; all correctness/lifecycle and frontend gates passed, while unchanged performance targets remain failed and are recorded for canopi-ltck.27.

title: Clean partial MapLibre construction before fallback
description:
Outcome: when MapLibre construction mutates the workspace container and then throws before returning a map, the MapLibre host rolls back only that synchronous attempt's DOM additions so the accepted Canvas2D fallback has one connected canvas and no stale MapLibre shell.

Reproduction: the production workspace capacity harness forces WebGL acquisition failure. It reaches fallback-ready but reports [single-owner]; the workspace contains one maplibregl-canvas plus one data-canopi-renderer=canvas2d canvas. This blocks canopi-ltck.24.

Non-goals: no rendering architecture change, fallback removal, MapLibre fork, broad DOM cleanup, performance optimization, LiDAR changes, or private fixture dependency.
design: Fix the explicit MapLibre ownership seam at both boundaries exposed by the real fallback run. MapLibreHost snapshots the synchronous constructor call direct-child identities and container class delta, rolls back only that delta when construction throws, and retains an idempotent rollback with the returned map so every later removal path cleans constructor-owned remnants even if map.remove throws. WorkspaceMapControls probes browser WebGL2 before surface attachment; unavailable WebGL2 rejects map admission before MapLibre can install browser listeners, allowing RendererHost to select Canvas2D cleanly. Preserve the original create error, pre-existing and later DOM, generation fencing, retry behavior, and the Surface Adapter as the only map-removal owner.
acceptance_criteria: Constructor failure removes only synchronous attempt-owned DOM additions, preserves pre-existing children and original error, and permits a later successful retry. Focused host/surface/workspace tests, TypeScript, full frontend gates, and the headed representative forced-fallback capacity scenario pass with one mounted Canvas2D canvas and complete teardown.
notes: Accepted after two consecutive headed production all-scenario runs. Forced fallback reached fallback-ready with exactly one mounted Canvas2D canvas, zero MapLibre construction/removal, pan/zoom/select/edit/undo passing, zero connected canvases and scoped persistent listeners after disposal, and no new post-disposal page error. Focused MapLibre lifecycle tests, TypeScript, 2,600-test frontend suite, UI typecheck, Desktop/Web builds, and independent Sol integration review passed. Measured lead wall-clock effort: 39 minutes from scoped branch creation through accepted review; one bounded Terra implementation pass plus lead integration/debugging.
close_reason: Shipped exact MapLibre constructor DOM rollback plus pre-attach WebGL2 rejection; all focused/full frontend gates and two real headed forced-fallback runs passed with single-owner cleanup.

title: Qualify production workspace capacity
description:
Outcome: add a development-only production workspace capacity harness that mounts the public WorkspaceRuntimeComposition and records reproducible aggregate browser evidence for the private 2,201-Plant representative Design plus temporary dense and dispersed 10,000-Plant derivatives.

Prerequisite: accepted production mount ba1604e342f5ad0372d8e06a419ad10936f3d006. Read plan sections 6E, 7 and 9; docs/agent/canvas-performance.md; the fixture receipt tools; public workspace runtime composition and edition adapters.

Non-goals: native/Tauri or release qualification, real tile cold/warm qualification, GPU completion timing, concurrent LiDAR processing, renderer optimization, LiDAR code changes, ADR acceptance, Rust/contracts, packaging, release publication, or compatibility conversion. Never modify or commit the private fixture, its path, raw payload, screenshots, or generated derivatives.
design:
Implement a development-only Node/browser runner around the public createWorkspaceRuntimeComposition factory. Load a memory-only v6 clone of the v5 private fixture by changing only format version and attaching newDesignSpatialFrame; do not create a shipping converter. Use memory-only app, panel, contribution, snapshot and basemap adapters. Load through composition.surfaces.documents and then call start; do not reconstruct camera, renderer, coordinator or controls.

Run serial scenarios: real 2,201 shared renderer; real 2,201 forced Canvas2D fallback; dense 10,000 shared; dispersed 10,000 shared. For each, assert one lifecycle owner, expected ready outcome, pan/zoom, selection, Plant edit and undo, stable semantic layer order, and complete disposal. Reuse and strengthen fixture-receipt derivative support so temporary directories are removed on success and failure and receipts never expose paths or fixture content.

Emit aggregate JSON only: fixture receipt; renderer/backend and browser/OS/GPU/hardware metadata; dimensions/DPR/warmups/samples; p50/p95/p99 presented-frame proxy intervals; stalls over 100 ms; input-to-second-requestAnimationFrame proxy; available renderer/work/render/memory counters; correctness and cleanup results. Label browser and proxy limits exactly. Missing metrics are unavailable. Classify the fixed plan targets without weakening them.

One writer owns scripts/canvas-performance/production-workspace.mjs, production-workspace.node.mjs, fixture-receipt.mjs, fixture-receipt.node.mjs, package.json, docs/agent/canvas-performance.md, and the focused evidence record. Exclude docs/README.md and all pre-existing dirty/untracked files. Lead owns bd, git, real runs, performance interpretation and integration.

Escalate if the public composition lacks required observation instead of broadening its production interface; if v6 preparation needs anything beyond version plus spatial_frame; or if correctness, fallback, stale-state or cleanup checks fail. A performance miss is a failed gate and requires a focused optimization bead; do not change thresholds.
acceptance_criteria:
Original fixture SHA-256 is verified before and after every real run and remains 446c656e12eca21ddf5c03e79cd1f8d7862eae88626c4cb550d55b505d246f40. Representative receipt reports the pinned 2,201-Plant counts. Both derivative layouts contain exactly 10,000 unique Plants with valid remapped references; temporary files/directories are removed on success and failure; output omits private paths, names, payload and raw screenshots.

The runner mounts the public production composition rather than rebuilding its owners. Shared and forced-fallback representative scenarios pass pan, zoom, selection, edit, undo, semantic ordering and disposal with zero connected canvases/listeners. Dense and dispersed capacity scenarios finish without correctness, stale-state, fallback-loop or cleanup failure.

Evidence records exact environment/method, labels proxy versus native/GPU facts, and classifies p95 presented-frame near 16.7 ms, p95 input-to-visible below 50 ms and sustained stalls above 100 ms. Any miss is reported and receives a bounded follow-up bead.

Run node --test scripts/canvas-performance/fixture-receipt.node.mjs scripts/canvas-performance/production-workspace.node.mjs, npx tsc --noEmit, full npm test, npm run check:ui, npm run build, npm run build:web, the four real harness scenarios, git diff --check, and final fixture hash verification. Update the performance agent guide/evidence record and report measured accepted effort.
notes: Accepted functional/capacity evidence from two consecutive serial headed Chrome runs on the pinned 2,201-Plant source and temporary dense/dispersed 10,000-Plant derivatives. All four scenarios passed shared/fallback readiness, pan, zoom, exact pointer selection, Plant edit, undo, semantic order where applicable, single canvas ownership, disposal, listener cleanup, and source integrity. Browser proxy performance failed unchanged targets in every scenario; native/GPU qualification is unavailable and canopi-ltck.26 owns profiling/optimization. Full required frontend, build, harness, privacy, and independent Sol review gates passed. Measured lead wall-clock effort: 67 minutes from scoped branch creation through accepted review, including one bounded Terra implementation attempt and one Sol review/re-review.
close_reason: Shipped the production composition capacity harness and aggregate evidence; all four correctness/lifecycle scenarios passed twice, fixed performance targets failed as recorded, and bounded optimization follow-up canopi-ltck.26 is open.

title: Mount shared workspace in both production editions
description:
Outcome: mount WorkspaceRuntimeComposition in Desktop and Web as the sole production camera, renderer, MapLibre and Canvas2D owner. Desktop removes its nested MapLibreCanvasSurface; Web gains the qualified confirmed-placement basemap. Existing LiDAR, terrain/reference, Targets, state, bounds and diagnostics flow through the accepted contribution adapters.

Prerequisite: accepted shared-map contribution lifecycle ddebaf1d4b9732968fbda598c6f6b47ce436863b. Read plan sections 4, 6D-F, 7 and 9; docs/agent/canvas-runtime.md, maplibre.md, document-lifecycle.md and edition-development.md; WorkspaceRuntimeComposition, Desktop DesignSessionLifecycle, WebCanvasWorkspace, CanvasPanel and their tests.

Non-goals: no GIS editing, Web Location editing, LiDAR library/analysis redesign, persistence/contracts/Rust, map interactivity, PDF maps, release work, private fixture content or gallery architecture rewrite.
design:
Add shallow WorkspaceRuntimeMountOptions and Desktop/browser edition composition factories that bind existing app, panel-target and map-contribution adapters. Lifecycle test seams become createRuntimeComposition(options); callers know only surfaces, start and dispose. Composition remains sole viewport initialization owner.

Desktop order: acquire lifecycle lease; construct with final container plus map-state/failure observers; await start; attach rulers; await startAttachedDesignSession; install resize observer; consume queued load; publish surfaces. Teardown synchronously hands off Design first, then clears autosave/cancels load/disconnects observer, flushes settings, awaits composition disposal and guarded unpublish. Failed attachment retains existing abort behavior.

Web order: acquire lease; construct browser composition; await start; attach rulers; attachCanvasSession and retain exact disposer; initial resize then observer; publish. Teardown synchronously invokes retained Design handoff before observer/composition cleanup and guarded unpublish. Reentrant unmount waits for construction/attachment settlement.

Accept shared-ready, fallback-ready and no-design. Treat non-disposal cancelled start as unpublished initialization failure and release resources. Existing Design, empty startup, first later Design, replacement, map failure and terminal attachment failure retain accepted composition/reconciler semantics. The final canvasContainer is passed directly to the composition; no wrapper map, sync effect or second camera. Desktop map state continues into Location notices; Web data-map-active reflects composition state.

Own/add: app/canvas-map-surface/desktop-workspace-runtime.ts and web/browser-workspace-runtime.ts. Own/modify: workspace-runtime-composition.ts; app/document-session/lifecycle.ts and use-canvas-document-session.ts; CanvasPanel.tsx; WebCanvasWorkspace.tsx; web/browser-canvas-runtime.ts only to retain/move the browser app adapter; the directly affected Desktop/Web/panel/UI-gallery/architecture tests; canvas-runtime, maplibre, document-lifecycle and edition-development agent guides. Retire app/canvas-runtime/host.ts and the old MapLibreCanvasSurface component/controller plus app/canvas-map-surface lifecycle/snapshot/reconciliation modules and their obsolete dedicated tests. Keep generic canvas/runtime/host.ts for tests/gallery.

Escalate if this requires another camera/renderer/map/resize owner; moving Design handoff out of current persistence owners; a Web-to-Desktop/Tauri/IPC edge; weaker synchronous replacement fencing; loss of LiDAR/reference ordering; changed composition start outcomes/coordinator policy; or retaining both old and shared production map lifecycles. One writer owns all listed files; lead owns bead/git integration.
acceptance_criteria:
Desktop proves start -> rulers -> startAttachedDesignSession -> resize/queued-load -> publish, with no edition initializeViewport call. Web proves start -> rulers -> attachCanvasSession -> initial resize/observer -> publish. shared-ready, fallback-ready and no-design publish; cancelled/failed start and failed hydration do not. Synchronous Design handoff precedes autosave/settings/load/observer/composition cleanup; reentrant unmount and failed handoff preserve exact ownership and one disposal.

Exactly one production composition/camera and at most one MapLibre instance exist per edition. CanvasPanel contains one runtime container and no nested MapLibreCanvasSurface. Desktop LiDAR, terrain/reference, bounds, diagnostics and Location notice remain connected. Web has empty LiDAR/terrain policy, confirmed-placement basemap, truthful data-map-active and no native imports. Map failure selects Canvas2D through the same runtime. Existing/no-Design/first-later-Design/replacement flows pass. Old edition host factories and old Canvas Map Surface lifecycle have no production references.

Focused Desktop/Web lifecycle, panel, UI-gallery, architecture, composition, generation, activation, controls, contribution and browser-adapter tests pass; then npx tsc --noEmit, full npm test, npm run check:ui, npm run check:types, npm run build, npm run build:web and git diff --check. Representative fixture hash remains unchanged. Update relevant agent guides and report measured accepted effort.
notes:
Accepted effort and validation (2026-09-16):
- Measured elapsed time: 44m18s from claim at 12:32:20Z through accepted implementation/review at 13:16:38Z. This wall-clock interval is the available effort proxy; token and monetary usage were unavailable.
- Delegation: one Sol high architecture pass and independent final review; one Terra high implementation pass plus two targeted repair attempts; lead integration, browser dependency repair, acceptance-test repair, gates, bead and git ownership. The Terra retry loop stopped after the second targeted attempt per section 9.
- Outcome: Desktop and Web mount WorkspaceRuntimeComposition as the sole production camera/renderer/map owner; retired edition host and standalone Canvas Map Surface paths were removed; Desktop contributions and Web confirmed-placement basemap remain edition-shaped; browser workspace graph is native-free.
- Focused: 14 files, 259 tests passed; npx tsc --noEmit and git diff --check passed.
- Broad: npm test passed 268 files/2593 tests; npm run check:ui, npm run check:types, npm run build, and npm run build:web passed. Desktop/Web builds emitted only the existing chunk-size advisory. Representative fixture SHA-256 remained 446c656e12eca21ddf5c03e79cd1f8d7862eae88626c4cb550d55b505d246f40.
- Review: independent integration review approved after exact startup-order and injected-browser-store coverage were added; no remaining P0-P2 findings.
- Agent docs updated: canvas runtime, document lifecycle, edition development, and MapLibre ownership/mount guidance.
close_reason: Mounted the shared workspace composition in Desktop and Web, removed the retired standalone production map/runtime paths, preserved edition contributions and fallback ownership, added exact lifecycle/native-boundary coverage, updated agent guides, and passed 14 focused files/259 tests, full 268 files/2593 tests, TypeScript, UI, generated types, both edition builds, diff hygiene, independent review, and fixture hash verification.

title: Qualify shared-map contributions and status lifecycle
description:
Outcome: qualify an unmounted shared-map contribution manager so one WorkspaceMapControls map can reproduce the existing Canvas Map Surface display and status responsibilities before either edition mounts it. The shared map receives the latest ordered LiDAR, terrain/reference, shared scene and panel-target overlays while production edition roots continue using the existing mounted surface.

Prerequisites: accepted runtime-composition commit 2ea3ca310824e33cfab3d74c9640a3bdb2d350b5 and the qualified shared renderer/camera lifecycle. Reuse existing lidar.ts, overlays.ts, terrain-sync.ts, layer-stack.ts, Surface Adapter, activation coordinator and generation reconciler.

Non-goals: no edition mounting, old-surface removal, GIS expansion, LiDAR analysis changes, persistence or shared contracts, Rust, release work, private fixtures, Web LiDAR/terrain, raw MapLibre exposure, or second camera path.
design:
Add a required edition contribution adapter and a generic workspace map contribution manager. The snapshot carries session identity, ordered LiDAR, terrain state and panel-target overlay state. Desktop supplies current LiDAR/terrain/targets, terrain protocol loading and view-bounds publication. Browser supplies targets and explicit empty LiDAR/terrain capabilities without Desktop IPC imports. WorkspaceMapControls remains the single map/resource owner and serializes basemap, scene and contribution restoration across style reloads. The manager owns session freshness, incremental LiDAR sync, async terrain generations, overlays, semantic ordering, map/terrain status, view bounds, diagnostics and cleanup before map removal.

Preserve semantic order: basemap -> ordered LiDAR -> terrain/reference -> shared scene -> panel-target overlays. Keep MapLibreCanvasSurface as the only mounted production map in this bead. Do not edit CanvasPanel, Desktop/Web edition roots or current session lifecycle modules. If the implementation requires exporting the raw map, introduces a Web-to-Desktop dependency, cannot fence stale terrain/style work, retains MapLibre after Canvas2D fallback, or changes document/LiDAR authority, stop and escalate rather than broadening scope.

Worker ownership: workspace-map-contributions and edition contribution-adapter modules; workspace-map-controls, workspace-activation and workspace-runtime-composition plus their focused tests; map loader types only if actual public APIs require it; maplibre/canvas/document lifecycle docs. One writer owns these files for the slice.
acceptance_criteria:
Existing Design: the shared map restores basemap, ordered LiDAR, terrain/reference, shared scene and panel-target overlays in semantic order from the latest session snapshot.
No Design: no map, terrain loader, contribution mutation or remote request. A first later Design activates contributions once for its new identity.
Opacity-only updates use paint mutations; LiDAR source-shape updates rebuild only affected sources/layers; neither recreates the map.
Style reload uses the latest snapshot, serializes reentrant updates and reconstructs all contributions in order.
Stale terrain loads, stale sessions, replaced maps and disposed controllers cannot mutate the active map. Passive LiDAR failures omit only that contribution; terrain failures publish terrain error state without destroying editing.
Fallback/removal publishes non-ready state and clears overlays, terrain, LiDAR, view bounds, diagnostics, listeners and async work before map removal; repeated teardown joins one result.
Browser policy provides targets with no LiDAR/terrain and keeps the Web graph free of Desktop IPC/Tauri imports. The mounted Canvas Map Surface behavior remains unchanged.
Focused contribution/control/activation/composition plus existing LiDAR/terrain/overlay/layer regressions pass, followed by TypeScript, full frontend tests, UI check, Desktop/Web builds and git diff --check.

title: Pin Rust 1.97.1 across development and CI
description: Canopi currently has no checked-in Rust toolchain policy while five GitHub Actions jobs use floating stable.
