title: Enforce native command execution policy
description:
## Slice Summary
After migration, encode the small reviewed allowlist of truly constant/pure synchronous native commands and fail architecture checks when blocking work escapes the executor.

## User Value
Future native features cannot silently reintroduce UI-blocking or unbounded command work.

## Out of Scope
Generating TypeScript IPC wrappers or requiring async syntax for demonstrably constant/pure commands.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** chore
**Summary:** Make native blocking-execution policy an executable architecture guard.

**Current behavior:**
After command migrations, a future synchronous handler could call filesystem, SQLite, network, rendering, or other blocking work without any gate noticing.

**Desired behavior:**
One reviewed allowlist names only truly constant/pure synchronous commands. Parsed or structurally reliable architecture checks fail for every other synchronous Tauri command and for direct global blocking-pool use outside the executor.

**Key interfaces:**
- Native command registry
- Native Operation Executor
- CI architecture/quality gate

**Out of scope:**
- Typed TypeScript IPC generation
- Requiring async syntax for constant/pure commands

## TDD Order

Add a fixture/temporary violation that the proposed guard initially misses, make the guard fail on it, then encode the minimal allowlist and remove obsolete blocking helper access. Verify every command rather than sampling.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every native Tauri command is classified as executor-backed async or explicitly allowlisted constant/pure sync.
- [ ] The allowlist is small, named by intent, and rejects filesystem, SQLite, network, rendering, compression, or long CPU work.
- [ ] Direct global blocking-pool calls outside the Native Operation Executor fail the guard.
- [ ] A regression fixture proves new unclassified synchronous commands fail.
- [ ] Native execution policy and required gate are documented in agent guidance.
- [ ] Architecture, formatting, Clippy, workspace check, and Rust test gates pass.
close_reason: Shipped a test-only syn AST architecture guard that cross-checks every #[tauri::command] against the Tauri registry, requires async commands to carry and await managed executor work, enforces a five-command reasoned bounded-sync allowlist, rejects stale allowances and direct filesystem/SQLite/network/rendering/codec/compression/loop effects, and confines blocking-pool/raw-thread execution to NativeOperationExecutor. Removed the duplicate string-scan guard and obsolete immutable AppHealth mutex; updated AGENTS/build guidance and corrected the no-bundled-DB test command. TDD: 13 policy fixtures plus live repository audit. Gates after rebase: cargo fmt --check; Clippy -D warnings; workspace check; workspace test (307 passed, 2 ignored). Frontend tests were not needed because IPC names/arguments/results and frontend code did not change.

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** task
**Summary:** Introduce bounded native blocking execution and migrate existing async blocking paths.

**Current behavior:**
A shallow helper delegates closures directly to the runtime global blocking pool. It owns no class capacity, admission bound, overload error, fair wait, or started-work permit lifetime.

**Desired behavior:**
A managed executor accepts class, static label, and owned closure. Class admission is immediate and bounded; admitted work waits fairly for running capacity; both permits remain inside started work; cancellation before spawn and panic/join failures release capacity; static tracing records safe settlement. Existing search, geocoding, image, and template acquisition paths use it.

**Key interfaces:**
- Native Operation Executor

**Out of scope:**
- Migrating synchronous command families

- Adding a second async runtime

## TDD Order

First prove unbounded admission/early permit release with controlled closures. Implement small-capacity executor tests for busy rejection, FIFO order, class isolation, caller drop, panic, and join failure. Register managed production policy, migrate each existing call site, then delete the shallow helper.

description:

title: Decision: Bound native blocking work with one managed executor
description:
## Decision

All potentially blocking native command work runs through one managed Native Operation Executor. Its small interface accepts an operation class, static label, and owned closure. Each class has bounded admitted and running capacity, fair waiting after admission, immediate busy rejection when its total bound is full, and permits that remain owned by started blocking work until completion.

## Rationale

The native surface has 50 Tauri commands, 46 synchronous and four async. A nine-line helper delegates five call sites to the global blocking pool without admission policy, while heavy Design/file, export, report, Species Catalog, and User App Data operations remain synchronous. Started blocking work cannot be aborted, so caller cancellation alone cannot bound resource use.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep the global pool and convert handlers ad hoc: centralizes no capacity, overload, or lifetime policy.
- Use one semaphore for all work: lets slow network or export work starve unrelated catalog and user-data operations.
- Give every service its own executor: fragments scheduling policy and makes overload behavior inconsistent.
- Convert all synchronous commands blindly: adds async surface area to constant/pure commands without health benefit.
design:
## Interface Contract

- Operation classes are Catalog, User Data, Local, and Network.
- Admission is non-blocking and bounded across queued plus running work; a full class returns a stable busy error before spawning.
- Admitted work waits fairly for class running capacity.
- Admission and running permits move into the blocking closure so dropping the caller future cannot free capacity while started work continues.
- Queue cancellation before spawn releases admission. Panics/join failures include the static label and release all permits.
- Static tracing records class, label, queue/start/finish settlement, and duration without logging request payloads.
- Capacities are construction inputs for deterministic tests and fixed reviewed production policy.

## Owned Complexity

The executor owns native blocking admission, fairness, started-work lifetime, overload errors, and telemetry. Commands retain validation and caller-shaped results; storage/services retain domain and persistence behavior.

## Dependency Strategy

This is one local-substitutable managed module. A direct Tokio sync dependency is acceptable only to use the runtime's fair semaphore explicitly; it introduces no second runtime and must be justified in the implementation bead. Tests construct small-capacity executors and controlled closures.

## Consequences

Migration is incremental: existing async blocking paths first, then high-risk local CPU/filesystem work, Species Catalog reads, and User App Data. A final explicit allowlist retains only demonstrably constant/pure synchronous commands. ADR 0008 and the Mutex-backed SQLite policy remain unchanged.

## Testing Strategy

Prove immediate busy rejection, FIFO running order, pre-spawn cancellation, caller-drop permit retention, panic cleanup, and class isolation before migrating commands. Each command-family slice adds responsiveness/concurrency regression coverage; the final guard fails when non-allowlisted synchronous commands return.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Executor interface, operation classes, bounds, fairness, and error modes are explicit.
- [ ] Started-work permit lifetime and cancellation semantics are explicit.
- [ ] Dependency rationale and SQLite/ADR compatibility are recorded.
- [ ] Rejected global, single-class, per-service, and blind-conversion alternatives have reasons.
- [ ] Incremental migration and final synchronous allowlist strategy are recorded.
- [ ] Follow-up implementation work is represented separately.
close_reason: Accepted in architecture health loop 3 after detailed evidence review; the selected interface, ownership, invariants, alternatives, dependency strategy, TDD plan, and dependent implementation slices are recorded.

title: Decision: Make translation reactive and inject Canvas localization
description:
## Decision

The translation module is the reactive authority for application text: every render-time translation reads and pins the current locale. Canvas Runtime receives translation through its existing app adapter seam and exposes one locale-refresh operation for mounted imperative interaction chrome. Runtime core must not import application i18n or settings modules.

## Rationale

The bound translation function does not read the locale signal, so callers recreate reactivity manually and mounted components without that incidental dependency stay stale. Six Canvas Runtime interaction modules import app-backed i18n directly, and the runtime locale callback only invalidates scene rendering; open menus, affordances, and the Plant Spacing HUD retain old labels.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep manual locale reads in each component: duplicates a subtle invariant and continues to miss callers.
- Force a root-app rerender on language change: widens invalidation and still does not update imperative DOM.
- Let Canvas Runtime import i18n directly: reverses the Canvas Runtime App Adapter seam and keeps application settings transitive.
- Rebuild all Canvas interaction chrome on locale change: risks losing active tool state, input value, and focus.
design:
## Interface Contract

- Render-time translation synchronously observes the current locale and requests text for that exact locale.
- Translation options preserve existing interpolation/count behavior.
- Application and browser Canvas adapters inject a translator with the same key/options/result contract.
- Canvas Runtime interaction ownership exposes one locale refresh that updates mounted labels, aria text, hints, and messages in place.
- Locale refresh preserves open/closed state, active tool phase, Plant Spacing interval and generated-count state, input selection, and focus.
- Detached/runtime tests may inject a deterministic translator; runtime core has no application i18n/settings import.

## Owned Complexity

The translation module owns locale reactivity and exact-locale lookup. Canvas interaction modules own how their mounted DOM refreshes. The Canvas Runtime App Adapter owns dependency direction, not translation state.

## Dependency Strategy

Translation is an in-process dependency injected through the already-justified Canvas Runtime App Adapter. No new public service or runtime dependency is introduced.

## Consequences

Scattered locale reads used only to force translation rerenders become obsolete. Locale-sensitive data reads remain explicit. Frontend architecture policy forbids Canvas Runtime imports of application i18n/settings while allowing the injected translator.

## Testing Strategy

Start with mounted-component tests that change only locale and currently remain stale. Then add open-overlay runtime tests with a fake translator, including Plant Spacing focus/state preservation, before removing direct imports and obsolete manual subscriptions.

- [ ] Reactive exact-locale translation semantics are explicit.
- [ ] Canvas translator injection and one-way dependency direction are explicit.
- [ ] Mounted-overlay refresh and Plant Spacing state/focus invariants are explicit.

- [ ] Architecture guard and TDD migration strategies are recorded.

title: Decision: Own Design Template acquisition and ordering
description:
## Decision

Design Template acquisition crosses the platform seam as a validated Design envelope, never as a temporary path or untrusted text. The import coordinator claims a monotonic intent before acquisition. The native adapter resolves a catalog identity, fetches bounded bytes, and decodes them through the native Design format authority; the Web adapter fetches an allowed static asset and decodes it through the Web ingestion authority. The Design Session accepts or queues the exact decoded envelope, and only the newest import intent may mutate session or Community UI state.

## Rationale

The current desktop path has no temp-file lifecycle owner, reloads downloaded templates through ordinary saved-path behavior, and can add disposable paths to Recent Designs. Desktop and Web both start replacement ordering only after acquisition, so older slower imports can replace newer intent and settle shared loading/error state incorrectly.

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep temporary paths and add a release command: retains a cross-process lease protocol and every cancellation/error cleanup branch.
- Let frontend workflow delete paths: cannot safely own native failure, queued-load, shutdown, or overlapping-import lifetime.
- Move acquisition into the Design Session: couples lifecycle authority to HTTP/static-asset policy instead of using platform adapters.
- Preserve completion-order behavior: contradicts user issue order and existing stale-result policy.
design:
## Interface Contract

- Import begins by issuing a monotonic intent for one Design Template identity.
- A platform acquisition adapter returns a fully decoded, compatibility-validated Design or a typed failure; it returns no path, lease, or raw untrusted payload.
- Native acquisition accepts a known catalog identity, resolves its URL internally, enforces transport/size policy, and invokes the Design format decoder directly.
- Web acquisition preserves the static-origin policy and invokes the Web Design ingestion trust boundary.
- The Design Session opens or queues the exact decoded Design plus caller-owned display identity as one envelope.
- A stale acquisition may finish internally but cannot replace a Design, overwrite the queue, clear the current selection, publish an error, or settle the newest loading state.

## Owned Complexity

The Design Template import module owns acquisition ordering, stale completion, envelope construction, and Community import settlement. Platform adapters own transport policy and decoding. The Design Session continues to own dirty guards, replacement, queued loads, and Design identity publication.

## Dependency Strategy

This is a ports-and-adapters seam with two justified production adapters: native bounded network acquisition and Web static-asset acquisition. Tests use deterministic acquisition adapters and deferred completions. No new runtime dependency is required.

## Consequences

Desktop temporary template files and their Recent Design side effects disappear. ADRs 0009, 0017, 0021, and 0023 remain intact: both editions ingest real Designs, Web uses static assets and compile-time adapters, and imports apply without Site Adaptation.

## Testing Strategy

Migrate path-shaped workflow tests before deleting the path command. Add native byte-decoding/no-temp/no-recent coverage, Web trust-boundary coverage, queued-envelope identity coverage, dirty-cancel/failure coverage, and reversed-completion concurrency tests for both session and Community UI settlement.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The decoded Design-envelope interface and monotonic intent ordering are explicit.
- [ ] Native and Web adapter responsibilities and validation failures are explicit.
- [ ] Design Session queue ownership and stale-settlement invariants are explicit.
- [ ] Temp-path, frontend-cleanup, and completion-order alternatives are rejected with reasons.
- [ ] ADR compatibility, dependency strategy, and TDD migration strategy are recorded.
- [ ] Follow-up implementation work is represented separately.

title: Partition Web app data into versioned resource records
description:

## Out of Scope

design:
## Behavioral Contract
Retain the public synchronous BrowserAppDataStore and adapter. Implement four versioned partitions with per-resource normalization. Read/migrate v1 lazily and idempotently; remove or mark v1 only after all required partition writes succeed. Preserve corrupt-Draft isolation.

## TDD Order

title: Fence mutable Workbench loads, mutations, and disposal
description:
## Slice Summary
Add local ordering/lifetime ownership to Design Notebook and Saved Object Stamps so stale loads and post-disposal continuations cannot publish.

## Steps to Reproduce
Start a library/notebook load, complete a create/remove/move mutation before that load resolves, then resolve the older load; the old snapshot overwrites the newer collection. Dispose during a mutation and its continuation can still publish.

## User Value
Concurrent user actions cannot resurrect removed/reordered items or update an unmounted Workbench.

## Out of Scope
A generic Workbench framework or changes to Plant Browser coordination.
design:
## Behavioral Contract
Each Workbench owns a mutation tail, snapshot epoch invalidated at mutation admission, and lifetime generation checked after each await. Mutations publish in admission order. Saved Stamps gains idempotent disposal and composition/HMR ownership.

## TDD Order
Use deferred adapters: Saved Stamps load after create, Notebook load after remove/move, overlapping mutations, and disposal during mutation. Make each red independently before implementing local coordination.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Old loads cannot overwrite later admitted mutations
- [ ] Mutations publish in admission order
- [ ] No continuation commits after dispose
- [ ] Saved Stamps has an explicit lifecycle owner
- [ ] No generic Workbench framework is introduced
- [ ] Focused/full frontend tests, TypeScript, HMR checks, and guide updates pass
close_reason: Shipped local mutation-tail, snapshot-epoch, and lifetime ownership for Design Notebook and Saved Object Stamps, including stable Design admission and explicit singleton/HMR disposal. title: Unify versioned Species Search normalization
description:

## TDD Order

title: Enforce .canopi compatibility conformance in Rust and Web
description:
## Slice Summary

design:
## Behavioral Contract

Cover missing/v1-v5, malformed nesting, all transforms, group ambiguity/dedupe, version zero, future versions, and unknown fields. Move group compatibility out of custom deserialization into ingestion.

## TDD Order
Land shared fixtures first and observe current zero/future mismatches. Add runners in Cargo and Vitest, align admission/error categories, then move group migration while retaining behavioral coverage.

title: Make UserDb publish only integrity-ready connections
description:
## Slice Summary

Interrupt the multi-statement v7 migration after its first ALTER, or reopen a current-version database and insert an orphan notebook membership. Partial schema commits while user_version remains old, and reopened connections do not enforce declared foreign keys.

## User Value

## Out of Scope

design:

Repair/check legacy membership integrity, enable/verify foreign_keys, and use declared cascades.

## TDD Order
Red tests cover synthetic multi-statement rollback/retry, future-version rejection, reopened-current FK enforcement, orphan rejection/cascade, and real v7 data preservation before composition and callers migrate.

description:

title: Decision: Preserve typed Design Object identity through Scene Session
description:
## Decision
Carry kind plus id as the canonical Design Object identity through Scene Session selection, hover, history, locks, queries, interaction, and renderer projection by deepening the existing Scene target module.

## Rationale
Hit testing and Object Groups already preserve kind, but session state drops it to raw strings and later guesses by lookup order. Cross-kind identifier collisions are legal and can affect the wrong or multiple objects.

## Alternatives Considered
- Keep globally unique raw IDs: not guaranteed for imported Designs.
- Add more lookup-order rules: preserves ambiguity.
- Introduce a second identity abstraction: duplicates the existing typed target seam.
design:
## Selected Design
Use SceneDesignObjectTarget and sceneTargetKey as the single identity vocabulary. Store lossless typed identity in session state and transaction/history patches; lock and mutation APIs accept targets; renderer projections derive per-kind sets at the presentation boundary.

## Invariants
- No operation infers kind from a raw identifier.
- Cross-kind collisions select, hover, lock, delete, duplicate, undo, and render independently.
- Transport entity identifiers remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Selected authority and boundary are recorded.
- [ ] Invariants and failure semantics are explicit.
- [ ] Rejected alternatives and tradeoffs are durable.
- [ ] Implementation bead(s) depend on this decision.
close_reason: Accepted in architecture health loop 2 after evidence review; selected seams, invariants, alternatives, and implementation dependencies are recorded in each decision.

title: Make Web Species Catalog Retry and teardown truthful
description:
## Slice Summary
Implement a retryable, resource-owning Web Species Catalog composition from the visible Retry action through filter/sidebar recovery to DuckDB connection/database/Worker teardown, including in-flight lifecycle races.

## User Value
A transient first-load failure can recover with one Retry, and HMR or final disposal cannot leak catalog resources or publish stale results.

## Out of Scope
Automatic retry/backoff, offline catalog fallback, fatal-query classification without evidence, or Desktop IPC changes.
design:
## Behavioral Contract

Add an owned DuckDB catalog reader returned by `createDuckDbReducedSpeciesCatalogReader()` and a small Web composition owner that keeps the public Workbench unchanged for components. Reader calls go through one admission/lifecycle function. Opening order is manifest fetch/admission → database creation → connection → base registration → publish.

Move all acquired resources under rollback protection. Abort/fence unpublished opening work during disposal; default Worker/database construction must revoke object URLs and terminate on construction/instantiate failure. Track admitted operations so disposal cannot close under a query.

Use rejection-evicting single-flight Promises for reader initialization, filter options, locale registration, and image registration. Broaden user Retry to reload unresolved metadata/sidebar projections. Workbench disposal invalidates search/filter/sidebar/favorite/detail generations before resource teardown.

## TDD Order

Write one failing lifecycle test at a time: fail-once retry; connect rollback; registration rollback; ready disposal; in-flight disposal; post-dispose rejection; single-flight locale/image/filter retry; Workbench Retry recovery; HMR composition ownership.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A failed initial manifest/DB/connect/register attempt can succeed on the next user Retry.
- [ ] One Retry reloads search and unresolved filter/sidebar projections.
- [ ] Concurrent initialization and per-locale/image registration are coalesced; rejected caches are evicted.
- [ ] Every acquired connection/database/Worker is closed or terminated on failure and final disposal.
- [ ] Dispose is terminal/idempotent, handles in-flight opening/queries, and prevents late Workbench publications.
- [ ] Cleanup attempts all steps and retains the primary error when cleanup also fails.
- [ ] HMR reaches Workbench and DuckDB resources through one owner.
- [ ] Focused lifecycle/UI tests, full frontend tests, TypeScript, Web build/package gates pass.
- [ ] `docs/agent/database.md` matches the implemented owner and Retry semantics.
notes: Review refinement recorded in canopi-soxg: terminal disposal gives admitted operations and connection close a bounded graceful window, then force-terminates DuckDB or its Worker if either stalls. A rollback cleanup failure remains observable and non-retryable because resource ownership cannot be proven released.
close_reason: Shipped retryable owned Web Species Catalog lifecycle with bounded drain/forced teardown, retry-evicting single-flight initialization, terminal Workbench disposal, coalesced Favorites refresh, stale-publication fences, HMR ownership, and updated database guidance. Verified with focused lifecycle/UI coverage, 1,736 frontend tests, TypeScript, native/Web builds, Web package, and CLEAN independent reviews.

title: Decision: Trust Web Design ingestion through one decoder
description:
## Decision
Adopt one browser-safe Design ingestion seam that accepts unknown data, migrates supported historical formats, validates the wire shape, applies defaults, preserves unknown fields, and returns a normalized runtime Design. Generate format facts from shared Rust authority.

## Rationale
Web file, template, and Draft boundaries currently admit arbitrary objects by type assertion, unlike Desktop Serde and migration handling. Validation and migration policy must be localized before Design Session authority.

## Alternatives Considered
- Keep casts and rely on downstream code: preserves distributed late failures.
- Add separate validators at each caller: duplicates format policy and drifts.
- Add an unmotivated runtime dependency: avoid unless existing tooling cannot generate a focused decoder.
design:
## Selected Design

Introduce a browser-safe Design decoder at the raw-data boundary. It accepts `unknown`, applies the same v1→v5 migration semantics as Desktop, validates required and nested wire fields against generated shared-contract facts, supplies documented optional defaults, preserves unknown top-level fields in `extra`, and returns a normalized runtime Design type distinct from raw wire input.

Generate the current format version and validator/schema facts from `common-types`; do not retain a second handwritten `WEB_CANOPI_FILE_VERSION`. File open, static templates, and browser Draft hydration must call this seam before Design Session replacement.

## Invariants

- No `unknown` file/storage value reaches Design Session through a type assertion.
- Supported historical formats migrate deterministically to the current version.
- Unsupported/future or malformed required values fail at ingestion with path-bearing errors.
- Unknown top-level fields survive the existing `extra` round trip.
- Desktop behavior and shared contracts remain authoritative.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Selected boundary, authority, and runtime/wire type distinction are recorded.
- [ ] Migration, validation, default, and unknown-field invariants are explicit.
- [ ] Rejected alternatives and their tradeoffs are durable.
- [ ] The implementation bead depends on this decision.
close_reason: Accepted in architecture health loop 1 after evidence review; selected interfaces, invariants, alternatives, and implementation dependencies are recorded in each decision.

title: Decision: Own the Web Species Catalog lifecycle
description:
## Decision
Give the Web Species Catalog composition one explicit lifecycle owner for lazy DuckDB acquisition, retry/reset, coalesced asset setup, rollback, Workbench recovery, and terminal idempotent disposal.

## Rationale
The visible Retry currently reuses a permanently rejected Promise and HMR cannot reach successful DuckDB resources. Acquisition and teardown are one correctness concern.

## Alternatives Considered
- Add dispose only to the reader: leaves Retry and Workbench recovery split.
- Recreate on every operation: discards intended database reuse.
- Add a generic service container: adds breadth without caller value.
design:
## Selected Design

Use a small owned browser composition: `createBrowserSpeciesCatalogRuntime()` returns the existing caller-facing Workbench plus terminal `dispose()`. Its DuckDB reader is a concrete owned reader with retryable lazy acquisition and idempotent disposal; the storage-neutral `ReducedSpeciesCatalogReader` stays operation-only.

The visible Workbench Retry remains the user authority but retries every unresolved initial projection (search, filter metadata, favorites/recents), not search alone. The generic Workbench fences late async publications on disposal. HMR disposes the Workbench first, then awaits reader teardown.

Reject the generational observable/blue-green reload API: it adds unneeded dual-WASM and public state. Reject the minimal reader-only design because it leaves swallowed filter/sidebar recovery and Workbench stale updates unresolved.

## Invariants

- One opening attempt and at most one ready DB/connection.
- Failed opening fully rolls back and returns to retryable idle; a rollback cleanup failure stays non-retryable and observable because ownership could not be proven released.
- Locale/image/filter lazy work is single-flight and evicts rejection.
- Dispose is terminal/idempotent, rejects new work, wins opening races, and gives admitted work plus connection close a bounded graceful-settlement window.
- The normal teardown order is drain admitted work, close the connection, then terminate the database/Worker. If admitted work or close stalls past the terminal window, database/Worker termination is the cancellation fallback so HMR cannot wait forever.
- Cleanup attempts every safe owned step, preserves the primary failure, and reports cleanup failures.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Owned composition, reader boundary, Retry scope, and terminal disposal are recorded.
- [ ] Acquisition, retry, single-flight, stale-publication, and cleanup invariants are explicit.
- [ ] Minimal and generational alternatives are compared and rejected with tradeoffs.
- [ ] The implementation bead depends on this decision.
notes: Implementation review refined the disposal invariant: an unbounded drain or close can itself leak an old HMR runtime. The accepted implementation therefore uses a bounded graceful window followed by database or Worker termination, while retaining cleanup failures and refusing a fresh opening when rollback ownership is uncertain.
close_reason: Accepted in architecture health loop 1 after evidence review; selected interfaces, invariants, alternatives, and implementation dependencies are recorded in each decision.

title: Trust every Web Design ingestion path
description:
## Slice Summary
Route Web file open, template open, and browser Draft hydration through one generated-fact-backed decoder/migrator that produces normalized runtime Designs and rejects malformed or unsupported input before Design Session replacement.

## User Value
Corrupt, stale, or malformed Designs fail at the boundary with actionable errors; supported old Designs and unknown future fields retain predictable round-trip behavior.

## Out of Scope
Changing Desktop file semantics, replacing Design Session, or introducing a general validation framework unrelated to Canopi files.
design:
## Behavioral Contract

Create a decoder module with one main entry point such as `decodeCanopiDesign(value: unknown): CanopiFile`. Parsing text remains a thin caller concern. The decoder owns sequential migrations, structural validation, normalization, and readable path-specific errors. Generate current version and validation facts alongside existing bindings so Rust/shared types remain the source of truth.

Route all raw Web sources through it:

- selected `.canopi` JSON;
- static template JSON;
- each browser Draft body during app-data hydration/open.

Corrupted Draft records must be omitted or surfaced predictably without poisoning other browser app data. Preserve existing Design replacement/persistence concurrency semantics.

## TDD Order

Start with one malformed nested input regression, then add current valid input, historical migrations, future/unsupported version, unknown-field round trip, template ingestion, and corrupted Draft isolation one at a time. Regenerate bindings in the same change and keep Desktop format tests passing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Web file, template, and Draft ingestion accept `unknown` only through one decoder.
- [ ] Required top-level and nested contract fields are validated with actionable field paths.
- [ ] Supported v1–v4 inputs migrate to the current generated format version.
- [ ] Unsupported/future versions and malformed values are rejected before Design Session replacement.
- [ ] Unknown top-level fields survive load/save through `extra`.
- [ ] Browser Draft corruption cannot poison unrelated app-data records.
- [ ] Duplicate Web format-version authority and ingestion casts are removed.
- [ ] Focused decoder/Web session/app-data tests, generated-binding checks, full frontend tests, TypeScript, and required Rust gates pass.
- [ ] Relevant document-lifecycle agent guidance is updated if commands or boundaries change.
close_reason: Shipped one generated-schema-backed Web Design decoder for file, template, and Draft ingestion; v1-v4 migration, malformed/future rejection, unknown-field preservation, corrupt-Draft isolation, shared version authority, docs, and generator guards are covered. Passed 1,757 frontend tests, TypeScript, native/Web builds and package, generated checks, Rust fmt/Clippy/check, and cargo test --workspace; three independent reviews were CLEAN.

title: Prune obsolete Web catalog JSONL writer helpers
description:
## Slice Summary
Remove the three unreferenced JSONL shard writer helpers left behind after the Web Edition production catalog moved to Parquet.

## User Value
The catalog generator exposes only its supported Parquet/JSON manifest paths and no longer implies an unused NDJSON generation mode.

## Out of Scope
Preserve JSON helpers still used for manifests, NDJSON test fixtures outside this production generator, and historical performance evidence.
design:
## Context

A repository-wide reference audit found that open_shard_files, close_files, and write_jsonl in scripts/generate-web-catalog.py have no callers. They emit the retired JSONL shard shape while current generation uses write_simple_parquet and write_json.

## Implementation approach

Delete only the three unused helpers. Add or strengthen a source-level absence assertion if an existing catalog-boundary test provides a durable home; otherwise rely on generator and contract coverage because no behavior changes.

## Invariants

Parquet generation, manifest JSON output, publication safety, artifact admission, and fixture-only historical NDJSON coverage remain unchanged.

## Verification strategy

Run Web catalog Python tests, the focused frontend catalog/package tests, source-reference search, and git diff checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- The three unreferenced JSONL writer helpers are absent from scripts/generate-web-catalog.py.
- No production generator path emits JSONL shards.
- Parquet generator/contract and focused Web catalog tests pass.
- Historical evidence and fixture-only NDJSON tests remain intact.
close_reason: Removed the three unreferenced JSONL shard writer helpers from the production Web catalog generator while preserving manifest JSON, Parquet generation, fixture/history readers, and publication safety. Verified 67 Web catalog Python tests, 47 focused frontend catalog/packaging tests, zero-reference search, and git diff checks. Independent review is CLEAN; no tombstone source test was added because behavior-level generator/contract coverage is the stable seam.

title: Remove superseded raw file IPC
description:
## Slice Summary
Delete raw-byte export and file-read commands left behind by removed background-image import and legacy binary export callers, together with trivial dead backend exports discovered in the same reachability audit.

## User Value
The native command surface exposes only file operations used by current Design, Budget, Saved Object Stamp, and snapshot-export workflows.

## Out of Scope
Preserve Design persistence, Budget CSV export, Saved Object Stamp portability, and native PNG/PDF canvas snapshot export.
design:
## Context

Raw-byte file export and file-read IPC survived the removal of background-image import and legacy binary export callers. Their only remaining references are declarations, Tauri registrations, frontend adapters, and self-tests. Current Design persistence, Budget CSV, Saved Object Stamp portability, and snapshot export use different focused interfaces.

## Implementation approach

1. Remove frontend `exportBinary` and `importFileDialog` adapters.
2. Remove Rust `export_binary` and `read_file_bytes` commands/services and Tauri registrations.
3. Remove or narrow self-tests that exercise only deleted APIs while retaining focused `export_file` coverage.
4. Remove tiny declaration-only backend symbols found in the same reachability audit only when they have no contract role: the suppressed schema version constant and test-only query re-export suppression.

## Invariants

- Design open/save, Budget CSV export, Saved Object Stamp import/export, and native PNG/PDF export remain unchanged.
- No generic replacement IPC is added.
- Query-builder production visibility is not broadened for tests.

## Verification strategy

Run source searches, focused Rust export/query tests, frontend typecheck/tests, then complete Rust format/Clippy/check/test gates.
acceptance_criteria:
- Raw binary export and file-byte read adapters, commands, services, registrations, and self-only tests are removed with no remaining references.
- Current Design, Budget CSV, Saved Object Stamp, and PNG/PDF export paths remain compiled and covered.
- The unused schema-version constant is removed, and test-only query imports no longer require a production unused-import allowance.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and relevant frontend tests pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo check --workspace`, and `cargo test --workspace` pass.
close_reason: Removed superseded raw-byte export/file-read IPC, moved live Budget CSV text export to a focused adapter, pruned dead translations and trivial backend exports, retained current Design/Stamp/native export paths, and added exact locale plus adapter guards. Gates: focused Vitest 60 tests; full frontend 181 files/1720 tests; TypeScript; cargo fmt; Clippy -D warnings; workspace check; workspace tests. Three reviewers CLEAN after fixes.

title: Replace obsolete operating and domain documentation
description:
## Slice Summary
Bring current operating docs, prerequisites, migration evidence, and the domain glossary into agreement with shipped Web Edition, Species Catalog, and retired Site Adaptation decisions; delete orphan guidance that no longer matches the skill catalog.

## User Value
Contributors and agents receive current commands, contracts, prerequisites, and domain scope instead of completed implementation plans presented as future work.

## Out of Scope
Preserve historical release notes, accepted or explicitly superseded ADRs, and durable architecture guardrails.
design:
## Context

Several current-state guides still present completed work as future plans or retain prerequisites and domain terminology contradicted by shipped code and accepted decisions. Historical release notes and ADRs remain valuable records and are not cleanup targets.

## Implementation approach

1. Replace the Web Edition website integration implementation plan with a concise durable artifact/routing/deployment contract matching the shipped website integration.
2. Rewrite Species Catalog Parquet/DuckDB guidance and performance evidence in present/past tense with the recorded smoke result.
3. Make frontend mobile workbench guidance present-tense.
4. Update the README Node prerequisite to the supported CI/toolchain version and declare it in the frontend package manifest if absent.
5. Use the domain-modeling workflow to mark Site Adaptation as a retired concept rather than an active repo-wide workflow.
6. Remove the stale AGENTS legacy activity/status caveat and delete orphan `docs/invocation.md`, whose invocation field is not used by the installed skill catalog.

## Invariants

- Accepted and superseded ADRs, release notes, architecture guardrails, and Site Adaptation absence tests remain as historical/decision evidence.
- Commands and paths are checked against current package scripts and implementation before editing.
- Package engine metadata matches the repository's Node CI version and installed tool requirements.

## Verification strategy

Search for stale claims, validate package JSON, run documentation link/path checks available in the repo, run frontend typecheck if package metadata changes, and use `git diff --check`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Current Web Edition integration guidance describes the shipped artifact, root/subpath routing, and deployment ownership without obsolete proposed steps.
- Database/catalog and frontend pattern docs describe implemented behavior in present tense; performance evidence records the completed smoke result.
- README and package engine metadata consistently require Node 22, matching CI and current tooling.
- `CONTEXT.md` identifies Site Adaptation as retired by ADR 0023 and no longer presents it as an active workflow.
- The stale AGENTS legacy-component warning and orphan invocation guide are removed, while historical ADRs/release notes remain.
- Documentation paths/scripts are verified, package JSON is valid, `npx tsc --noEmit` passes for package metadata changes, and `git diff --check` passes.
close_reason: Replaced the obsolete Web Edition implementation plan with the shipped root/subpath artifact and routing contract; made Web catalog/database/mobile guidance and performance evidence current; aligned README/package/lock to Node ^22.13.0; marked Site Adaptation retired in the living domain glossary; removed the stale AGENTS caveat and orphan invocation guide while preserving ADRs and release history. Verified package metadata/lock parity, documentation paths and sibling website contracts, TypeScript, 16 app packaging tests, website installer tests, and git diff checks. Three independent reviewers are CLEAN. Full frontend suite was not rerun because runtime code did not change.

title: Prune speculative desktop platform scaffolding
description:
## Slice Summary
Remove uncalled file-watching, thumbnail, and Linux desktop-registration scaffolding plus a duplicate generated icon while retaining the supported native snapshot export seam.

## User Value
Platform code and dependencies describe capabilities Canopi actually exposes, reducing cross-platform stub and release maintenance.

## Out of Scope
Preserve native PNG/PDF canvas snapshot export, platform marker crates, current Tauri icons, and supported OS compile paths.
design:
## Context

The platform abstraction exposes file watching and thumbnail generation with Linux implementation/stubs, but no command, service, frontend, or release flow calls either capability. The Linux native crate also retains unused XDG registration code and dependencies. Native PNG/PDF snapshot export is a separate supported seam retained by ADR 0011.

## Implementation approach

1. Remove `FileWatchHandle`, watch/thumbnail methods, their implementations/stubs, and error variants used only by those paths.
2. Delete file-watcher modules in `lib-c`, `lib-cpp`, and `lib-swift`; delete unused Linux XDG registration.
3. Remove associated module exports, crate-documentation claims, direct `inotify`/`libc` dependencies, and refresh `Cargo.lock` mechanically.
4. Delete `desktop/icons/256x256.png`, which is byte-identical to the configured `128x128@2x.png`, and stop generating the duplicate.
5. Update platform/build guidance and renderer terminology while retaining CanvasSnapshot, PrintLayout, export methods, NativePlatform, and supported errors.

## Invariants

- Native PNG/PDF snapshot export remains behaviorally unchanged.
- All three platform marker crates remain valid workspace members on their supported targets.
- No configured Tauri icon is removed.
- Dependency removal is limited to dependencies made unreachable by this cleanup.

## Verification strategy

Run targeted source/dependency checks, icon configuration checks, Rust format/Clippy/check/test gates, and record that the remote OS compile matrix remains the final cross-platform verification.
acceptance_criteria:
- Uncalled file-watch, thumbnail, and Linux XDG registration code is removed from the platform abstraction and native crates.
- Dependencies used solely by the deleted Linux scaffolding are removed and `Cargo.lock` is refreshed without unrelated upgrades.
- The duplicate unconfigured 256px icon and its generation step are removed; every configured Tauri icon remains.
- Native canvas snapshot PNG/PDF interfaces and their tests remain intact.
- `docs/agent/build-release.md` and relevant source comments describe the current platform surface.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo check --workspace`, and `cargo test --workspace` pass.
close_reason: Pruned uncalled file-watch, thumbnail, and Linux XDG scaffolding; removed inotify/direct libc dependencies and duplicate 256px icon; preserved native PNG/PDF snapshot exports; refreshed platform/build docs and renderer terminology. Gates: icon generator smoke/config check; bash syntax; cargo fmt; Clippy -D warnings; workspace check; workspace tests. Three reviewers CLEAN after one docs fix. macOS/Windows target compilation remains CI verification because those targets are unavailable locally.

title: Retire the dormant offline tile downloader
description:
## Slice Summary
Delete the desktop offline map-tile download/cache capability after its final UI and frontend adapter were removed.

## User Value
The desktop backend no longer ships an unreachable network, storage, event, and IPC surface or translations for controls users cannot access.

## Out of Scope
Preserve live MapLibre basemaps, contours, hillshading, terrain loading, and Web Edition offline policy.
design:
## Context

The desktop still compiles an offline tile downloader, cache manager, Tauri commands, events, tests, and translations after commit `96b559d` removed the frontend IPC adapter and download modal. No desktop or Web entry point invokes or listens to this capability.

## Implementation approach

1. Delete `desktop/src/commands/tiles.rs` and `desktop/src/services/tiles.rs`.
2. Remove their module declarations and four Tauri command registrations.
3. Remove only the eight offline-download UI keys from all 11 locale files.
4. Preserve current MapLibre basemap selection, terrain/contour/hillshade behavior, and user cache directories.

## Invariants

- Do not delete any user cache or migrate user data.
- Do not change live terrain fetch/rendering code or the Web Edition offline policy.
- Do not remove contour, contour interval, hillshade, or hillshade opacity translations.

## Verification strategy

Use source searches to prove commands/events are absent, run i18n completeness and frontend type/tests, then Rust formatting, Clippy, workspace check, and workspace tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Offline tile command/service modules and all four Tauri registrations are deleted, with no remaining references to their commands or events.
- The eight unreachable offline tile UI translations are removed from all 11 locales while live terrain translations remain.
- No user cache deletion or runtime migration is introduced.
- Frontend i18n completeness and relevant tests pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo check --workspace`, and `cargo test --workspace` pass.
close_reason: Removed the unreachable offline tile service, commands, Tauri registrations, self-only tests, and eight UI keys from all locales while preserving live MapLibre terrain/basemap paths and user cache data. Updated MapLibre agent guidance. Gates: i18n exact parity 11 locales; TypeScript; cargo fmt; Clippy -D warnings; workspace check; workspace tests. Three reviewers CLEAN.

title: Remove unconsumed persisted settings fields
description:
## Slice Summary
Remove ten settings fields that are defaulted, projected, diagnosed, or fixture-populated but never control runtime behavior; keep old settings JSON forward-compatible through serde's unknown-field handling and regenerate shared bindings.

## User Value
The public settings contract reflects actual preferences, fixtures stop implying unsupported behavior, and diagnostic reports no longer disclose meaningless values.

## Out of Scope
Preserve every setting with a production read, the current settings persistence format, and compatibility when opening files written by older versions.
design:
## Context

Ten fields in the shared `Settings` contract are populated by defaults, fixtures, projection spreading, or diagnostics but never read to control runtime behavior: `show_smart_guides`, `confirm_destructive`, `default_currency`, `measurement_units`, `show_botanical_names`, `debug_logging`, `check_updates`, `default_design_dir`, `recent_files_max`, and `last_active_panel`. `Settings` uses serde defaults and permits unknown fields, so older JSON can remain readable after pruning.

## Implementation approach

1. Add a regression test that deserializes legacy settings JSON containing retired keys, preserves live values, and serializes only the live contract. It must fail before field removal and pass afterward.
2. Remove the ten fields and defaults from `common-types/src/settings.rs`.
3. Remove meaningless diagnostic output/redaction cases and fixture literals tied only to those fields.
4. Regenerate TypeScript bindings and update frontend fixtures/expectations without changing live projection behavior.

## Invariants

- Old settings JSON containing the removed keys still deserializes successfully.
- Every remaining field has a production behavior or intentional persistence role.
- Live settings values, recent-file behavior, theme/language, canvas presentation, and persistence format continue to work.
- Generated bindings remain source-controlled and match Rust.

## Verification strategy

Follow red-green-refactor around legacy JSON compatibility, run generated-binding checks, settings/problem-report focused tests, full frontend tests/typecheck, and full Rust gates.
acceptance_criteria:
- A red-first regression test proves legacy JSON with retired settings keys remains readable and that those keys are not emitted by the current serializer.
- All ten unconsumed fields are absent from the Rust settings contract, generated TypeScript binding, diagnostics, redaction fixtures, and frontend test fixtures.
- Every retained settings field has a verified runtime or persistence role.
- `npm run gen:types`, `npm run check:types`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, focused Vitest coverage, and `npm test` pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo check --workspace`, and `cargo test --workspace` pass.
close_reason: Removed ten unconsumed Settings fields while preserving legacy JSON compatibility. TDD proved retired keys deserialize but do not serialize; tightened exhaustive frontend projection and fixed order-sensitive equality exposed by the regression. Verified generated bindings, TypeScript, 25 focused frontend tests, full frontend suite (182 files/1722 tests), common-types regression, problem-report tests, and full Rust fmt/clippy/check/workspace tests. Three independent reviews are CLEAN.

title: Prune obsolete frontend compatibility surfaces
description:
## Slice Summary
Remove frontend interfaces, styling, and tests whose production callers were superseded by the Canvas Layer Presentation, projection backend, and current canvas runtime seams.

## User Value
Maintainers have one production path per behavior and no longer need to distinguish live interfaces from historical compatibility wrappers.

## Out of Scope
Do not change visible behavior, remove accepted architecture guardrails, or remove MapLibre global styling.
design:
## Context

The renderer, canvas settings, location, and panel implementations have accumulated compatibility exports, wrapper tests, stale translations, and CSS left behind by completed migrations. A static entry-point reachability audit found no orphaned TypeScript modules other than the tooltip stylesheet, but it found numerous declaration-only exports and selectors.

## Implementation approach

1. Remove superseded Canvas Layer Presentation wrappers from `app/canvas-settings`, retain only the mounted bottom-panel actions, and remove the unused imperative panel setter from the canonical presentation seam.
2. Remove the retired stage-shaped projection helper and the subset MapLibre camera wrapper. Migrate useful camera assertions to `createMapFrame`; keep canonical projection behavior coverage.
3. Remove declaration-only runtime helpers, toolbar icon exports, the orphan tooltip stylesheet, and CSS selectors whose owning components were deleted.
4. Remove translations only where all static and dynamic lookup paths prove the UI surface is gone. Preserve `plantStamp`, MapLibre global selectors, accepted Site Adaptation absence checks, Web Drafts behavior, legacy-format rejection, and other durable boundary tests.
5. Delete one-time regression/source-absence tests only when stronger current behavior or contract coverage exists. Update stale Konva/fixed-size comments to renderer-neutral current terminology.

## Expected file areas

- `desktop/web/src/app/canvas-settings/`
- `desktop/web/src/app/canvas-layer-presentation/`
- `desktop/web/src/canvas/` and `desktop/web/src/canvas/runtime/`
- `desktop/web/src/components/`
- `desktop/web/src/__tests__/`
- `desktop/web/src/i18n/locales/*.json`
- `AGENTS.md` only for the verified stale legacy-component caveat

## Invariants

- No mounted behavior changes.
- Canonical layer presentation, projection, MapLibre, location, and scene ownership seams remain.
- Dynamic translation keys and architecture guardrails are not removed merely because literal search cannot find them.
- Desktop and Web Edition entry points both continue to build.

## Verification strategy

Run focused migrated tests first, then TypeScript, the complete frontend suite, desktop and Web builds/packages, i18n completeness, zero-reference searches, and `git diff --check`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Superseded canvas-settings layer wrappers, `layerPanelView`, the unused presentation panel setter, `stageViewportCenter`, and `computeMapLibreCamera` are removed with no remaining references.
- Useful camera/projection/settings assertions exercise the canonical interfaces; duplicate or incidental tombstone tests are removed without weakening durable architecture and compatibility guardrails.
- Declaration-only runtime helpers and toolbar icon exports identified by the audit are removed, while intentionally stable document-session inspection surfaces remain.
- The orphan Plant tooltip stylesheet and verified unreferenced CSS selectors are removed; MapLibre global rules and all mounted classes remain.
- Verified obsolete translation keys are removed consistently from all 11 locales, and i18n completeness passes.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, focused Vitest coverage, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:web`, `npm run package:web`, and `git diff --check` pass.

title: Compile and consume the Web Species Catalog artifact contract
description:
## Slice Summary
Replace the three independently maintained Web Species Catalog manifest interpretations with one authored artifact contract, a caller-shaped Python generation plan, and one shared generated JavaScript admission path consumed by packaging and the browser.

## User Value
A Web Edition catalog that packages successfully is admitted by the browser under the same owner, version, schema, locale, Filter, asset, and provenance rules, so contract drift fails during development or packaging instead of after deployment.

## Out of Scope
Do not change the physical Species Catalog SQLite storage contract, expand reduced Web detail scope, redesign DuckDB queries, add a generic schema framework, support multiple artifact versions, or change Web Edition deployment limits.
design:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** task
**Summary:** Compile and consume one strict Web Species Catalog artifact contract across generation, packaging, and browser admission.

**Current behavior:** The Web catalog generator constructs manifest semantics from local constants, the package verifier parses a release-oriented subset, and the browser parses a different runtime-oriented subset. Owner/version, exact row schemas, locale coverage, Filter predicates, asset metadata, and redundant DuckDB projections are not admitted under one executable contract. A stage can accept an artifact another stage cannot safely consume.

**Desired behavior:** One authored v1 artifact contract compiles into a caller-shaped Python generation plan and one dependency-free ESM admission module with declarations. Generation uses the plan for row fields, locales, Filters, and complete manifest construction. Node packaging and the browser call the same admission function before any filesystem packaging or DuckDB construction. Generated drift is a committed build gate. Invalid artifacts fail with deterministic, path-addressed diagnostics and no partial admitted value.

**Key interfaces:**
- The authored Web Species Catalog artifact v1 contract, distinct from physical Species Catalog storage
- `WebCatalogArtifactPlan` and complete manifest construction from source provenance plus asset metadata
- `admitWebCatalogManifest(unknown)` and its normalized immutable admitted value
- The Web catalog generator, Web Edition package verifier, and DuckDB-WASM catalog reader adapters
- Existing generated-binding/check commands and build/release guidance

**Behavior priorities for TDD:**
1. A known-good authored contract compiles deterministically; malformed or stale generated facts fail without writes.
2. Manifest construction derives all static semantics from the plan and rejects contradictory dynamic provenance or asset metadata.
3. Shared ESM admission accepts the generated v1 shape and rejects owner/version/fingerprint/schema/locale/Filter/reader/path/byte/checksum drift.
4. Browser loading admits before constructing DuckDB; invalid manifests have no database side effect.
5. Packaging admits through the same parser and retains real containment, existence, byte-limit, byte-count, and SHA-256 verification against temporary files.
6. Existing valid catalog generation, Parquet querying, staged publication, and Web Edition packaging behavior remain intact.

**Out of scope:**
- Physical SQLite schema/version verification and the storage-contract compiler
- New Web Species detail fields, Filters, locales, formats, asset roles, deployment limits, or artifact-version compatibility
- A generic JSON Schema engine, registry framework, public filesystem port, or new dependency
- Changes to DuckDB query semantics, lifecycle, or fallback behavior beyond consuming admitted data

The accepted architecture is recorded by decision bead `canopi-foh0`; implementation must preserve that seam rather than folding artifact behavior into the physical storage module.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One strict authored Web Species Catalog artifact v1 contract owns exact owner/version/format/reader, ordered row schemas, locales, supported Filters, excluded detail fields, asset roles, and safe layout facts without absorbing physical SQLite storage.
- [ ] The standard-library Python compiler returns a typed caller-shaped plan, builds and validates the complete deterministic manifest from dynamic provenance/asset metadata, and checks or atomically writes its generated outputs.
- [ ] A committed dependency-free ESM admission module and declaration file are generated deterministically, and the normal generated-binding/build gate fails when either is stale.
- [ ] Node packaging and the browser import the same admitWebCatalogManifest(unknown) implementation; their caller-local structural manifest parsers are deleted.
- [ ] Admission rejects wrong owner/version/fingerprint/format/reader, schema or locale drift, invalid Filter definitions, unsafe/duplicate asset paths, invalid byte/checksum metadata, and contradictory DuckDB asset projections with deterministic diagnostics.
- [ ] The browser admits the manifest before DuckDB construction, proven by a focused regression test that observes no database creation for an invalid or stale manifest.
- [ ] Packaging retains temporary-filesystem coverage for containment, missing assets, deployment limits, exact byte counts, and actual SHA-256 checks after shared admission.
- [ ] Generator tests prove plan-derived fields/locales/Filters and a valid complete manifest; existing Parquet, publication, browser-query, and package behavior remains green.
- [ ] Relevant agent/build/release guidance identifies the contract authority, regeneration/check command, generated files, and separate storage/artifact responsibilities.
- [ ] Required Python, generated-output, TypeScript, focused/full frontend, Web build/package, and applicable Rust/shared-contract quality gates pass; any unavailable gate is recorded with residual risk.

Final review round: CLEAN across correctness/security, architecture/API, and test/build lenses. Gates: 74 Python contract/preparation/generator tests; 47 focused Vitest tests; full frontend 181 files/1720 tests; TypeScript; npm check:types; real 47-asset catalog generation; npm package:web; cargo fmt, Clippy -D warnings, workspace check, and workspace tests.
