title: Decide the Settled Scene Authority and exact save receipt seam
description:
## Decision

Deepen the canvas runtime Scene Edit Coordinator into a role-sliced Settled Scene Authority. Preserve live preview rendering through SceneStore, but let the authority exclusively own active Scene Edit admission, committed-state projection, history state identity, persistence checkpoints, asynchronous presentation-backfill admission, and document-generation invalidation.

Persistence captures committed Scene state even while a gesture preview is visible and returns an opaque checkpoint for the exact captured history state. Design Session persistence pairs that checkpoint with the captured non-canvas revision and acknowledges those exact states only after successful I/O.

## Rationale

The current coordinator is a shallow transaction factory around a shared mutable SceneStore. Live preview mutations are visible to serialization, history, concurrent commands, and asynchronous backfills. Reproductions showed an aborted drag serialized into a Design, undo diverging from the restored Scene, a concurrent Layer command being erased while its history remained, and backfills being erased or absorbed into gesture history. Manual save also captures content before I/O but marks whatever history and non-canvas revisions exist afterward, so later edits can be overwritten or falsely reported clean.

One authority gives these ordering rules locality while retaining the existing renderer and interaction model. It also extends the intent of canopi-bu2.2 rather than replacing Scene Edit transactions with a second state system.

## Alternatives Considered

- Separate committed Scene state from a sparse presentation overlay. This makes preview leakage impossible by construction and makes abort cheap, but requires classifying at least 63 production Scene reads, migrating four live geometry writers, and introducing conflict/rebase semantics before fixing the present failures.
- Abort the active interaction before save, history, commands, or backfills. This is data-safe for some paths but autosave would cancel user gestures, interaction UI still needs separate cleanup ownership, and asynchronous save acknowledgments would remain inexact.
- Add independent active-edit checks in document, command, history, and presentation modules. This is the smallest patch but preserves shallow policy duplication, creates check/use races, and is likely to miss future writers.
- Keep history positions as array lengths and mark the current position after I/O. Undo branches and truncation alias positions, and edits made during I/O would still be falsely marked saved.
design:
## Interface Contract

The runtime composition root owns one aggregate Settled Scene Authority and passes callers only the role they need:

- Scene Edit role: run an immediate edit or begin one long-lived edit. At most one edit may be open or finalizing. Immediate edits return busy without invoking their callback; a second long-lived begin raises a typed busy error.
- History role: reactive undo/redo availability plus admitted undo/redo operations. Availability is false and execution returns busy during a live or finalizing edit.
- Persistence role: atomically capture serialized committed Scene state plus an opaque checkpoint, then acknowledge that exact checkpoint after I/O. A foreign checkpoint is a programmer error; a checkpoint from an old document generation is stale and changes nothing.
- Presentation-maintenance role: issue an opaque read ticket and apply or defer backfills only when its document generation and committed content revision remain valid.
- Document role: initial hydration and replacement invalidate old transactions, tickets, checkpoints, and history state. Replacement settles interaction before hydration; failure leaves the old Design intact.

SceneStore continues to hold live preview state for render and hit-test compatibility. While an edit is active, the authority retains its immutable before-snapshot as the committed persistence projection. Callers never receive a public hasActiveEdit flag or perform separate check/use admission.

## State And Ordering

Each document generation has unique committed state identities. History commands retain before and after state identities; undo and redo restore the matching identity. Saved cleanliness compares identities, not array indexes. Branches, truncation, and overlapping saves therefore cannot alias another state.

Commit or abort retains the active slot until the authoritative state transition succeeds. A failed pre-settlement operation remains retryable. Publication after settlement must be idempotent and must not duplicate history or restore the opposite outcome. All other Scene writes, history operations, and backfills remain non-admitting until settlement completes.

Persistence snapshots serialize the current Scene when idle and the active transaction before-snapshot during a preview. The checkpoint records authority identity, document generation, and exact committed state identity. Acknowledging an older successful write sets that exact state as saved, leaving newer state dirty.

Design Session persistence composes the canvas checkpoint with a session generation and exact non-canvas revision. Successful saves update path/display identity narrowly and acknowledge the captured revisions; they never replace currentDesign with stale captured content. Desktop recovery autosave does not advance the manual-save baseline.

## Complexity Owned

The authority hides transaction exclusivity, committed-versus-preview distinction, patch/history recording, state identities, dirty reporting, history admission, backfill freshness/defer policy, document generation, and canvas persistence checkpoints. Native and browser I/O remain outside. Scene Interaction Session retains gesture routing and tool/overlay cleanup.

Design-owned non-canvas state remains in the Design Session store. Active Design Edit preview isolation and full persistence-operation serialization are separate follow-up architecture concerns; this decision requires exact non-canvas revision receipts but does not move non-canvas data into the Scene authority.

## Dependency And Migration Strategy

Dependency category: in-process. No new runtime dependency. Production uses the existing SceneStore, Scene command patches, renderer scheduler, and Design Session store; tests use the same authority with in-memory adapters and deterministic callbacks.

Migrate in two vertical slices. First move single-writer admission, history execution, backfill tickets, and hydration gating behind the authority. Then replace separate serialize/mark-current-saved calls with committed snapshots and exact canvas/non-canvas receipts across desktop save, Save As, browser download/drafts, autosave, problem-report attachment, and teardown composition. Delete compatibility methods and add source guards after callers migrate.

## Testing Strategy

Test the role interfaces for exclusivity, busy behavior, retryable settlement, exact history identity, branch/truncation behavior, stale document tokens, committed snapshot projection, and backfill defer/stale outcomes. Add runtime event tests for drag plus Undo/Delete/Layer command, drag plus serialization, replacement after failed cancellation, and async backfill races. Add Design Session tests for canvas and non-canvas edits during save I/O, stale completion after replacement, Save As preserving later edits/name changes, and autosave/teardown never serializing a live Scene preview.

No ADR conflict is known. The decision preserves the documented two-authority Design model and the Canvas Document Surface save-composition seam.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Selected role interfaces and ownership are explicit
- [ ] Active-edit, settlement, history, persistence, backfill, and hydration ordering is recorded
- [ ] Exact canvas and non-canvas checkpoint semantics are recorded
- [ ] Selected and rejected alternatives include decisive trade-offs
- [ ] Dependency, migration, testing, and ADR strategies are recorded
- [ ] Follow-up implementation work is represented separately
notes: Loop 5 architecture review accepted a purpose-aware Design Persistence Operation rather than exposing a raw content/receipt pair. It privately owns session generation, non-canvas revision, canvas checkpoint, attachment epoch, destination intent sequence, captured identity, baseline policy, and idempotent settlement. Destination identity follows issue order; detached runtime A cannot clean runtime B; settlement exposes the captured snapshot for notebook metadata and never replaces canonical state. An immutable Design-revision ledger was rejected as too broad. Active Design Edit preview isolation remains a separate strong recommendation.
close_reason: Architecture decision accepted: use the role-sliced Settled Scene Authority with committed projections and exact save receipts; defer the separate presentation-overlay model.

title: Make Scene Interaction Session the lifecycle and routing owner
description:
## Slice Summary

Replace the callback-driven Scene Interaction Frame, oversized Controller ownership, and forwarding tool-module façade with the accepted stateful Scene Interaction Session. Route the canvas runtime through the small Session interface and add loss-of-pointer/focus cancellation behavior.

## User Value

Canvas interactions cannot remain stuck after pointer cancellation or window focus loss, and future tool behavior has one reviewable owner for routing, transaction completion, cancellation, refresh, and resource teardown.

## Out of Scope

Do not redesign individual tool geometry/draft algorithms, Scene Edit history, selection semantics, rendering, plant presentation data, drag payloads, document persistence, or IPC contracts. Do not introduce a general reducer/event bus or runtime dependency.
design:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** task

**Summary:** Complete the Scene Interaction Session boundary and remove the shallow Frame/Controller/tool-facade ownership split.

**Current behavior:**

`interaction/frame.ts` installs listeners and stores pointer/Space state but accepts eleven raw callbacks and exposes granular lifecycle mutators. `scene-interaction.ts` still owns event priority, tool transitions, commit/cancel/refresh order, focus animation, and resource disposal. `tool-modules.ts` mirrors most optional adapter hooks. There are no `pointercancel` or window-blur routes.

**Desired behavior:**

One stateful Session constructs and owns fixed collaborators, installs/removes all host listeners, holds the single interaction session, routes events in explicit priority order, synchronizes the active adapter, owns transient cleanup/refresh/disposal, and exposes only the runtime operations already needed by `SceneCanvasRuntime`. Cancellation from `pointercancel` or blur rolls active work back without history, releases Space/cursor state, and preserves only a valid passive draft.

**Key interfaces:**

- `SceneInteractionSession` runtime seam.
- Existing `SceneToolAdapter` varying-tool seam and a private adapter registry.
- `SceneInteractionSharedGestures`, direct-manipulation controllers, annotation editor, overlays, and `SceneEditCoordinator` as Session-owned collaborators.
- User-equivalent `SceneInteractionEventHarness` for public behavior.

**Out of scope:**

- Tool-local draft/geometry rewrites.
- Scene transaction/history redesign.
- Renderer, persistence, IPC, or shared-type changes.
- Plant Presentation Catalog work.
- Generic participant or reducer/effect architecture.
- New dependencies.

## Implementation Shape

Start with characterization and failing cancellation tests at the DOM/session surface. Add pointer-cancel and window-blur support to the shared event harness. Move raw listener ownership, pointer/Space/generic-drag state, event routing, transition/refresh ordering, pending focus, and teardown into the Session without a permanent wrapper layer. Internalize adapter lookup instead of forwarding each hook through `SceneToolModules`. Migrate runtime and integration imports, delete superseded Frame/Controller APIs and implementation tests, then strengthen the source-boundary guard and canvas-runtime guide.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `SceneCanvasRuntime` depends only on a small `SceneInteractionSession` interface for tool sync, refresh, transient history, and disposal.
- [ ] One Session owns all container/window listeners, active-tool identity, pointer/Space/generic-drag state, pending host focus, routing order, refresh order, and teardown.
- [ ] No raw handler-injection or public pointer/lifecycle-mutator Frame interface remains, and the former Controller is removed or reduced to a compatibility-free re-export.
- [ ] The tool adapter registry is internal and the Session routes directly to the active `SceneToolAdapter` while retaining focused adapter modules.
- [ ] Existing pointer-down/move/up, keyboard, context-menu, wheel, drag/drop, tool-transition, focus, and transient-history behavior remains covered through user-equivalent events.
- [ ] `pointercancel` and window blur abort active direct manipulation and Scene Edit transactions without a history entry, ignore mismatched pointer IDs, release Space, clear hover, restore the cursor, and permit the next interaction.
- [ ] Pointer cancellation and blur preserve a valid passive Polygon draft but disposal/tool transition clear the appropriate tool-owned state.
- [ ] Listener removal and disposal are exact and idempotent; pending focus animation is cancelled and all owned resources receive cleanup even if one cleanup path throws.
- [ ] Source-boundary tests prevent listener, pointer-state, transition-order, and resource-disposal ownership from drifting out of the Session.
- [ ] `docs/agent/canvas-runtime.md` documents the Session as the lifecycle authority and removes stale Frame/Controller guidance.
- [ ] Focused Vitest coverage, full frontend tests, TypeScript checking, and the Web Edition build pass.
close_reason: Shipped the Scene Interaction Session as the single listener, routing, transition, cancellation, refresh, and teardown owner; removed the superseded Frame and forwarding facade; added pointer-cancel/blur, failure-atomic lifecycle cleanup, user-equivalent regressions, source guards, and agent guidance. Verified 1,345/1,345 frontend tests, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build:web, and git diff --check.

title: Route Scene arrangement placement through the shared kernel
description:
## Slice Summary
Introduce the accepted transaction-owning Scene Arrangement Placement kernel and route Clipboard Paste/Paste At/Duplicate, Object Stamp, and Saved Object Stamp placement through it. Remove their duplicate identity, collision, geometry, Group-remap, insertion, and selection algorithms.

## User Value
Mixed copied arrangements remain fully selected after paste, and every arrangement-placement tool preserves the same identity, geometry, Group, history, and selection invariants as the canvas evolves.

## Out of Scope
Do not redesign clipboard capture, Object Stamp sampling, Saved Stamp wire format, previews, snapping, Layer eligibility, tool navigation, persistence, or general Scene Edit transactions.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** task
**Summary:** Replace three independent Scene arrangement-copy engines with the accepted shared placement operation.

**Current behavior:**
Clipboard, Object Stamp, and Saved Object Stamp each allocate identities, resolve Zone name collisions, translate ellipse geometry, remap Object Group members, append Scene arrays, and choose selection. Clipboard returns early when any Group is cloned, so a mixed Group-plus-ungrouped arrangement drops the ungrouped clone from post-paste selection.

**Desired behavior:**
An internal transaction-owning `SceneArrangementPlacement` accepts a normalized template with explicit source identities, a translation delta, and caller history type. It builds all clones, remaps valid Groups, inserts once, commits selection in the same Scene Edit, and returns a receipt. Every placement caller delegates to it while retaining its capture/decoding, eligibility, pin policy, snapping, preview, and tool lifecycle.

**Key interfaces:**
- `SceneArrangementTemplate` entity prototypes with explicit source identities.
- `SceneArrangementPlacement.place()` and its committed/created/selection receipt.
- `SceneEditCoordinator` transaction boundary.
- Clipboard capture and mutation controller.
- Object Stamp sample/placement tool.
- Saved Object Stamp payload adapter and placement tool.

**Out of scope:**
- Clipboard UX or external/system clipboard support.
- Object Stamp sampling and repeated-placement behavior.
- Saved Object Stamp payload/file schema.
- Layer lock/visibility policy, snapping, previews, or ghost rendering.
- General Scene Edit/history redesign.
- New runtime dependencies.

## Implementation Shape

Start with the mixed Group-plus-ungrouped regression at the public runtime surface. Add direct interface tests for source identity mapping (including Saved Stamp Zone ID versus name), multiple Zone collisions, ellipse translation, invalid Groups, immutable repeated placement, empty input, one history edit, and rollback. Migrate Clipboard first, then Object Stamp, then Saved Object Stamp in vertical red-green-refactor steps. Delete each old helper only after its caller is green. Finish with a source boundary guard and focused/full canvas runtime tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A canvas-runtime SceneArrangementTemplate represents normalized Plant, Zone, Annotation, Measurement Guide, and Object Group prototypes with explicit source identities.
- [ ] One transaction-owning placement operation returns committed state, created count, and canonical cloned top-level selection.
- [ ] Mixed valid Groups and ungrouped Design Objects are all selected after Clipboard Paste, Paste At, and Duplicate.
- [ ] Fresh identities, collision-safe Zone names, ellipse center-only translation, typed Group remapping, invalid-Group fallback, and immutable repeated placement are covered at the shared interface.
- [ ] A placement is exactly one undoable Scene Edit, and unexpected failures roll back without partial insertion.
- [ ] Clipboard retains its capture, offset, and Paste-versus-Duplicate pin policy outside the shared module.
- [ ] Object Stamp retains sampling, source revalidation, snapping, preview, and repeated-placement lifecycle outside the shared module.
- [ ] Saved Object Stamp retains payload decoding, destination Layer checks, snapping, ghost preview, and one-shot lifecycle outside the shared module.
- [ ] All three callers delegate placement and no longer define their own identity/name/ellipse/Group/selection copy algorithm.
- [ ] Canvas runtime subsystem guidance and source-boundary tests identify the shared placement authority.
- [ ] Focused Vitest coverage, full canvas runtime coverage, and TypeScript checking pass.
close_reason: Shipped shared transaction-owning Scene Arrangement Placement for Clipboard Paste/Paste At/Duplicate, Object Stamp, and Saved Object Stamp; fixed mixed selection and duplicate-member Group validity; added direct/integration/boundary coverage and canvas runtime guidance. Passed focused Vitest (35 tests), full npm test (174 files/1300 tests), npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build:web, and three independent review passes with no remaining findings.

title: Route desktop and Web Design replacement through the shared seam
description:
## Slice Summary
Route resolved Design replacement and initial canvas attachment through the accepted platform-neutral Design Session replacement module on desktop and Web. Remove Web Edition's reactive whole-Design hydration path.

## User Value
A designer's canvas-owned work remains intact when a non-canvas Design Edit such as rename occurs, and every real Design replacement follows one authority-safe lifecycle on both platforms.

## Out of Scope
Do not unify native file persistence with Browser Draft persistence, redesign dirty confirmation, replace the full Design Session state machine, or change user-facing Browser App Shell commands.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** task
**Summary:** Put initial canvas attachment and resolved Design replacement behind the accepted shared Design Session seam on desktop and Web.

**Current behavior:**
Desktop concentrates Design replacement ordering inside the Design Session state machine. Web Edition separately updates Design Session state, then observes every non-canvas Design snapshot identity and treats it as a canvas replacement. Because SceneStore-owned state is not mirrored into that snapshot, a later non-canvas edit can rehydrate stale canvas data.

**Desired behavior:**
One platform-neutral Design Session replacement module owns new-versus-loaded normalization, attached-versus-detached authority handoff, initial load versus explicit replacement, dirty-baseline reset, canvas history/chrome/zoom ordering, and Design Session workflow installation. Desktop and Web intent facades delegate resolved incoming Designs to it. Web canvas mounting attaches once and never infers replacement from ordinary Design snapshot changes.

**Key interfaces:**
- Design Session replacement attach/replace interface and its applied receipt.
- Design Session store identity and dirty-baseline interface.
- Canvas Runtime document surface.
- Design Session workflow runner.
- Desktop Design Session state machine and Web Design Session controller intent facades.

**Out of scope:**
- Combining native persistence with Browser Draft or download persistence.
- Reworking dirty confirmation, queued desktop loads, autosave policy, or Browser App Shell commands.
- Adding runtime platform flags or a generic provider registry.
- Changing SceneStore or Design Edit authority.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A platform-neutral Design Session replacement module exposes the accepted attach/replace behavior and imports neither Tauri nor browser infrastructure.
- [ ] Initial attachment, attached replacement, detached replacement, new/loaded normalization, baseline reset, canvas lifecycle ordering, and workflow installation are covered through the shared interface.
- [ ] Desktop Design Session transitions delegate authority handoff to the shared module without changing dirty guards, cancellation, queued loads, state reporting, autosave, or teardown behavior.
- [ ] Web new/open/template/draft flows and canvas attachment delegate to the shared module.
- [ ] Web canvas code no longer observes ordinary Design snapshot changes to call loadDocument or replaceDocument.
- [ ] A regression test proves a non-canvas Design Edit does not replace the canvas or discard live canvas-owned work.
- [ ] Browser/native import guardrails remain equally strong and allow only the platform-neutral replacement seam.
- [ ] Active Design Session and frontend subsystem guidance reflects the shared seam; stale instructions are replaced.
- [ ] Focused Vitest coverage and TypeScript checking pass.
close_reason: Shipped the shared platform-neutral Design Session attach/replace seam for desktop and Web, removed reactive Web canvas rehydration, and preserved canvas authority across detach/failure paths. Tests: 81 focused Vitest tests; full npm test (173 files, 1289 tests); npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build:web including artifact boundary check.

title: Support root-base Web Edition artifacts
description:
## Slice Summary
Add an explicit Web Edition package mode that builds and verifies a root-base artifact for deployment at `https://web.projectcanopi.com/`, while keeping the existing `/app/` artifact shape as the default.

## User Value
Release and deployment workflows can produce the correct static artifact for the dedicated Web Edition subdomain without breaking the current marketing-site `/app/` artifact path.

## Out of Scope
Do not remove or change the default `/app/` artifact mode, do not rewrite built files after Vite emits them, do not deploy to Cloudflare in this slice, and do not change Species Catalog data scope.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Support explicit root-base Web Edition artifacts for the dedicated Web Edition subdomain.

**Current behavior:**
The Web Edition package flow produces an artifact for the marketing-site `/app/` path. Its manifest and SPA fallback contract are tied to `/app/`, so deploying that artifact at a subdomain root would request the wrong asset paths.

**Desired behavior:**
The existing package command continues to produce the `/app/` artifact by default. An explicit root-base package mode builds the Web Edition with base path `/`, emits a manifest with `basePath: "/"` and SPA fallback `/* -> /index.html`, verifies the same Cloudflare limits and artifact file-set invariants, and packages root-relative static files suitable for `https://web.projectcanopi.com/`.

**Key interfaces:**
- Web Edition package command
- Web Edition build base-path configuration
- Web Edition artifact manifest contract
- Web Edition artifact verification and packaging tests
- Web Edition deployment runbook

**Out of scope:**
- Removing or changing the default `/app/` artifact mode
- Rewriting built HTML or JavaScript after Vite emits it
- Deploying to Cloudflare Pages
- Changing Species Catalog data scope or search behavior
- Importing app source into the website repository
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Default Web Edition packaging still emits an `/app/` artifact with `/app/* -> /app/index.html` fallback metadata.
- [ ] An explicit root-base package mode builds with base path `/` before Vite emits assets.
- [ ] Root-base packaging emits a manifest with `basePath: "/"` and `/* -> /index.html` fallback metadata.
- [ ] Root-base artifacts contain `index.html`, assets, catalog files, and `canopi-web-edition-manifest.json` at the archive root, not under a top-level `app/` directory.
- [ ] Root-base packaging enforces Cloudflare per-asset limits, file-count limits including the artifact manifest, catalog manifest presence, supported-filter metadata presence, checksum metadata, and raw DuckDB WASM rejection.
- [ ] Packaging tests prove both `/app/` default mode and explicit root-base mode.
- [ ] Agent docs and the subdomain deployment runbook stay consistent with the dual-artifact contract.
- [ ] Focused Web packaging tests and `npm run package:web` pass for the default artifact; root-base package verification passes for the explicit mode.
close_reason: Added explicit root-base Web Edition artifact support while preserving the default /app/ artifact. Vite now honors CANOPI_WEB_BASE_PATH before emitting Web assets; npm run package:web:root builds with base path / and packages canopi-web-edition-root-v<version>-<commit>.tar.gz with basePath / and /* -> /index.html fallback. The packager validates built HTML base references, Cloudflare limits, catalog metadata/checksums, file counts, raw DuckDB WASM rejection, and keeps the default /app/ artifact name/manifest unchanged. Updated AGENTS.md and Web Edition build/website agent docs. Gates: cd desktop/web && npm test -- --run src/__tests__/web-edition-packaging.test.ts; cd desktop/web && npm run package:web:root; cd desktop/web && npm run package:web; git diff --check.

title: Align Web Edition active search ordering
description:
## Slice Summary
Improve Web Edition Species Catalog active text search ordering so browser results follow the desktop Common Name relevance tiers as closely as the current Web catalog data scope allows.

## User Value
A user searching the Species Catalog in Web Edition sees the same most-relevant selected-language Common Name matches near the top that they would expect from desktop.

## Out of Scope
Do not expand the Web Edition catalog data scope, add desktop-only Species fields, add a full SQLite FTS/BM25 replica, change empty browse ordering, or change filter-only ordering.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Align Web Edition active Species Catalog Search ordering with desktop Common Name relevance tiers.

**Current behavior:**
Web Edition active text search filters reduced Species Catalog rows with broad text matching and returns results in canonical-name order. Desktop active search ranks selected-language Common Name matches first, so Web can show less relevant results ahead of exact or prefix Common Name matches.

**Desired behavior:**
For active text search only, Web Edition orders results using the same user-visible Common Name relevance tiers as desktop as far as the current Web catalog data scope allows: displayed selected-language Common Name exact match, displayed selected-language Common Name prefix match, displayed selected-language Common Name contains-all-tokens match, selected-language alternate Matched Common Name, then a deterministic canonical-name fallback. Empty browse and filter-only result ordering remain stable canonical-name ordering.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Search request and result contract
- Web Edition reduced Species Catalog reader
- Web Edition generated selected-locale Common Name assets
- Species Catalog Workbench active-search policy

**Out of scope:**
- Expanding Web Edition Species data scope
- Adding desktop-only Species fields to the Web catalog
- Recreating full SQLite FTS5 BM25 ranking in Web Edition
- Changing empty browse or filter-only ordering
- Changing supported filter fields
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Active Web Edition text search ranks displayed selected-language Common Name exact matches before prefix, contains, alternate matched-name, and canonical-name fallback results.
- [ ] Active Web Edition text search ranks displayed selected-language Common Name prefix matches before contains, alternate matched-name, and canonical-name fallback results.
- [ ] Active Web Edition multi-token text search ranks displayed selected-language Common Names containing all tokens before alternate matched-name and canonical-name fallback results.
- [ ] Active Web Edition text search returns selected-language alternate Matched Common Names before canonical-name fallback results when displayed-name tiers do not match.
- [ ] Empty text browse and filter-only Web Edition searches keep deterministic canonical-name ordering.
- [ ] Web Edition search ordering tests cover at least one non-English locale and do not rely on English Common Name fallback for that locale.
- [ ] Focused Web catalog tests and TypeScript checks pass.
close_reason: Aligned Web Edition active Species Catalog search ordering with selected-locale Common Name relevance tiers while preserving canonical ordering for empty browse and filter-only searches. Added DuckDB Web catalog tests for French active search ordering, locale shard use without English fallback, alternate matched names, and filter-only ordering. title: Verify complete Web artifact file set
description:
## Slice Summary
Tighten Web Edition artifact validation so the generated package and website installer account for every file that will be published, including the artifact manifest itself, and reject any unlisted extra archive files.

## User Value
A release engineer cannot accidentally publish hidden or oversized files that bypass the manifest, Cloudflare file-count limits, or website install checks.

## Out of Scope
Changing Web catalog data scope, changing DuckDB query behavior, changing website-side catalog behavior, or adding any storage/compute service.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Ensure Web Edition package and website install gates validate the full published file set, not only manifest-listed payload files.

**Current behavior:**
The app packager enforces file-count limits before writing `canopi-web-edition-manifest.json`, so the manifest file itself is not counted. The website installer verifies files listed inside the app manifest and copies the whole extracted archive, but it does not reject unlisted extra files or count the actual extracted file set.

**Desired behavior:**
The app packager treats the manifest file as part of the Cloudflare file-count budget. The website installer validates the actual extracted archive contents, permits only manifest-listed files plus the manifest file itself, checks the manifest file size against the per-asset limit, and rejects unlisted extras before copying anything into the website output.

**Key interfaces:**
- `desktop/web/scripts/package-web-edition.mjs`
- `desktop/web/src/__tests__/web-edition-packaging.test.ts`
- `canopi-website/scripts/install-web-edition.mjs`
- Website artifact install smoke

**Out of scope:**
- Changing catalog data scope
- Adding website-side catalog search/filter/storage/compute
- Changing DuckDB query behavior
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] App packaging tests prove the manifest file is counted against the Cloudflare file-count limit.
- [ ] App packaging still writes a valid manifest and archive for normal Web Edition packages.
- [ ] Website installer rejects archives with unlisted extra files.
- [ ] Website installer counts the actual extracted files, including `canopi-web-edition-manifest.json`, against the file-count limit.
- [ ] Website installer checks the artifact manifest file size against the per-asset limit.
- [ ] Focused app packaging tests and website install/build smoke pass.
close_reason: Fixed complete Web artifact file-set validation. App packager now counts canopi-web-edition-manifest.json in the Cloudflare Pages file budget and rejects oversized artifact manifests; website installer now validates actual extracted files, rejects unlisted extras, counts the artifact manifest, checks its size, and copies only after validation. Gates: cd desktop/web && npm test -- --run src/__tests__/web-edition-packaging.test.ts; cd desktop/web && npm run package:web; canopi-website npm test; canopi-website CANOPI_WEB_EDITION_ARCHIVE=/home/daylon/projects/canopi/desktop/web/dist-web-artifacts/canopi-web-edition-v0.9.2-4472f56a98ce.tar.gz npm run build:with-web; git diff --check in both repos.

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Preserve broader FTS candidates when the generated Species Search name-entry index is available.

**Current behavior:**
When the generated name-entry search index is present, relevance searches with tokenized text take the indexed search path. That path ranks Common Name, canonical, and taxonomy candidates from name-entry tables, but it no longer includes broader FTS matches from documented text columns such as uses text or other descriptive text.

**Desired behavior:**
Indexed relevance search should keep selected-language Common Name candidates and their ranking tiers, while also returning broader FTS-only matches behind those stronger name candidates. Count and list queries should describe the same candidate universe. The fix should keep non-English searches selected-language-only for Common Name ranking and display fallback.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Search request and result contract.
- Relevance-ordered Species Catalog list and count planning.
- FTS text matching for broader Species text fields.
- Selected-language Common Name ranking and matched-name display behavior.

**Out of scope:**
- Compatibility with older unpackaged plant DB assets.
- Changing the two-character active-search UX.
- Reintroducing English Common Name fallback for non-English locales.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A relevance search that matches only broader FTS text fields still returns matching Species when the generated name-entry index is available.
- [ ] Indexed list and count queries agree on the candidate set for broader FTS-only matches.
- [ ] Selected-language Common Name matches still outrank broader FTS-only matches.
- [ ] Existing apple/appl and French melis/melisse relevance expectations remain covered.
- [ ] No compatibility work is added for older unpackaged DB assets.

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Prevent active Species Search cancellation from interrupting unrelated plant DB reads.

**Current behavior:**
Active Species Catalog Search cancellation stores a connection-wide SQLite interrupt handle. If a stale search is queued behind another plant DB read, starting a newer active search can interrupt whichever statement currently owns the shared plant DB connection, including unrelated detail, favorites, filter, or browse reads.

**Desired behavior:**
Superseding an active search should make stale search work stop promptly without interrupting unrelated plant DB statements. Cancellation should only affect a stale search once that stale search owns the plant DB connection, or use an equivalent isolation mechanism. Stale cancellation remains an internal behavior, not a user-facing error.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Search IPC/service boundary.
- Plant DB connection ownership and SQLite interrupt semantics.
- Active search cancellation coordinator.
- Other plant DB read workflows that share the bundled plant DB connection.

**Out of scope:**
- Relevance ranking changes.
- Changing the active-search minimum length.
- Frontend stale-result generation handling.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Starting a newer active search cannot interrupt an unrelated plant DB read that currently owns the shared connection.
- [ ] A stale active search that has not yet started DB work is rejected before acquiring/running the search query.
- [ ] A stale active search that owns the DB read path is still cancelled or interrupted promptly enough to avoid blocking newer active searches.
- [ ] Cancelled stale searches remain internal and do not create a user-facing search error state.
- [ ] Existing search, favorites hydration, and selected-language Common Name tests continue to pass.
close_reason: Scoped active Species Search interruption to searches that have marked themselves running while owning the plant DB read. Queued stale searches are rejected without interrupting unrelated plant DB statements, and a running guard clears interrupt eligibility before favorite hydration. title: Stage short-prefix Species Catalog relevance before weaker matches
description:
## Slice Summary
Optimize short-prefix active Species Catalog Search so selected-language Common Name tiers are satisfied before weaker Canonical Name, family, genus, or broad text matches are ranked.

## User Value
Two-character searches keep the same UX and relevance expectations, but broad prefixes avoid unnecessary candidate ranking that causes first-search stalls.

## Out of Scope
Do not raise the minimum query length, reintroduce English Common Name fallback, or change the Species Catalog Workbench UI behavior in this slice.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Optimize short-prefix relevance by staging stronger selected-language matches first.

**Current behavior:**
Broad short-prefix active searches can materialize, group, and sort thousands of candidate Species before returning the first page. This preserves relevance but makes the first real backend search expensive, especially when the query has only two normalized characters.

**Desired behavior:**
Short-prefix active search should keep the same visible ranking rules while doing less work. Selected-language displayed Common Names and Matched Common Names should be satisfied before weaker Canonical Name, family, genus, or broad text matches are ranked. Canonical and taxonomy matches remain language-neutral fallback search behavior, but they should not force the first page to rank a huge weak candidate set when enough stronger selected-language Common Name results exist.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Search relevance ordering.
- Selected-language Common Name and Matched Common Name display behavior.
- Species Catalog read projection list query.
- Search-performance harness for broad first-active prefixes.

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the active-search minimum length.
- Reintroducing English Common Name fallback in non-English locales.
- Moving backend work to an async command boundary.
- Cancelling obsolete searches.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `apple`, `appl`, and representative `ap` searches still put `Malus domestica` first in English.
- [ ] French `melisse` and `melis` searches still prioritize selected-language Mélisse Common Name matches, including expected higher placement for Mélisse alpine and Mélisse des champs ahead of weaker matches.
- [ ] Non-English searches continue to ignore English Common Name fallback for ranking, matching, and display.
- [ ] Broad first-active prefixes such as `en-ap`, `fr-me`, and `fr-po` show a clear first-page list-latency improvement in the local harness, with before/after timings recorded in the bead or PR.
- [ ] Any generated DB asset or schema-index change is explicitly justified, regenerated, and documented; otherwise the change remains runtime-query-only.
close_reason: Implemented runtime-query-only short-prefix staging for unfiltered indexed Species Catalog relevance searches. Two-character active prefixes now rank selected-language Common Name candidates before canonical/taxonomy fallback work. Regression coverage added for staged short-prefix planning, conservative filtered planning, and longer-query broad planning. Bundled latency harness before -> after cold sample: en-ap 2527ms -> 279ms, fr-me 2487ms -> 261ms, fr-po 4023ms -> 556ms; warm after sample: en-ap 14ms, fr-me 10ms, fr-po 24ms. Bundled relevance harness still puts Malus domestica first for apple/appl and French Mélisse, Mélisse alpine, Mélisse des champs before weaker matches. No DB asset or schema/index regeneration was needed.

description:

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Move active Species Catalog Search off the synchronous Tauri invoke path.

**Current behavior:**
The first active Species Catalog Search starts when the user enters the second normalized character. That backend call performs SQLite read work through a synchronous command path and a shared plant DB read connection. Broad short-prefix queries can therefore make the app feel frozen while the command resolves.

**Desired behavior:**
The Species Catalog Workbench keeps the same two-character active-search UX and the same request/result contract, but active search SQLite work runs behind an async or background backend boundary. A slow first-page search should not block synchronous invoke handling. Existing list hydration, favorite marking, and selected-language Common Name behavior must stay intact.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Search IPC command and typed request/response contract.
- Species Catalog read projection for first-page search results.
- Plant DB and user DB lock ordering.
- Species Catalog Workbench search session.

**Out of scope:**
- Cancelling obsolete searches.
- Rewriting relevance SQL.
- Changing Common Name fallback rules.
- Changing the bundled Species Catalog schema or generated DB asset.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Active text search still starts at two normalized characters; one-character text remains a local short-query state.
- [ ] The frontend `searchSpecies` request/response shape remains compatible.
- [ ] Active Species Catalog Search SQLite list work no longer runs on the synchronous Tauri command path.
- [ ] Plant DB and user DB lock ordering remains explicit and avoids holding both locks at once.
- [ ] Existing search, favorites hydration, and selected-language Common Name regression tests pass or are updated with equivalent coverage.
close_reason: Moved Species Catalog Search through an async backend boundary using the existing run_blocking helper and cloneable single-connection DB handles, preserving the IPC request/response contract and lock ordering. design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Cancel obsolete active Species Catalog Search reads.

**Current behavior:**
The Species Catalog Workbench ignores stale frontend responses by generation, but an obsolete backend search can continue running after the user types a newer query. A broad two-character search can hold the plant DB read path and delay the newer query that the user actually wants.

**Desired behavior:**
When a newer active text search supersedes an older one, the older backend read should be cancelled or interrupted promptly. Stale cancellation should be internal behavior, not a user-facing error. The latest query should be able to complete without waiting for an obsolete broad-prefix read to finish.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Workbench search session generation/stale-result behavior.

## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug

**Desired behavior:**

Result ordering and display behavior should remain coherent with the selected app language. When the table is absent, runtime search should fall back to the legacy plan so older database assets still work.

**Key interfaces:**
- SpeciesSearchRequest
- Species Catalog Search read projection
- SpeciesListItem hydration
- selected-language Common Name and Matched Common Name display
- Species Catalog latency/relevance harnesses

**Out of scope:**
- User-facing sort controls
- Changing one-character search policy
- Fuzzy typo matching
- Removing support for older database assets

- [ ] Older database assets without the generated table continue to return active search results through a fallback path.

- [ ] Selected-language-only Common Name matching remains enforced.

title: Generate Species Catalog Search entry index
description:

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** chore
**Summary:** Generate a purpose-built Species Catalog Search entry index for selected-language active text search.

**Current behavior:**
Species Catalog Search uses raw Species, Common Name, token, and FTS tables at runtime to find and rank active text results. The runtime query recomputes normalized Common Name match facts and must scan/sort more rows than the first page needs.

**Desired behavior:**
Database preparation should create a generated search-entry table that contains one or more pre-normalized candidate rows per Species and language. The index should include enough stable fields for runtime search to find selected-language Common Name candidates, rank displayed and alternate Common Name matches, and explain a Matched Common Name without reading every raw Common Name row first. Older database assets without the generated table must remain valid for the app through runtime fallback work in a dependent slice.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog database preparation
- Species Catalog schema contract/versioning
- selected-language Common Name normalization
- Species Catalog latency/relevance harnesses

**Out of scope:**
- Runtime routing through the generated index
- Changing SpeciesSearchRequest
- Fuzzy typo matching
- User-facing Species Catalog Workbench changes
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Database preparation creates a generated Species Catalog Search entry table for active text candidate lookup.
- [ ] Search entries are selected-language scoped and do not introduce English Common Name fallback rows for non-English locales.
- [ ] Search entries carry normalized prefix-match data and enough display/matched-name fields to preserve current relevance behavior.
- [ ] Schema/version checks recognize the new generated table without breaking older database assets.
- [ ] Focused tests or generation checks cover diacritic-folded Common Name prefixes such as French `melis` matching `Mélisse`.

title: Make Saved Stamp reorder preview respond sooner
description: Saved Stamp reorder now stays active, but the preview feels behind the pointer when dragging downward because insertion waits too far into the target row. Adjust the pointer threshold so the reordered preview moves a little sooner while keeping preview and commit aligned.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a Saved Stamp downward updates the preview before the pointer reaches the target row midpoint, commits the same order on pointerup, and existing upward/downward/end reorder regressions continue to pass.
close_reason: Made Saved Stamp reorder feel less sticky by biasing the insertion threshold in the active drag direction: downward previews cross at 40% of the target row and upward previews at 60%. Added a regression that verifies downward preview updates just before the old midpoint and still commits the previewed order; verified with focused FavoritesPanel Vitest and TypeScript check.

title: Keep Saved Stamp downward reorder session alive
description: Dragging a Saved Stamp downward can revert to the original order or behave like it released after one row. The pointer reorder grip likely loses pointer capture when the dragged row reflows downward, and the current lostpointercapture handler cancels the session. The reorder session should survive capture loss and continue from document-level pointermove/pointerup so downward drags stay active until real pointerup/cancel.
acceptance_criteria: A downward Saved Stamp reorder that loses pointer capture after the first preview continues to update on document pointermove and commits the final previewed order on pointerup. Pointercancel still aborts. Upward reorder and stamp-body drag-to-canvas remain covered.
close_reason: Kept Saved Stamp downward reorder active after row reflow by moving pointermove/pointerup ownership to document listeners and no longer treating lost pointer capture as cancel. Pointercancel still aborts. Added a regression covering capture loss during downward drag; verified with focused FavoritesPanel Vitest and TypeScript check.

title: Replace Saved Stamp reorder with pointer session
description: Saved Stamp reorder preview can still diverge from the released result because native drag/drop computes preview from dragover targets and commit from later drop/dragend targets after the row list has already reflowed. The reorder grip should use a pointer-captured reorder session so preview and commit share one ordered-id state and one geometry model. Stamp body drag-to-canvas should keep native drag/drop.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a Saved Stamp reorder grip previews from pointer position and pointerup commits the same ids that were last previewed. Moving a stamp above, below, or to the end works without relying on DataTransfer. Dragging the stamp body to the canvas still writes Saved Object Stamp drag data. Regression coverage exercises pointer-based reorder and asserts preview order equals committed order.
close_reason: Replaced Saved Stamp grip reordering with a pointer-captured reorder session so preview and release share the same latest ordered ids. Removed native DataTransfer-based reorder handling from the grip while keeping stamp-body drag-to-canvas native. Added pointer-session regressions for before, after, after-last, and preview-equals-commit behavior; verified with focused FavoritesPanel Vitest and TypeScript check.

title: Keep Saved Stamp reorder stable after release
description: Saved Stamp reorder preview is correct during drag, but after releasing the mouse the row can snap back to its original position. The commit path should keep the intended order visible through async persistence and not clear the preview until the Saved Stamp library reflects that order or the persistence call fails.
acceptance_criteria: After dropping a Saved Stamp while reorder persistence is still pending, the visible list keeps the dropped order instead of reverting. Once persistence resolves with the same order, the preview can clear without a visual jump. Regression coverage should simulate pending persistence.
close_reason: Fixed release-time Saved Stamp reorder snapback by keeping the committed preview active through the post-drop dragend event until the Saved Stamp library order catches up, and reverting only on persistence failure. Added a regression that dispatches drop followed by dragend and verifies the dropped order remains visible; verified with focused FavoritesPanel Vitest and TypeScript check.

title: Improve Saved Stamp reorder drop targets
description: Saved Stamp reordering feels unlike modern playlist reordering: dragging over a row always inserts before it, so dragging below the last stamp has no after-last destination and lower-half row hovers feel delayed or wrong. Reorder preview and drop should use row midpoint intent, including inserting after the hovered row and therefore after the last row.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a Saved Stamp reorder grip over the upper half of a row previews/drops before that row. Dragging over the lower half previews/drops after that row. Dragging onto the lower half of the bottom row can move a stamp to the end. Persistence still happens once on drop.
close_reason: Fixed Saved Stamp reorder feel by switching row drops from before-only insertion to midpoint-based before/after insertion, and by making the list space below the final row commit the current after-last preview. Added regressions for lower-half row drops and bottom-space drops; verified with focused FavoritesPanel Vitest and TypeScript check.

title: Fix live Saved Stamp reorder preview

acceptance_criteria: Dragging a Saved Stamp reorder grip over another stamp changes the visible row order before drop. Persistence still happens once on drop. Regression coverage simulates protected dragover data where DataTransfer types are visible but getData returns an empty string until drop.
close_reason: Fixed live Saved Stamp reorder preview by keeping the active reorder source id in the Favorites panel during the drag session, because browser dragover exposes DataTransfer types but not custom payload data. Added a protected-dragover regression in favorites-panel.test.tsx and verified with focused Vitest plus TypeScript check.

title: Improve Saved Object Stamp UI and placement preview

title: Fix release promotion release-note printf bullets
description:

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Prevent release promotion from aborting while generating release-note lines that start with hyphens.

**Current behavior:**
The promotion script emits release-note headings or bullet lines through `printf` using literal format strings that begin with `-`. Under bash, `printf` can interpret such a format string as an option. With strict error handling enabled, the script aborts while generating release notes.

**Desired behavior:**
Release-note generation must safely emit literal text that starts with `-` without bash option parsing failures. The promotion script should continue to use strict error handling, and the fix should apply consistently to every release-note `printf` call in the affected block that can start with a hyphen.

**Key interfaces:**
- Release promotion shell script strict-mode behavior
- Bash `printf` invocation semantics for literal strings beginning with `-`
- Release-note generation output contract

**Out of scope:**
- Redesigning the release promotion flow
- Changing release-note content beyond the escaping or formatting needed for safe emission

title: Run MapLibre Host destroy hooks after post-create failures
description:
## Slice Summary
Fix the MapLibre Host post-create failure path so adapter cleanup hooks run before the failed map is removed and the initialization error is reported.

## User Value
Map-backed adapters cannot leave stale listeners, refs, or overlays behind when setup fails after the host has published a map context. Failed initialization cleans up both host-owned and adapter-owned resources.

## Out of Scope
Do not change successful map creation, normal destroy semantics, preserved view behavior, or product behavior for map-backed surfaces.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Run MapLibre Host adapter cleanup hooks when post-create setup fails.

**Current behavior:**
If post-create setup fails after the MapLibre Host has published a context, the host removes the MapLibre instance and clears host-owned state, but it can bypass the request's destroy cleanup hook. Adapters that attached listeners, refs, overlays, or other surface-owned resources during partial setup can therefore retain stale state after the map is removed.

**Desired behavior:**
Any failure after a MapLibre Host context is published uses the same adapter cleanup guarantee as normal destroy: the request cleanup hook runs and the MapLibre instance is removed in a finally-style path. The host still clears the current context, disconnects resize observation, and reports the create error after cleanup. Cleanup-hook failures should not prevent map removal.

**Key interfaces:**
- MapLibre Host lifecycle and current context semantics
- Request post-create and destroy cleanup hooks
- Map-backed surface adapter resource ownership
- MapLibre Host regression tests

**Out of scope:**
- Changing successful map creation, key rebuild, resize, or preserved view behavior
- Moving adapter-owned listener/ref/overlay logic into the shared host
- Changing product behavior for Canvas Map Surface, Location, or Design Template maps
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Regression coverage simulates post-create setup throwing after adapter-owned setup has partially run.
- [ ] The failed create path invokes the request destroy cleanup hook before/while removing the failed map.
- [ ] The failed create path still disconnects resize observation, clears the current context, removes the MapLibre instance, and reports the create error.
- [ ] If the destroy cleanup hook throws, the failed map is still removed and the initialization error path remains deterministic.
- [ ] Focused MapLibre Host tests and `cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit` pass.
close_reason: Fixed MapLibre Host failed-create cleanup to run adapter onDestroy hooks before removing failed maps, while still removing maps and reporting create errors when cleanup throws. Tests: npm test -- maplibre-host.test.ts; npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Clean up MapLibre Host after post-create setup failures
description:

## User Value

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Clean up MapLibre Host resources when caller post-create setup fails.

**Current behavior:**
If caller setup after MapLibre map creation throws after the host has installed its map context and resize observer, the host reports an initialization error but can leave the partially initialized map/context alive. A caller can then see an error while `current()` still exposes a live map, and a same-key update can reuse the failed context.

**Desired behavior:**
Any failure during map creation or post-create setup leaves no live MapLibre context, map instance, resize observer, or stale initialization state in the host. The host reports the create error only after tearing down the partial context, and a retry starts from a clean map creation path.

**Key interfaces:**
- MapLibre Host lifecycle and `current()` behavior
- Caller post-create setup callback
- Resize observer ownership
- Map-backed surface host adapter tests

**Out of scope:**
- Changing successful map creation, basemap style rebuild, or preserved view semantics
- Changing Canvas Map Surface, Location, or Design Template product behavior beyond the failure cleanup path
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Regression coverage simulates caller post-create setup throwing after the map context and resize observer are installed.
- [ ] The failed create path removes the MapLibre instance, disconnects the resize observer, clears the current host context, and does not leave `current()` exposing the failed map.
- [ ] A same-key retry after the failure creates a fresh MapLibre instance instead of reusing the failed context.
- [ ] Existing successful MapLibre Host create, rebuild, preserved view, resize, and destroy behavior remains covered.
- [ ] Focused MapLibre Host tests and `cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit` pass.
close_reason: Fixed MapLibre Host post-create failure cleanup so failed contexts are removed before reporting errors, with regression coverage for observer disconnect, map removal, current() clearing, same-key retry, plus npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Restore Plant DB shortcut from welcome state
description:
## Slice Summary

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Restore the Plant Database panel shortcut behavior from the welcome/no-Design state.

**Current behavior:**
The App Command Graph disables the Plant Database navigation command when no Design is open. As a result, pressing the Plant Database shortcut from the welcome state leaves the side panel closed, breaking the existing shortcut contract.

**Desired behavior:**
The Plant Database navigation command remains available from the no-Design state through keyboard shortcut dispatch and command execution. The command should still route through the App Command Graph, and any Design-dependent panel availability should remain deliberate and covered by tests.

**Key interfaces:**
- App Command Graph navigation commands
- Keyboard shortcut dispatch for panel navigation
- Shell panel and side-panel navigation state
- PanelBar disabled-state projection

**Out of scope:**
- Changing shortcut key assignments
- Changing the set of panels
- Reworking welcome-screen or shell layout
- Broadly changing Design-dependent availability beyond this regression
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Pressing the Plant Database shortcut from the no-Design state opens the Plant Database side panel.
- [ ] `runAppCommand()` preserves the intended Plant Database navigation behavior from the no-Design state.
- [ ] Existing shortcut contract coverage passes, including the panel shortcut test that exercises Ctrl+2.
- [ ] Focused frontend regression tests cover the no-Design Plant Database shortcut/command behavior.

title: Cap Plant Spacing preview materialization
description:
## Slice Summary
Bound Plant Spacing preview work so very small valid intervals or long spacing guides cannot eagerly allocate and render an unbounded number of preview placed plants during pointer movement.

## User Value
A designer can enter physically valid dense intervals without freezing the interface while previewing a long spacing guide.

## Out of Scope
Do not block physically valid Plant Spacing Intervals outright, change the dense-confirmation threshold, or change final commit behavior beyond what is needed to keep preview work bounded.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Bound Plant Spacing preview generation before preview placed plants are materialized.

**Current behavior:**
Plant Spacing preview generation can eagerly compute every generated position on pointer movement before dense confirmation can protect the interface. A very small physically valid Plant Spacing Interval over a long spacing guide can allocate many positions and render one preview marker per generated placed plant.

**Desired behavior:**
Preview computation must derive the generated count without unbounded allocation and must cap or summarize preview markers before materializing them. Dense valid inputs remain allowed, but the live preview must stay responsive and communicate the dense count/warning rather than rendering unbounded ghost markers.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Spacing sequence math
- Plant Spacing preview overlay
- Plant Spacing dense warning and dense confirmation
- Scene interaction pointer-move preview path

**Out of scope:**
- Blocking physically valid Plant Spacing Intervals solely because they are dense
- Changing the 100 generated-plant dense confirmation threshold
- Changing final dense commit behavior beyond any bounded-count helper needed by preview
- Adding new UX copy unless existing dense-warning copy is insufficient
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Live Plant Spacing preview does not allocate or render unbounded generated positions for very small valid intervals over long spacing guides.
- [ ] The preview still reports the generated count and dense warning for dense valid intervals.
- [ ] Normal previews at or below the safe preview cap still render generated ghost markers as before.
- [ ] Dense commits still require confirmation when generated count is greater than 100.
- [ ] Focused tests cover a tiny valid interval over a long spacing guide without materializing all generated positions.
close_reason: Bounded Plant Spacing live preview materialization with constant-time generated counts and capped ghost positions, deferred full dense position materialization until explicit confirmation, added focused preview-cap coverage, and verified with Plant Spacing sequence tests, SceneInteraction tests, and npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Block Plant Spacing HUD clicks from canvas commits
description:
## Slice Summary
Prevent Plant Spacing HUD pointer interactions from being interpreted as spacing guide endpoint clicks by the canvas.

## User Value
A designer can edit the Plant Spacing Interval or press Cancel/Confirm without accidentally creating placed plants or changing the current spacing guide.

## Out of Scope
Do not change Plant Spacing generation math, dense-count thresholds, keyboard shortcuts, or general canvas pointer handling outside Plant Spacing HUD interactions.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Prevent Plant Spacing HUD pointer interactions from becoming canvas spacing guide endpoint clicks.

**Current behavior:**
When Plant Spacing has a sampled placed plant, pointer interactions from the HUD can bubble into the canvas pointerdown handler. Editing the Plant Spacing Interval or pressing HUD actions can be treated as a spacing guide endpoint click before the control action runs.

**Desired behavior:**
Pointerdown interactions that originate inside the Plant Spacing HUD or its editable controls are consumed as HUD interactions only. They must not commit, update, or replace a Plant Spacing spacing guide endpoint. Canvas pointerdown interactions outside the HUD continue to drive Plant Spacing normally.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Spacing Tool HUD
- Canvas pointer interaction handling
- Plant Spacing Interval input
- Plant Spacing cancel and dense-confirmation controls

**Out of scope:**
- Changing Plant Spacing sequence math
- Changing dense-count confirmation behavior
- Changing non-Plant Spacing canvas tools
- Reworking general overlay architecture
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clicking or pointerdowning the Plant Spacing Interval input does not create placed plants or commit a spacing guide endpoint.
- [ ] Clicking Plant Spacing HUD Cancel does not first commit generated placed plants.
- [ ] Clicking dense Confirm or dense Cancel is handled once by the HUD and is not also interpreted as a canvas endpoint click.
- [ ] Canvas clicks outside the Plant Spacing HUD still sample a source placed plant or commit a spacing guide endpoint as before.
- [ ] Focused SceneInteraction or overlay tests cover HUD-origin pointer events.
close_reason: Stopped Plant Spacing HUD pointerdowns from bubbling into canvas endpoint commits, added focused SceneInteraction regression coverage for interval-input pointerdowns, and verified with the focused SceneInteraction test file plus npx tsc --noEmit.

title: C18 User content formatted into free text; privacy rests on a downstream scrubber: Phase 1 mechanism and detector (1a, 1b)
description:

Definition: Native or page code writes paths, Design names or other user content into error, log or job-message text when it creates them, so the privacy boundary depends on a pattern scrubber recognising every shape.

Exit: 0 user paths formatted into failure or log text (about 50 path.display() sites); the corpus carries every path shape and passes on both sides.

Definition: A seam takes optional, whole-object or untyped arguments, or publishes a status or read model that does not name its subject or snapshot, so a caller can skip a required input, bypass the owner, or pair a value with the wrong subject without a compile error.

Mechanism (prevents a new member): Typed command map, branded ids and units, generated unions; seam inputs required and typed (no optional owner parameter, no whole CanopiFile or settings record outside its owner, no open-string kinds or shortcuts); a published status is a record keyed by its subject; a read model takes every input as a parameter and reads no signal; a domain type enforces its convention at construction.

Detector (fails on a new member): tsc with the guardrail types; contract tests; ast-grep rules: subject-keyed *Status fields, get*ReadModel and read*Snapshot modules import no signal (options.x ?? signal banned), no optional owner parameter or whole-Design argument; a typed shortcut (keymap row id); a model-based test of the map notice switching background between failure and read.

Exit: t accepts only generated locale keys; branded LonLat, PlaneMetres, Degrees, Radians and Design, item and job id brands in types/ with Rust newtypes in canopi-types; each later stream adopts them in its files.

Member finding keys: none in this phase; this bead lands the class's mechanism and detector that later phases' members are counted by.

Other members: t5 (optional params skipped silently), t4 (native command policy ordering trap).

title: Web plant search matches mid-word and picks a different display name than Desktop
description: H6, NAT-12, WEB-17 (2.1 analysis, dup-inventory.md and area reports). Desktop matches FTS5 MATCH or a common-name token prefix (word start); the Web DuckDB reader (web/duckdb-wasm-catalog.ts, about lines 791-1050) matches substring LIKE %q%, so a mid-word query finds plants only on Web. Desktop's displayed common name comes from best_common_names, then is_primary=1 by display_order; Web orders by display_order before is_primary and needs no primary, so it can show another name. Ranking is written three times (Rust SQLite, DuckDB SQL, the test fake in __tests__/support/in-memory-reduced-species-catalog.ts) with no parity test. Fixed by canopi-f47t.52.68 (the build owns keys and display names; one ranking contract generates both queries; the user-reviewed corpus gates both readers), not by patching the Web SQL. Regression tests name this bead: Web matches word starts only, like Desktop; Web shows Desktop's display name for the same plant and locale. User hears: Web search now matches Desktop (word-start matching, Desktop's order and display name).
notes: Q45 pass (2026-10-17), scope added; details in docs/plans/2-1-foundations.md 'Q45 owners' lines under the keys named: Also fixed by .52.68 (Q45 pass): Web browse order differs from Desktop (test 'canopi-f47t.52.69: Web browse orders plants as Desktop does'); the catalog highlight can mark a mid-word or typo fragment (test 'canopi-f47t.52.69: the highlight marks the word that matched'); Web canvas labels (test in .52.53).

title: One catalog search ranking contract and a user-reviewed corpus gate both readers
description: Q43, Q44, Q46 (user, 2026-10-17); ADR 0027 'Catalog search has one owner'; plan Phase 3 stream N4; contracts §15. The catalog build writes the search keys (name tokens, scientific names, synonyms) and the chosen display name per locale into both outputs (SQLite and the Web Parquet), derived from catalog data without changing it. Today's Desktop tiers and tie-breakers (exact, starts with, all tokens at word starts in the locale display name, all tokens in any locale name; then token positions, display-name length, BM25, canonical name) become one ranking contract (data, beside the normalisation contract) from which the SQLite and DuckDB queries are generated: static, parameter-bound, no string-formatted SQL. Deleted: the hand-written Web ranker in the DuckDB reader, the test fake's tiers (fakes return fixed results), the gallery's searchCatalog ranking. BM25 is replaced by a build-computed static weight only if the corpus shows no change. A corpus of real queries per locale with expected top results in order (e.g. pommier -> Malus domestica 'Pommier cultivé' first), captured from today's Desktop ranking, reviewed by the user once, gates both readers (the Web species reader contract suite). A prototype shows Desktop and Web side by side before the contract is final. Exit: rankers 3 -> 1; string-formatted catalog SQL sites -> 0 (baseline recorded in the ratchet file at the stream's start). Fixes the Web search bug filed beside it. Gates: Rust rows, Frontend, Species catalog queries (species_catalog_contract.py check and its Python tests), Web check Chromium and WebKit.
notes:
Decision (user, 2026-10-17, Q46): no popularity signal now. Whether to add a popularity column to the catalog build is asked again after the side-by-side prototype, before the contract is final.
Q45 pass (2026-10-17), scope added; details in docs/plans/2-1-foundations.md 'Q45 owners' lines under the keys named: Search prototype folded in (proto/search; user 2026-10-17: best results first). Q46 (today's Desktop tiers; BM25 replaced only with no change) stands until the user decides. PROPOSED for the user at the corpus review: whole-word tiers above partial word starts; BM25 deleted from the order (51/54 identical, the 3 changes already wrong); kana folding (りんご). Static weight rejected (18/54, fails Q46's condition). Also OPEN there: a build-derived popularity signal (locale count, after token positions, before length), the Desktop-only full-text tier, a substring last tier for CJK and compounds. Also [search-highlight-second-matcher, desktop-ranker-three-variants, desktop-ranking-fallback-paths, recommended-browse-order, search-normalisation-copies/-three-implementations/-three-copies, web-catalog-artifact-generation, web-catalog-manifest-admission, photo-attribution-owner, catalog-fixed-filter-option-lists, catalog-test-schema-copies, reduced-catalog-fake-filters]: one fixture catalog via prepare-db.py; canopi-search-text crate plus in-page wasm (Python/TS copies and 9,228 generated lines deleted); Web Parquet by the Python duckdb package (build-time dependency); admitWebCatalogManifest; browse score column; attribution read model; filter value lists; matched entry returned for the highlight; relevance.rs, fallbacks and probes deleted; admission refuses missing entry tables; fake deleted for the real DuckDB reader. Exit: rankers 5 to 1, normalisers 3 to 1, manifest admissions 2 to 1, Recommended orderings 2 to 1, filter value lists 2 to 1.

title: A position moved past the antimeridian is saved with longitude beyond ±180, and Canopi then refuses to open the file
description: Found by the phase 2 cut stage's second review (2026-10-06). roundGeoPosition (canvas/runtime/scene/geo-frame.ts) clamps latitude to ±85.051128779 but not longitude; session-plane toGeo (lngFromMercatorX) neither wraps nor clamps, and nudge/drag deltas have no world bound. A position moved east of 180° is written as lon > 180, and both decoders (common-types design.rs GeoPoint::is_valid, the TS schema) refuse the file; neither save path checks geometry. Predates the cut. Fix: wrap or clamp longitude at write (or bound the edit), with a guard beside 'writes a latitude at the Web Mercator limit'.
close_reason: Fixed in phase 3 (d7ed85ca, merge e9c2343d): longitude clamped to ±180 at save only; silent, kept by the user (U42). Guard: 'a point at lon 181 saves as 180 and the file reopens'. Gates and CI: see canopi-f47t.3.

title: Saved views and story steps keep their framed area in any window
description: User decision 2026-10-03 (U21), replacing phase 1's camera-zoom go-to rule (A12). A saved view (and a story step) stores its centre, its bearing and the visible ground size (width x height in metres in the view's own turned frame), as an optional field of the saved view in .canopi. Going to it fits that turned rectangle inside the current window at the saved bearing ('contain'): same window = the exact saved camera; a smaller window, projector or phone zooms out just enough that nothing framed is cut off; a larger window shows more around it and never zooms in past the saved zoom. Thumbnails use the same rule, so a thumbnail shows what going to the view shows. A saved view without the field (2.0 builds so far) falls back to the camera zoom; no migration (ADR 0021; name the format change in the handoff). Tests first: 'a view saved in a 1400x900 window and opened in a 1000x700 one keeps every corner inside'; 'the same window restores the exact camera'; 'a larger window never zooms in past the saved zoom'; 'a story step saved at 30 keeps its frame on a smaller screen'; 'a saved view without the size falls back to the camera zoom'; one test through the real snapshot map (AGENTS.md seam rule). Built in the 2.0 bug-fix step.
