title: Location map recreates itself on every basemap change
description:
Found while implementing the provider binding at 16c5f695. app/location/map-editing.ts (used by both Desktop's components/canvas/LocationTab.tsx and Web's web/WebLocationPanel.tsx) passes basemapStyle as the surface map `key` and as a createMap option, and it performs NO basemap reconciliation of any kind. A provider, key or session change therefore recreates the whole map, which the C4 contract forbids: 'no settings-owned map, no setStyle() or map recreation on key/provider/session changes'. The camera, placement crosshair and any in-progress coordinate edit are lost on a basemap change.

The world map was fixed at 16c5f695 by adding maplibre/basemap-bind.ts and making WorldMapSurface's key independent of the basemap style. Location is a DIFFERENT surface (maplibre/location-map.ts via app/location/map-editing.ts), so it is unaffected by that commit and still broken. Do not assume the world-map fix covers it.

REQUIRED WORK: make map-editing's surface key independent of basemapStyle; create one BasemapProvider per map lifetime and bind it with bindBasemapProvider from maplibre/basemap-bind.ts; apply a style change by calling provider.update({ style }) plus a viewport read rather than recreating; keep the map's createMap call supplying a starting style so the map has a basemap before the provider publishes; tear the provider down with the map lifetime. Verify the Location camera, crosshair and placement survive a provider switch, per the C4 exit criterion that both editions change provider/key/opacity without losing camera, scene, overlays or placement.

NOTE: the shared-workspace map (maplibre/workspace-map.ts + app/canvas-map-surface/workspace-map-controls.ts) already documents a real reconciliation path that never calls setStyle or recreates the map; check whether Location should route through that existing owner rather than duplicating a second reconciler.
close_reason: Fixed and verified at 229b61f2. app/location/map-editing.ts now keys its surface map independently of basemapStyle, creates one BasemapProvider per map lifetime and binds it with bindBasemapProvider in onCreate alongside the map's other lifetime cleanup, and applies a style change through provider.update({ style }, viewport) so the provider reconciles the contribution into the live map instead of recreating it. The test that encoded the violation is inverted rather than deleted: it used to require the map to be rebuilt and now asserts the map is NOT rebuilt, the camera and zoom survive, and remove was never called. Verified by mutation -- restoring key: preferredBasemapStyle and the style-keyed effect makes the inverted test fail, so it detects the regression rather than merely passing. FakeLocationMap and FakeLocationTabMap gained the reconcile surface through a new shared __tests__/support/fake-basemap-contribution.ts. docs/agent/maplibre.md records the rule that a live map takes its basemap from the provider binding, never from its own creation options, and that a surface's map key must be independent of the basemap style. Gates: tsc clean, check:ui pass, both edition builds pass, full Vitest 281 files / 2736 tests pass. NOTE: this establishes that both editions change provider without losing camera, scene, overlays or placement in the SURFACE layer; live provider evidence and isolated Web placement remain outstanding under canopi-j571.1.

Authority: docs/design/raster-rework/completion-design.md (C0-C5) and its prompt. The accepted foundation 34e4ded4 is integrated into main at f61f8494. New completion implementation stays on a reviewable candidate branch until independent review; public release and branch deletion are not authorized.
design:
Authority: docs/design/raster-rework/completion-agent-prompt.md and
docs/design/raster-rework/completion-design.md (C0–C5). Product contract:
docs/design/raster-data-analysis-rework.md. Approved UI reference: 0e696722
(desktop/web/ui-gallery/raster-reference-prototype/). Ordered-source contract:
docs/design/raster-rework/ordered-cog-design.md. ADR 0027 owns the composition
rationale.

One cohesive implementation bead with internal milestones C0–C5. Existing
narrower beads remain linked evidence/follow-ups, not competing assignments.
Branch: feature/raster-rework-completion from the integrated baseline.

C0 integration (done): accepted foundation feature/bounded-raster-generations
34e4ded4 fast-forwarded into main, then the whole-rework handoff a96dcfd9
merged deliberately (branches diverged because the bounded stack re-parented
af8aed87 under 34bf6041). Doc conflicts resolved toward the handoff's current
status with the bounded branch's revision-labelled evidence preserved.
Integration commit f61f8494. Candidate branch starts from that baseline.

C1 conditional larger-raster policy: production limits stay unchanged until
measurement passes. Authorized initial policy for new ordered imports only —
at most 24 selected files, 2 GiB per file, 2 GiB total selected bytes
(equality admitted, excess refused by name before publication); at most
400,000,000 processing cells in the proposed active collection, computed with
checked arithmetic as the sum of each source occurrence's full native
width × height including NoData and overlap. A preserved dense member
contributes its full grid size; a preserved sparse member contributes the sum
of unique stored chunk footprints. Deduplicate result/quality roles. Remove
the old 25-million-cell union-envelope admission only from the ordered path;
retain coordinate/index representability and legacy dense guards. Reorder,
remove, Undo/Restore and reads of accepted generations stay grandfathered —
no new refusal may make saved history unreadable. Recheck against the expected
current head at Apply. Start with the existing test-only admission::limits_probe;
enable the production policy only after the measured gates pass.

Fixtures (representative, read-only, outside Git): the 12-tile IGN MNH batch
(48M cells); the real ground MNT tile; a separate uncompressed 20,000×20,000
Float32 0.5 m analytical plane above 1 GiB with block-crossing holes and
z=0.25x+0.5y-100; at least 24 small adjacent/separated sources including a
million-pixel gap. Never substitute MNH for slope input or resample private
data into a purported survey.

Resource gate: simultaneous incremental raster workload within 1 GiB
including native app increment above recorded idle, decoder caches and live
children; 128 MiB decoded caches, 512 MiB reproducible disk cache and 256 MiB
free-space reserve retained; cancellation settles owned work within 5 s;
no >50 ms UI-thread raster compute. One cold and three warm display runs with
median/p95 tile timings. If a required fixture or the measurement environment
is unavailable, keep production limits unchanged and report capacity pending;
never lower the required evidence or pick different ceilings.

C2 production Data/Analysis/Layers: faithful adaptation of 0e696722 to the
accepted ordered-source workflow (obsolete replacement controls are
superseded). Data owns reusable datasets, compatible imports, Add to Design,
rename, source priority, history/Undo/Restore and confirmed library deletion.
Analysis offers Slope only with compatible ground inputs, ineligible reasons,
result name, degrees/percent, Run/Cancel/Retry and previous-result visibility.
Layers becomes a flat geographic presentation list in actual saved order with
independent source/result eyes, opacity, ramp/legend, extent navigation and
undoable Remove from Design. Reuse app/lidar/actions.ts, library-store.ts and
app/design-edit/lidar.ts; no controller-to-controller imports, no mirrored
canvas entity stores, no second job scheduler.

C3 numeric inspection: implement sample(entity, expected generation, WGS84
point) as a new typed operation under common-types/src/lidar.rs with one
executor-backed command and policy entry. Refuse a head mismatch at admission,
recheck currency before returning, return the generation with physical value
and units, explicit NoData or categorized unavailable/stale. Inverse CRS
transform then the containing north-up half-open pixel; no bilinear display
sample or PNG decoding. One inspection session owned by the canvas/workspace
lifecycle; supersede older requests; reject late responses on
layer/head/Design change; Escape/toggle-off/removal/Location/teardown exits and
releases listeners. Status is read-only and not saved in a Design.

C4 Web Location and shared basemap providers: establish the replacement ADR
for the specific Web-v1 restrictions in ADRs 0013/0016, then update status
links, the relevant guide and equivalent/stronger guards together. Web
composes coordinate-workbench.ts directly with a browser-safe Location
surface; Desktop retains native search as an injected capability. Preserve
the complete spatial frame, altitude and north bearing; camera movement alone
never commits. Shared provider module under maplibre/ returning
idle|loading|ready|unavailable with update/dispose and one HTTP adapter per
edition. Extend BasemapStyle with google_satellite; keep street = OSM and
serialized satellite = MapTiler (preserve saved values, show unavailable
rather than normalizing); add nullable device-local google_maps_api_key.
Keyless path uses the exact non-blocking prompt; a configured official-key
failure never silently downgrades. No setStyle() or map recreation on
provider/key/session change. Fake recognizable credentials for fault tests;
never infer service success from mocks.

C5 final candidate: repository gates on the final combined diff (fmt, strict
workspace Clippy/check/tests, native command policy, GDAL-backed ignored LiDAR
lane with the external fixture identified, generated bindings drift,
TypeScript, full Vitest, gallery check, both frontend builds, docs validator).
Rebase preserving merges onto current main before final mixed-architecture
gates. Build/packaging workflows for Linux, Windows and macOS; no release
publication. Exercise the complete isolated Desktop flow ending in a confirmed
Design Location, plus a disposable historical library through the actual app.
Fresh final diff/contract review before forwarding; repair in-scope findings.

Out of scope unless a demonstrated required workflow cannot work without it:
reclamation, per-occurrence filename schema changes, new analysis types.
Preserve the primary checkout's desktop/src/native_operation.rs modification
and .beads.gate.lock.
acceptance_criteria:
C1: exact larger-raster policy implemented and enabled only after the measured gates pass through real production callers with no bypass; or production limits unchanged with a named capacity blocker and C2-C4 continued against existing safe limits.
C2: Data -> import -> Analysis -> Layers works through real native commands; panel/Design changes during jobs cannot misattach results; independent eyes/order/legends survive save/reopen; Remove is undoable without deleting the library; both themes, 390px width, keyboard/focus and all 11 locales checked through production gallery fixtures; Web preserves unavailable local references.
C3: click and keyboard-center return independently known physical values for source and slope; holes and excluded edges report NoData while included edges return the containing cell; a late answer after head/selection/Design replacement never appears current; Escape restores normal tools and repeated mount/unmount leaves no listeners or reads.
C4: both editions change provider/key/opacity without losing camera, scene, overlays or placement; out-of-order session/viewport answers are fenced; hidden/provisional Canvas issues no remote imagery work; actual isolated Web placement saves/exports/reopens the same frame including Undo and map-error entry; fake-key redaction verified in errors, URLs, response bodies and diagnostics; replacement ADR for ADRs 0013/0016 established with guards updated.
C5: repository gates green on the final combined diff; rebase preserving merges onto current main before final mixed-architecture gates; final diff/contract review performed with in-scope findings repaired; receipt, guides and debrief updated; candidate pushed to both destinations with ancestry verified; a required unavailable gate yields partial delivery, never a verified-release-candidate claim.

ROUND 5 at 60ac945f (pushed and verified at that exact revision on BOTH destinations).
C2 PRESENTATION DELIVERED IN TWO COMMITS.
b0612a0a -- undoable presentation reordering through Design Edit: moveLidarEntry swaps one presentation entry with its neighbour in the Design's saved display order, renumbers densely from zero, and returns the Design untouched for a no-op move (so nudging the topmost entry up creates no history entry). Exposed as movePresentationEntry. Tests cover a real swap, dense renumbering, both no-op boundaries, that display settings travel with the entry, and that an unpresented id is ignored. Writing them exposed an oracle subtlety: readLidarEntries returns the stored array's insertion order while the panel displays by the order field -- the first assertion version failed against correct behaviour and now sorts by order the way the panel does.
60ac945f -- the flat geographic list the contract requires. The panel had nested each analysis result inside its source group, which made source and result visibility the same act (hiding or collapsing a source took its results with it) and left result rows unreorderable. The list is now ONE flat sequence in the Design's saved order: every row carries a source/result badge, its own eye, keyboard-accessible move up/down writing through Design Edit, and only its own kind's actions (history/delete-from-library for a source, delete-result for an analysis). Removed with the nesting: the disclosure state, collapsed-result summary, source group wrapper, analysis-row indent and their dead stylesheet rules. selected and the entry count now read the presentation list rather than sources alone.
GATES this round: full Vitest 274 files / 2681 tests PASS (twice, including after the CSS fix); npx tsc --noEmit PASS; npm run check:ui PASS; npm run build PASS. A first attempt tripped the CSS module spacing policy with a literal gap: 2px and was fixed with the spacing token -- worth noting because the policy test is the only thing that catches that class of drift.
C3 FRONTEND COORDINATE SEAM -- DESIGN GAP FOUND, NOT YET RESOLVED: sample() takes a WGS84 point, but the canvas workspace knows scene-local metres relative to the Design's anchor (lat/lon + north bearing). There is no frontend projection library (no proj4/geodesy installed) and converting metres to WGS84 with a flat-earth approximation could select the WRONG native pixel -- exactly the wrong answer the contract designs against. I deliberately did not ship an approximate conversion. Options for the next round: (a) decompose the request into the anchor WGS84 point plus a north/east offset and let native use gdaltransform for the anchor then rotate in the projected plane (accurate, keeps gdaltransform authoritative, small contract addition); (b) add a frontend projection dependency (needs justification per the repository dependency rule); (c) a second native operation taking scene-relative metres. I recommend (a).

title: LiDAR undo leaves the slope analysis of the undone generation as current
description:
Found in the real-Desktop smoke of canopi-jv8a.4 (isolated profile, 2026-09-21).

Reproduction: create a layer, import a source (generation A), create a slope analysis (analysis generation X from A), import an overlapping replacement (generation B; the dependent-refresh path correctly enqueues one refresh, producing analysis generation Y from B and re-pointing lidar_analysis_heads to Y), then Undo the replacement (layer head becomes generation C, members reverted). Observed: no analysis job is enqueued and lidar_analysis_heads still points at Y, whose source_generation_id is B. The map therefore keeps showing the slope of the composition the user just undid, presented as the current ready result.

Evidence (preserved disposable profile .rq-scratch/smoke-profile-Ev4FZ3/data/com.canopi.app/lidar/lidar-library.sqlite): anl-18d76b0468aee9fd0007 (20:57:23-31, complete) -> agen-18d76b062f16691a0008 from gen-18d76af20871ce6b0004; anl-18d76b3810ba20050010 (21:01:05-15, complete) -> agen-18d76b3a708abf260011 from gen-18d76b3764d937ef000e (min_value 0.0012 -> 0.0 after the replacement); after the undo published gen-18d76b8cda55f5790012 (21:07:12) the analysis tables are unchanged: lidar_analysis_heads -> agen-...0011, no third job.

Cause: mod.rs::begin_undo settles the undo (settle_cancel + refresh_snapshot_quiet) but never calls refresh_dependents, while the Apply route does (finish_apply -> refresh_dependents -> analysis::enqueue_refreshes). enqueue_refreshes would already do the right thing: it skips only when the analysis head's source_generation_id equals the layer head.

Two options, and the choice is a product decision the design does not settle, so it is not changed under the canopi-jv8a.4 scope freeze:
1. Recompute: call refresh_dependents after an undo that changed the head (small, uses the existing mechanism, mirrors Apply; costs one analysis run).
2. Re-point: when a ready analysis generation exists for the restored head (for example agen-...0008 was computed from gen-...0004, which the undo restored), re-point lidar_analysis_heads to it and skip the recomputation; enqueue a refresh only when no matching result exists. Cheaper and consistent with 'undo restores accepted history', but it adds a new re-point semantic that the design and receipt do not currently describe.

Acceptance: after an undo that changes the layer head, the analysis head matches the restored generation - either recomputed or re-pointed - and the Desktop shows a result consistent with the current coverage. A caller-level regression must drive the undo settlement path (not just undo_import) and assert the analysis head/source generation, with the Apply-path refresh as the control.

## Required repairs

1. **P1 — Collection reads deadlock.** mod.rs:749 holds CatalogueGuard until function return; :819 calls layer_history, which acquires the same mutex at :721. A real layer_collection call on an empty layer timed out. Read history under the existing connection, retaining a consistent snapshot, and exercise this public read surface.

2. **P1 — Edit completion and the visible selection are not connected reliably.** mod.rs:1100 spawns an edit and returns acknowledgement; settlement logs errors and discards library_snapshot output. actions.ts:162 refreshes immediately; library-store.ts:49/77 only keeps polling for import/analysis jobs. A slow member edit can finish after polling stops, with no map update or reported error. In LidarLayersSection.tsx:93-143, History is loaded only when opened, the effect skips history mode, and late collection/history answers are never fenced against the selection/head. SourcePriorityList's Undo uses collection.layer_id, so a late response can even target the previous layer while the header shows the new one. Use an explicit completion result through the existing async command/executor seam, refresh selected source/history/map state after settlement, fence stale responses, and keep failed-edit messages visible. Busy/loading controls must not send edits without the snapshot the user actually saw. No event bus or new scheduler is needed.

3. **P1 — Published statistics use different composition semantics.** import.rs:3332-3450 builds incoming members with the obsolete Add/ReplaceOverlap role; CollectionReader::new at generation.rs:306 reverses them but retains that role. Persisted rows are later loaded as Replace. A full-cover import of 9 above 5 reads back as 9 but publishes min/max 5/5. Construct every new ordered occurrence with topmost-valid semantics, including the measuring/review path. Preserve old role semantics only for historical reads.

4. **P1 — Import admission is incomplete.** stage_import checks every first-batch source against an absent layer CRS, so equal-coordinate EPSG:3857 and EPSG:4326 inputs are accepted together. stage_source_samples discards the valid sample count, allowing all-NoData members. prepare_apply/apply_import permit publication of the compatible subset of a rejected batch; the UI disabling Add sources is the only guard. Review/Apply envelope checks use manifest.grid (the fixed original lattice dimensions) plus incoming inputs, omitting prior ordered members. An actual 32,000,016-cell collection was admitted under the unchanged 25M limit. Validate a batch against one common interpretation, reject each zero-valid source by name, recheck whole-batch admission in the backend, and measure the current composition's extent separately from its fixed coordinate anchor. Do not increase limits.

5. **P1 — Transition can alter accepted historical data.** collection.rs:208 describes a sparse previous composition using its original manifest grid dimensions; generation.rs:202-215 clips it to that box. A valid chunk at x=2048 becomes entirely invalid through the adapter although the original chunk reader returns all 16 samples. Separately, import.rs:3478 follows head.base_generation_id instead of wrapping the actual accepted head: a historical overlay valued 7 becomes the older base valued 5 after adding a new source. Preserve the latest head itself as the indivisible member and retain its signed sparse chunk extent/coordinates through the existing reader. No re-encoding or historical source reconstruction is needed.

6. **P1 — Slope has three remaining correctness holes.** analysis.rs:108-116 only accepts a direct source COG as a representative raster; after Undo leaves only Previous composition, valid slope input fails with 'generation has no stored raster to inspect'. A queued job whose captured source is superseded returns a plain publication error, while mod.rs:1700 only coalesces Ok(stale=true); the latest-head refresh can be lost. presentation.rs:80-98 never compares source and result heads and reports old results Ready after failed/cancelled refresh or restart. A restart after source publication reproduced Ready with no stale detail. Reuse the preserved reader for eligibility, route superseded work through the existing stale/coalescing outcome, and derive readiness from source identity, including empty composition and startup. Retain last-good results with truthful stale/unavailable state.

7. **P1 — Undo/history boundaries and restore equality are inconsistent.** First import exposes can_undo=false; a direct Undo reaches empty, but another Undo reinstates the import. Restore only compares generation IDs and republishes identical ordered member identities. History infers operation from interpretation lists and the undo cursor, so labels such as import/remove can describe an Undo, and duplicate occurrences are conflated. Represent the empty baseline/exhausted Undo consistently, compare ordered occurrence identities for restore no-ops, and record the real operation instead of guessing it. Keep this as metadata and local history logic.

8. **P2 — Source-region facts reread the first block.** generation.rs:1227 uses chunk-local clip_x0/clip_y0 as source pixel coordinates without the chunk origin offset. A 2048x1 source with 1024 invalid cells followed by 1024 valid sevens has exact review coverage 1024 but stored source-list coverage 0/range 0-0. catalogue.rs:1069 also includes zero-valid blocks in extrema. Fix the source-coordinate translation and exclude zero-valid blocks from numeric extrema. This is separate from the explicitly deferred source preview-range sentinel behavior tracked in canopi-jv8a.2.

9. **P2 — Bound the incremental read surfaces already promised.** collection_members and history return complete vectors; layer_collection bundles every version and its membership into every source-list refresh. Each new tile reader resolves every current member. The 16-file selection limit does not bound lifetime membership/history. Keep this repair narrow: use existing catalogue indexes/region queries and small member/history pages for incremental consumers, and select intersecting members for bounded reads. A short-lived member vector during a mutation is not itself a reason for a generic pagination layer. No new cache architecture, custom spatial engine or capacity campaign is required.

10. **P2 — Finish the existing UI contract with existing data.** The source list shows a 12-character interpretation hash despite lidar_sources.original_filename already being populated (import.rs:937). Use that stored name through the existing interpretation/source relation; no schema migration is needed for the available original name. HistoryDetail shows only operation/time/cell count, omitting the required unique version cue. The import confirmation still renders obsolete uncovered/overlap/invalid counters at LidarLayersSection.tsx:449. Add the small identity cue and remove the old counters; keep the accepted dock layout and Add sources interaction.

11. **P2 — Propagate cancellation through the compatibility read.** collection.rs:237 calls compat_lease with AtomicBool::new(false), so a cold legacy conversion ignores the real import/tile/analysis cancellation token. Carry the caller's token through the existing load/adapter chain and check cancellation at the publication boundary. This needs no new cancellation service.

comments.text:
Independent review of 524eef55 (2026-09-22)

Disposition: partial. Keep the ordered snapshot architecture. Three reproduced defects remain, plus the already-required mounted-map observation. No capacity increase, engine change, new scheduler, cache framework or per-occurrence naming project is needed. No production source changed during review; diagnostic additions live only in this ignored archive of the delivery revision.

1. P1 — Tile candidate bounds omit the reduction footprint. desktop/src/services/lidar/tiles.rs:566-592 bounds sample centres with one native cell of padding, but lines 674-680 request the surrounding level-dependent reduced cells. A source can contribute valid values to those cells while its extent lies outside this prefilter. Reproduction: import a 2x2, 1m EPSG:3857 source of valid sevens at the NW corner of XYZ tile 14/8192/8191, then render that tile through tiles::render_tile. Its four valid cells contribute to the first level-3 reduction cell, but the result is Empty. Diagnostic review_tile_keeps_source_inside_first_reduction_footprint fails. Control: disable only this candidate prefilter (pass None instead of tile_read_bounds); the same renderer/test passes. Restore was byte-verified afterwards. Fix by deriving candidate bounds from the actual native/reduced windows the renderer will read, retaining bounded filtering; do not remove filtering as the production fix. Add an ordinary tile regression including coverage near the tile edge.

2. P2 — Changing view during an edit leaves pending set forever. LidarLayersSection.tsx:95 increments requestGeneration on selection/openHistory, but runEdit's finally at 189-190 clears pending only if the old generation still matches. Reproduction: begin a deferred Move, open History before it settles, resolve Move successfully. Undo and other edit controls stay disabled despite loading completing and Undo being available. Diagnostic 'leaving an editing view does not leave all controls permanently pending' fails. Settle edit lifetime independently from view-response identity (with appropriate operation ownership), so navigation cannot orphan pending state. No new async subsystem.

3. P2 — Same-layer responses are not fenced against refresh/head changes. LidarLayersSection.tsx:108-147 captures a generation that increments only in select(); the library-refresh effect at 156-161 launches new reads with that same value. Reproduction: hold a collection read for gen-old, refresh the library, resolve the new read displaying new.tif, then resolve the old read. The panel replaces new.tif with old.tif. The same pattern applies to History and page appends; a shared loading boolean also finishes when only one of concurrent reads completes. Diagnostic 'a late same-layer read cannot replace the new head after refresh' fails. Give collection/history traversals their own current request/head identity and settle their own loading state; reject superseded results and mixed-head pages. Keep this within the existing component/store owner.

Remaining required evidence: the live workflow did not mount the map. Receipt lines 198-202 and screenshot 84-final-state show the provisional Design Location and explicit 'Set a Design Location to mount the map' prompt. Confirm Location in the isolated profile and observe rendered overlap changing after reorder/Undo/Restore, including generation replacement and a zoomed-out edge. The panel/catalogue pass is accepted as evidence at its actual boundary, not as the complete display pass. No requirement to run a new capacity campaign or migrate legacy libraries through a new UI route.

Independently checked:
- 14 existing native regressions pass (51.07s): public lock, v15 migration, first-batch CRS, all-NoData, reopened statistics, sparse extent, actual legacy head, superseded analysis, stale readiness, Undo/recompute, Undo exhaustion/equal-composition restore, region facts, intersecting member payloads and compatibility cancellation.
- 15 existing frontend tests pass across lidar-layer-priority and lidar-layer-collection; the two added deferred-response probes fail.
- New native tile probe fails on delivered production code and passes when only its candidate prefilter is disabled in the diagnostic copy. Delivered checkout untouched.
- check_docs.py: 0 errors. Full suites were not repeated; earlier totals remain delivery evidence.
- Read-only smoke database matches Import/Reorder/Remove/Undo to empty/Restore/Undo sequence; final result source identity equals current head and its job is complete. Inspected saved screenshots for exhausted Undo and final source list/provisional map state. Did not independently rerun the GUI.

Local diagnostic evidence: ui-review.log, tile-review.log, tile-control.log, native-controls.log and added probes in this archive. These scratch paths are convenient evidence, not required production fixtures. Carry the three reproductions into normal repository regressions. The primary user-owned desktop/src/native_operation.rs and .beads.gate.lock were not read or modified. No code fixes, integration or release performed.

Debrief: new tests cover the selected layer remaining unchanged during a pending edit but miss navigation and out-of-order same-layer refresh. Display tests exercise earlier chunk readers but do not detect the new ordered-member prefilter discarding reduction contributors. The smallest improvement is these concrete caller regressions and a mounted-map smoke, not more architecture or broad test-count targets. Also reconcile current receipt/guide text that still says the live workflow is unavailable or this delivery checkout contains no implementation.

title: Remove abandoned analysis staging left by failed or cancelled slope jobs
description: Inherited lifecycle gap confirmed during the GeoLibre integration review correction (R1). analysis.rs::run_slope_job creates prepared/analysis/<definition_id>/staging-<job_dir_id>/ (analysis.rs ~line 89) and then propagates errors with '?' from gdaldem, the quality-mask free-space check, grid::erode_mask_file, display::gdalinfo_json, result_statistics and the manifest write; none of those paths removes the staging directory. The settlement caller in mod.rs (the Err arm of the analysis job run, ~line 930) only updates lidar_analysis_jobs state to failed/cancelled. prune_transient_artifacts (mod.rs ~line 108) removes settled import job dirs and stale display dirs but never scans analysis staging-* directories, so the scratch survives until the definition or layer is deleted (delete_analysis/delete_layer do remove the whole analysis pipeline dir). The GeoLibre derivative itself is NOT part of this leak: PreparedRaster removes its own file on drop, including cancellation and failure. Dynamically observed once (temporary inspection test, not retained): with the capacity observation overridden so the statistics reader's combined budget fails after the slope step, run_slope_job returned the capacity error and left staging-anl-.../ containing result.tif and quality.bin; a pre-cancelled run left an empty staging-anl-.../ directory. Accepted results are unaffected: published generations live in gen-<generation_id> directories referenced by lidar_analysis_heads, and the previous head/result stays published. Scope: remove abandoned staging on failure/cancellation in the existing analysis settlement path (and/or bounded startup pruning), without changing publication, scientific results, capacity limits or the derivative ownership already delivered. Required future test: a failure/cancellation test through run_slope_job that asserts the staging directory is gone and the prior accepted result/head is intact.
acceptance_criteria: A failing or cancelled analysis job leaves no prepared/analysis/<definition_id>/staging-* directory; a regression test drives run_slope_job through at least one mid-pipeline failure and one cancellation and asserts cleanup plus an unchanged accepted head; normal publication behaviour and existing statistics/quality-mask tests stay green.
notes: Fixed on feature/bounded-raster-generations (commit pending). analysis.rs now owns each job's staging root through a StagingGuard: created before any output, removed on drop unless publication renamed it into gen-<generation_id> and disarmed the guard, so every early return, propagated error, cancellation and panic removes unpublished artifacts. The previous explicit stale-result removal is now the guard's job. mod.rs::prune_staging_roots runs at startup (from prune_transient_artifacts) and removes staging-* roots under prepared/layers/* and prepared/analysis/* left by a crash, never touching published gen-* directories, member assets or originals. Tests: failed_slope_job_removes_its_staging_root_and_keeps_the_accepted_head (capacity override fails the run after the slope step wrote its staged result; asserts the failure names the quality mask, the staging root is gone and the accepted layer head is unchanged), cancelled_slope_job_removes_its_staging_root (pre-cancelled run returns 'cancelled' with no staging root), and hermetic startup_pruning_removes_abandoned_staging_roots_only. Publication, scientific results, capacity limits and derivative ownership are unchanged; the full services::lidar suite with --include-ignored is 86 passed with only the external IGN fixture e2e unavailable, and fmt/clippy/check/workspace tests/docs are green.
close_reason: Abandoned analysis staging removed on every failure/cancellation path by an RAII staging guard, plus bounded startup pruning of staging-* roots left by a crash. Verified by failed_slope_job_removes_its_staging_root_and_keeps_the_accepted_head (mid-pipeline failure after the slope step, accepted head unchanged), cancelled_slope_job_removes_its_staging_root, and startup_pruning_removes_abandoned_staging_roots_only; full services::lidar suite with --include-ignored 86 passed (only the external IGN fixture e2e unavailable), Rust gates and docs validation green.

title: Exclude declared NoData from source range statistics without changing raster validity
description: Inspected at 71abad0f: import.rs raw_value_range filters non-finite values but includes finite declared NoData in source ranges. The compatibility-first G1-G5 migration deliberately preserves this output; correct it separately against the valid-only statistics contract and inspect preview/ramp consumers.

close_reason: Fixed and verified at 4ca49cc8. scan_source_facts spanned every finite sample, so a declared finite NoData sentinel entered the source value_range and dominated it. It now spans only samples the reader's validity flag marks valid, which is already exactly the contract rule (value.is_finite() && nodata.is_none_or(|nd| value != nd) in prepared_raster read_into), so the sentinel is excluded, valid zero and negative samples are kept, a source with no valid sample reports no range with the valid count as the discriminator, and a legitimate value is only NoData when the source actually declares it. Reproduction recorded, not assumed: the new regression test source_range_excludes_declared_nodata_and_keeps_zero_and_negative failed before the fix with left [-9999.0, 2.5] against right [-1.5, 2.5] and passes after, asserting both the declared and undeclared cases from one fixture converted through the production controlled-COG writer. Consumer check the bead asked for: value_range readers are the library presentation snapshot and AnalysisPanel's previous-result range display, both informational, so a correct range improves them and none depends on the sentinel. Existing semantics untouched -- values, masks, publication and presentation unchanged. Gates: services::lidar:: 114 passed / 75 ignored; cargo test --workspace green; cargo fmt and strict workspace Clippy clean.

5. The Whitebox WASI slope tool is rejected for edge interpolation and all-cells-valid output.

title: Decide sequential deepening of complete operations and lifecycle owners
description:
## Decision
Implement the five architecture recommendations in the user-approved sequence: atomic Design Notebook relocation, shared panel reorder lifetime, Workbench-owned Species Catalog refresh, shared canvas viewport presentation, and shared Design replacement retry ownership.

## Rationale
Concentrate complete operations and lifecycle policy behind existing domain seams. The user approved all five and sequential delivery on 2026-09-11. Keep each change independently testable and committed, retaining prior fixes in the delivered checkout.

## Alternatives Considered
- One large refactor: rejected because overlapping panels and authority changes make failures harder to localize.
- Broad Scene Edit, storage-engine, arrangement-placement or PDF rewrites: rejected because existing deep modules already hide meaningful complexity.
- Helpers that only shorten duplicate expressions: rejected because callers would retain the lifecycle and ordering obligations.
design: Notebook relocation accepts path, section and order, committing atomically through the existing UserData/SQLite adapter. Reorder lifetime owns pointer identity, listeners and stale completion while domain adapters retain geometry. Catalog view lifetimes own demand-driven refresh behind the Workbench. Renderer presentation owns retained snapshots and pan/zoom label projection. Replacement owns pending baseline freshness with its existing exact identity and finalizer; edition acquisition and dirty prompts remain outside. Local in-memory SQLite, DOM and controlled read/surface adapters provide tests; no new runtime dependencies or ADR reversals. Preserve existing regression coverage, add behavioral failure tests, and retain edition integration tests. The replacement decision canopi-acik remains authoritative and will be refined with the implementation. Implementation beads: canopi-xw7g, canopi-j067, canopi-s5o5, canopi-6kej, canopi-qhiq.
acceptance_criteria: Scope, seam ownership, rejected alternatives, dependency/test strategy, compatible ADRs and separate implementation beads are recorded.

title: PRD: Canvas PDF for sharing and field printing
description:
# PRD: Canvas PDF for sharing and field printing

## Problem Statement

People designing agroecological sites need to share their spatial Design and carry a readable printed plan into the field. A screen view depends on zoom, theme, and interactive identification, so exporting the current viewport is insufficient. A large site needs selected detail coverage at meaningful physical scales, while dense planting needs complete, readable Species identification without clutter or automatic changes to authored presentation. Users on Linux, macOS, Windows, and Web Edition need equivalent output.

## Solution

Offer one Canvas PDF workflow across all four platforms: choose printable Design Layers, work in a page-centred print workspace, and save or download a PDF containing an overview and optional numbered detail sheets for drawn temporary Print Areas. Use physical scale, readable page-specific plant legends, and white backgrounds. Export is derived output and never changes the Design.

The first release includes Design Layer selection and excludes every map background. Timeline, Budget, and Consortium PDF sections remain deferred. ADR 0024 is the accepted scope authority; the dated Canvas PDF research brief supplies evidence and candidate approaches without overriding approved defaults.

## User Stories

1. As a designer, I want to preview and export a Canvas PDF on Linux, macOS, Windows, or Web Edition, so that I can share the same plan regardless of my device.
2. As a designer, I want an overview that fits printable objects and selected detail-sheet coverage rather than my screen viewport, so that the printed plan includes the intended site context.
3. As a designer, I want to choose exportable Design Layers, initially matching their canvas visibility, so that I can control printed content without changing saved Layer visibility.
4. As a field worker, I want detail pages for drawn Print Areas with surrounding context, so that I can find nearby Plants and paths while working in one part of the site.
5. As a designer, I want to draw temporary rectangular Print Areas in the preview, so that I can print useful detail coverage without creating or changing Design Zones.
6. As a designer, I want A4 or US Letter and automatic fitting with an individual orientation override for every page, so that each requested area fits naturally on its own sheet.
7. As a field worker, I want an independent numeric canvas zoom for each page, with full-area Fit and a physical scale bar, so that I can adjust framing and measure actual-size prints.
8. As a field worker, I want each drawn Print Area fitted completely on one canvas page by default, with its coverage and final page number on the overview, so that creating detail pages never unexpectedly crops or splits my selection.
9. As a field worker, I want each plant-identification legend to describe the Species and authored appearances visible on its source canvas page, using a local Common Name or otherwise the full Canonical Name, so that I can identify what is shown without a code beside every Plant.
10. As a designer, I want my Plant Symbols, Plant Colors, Annotations, and Pinned Plant Names preserved in print, so that export does not reinterpret or modify the Design.
11. As a field worker, I want complete legends at a readable size, with continuation pages offered when needed, so that no Species disappears through truncation or unreadable shrinking.
12. As a designer, I want the preview to flag indistinguishable Species appearances without changing them or blocking an otherwise valid export, so that I can decide whether to return to the Design and edit it.
13. As a designer, I want print setup retained while I close the preview and edit the same Design, so that reopening shows current content with my choices intact.
14. As a field worker, I want white print backgrounds and dark legend and navigation text regardless of app theme, so that paper stays readable and uses less background ink.
15. As a multilingual user, I want local names and mixed-script text to print correctly across supported languages and platforms, so that a shared PDF does not lose names or glyphs.
16. As a designer, I want export cancellation, errors, and Design replacement handled without corrupting the Design or delivering stale output, so that printing remains a trustworthy operation.
17. As a designer, I want v1 PDF export to work independently of saved Location and interactive map availability, so that map providers cannot prevent me from printing my Design.
18. As a field worker, I want defaults validated on ordinary paper and printers, so that a PDF that looks acceptable on screen is also useful outside.

## Success Criteria

1. The same Design and print setup produce equivalent page geometry, printed content, naming, and preview/PDF results on Linux, macOS, Windows, and Web Edition. Saving or downloading delivers a usable PDF through the appropriate edition surface.
2. A new setup contains an overview only, no detail pages, and the currently visible exportable Design Layers. Independent Layer overrides change printed content, legends, and extent without changing saved visibility.
3. The default fitted overview includes printable objects on selected Layers plus every selected detail sheet's ground coverage. Excluded objects and interactive pan/zoom do not enlarge or determine its extent.
4. A single Add page action opens a fitted overview for drawing temporary rectangular Print Areas. No Zone picker or click-to-select Zone behavior remains. Adding and cancelling preserve the printed overview framing. Thumbnails and numbered overview outlines navigate detail pages. Print Areas use independent bounds; renaming, resizing or removing Zones only refreshes printable artwork. The drawing overview fits selected print content and existing detail coverage, excluding hidden Zone extents.
5. A4 and US Letter fit each newly selected area completely into one detail page at 100% canvas zoom with no manual displacement. Automatic orientation maximizes its fitted drawing scale beside the legend; exact squares choose portrait. Every canvas page has independent numeric zoom, and every page has its own orientation override.
6. Newly selected or drawn areas never crop or split automatically. Explicit canvas zoom or direct print-view movement may crop; lower zoom values show more surroundings. Dragging or arrow keys adjust only print framing. Fit resets both zoom and displacement. Text inspection temporarily magnifies the screen preview without changing PDF scale. The overview marks final page numbers and detail coverage. Canvas pages have calibrated scale bars and approximate ratios; legend-only continuations do not require one.
7. Detail sheets use a wide canvas column and a narrower readable legend covering the Species and appearances visible there, including the chosen zoom, framing and surrounding context. An overview-only export uses the same canvas/legend arrangement. When details exist, the overview provides navigation and Species legends belong to details and their continuations.
8. A legend entry shows one name: the selected-language Common Name when available, otherwise the full Canonical Name. Canonical Name remains Species identity even when Common Names coincide. Authored Annotations and Pinned Plant Names remain visible independently of interactive text fading.
9. Legend overflow offers clearly linked continuation pages through an explicit Add legend pages action, grouped below their source thumbnails. Unresolved overflow blocks export. Nothing is truncated or shrunk below the validated readable size. Continuations count in page totals and final references. Distinct Species sharing symbol and colour trigger a non-blocking notice across the entire source page's Species list, including continuation entries.
10. Authored Plant Colors and Plant Symbols are unchanged. Export adds no per-Plant species codes by default and performs no automatic appearance remapping. White page/canvas backgrounds and dark legend/navigation text are independent of app theme.
11. Print setup survives preview closure within the current Design Session, rebuilds from current Design content on reopening, refreshes an open workspace automatically with stale-result cancellation, and is discarded on Design closure or replacement. Setup and export do not change Design content, undo history, dirty state, save acknowledgement, or persistent settings.
12. No v1 print option, capture, or export request includes street maps, satellite imagery, contours, or hillshade. PDFs have the same Design output whether interactive maps are visible, unavailable, or absent; saved Location is not required.
13. Supported-language and mixed-script samples retain readable complete text without silent missing-glyph output. Cancellation, failed generation or delivery, repeated exports, and Design replacement have observable outcomes and do not publish stale success or leak resources.
14. Representative dense, mixed, large, and legend-heavy Designs have recorded automated/platform evidence and explicit user approval of the completed feature and current defaults. Preserve actual runtime versions and available measurements; do not invent printer settings or measurements not supplied with approval.

The workspace keeps paper and Layer choices compact and export visible with the total page count. Page controls sit beside the preview: Fit, minus/numeric zoom/plus and Automatic/Portrait/Landscape. Individual orientation changes retain zoom and manual framing. Removing a source page removes its continuations. Ordinary updates require no Refresh action.

## Implementation Decisions

- Shared browser-compatible layout and PDF generation serve all editions. Desktop and Web saving/downloading vary at compile-time platform adapter seams. The static Web bundle must not acquire a backend dependency or native imports.
- An export workflow module should own the user operation through a small interface: capture valid input, update temporary print setup, build/review the page plan, generate output, and deliver or cancel it. Internal modules may separate layout, identification, font handling, and encoding without exposing those concerns to every caller.
- Read settled canvas content and freshness through Canvas Runtime Surfaces, with required non-canvas metadata from the Design Session's read seam. Keep SceneStore and the document layer authoritative. A coherent export input is immutable for an admitted job and carries its Design Session and revision identity; it is not a second editable Design model.
- Keep PDF delivery distinct from Design persistence. Existing save acknowledgements and browser Design-download workflows must not be reused as though producing a PDF saved the editable Design. Any necessary native binary-save operation follows the Native Operation Executor policy.
- One physical page plan supplies preview and PDF content, transforms, extents, legends, continuation placement, and final navigation references. Resolve the selected font metrics before final pagination. Physical units must not depend on screen zoom, device pixel ratio, or bitmap metadata.
- Print setup belongs to the Design Session and outlives preview teardown; export jobs and preview resources have explicit lifecycle owners. Late work must not target a replaced Design. Reopening uses current content while retaining valid setup choices.
- Reuse established geometry and authored-appearance rules through runtime interfaces. Interactive viewport capture, screen-dependent text fading, hover labels, and transient editing controls are not an adequate print representation.
- New UI follows existing Preact, signals, i18n, and ochre/ink design conventions. All 11 supported UI languages remain in scope. Fixed print styling is separate from app theme and does not permit changing authored Plant presentation.
- No Design-format or persistent-settings change is implied. Introduce shared contracts or runtime dependencies only when justified by the implementation and the encoder/font evaluation.
- The retired structured Design Report and its Rust PDF renderer remain retired. Interactive Web maps remain an independent approved direction and are not prerequisites for Canvas PDF.

## Testing Decisions

- Test through caller-facing export and runtime interfaces. Assert rendered content, physical geometry, user-visible state, and delivery effects rather than implementation structure or strings mirroring code.
- Directly exercise physical layout and identification with deterministic Designs: automatic fit and individual zoom, both paper sizes/orientations, filtered bounds, complete area coverage, Species identity, duplicate Common Names, long names, final references, and refusal or acceptance of legend continuations.
- Verify the complete preview-to-PDF-to-delivery workflow in both edition compositions. Use an independent PDF renderer and text inspection to check output against the page plan; do not treat a preview screenshot as PDF evidence.
- Exercise clean and dirty Designs, retained setup, editing and reopening, cancellation, failed fonts/encoding/delivery, repeated exports, and Design replacement. Assert that Design content, dirty baselines, and persistence acknowledgements remain unchanged.
- Include all supported locale naming paths and mixed Latin, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean text. Check full Canonical Name fallback and text requiring a script different from the UI language.
- Assert that export initiates no map requests or map surface capture and remains usable with and without Location and with interactive map failures.
- Existing canvas query-surface fixtures, plant-presentation tests, Design Session persistence tests, command availability tests, Web build guardrails, and zoom-calibration scenes provide prior art. Screen-calibration fixtures need realistic repeated Species and denser spacing for print validation.
- The research brief proposes dense beds, mixed gardens, large sparse sites, legend stress, language stress, and map-exclusion samples. Compare candidate font/column/margin settings one variable at a time. Generate actual-size calibration output and record measurements before selecting defaults.
- Physical review uses ordinary colour and monochrome printers and intended field users, including outdoor reading. Verify representative output in the actual desktop WebViews and major Web browsers; one Chromium run does not establish parity. The sample settings, 1/10/50-page stress fixtures, and proposed measurement tolerances remain evaluation inputs until validated.
- Each delivery bead must apply repository quality gates for the surfaces it changes, including TypeScript and meaningful frontend coverage, Web packaging boundaries, native executor and Rust gates when native commands change, and generated-contract gates when relevant.

## Out of Scope

- Timeline, Budget, and Consortium PDF sections.
- Every map background, map provider selection, map acquisition or alignment, map attribution UI, and map-failure controls in v1 PDF. Preserve their research and agreed policies for later map work.
- Implementing interactive Web maps or Web Location editing as part of this epic.
- PNG, SVG, CSV, the former structured Design Report, server-side rendering, offline/PWA support, or changes to unrelated export permissions.
- Editing the Design through print setup; automatic colour/symbol substitutions, including PDF-only substitutions; automatic species codes beside Plants; both botanical and local names on every legend entry.
- Saving print setup in the Design or persistent settings; adding new arbitrary Design Layers.
- Automatically adding legend continuations, silently omitting Species, or shrinking text until it becomes unreadable.
- General canvas, catalog, or architecture cleanup beyond a delivery slice's actual requirements. Existing independent bugs stay in their current beads.

## Completion decision

The user reviewed and approved the completed PDF feature on 2026-09-10 and instructed closure of the remaining beads. canopi-h0q3 records acceptance of the current defaults and engineering limits. canopi-1zbj audits the delivered implementation and removes obsolete native snapshot-PDF code. The compact legend, drawing-only detail creation and spacing-aware readability changes are included.

The dated research and earlier test plans above explain the original approach. Current behavior and evidence are authoritative in ADR 0024, docs/agent/canvas-pdf.md and docs/canvas-pdf-validation.md. Approval supplies no undocumented printer measurements or packaged-app test results. Historical baseline evidence retains those limitations. The standalone native snapshot-PDF path is retired; shared byte delivery is the only app PDF path.

Preserve selected Layers, Zones, Print Areas, scales, and other print options while rebuilding the preview from the latest Design. Closing or replacing the Design discards the setup; the next Design starts with the agreed defaults. This is temporary session state, not .canopi content or persistent settings, and changing it does not mark the Design dirty. An export with no detail pages selected uses the same wide canvas and narrow legend columns and name policy as detail pages. All printable objects on selected print Layers fit the available canvas column; the legend covers the Species shown on that overview. When detail pages are included, the overview serves as a navigation page with numbered outlines showing the coverage of each detail sheet, labelled with that sheet's page number. Species legends belong to the detail sheets and any linked continuation pages. Users add detail pages by selecting Zones or drawing Print Areas in the export preview, which shows the resulting page count. Record the accepted overview of printable objects and selected detail-sheet coverage, numbered detail pages focused on user-selected Zones or temporary rectangular Print Areas drawn in the export preview, print Layer choices initially matching current visibility of exportable Design Layers and then independently adjustable in the export preview, a wide canvas column alongside a narrower plant-identification legend column on each detail page, limited to the Species shown there, A4/US Letter, six initial real-world detail-scale presets (1:20, 1:50, 1:100, 1:200, 1:500, 1:1000), a common export scale with individual overrides for Zones and Print Areas, and automatic portrait/landscape orientation minimizing page count with a manual override. Canonical Name remains Species identity. Legend text must remain readable, with exact column widths and typography awaiting print validation. The narrow legend column remains the normal layout. If its Species list cannot fit at a readable size, the preview offers clearly linked legend continuation pages only as an explicit user option. Continuations identify their source overview or detail page and count in the preview's total page count. Unresolved legend overflow blocks PDF export. If the user declines continuation pages, they must adjust the print setup until every legend fits completely at a readable size. Do not truncate the Species list or shrink text below a readable size to force it to fit. Continuation pages still require explicit user choice. An overview with only legend continuations keeps its plant-identification legend. Overview navigation and neighbouring-sheet references use the resulting page numbers. Scale bars apply to overview and detail pages showing canvas content. Neighbouring sheets covering the same Zone or Print Area overlap slightly by default, with neighbouring page references at their adjoining edges to support field navigation. This may increase the page count; the overlap size remains unresolved. Print Areas belong to the export setup and provide detail coverage without creating or modifying Zones, including in Designs without Zones. For each overview or detail page with a plant-identification legend, the export preview flags distinct Species in that page's canvas view that share identical Plant Symbols and Plant Colors, including Species whose legend entries continue on another page. The first Canvas PDF release omits all map backgrounds, including street basemaps, satellite imagery, contours, and hillshade, even when visible on the interactive canvas. Retain print selection for exportable Design Layers, initially matching visible Layers and independently adjustable without changing saved visibility. The PDF export path does not require a saved Location or map provider, fetch map assets, or mount/capture MapLibre. Map export is a release deferral, not a permanent exclusion. Provider selection, acquisition/alignment, and map-failure handling are not v1 prerequisites. Interactive Web maps remain separately approved under ADR 0013 and do not block Canvas PDF v1. Web Location editing remains deferred. title: Probe each canvas rendering context on a fresh canvas
description: Integrated zoom verification found that detectRendererCapabilities requests 2d, webgl, and webgl2 on the same HTMLCanvasElement (and the same OffscreenCanvas). Creating a 2d context fixes that canvas context mode, so subsequent WebGL probes return null even when a fresh canvas supports WebGL2. In software-WebGL Chrome, direct Pixi initialization succeeds, but the default RendererHost chooses Canvas2D. Fix context probing with independent canvases for incompatible context modes, including OffscreenCanvas. Add a browser-faithful regression where a canvas refuses a second context type, and verify initial backend choice and fallback. Root cause: desktop/web/src/canvas/runtime/renderers/capabilities.ts. This predates canopi-fido and is outside zoom sizing scope; zoom acceptance uses independently verified capability facts to exercise actual Pixi-to-Canvas2D failover.
design: Root cause confirmed before the fix in context-locking regression tests and headless Chrome with ANGLE SwiftShader: fresh WebGL2 succeeds, detection reports webgl/webgl2 false, and real RendererHost starts Canvas2D. Fix gives HTMLCanvasElement and OffscreenCanvas independent objects for incompatible context modes, retaining existing failure handling and capability contract. Tests cover both APIs, mixed support, absent/throwing APIs, and automatic host selection using production backend support predicates without injected capability facts. After fix, Chrome reports WebGL/WebGL2 for DOM and Offscreen-only environments, initializes actual Pixi, and performs actual Pixi-to-Canvas2D runtime fallback under an injected render failure with one canvas remaining. No physical GPU/native WebView verification claimed. Updated canvas-runtime guide with the context isolation invariant.

title: Deliver smooth scrolling and zoom gestures
description:
## Slice Summary
Deliver ordinary-scroll panning and proportional modified-wheel/pinch zoom through the canvas interaction and camera workflow.

## User Value
Mouse and trackpad navigation respond to gesture magnitude and preserve the point of interest without fixed zoom jumps.

## Out of Scope
Changing fixed zoom percentage semantics, text visibility, symbol sizes, precision limits, map projection, or adding unrelated navigation modes and preferences.

PRD: canopi-fido. User stories: 6, 8.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Deliver ordinary-scroll panning and proportional modified-wheel/pinch zoom through the canvas interaction and camera workflow.

**Current behavior:**
SceneInteractionSession prevents wheel defaults and applies a fixed zoom factor based only on deltaY sign, so ordinary trackpad scrolling zooms and small/zero gestures are not handled proportionally.

**Desired behavior:**
Consume calibrated input normalization and sensitivity. Ordinary wheel/two-finger scrolling pans on both axes; Ctrl/Cmd + wheel and browser-delivered trackpad pinch zoom around the pointer. Normalize supported delta units, handle zero motion as a no-op, keep scale finite and clamped, and preserve pointer anchoring. Route effective camera changes through the existing viewport update seam so map, rulers, measurements, rendering, and query readers remain synchronized. Retain the camera as the single authority; do not add map deadbands or a separate animated camera. Respect live interaction cancellation, tool drafts, overlays, event ownership, and session teardown/HMR cleanup. Verify intended canvas gestures do not accidentally trigger browser page zoom on tested hosts, record untested native/physical-device behavior accurately, and avoid device-type guessing to differentiate plain mouse and trackpad scrolling. Production frontend changes pass TypeScript checking, focused behavior-level Vitest coverage, and the full frontend suite. Update affected canvas guidance in the same change. Record exact unavailable checks and residual risk rather than weakening a gate.

**Key interfaces:**
- SceneInteractionSession event ownership and cancellation
- CameraController pan and pointer-anchored zoom
- Viewport invalidation and overlay refresh
- Canvas Map Surface camera synchronization

**Out of scope:**
Changing fixed zoom percentage semantics, text visibility, symbol sizes, precision limits, map projection, or adding unrelated navigation modes and preferences.

**Delivery context:**
Parent PRD: canopi-fido. Execution: AFK. Blocked by: calibration. Consume the verified outcomes of prerequisites rather than guessing unresolved defaults.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unmodified wheel/two-finger scroll pans using both axes; Ctrl/Cmd + wheel and supported pinch events zoom rather than pan.
- [ ] Gesture magnitude and supported delta units produce normalized proportional behavior using calibration defaults; zero movement is a no-op and all resulting scales remain finite and within existing limits.
- [ ] The world point under the cursor remains fixed during zoom, including near clamps; camera, map, rulers, and live measurement overlays agree after each effective update.
- [ ] Navigation respects ongoing tool/drag/cancellation semantics, does not leak listeners after disposal, and does not alter Design content, dirty state, or history.
- [ ] Browser testing records intended canvas gesture handling and simulated versus physical/native-host limitations; dense-scene responsiveness is compared with the calibration baseline.
- [ ] Focused interaction/camera/map regression coverage, TypeScript checking, and the full frontend suite pass; current navigation guidance replaces its pending wording.
close_reason: Delivered two-axis scroll panning and calibrated proportional Ctrl/Cmd-wheel/pinch zoom with unit normalization, pointer anchoring, bounded gestures, no-op/overflow protection, and editor/overlay event ownership. Focused 313 tests, TypeScript, all 2041 frontend tests, and whitespace checks passed. Real SceneCanvasRuntime in software-WebGL Chrome verified browser-generated wheel pan/zoom, one revision per input, unchanged browser page scale, and teardown. Physical-device/native-WebView feel remains explicitly unmeasured. Agent guidance and evidence updated.

title: Make zoom percentages consistent
description:

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Use the calibrated fixed absolute scale for the canvas zoom percentage across the camera and user-facing zoom controls.

**Current behavior:**
Camera initialization derives referenceScale from the initial viewport dimensions, and zoom controls divide actual scale by that reference. Resizing preserves the old reference, while reinitialization can choose a different one.

**Desired behavior:**

Retain the distance scale bar and existing physical scale semantics. A fixed 100% reference does not require every Design to open at 100%; preserve existing useful initial framing and auto-fit behavior. Keep the current absolute minimum and precision maximum, camera authority, and exact map synchronization. Verify at equal absolute scale across different initial window sizes; do not compare only two windows with the same inherited session reference. This slice includes observable control behavior and camera tests, not only a changed constant. Production frontend changes pass TypeScript checking, focused behavior-level Vitest coverage, and the full frontend suite. Update affected canvas guidance in the same change. Record exact unavailable checks and residual risk rather than weakening a gate.

title: PRD: Coherent Canvas Zoom And Text Visibility
description:
# PRD: Coherent Canvas Zoom And Text Visibility

## Problem Statement

When a designer zooms out, Annotations and Pinned Plant Names retain their screen size and remain visible, crowding the canvas. The zoom percentage depends on the initial window dimensions, so the same percentage does not consistently represent the same magnification. Wheel input applies one fixed zoom step per event and treats ordinary trackpad scrolling as zoom.

Text visibility must also be evaluated alongside Plant Symbols, Annotation markers, Zone boundaries, selection cues, handles, and measurement aids so the canvas remains visually coherent from a site overview to precision editing.

## Solution

Provide consistent, smooth canvas navigation and progressively simplify text presentation at overview scales. Annotations and Pinned Plant Names keep their readable text size, then fade out across one shared range of absolute canvas scales. Hidden Annotations retain subtle selectable markers. A single directly selected object's text, or an Annotation being edited, remains readable; selecting multiple objects does not reveal all their text.

Keep the zoom percentage with a fixed reference for 100%, alongside the distance scale bar. Ordinary scrolling pans. Ctrl/Cmd + wheel and trackpad pinch zoom in proportion to the gesture, preserving the canvas point under the pointer.

Begin delivery with an agent-led visual tuning pass across representative Designs. Compare text, symbols, markers, outlines, badges, handles, and measurements together, and retain or adjust presentation sizing only where the evidence supports the change. Physical geometry and distances continue to scale accurately with the camera. This pass produces recommended defaults and reproducible visual evidence before production values are finalized.

## User Stories

1. As a designer, I want Annotations and Pinned Plant Names to disappear smoothly when I zoom out, so that I can see the overall planting and spatial arrangement.
2. As a designer, I want hidden Annotations to leave subtle selectable markers, so that I can find and read notes without first zooming in.
3. As a designer, I want the text of one directly selected object, or an Annotation I am editing, to remain readable, so that zoom does not interrupt identification or editing.
4. As a designer, I want multiple selection to preserve the overview's reduced text density, so that selecting an arrangement does not cover it with names and notes.
5. As a designer, I want an equal zoom percentage to mean equal magnification across windows and Designs, so that the zoom indicator is predictable while the scale bar explains physical distance.
6. As a mouse or trackpad user, I want scrolling to pan and modified scrolling or pinching to zoom smoothly around my pointer, so that I can navigate without abrupt jumps or losing my point of interest.
7. As a designer, I want Plant Symbols, Annotation markers, outlines, badges, and editing handles to remain distinguishable across zoom levels, so that overview clarity and precise editing work together.
8. As a designer, I want visual simplification to preserve Design content, physical measurements, Layer visibility, and editing constraints, so that zooming changes presentation without changing my Design.

## Success Criteria

- A reproducible visual comparison covers a sparse garden, a dense planting, and a large site at overview, working, and precision scales. It records the selected zoom reference, fade range, navigation sensitivity, and the retained or adjusted presentation sizes with reasons and screenshots.
- Unselected Annotations and Pinned Plant Names fade through the same scale interval, reach fully hidden text at the overview threshold, and return on zoom-in without shrinking to unreadable text or flickering near the threshold.
- Hidden Annotation markers remain discoverable and selectable wherever existing visibility and editing policy permits. A single direct selection reveals the appropriate text without duplicate plant names; editing keeps Annotation text readable. Multiple and Object Group selection follow normal fading.
- Repeated navigation, fading, and selection do not change saved content, pinning choices, dirty state, or undo history. Hidden Layers and locked-object rules remain effective.
- Equal percentages produce equal canvas magnification independent of initial window size. The scale bar and measurements remain consistent with actual geometry, and existing precision zoom limits remain available.
- Ordinary scrolling pans; Ctrl/Cmd + wheel and pinch zoom proportionally around a stable pointer anchor. Zero movement produces no camera change, zoom limits remain effective, and small gestures do not become full fixed zoom steps.
- The visual comparison demonstrates readable selection and editing cues without disproportionate symbol, marker, badge, or handle growth. Physical Zone and Measurement Guide geometry stays correctly scaled, and existing measurement visibility rules remain intact.
- Pixi and Canvas2D agree on visible presentation and interaction geometry, including after viewport-only updates, resizing, and renderer fallback. Map alignment and Fit to content remain correct after the presentation changes.

## Implementation Decisions

- CameraController remains the authority for viewport transforms, scale limits, and transient viewport publication. Zoom controls project its scale consistently; the in-canvas map follows that camera through the existing map adapter.
- SceneInteractionSession continues to own navigation input and listener lifetime. Gesture normalization and camera updates must preserve existing interaction cancellation and teardown behavior.
- Renderer-independent scene presentation and geometry are the seams for zoom-dependent visibility, Visual Footprint, and Annotation layout. Pixi and Canvas2D consume consistent results rather than choosing independent thresholds or sizing rules.
- Rendering and interaction must agree on whether an Annotation presents text or a marker. Hit testing, selection outlines, group bounds, arrangement placement, and camera framing must use a coherent interpretation of that presentation.
- Plant Symbols remain symbolic position markers with a smooth absolute-scale Visual Footprint and a low-scale dot fallback. The current radius curve is the comparison baseline, not a preselected defect. Any recommended change must propagate through the existing shared footprint rather than alter glyph drawing alone.
- Physical Design geometry follows the camera scale; text, strokes, badges, handles, and other readability aids retain appropriate screen-space visual weight. Global coherence does not require every category to use an identical scaling curve.
- Selection-based text revelation applies only to one directly selected Placed Plant or Annotation, plus active Annotation editing. Pinned plants reveal their Pinned Plant Name; unpinned plants retain their existing Selection Label. No general automatic plant-name labeling is introduced.
