title: Browse Web Species from Parquet Manifest
description:
## Slice Summary
Create the first complete Web Species Catalog path backed by a generated Parquet manifest. A browser build can initialize the catalog reader, query browse results through DuckDB-WASM, and show visible retry behavior for manifest, initialization, or query failures.

## User Value
A Web Edition user can open the Plant Database and browse species without relying on an eager JavaScript full-catalog scan.

## Out of Scope
Localized search shards, backed filter UI, expanded Species data scope, full desktop Plant Detail, and website publication are separate slices.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Establish the first Web Species Catalog browse path backed by a generated Parquet manifest and DuckDB-WASM.

**Current behavior:**
The Web Edition catalog uses a reduced static catalog path that eagerly loads catalog data into JavaScript structures before browse and filtering. That keeps the current payload small, but it does not provide the storage/query path needed for reliable Web catalog performance as the artifact grows. Catalog asset or query failures can also be hard to distinguish from an empty catalog.

**Desired behavior:**
The Web Edition build produces a Cloudflare-safe catalog manifest that points at generated Parquet catalog assets for the current Web data scope. The browser catalog reader initializes DuckDB-WASM for the catalog reader lifetime, queries browse pages from the generated Parquet assets, and reports manifest, initialization, and query failures through visible Workbench error/retry behavior.

**Key interfaces:**
- Web catalog artifact manifest
- Web Species Catalog reader adapter
- Species Catalog read projection consumed by the Workbench
- Workbench loading, error, and retry states
- DuckDB-WASM catalog reader lifecycle

**Out of scope:**
- Locale-aware search shards
- Backed filter UI
- Expanded Species data scope
- Full desktop Plant Detail payload
- Website publication behavior
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The generated Web catalog manifest lists Parquet catalog assets with byte counts, checksums, and Cloudflare-safe limit metadata.
- [ ] The browser catalog reader initializes DuckDB-WASM for the catalog reader lifetime and uses it to fetch a browse page from Parquet assets.
- [ ] Browse results preserve the current Web Edition Species data scope and do not require exporting desktop-only fields.
- [ ] Manifest load, DuckDB initialization, and query failures surface as visible Workbench error/retry states rather than silent empty results.
- [ ] Focused tests cover manifest validation, adapter browse pagination, and error/retry behavior.
close_reason: Implemented the first Web Edition Species Catalog Parquet browse slice: generator emits Parquet-framed Species shards with manifest byte/hash metadata; DuckDB-WASM reader accepts Parquet manifests, registers catalog asset URLs, keeps DuckDB alive, and queries browse pages from read_parquet; Web catalog errors now show a retry action. Verified: python3 scripts/test_generate_web_catalog.py; cd desktop/web && npm test -- --run src/__tests__/duckdb-wasm-catalog.test.ts src/__tests__/web-species-catalog-panel.test.tsx src/__tests__/web-species-catalog-adapter.test.ts; cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit; cd desktop/web && npm test; cd desktop/web && npm run build:web; git diff --check.

title: Cloudflare-Safe Catalog Packaging Gates
description:
## Slice Summary
Add packaging checks that verify generated Web catalog assets, supported-filter metadata, checksums, per-asset byte limits, file-count limits, and the absence of raw bundled DuckDB WASM from the static artifact.

## User Value
A release engineer can build a Web Edition artifact that is safe to publish on Cloudflare Pages without moving catalog search or filtering into website infrastructure.

## Out of Scope
Deploying the website, adding Workers or Pages Functions, using R2/KV/D1, and changing the app hosting architecture are separate work.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** chore
**Summary:** Add packaging gates that prove the generated Web catalog artifact is safe for Cloudflare Pages.

**Current behavior:**
The Web Edition package flow does not yet enforce all catalog-specific artifact requirements for the Parquet migration: catalog asset presence, supported-filter metadata presence, checksums, conservative Cloudflare asset size and file-count limits, and absence of raw bundled DuckDB WASM.

**Desired behavior:**
The Web Edition packaging path validates the generated catalog artifact before it can be published. A release engineer gets a clear failure when catalog assets are missing, checksums do not match, supported-filter metadata is absent, asset sizes exceed the conservative limit, total file count exceeds the fallback limit, or raw DuckDB WASM is bundled into the static artifact.

**Key interfaces:**
- Web Edition package artifact manifest
- Catalog asset checksum and byte-count metadata
- Supported-filter metadata asset
- Cloudflare Pages asset and file-count guardrails
- Release/package quality gate output

**Out of scope:**
- Deploying the website
- Adding Workers, Pages Functions, R2, KV, or D1
- Self-hosting raw DuckDB WASM
- Changing website hosting architecture
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Packaging fails clearly when required catalog assets or supported-filter metadata are missing.
- [ ] Packaging validates manifest checksums and byte counts for generated catalog assets.
- [ ] Packaging enforces conservative Cloudflare-safe per-asset and file-count limits.
- [ ] Packaging rejects raw bundled DuckDB WASM unless a future explicit release decision changes that constraint.
- [ ] Focused tests cover missing assets, missing supported-filter metadata, checksum mismatch, oversize assets, excessive file count, and raw WASM detection.

title: Backed Web Filter Workbench UI
description:

The Web Edition Species Catalog exposes a small hardcoded filter surface that differs from the desktop Workbench shape. Unsupported desktop-only fields are a product risk if they appear as controls before the Web artifact actually contains backing data.

The generated Web catalog metadata declares which filter fields are backed by the current Web data scope. **Out of scope:**
- Exporting hardiness, height, stratum, edibility, risk, or other desktop-only Species attributes
- Showing unsupported controls as disabled
- Changing the current Web data scope
- Reworking unrelated Web Edition panel chrome
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Backed Web filters come from generated supported-filter metadata, not a hardcoded UI list.
- [ ] Search, backed strip filters, active chips, and More Filters behavior match the desktop Workbench rhythm where current Web data supports the fields.
- [ ] Unsupported desktop-only filters are absent rather than disabled.

title: PRD: Web Edition Species Catalog Parquet Query Adapter
description:
## Problem Statement

The Web Edition Species Catalog needs to feel like the real Canopi Species Catalog Workbench rather than a separate lightweight catalog widget, but its current browser implementation is constrained by a reduced static data payload and Cloudflare Pages hosting limits. The current Web catalog path hardcodes a small set of filter controls and loads catalog assets into JavaScript arrays before filtering, which creates two problems for users: the filter experience does not follow the desktop Workbench shape, and search/filter performance will not scale reliably as the browser catalog grows.

At the same time, the Web Edition must not expand its Species data scope in this slice. It should keep the current Web catalog data: climate zone, habit or growth form, life cycle, selected-locale Common Name/search data, and one hero image metadata row. Desktop-only Species attributes such as hardiness, height, stratum, edibility, and risk remain out of scope until a later explicit data-scope decision.

## Solution

Move the Web Edition Species Catalog onto a Cloudflare-safe Parquet and DuckDB-WASM query path while preserving the existing Web Edition data scope. The Web catalog generator will emit DuckDB-queryable Parquet shards, locale/search shards, image metadata, and generated supported-filter metadata. The Web catalog adapter will keep DuckDB-WASM alive as the query engine and query the generated catalog assets directly instead of eagerly loading all rows into JavaScript arrays.

From the user's perspective, the Web Edition Plant Database should show the desktop-style filter rhythm for backed fields: text search, always-visible backed strip filters, active chips, and More Filters only when backed fields exist. Unsupported desktop-only filters should not appear disabled; they should be absent until the Web catalog actually ships backing data. Web Edition Plant Detail remains reduced.

The website repository remains only a static artifact publisher. It should verify and serve the generated Web Edition artifact, including catalog and supported-filter metadata assets, but must not implement search, filtering, DuckDB integration, or catalog optimization itself.

## Success Criteria

- Web Edition Species Catalog search and backed filters run through DuckDB-WASM over generated Parquet catalog assets instead of JavaScript full-catalog scans.
- The generated Web catalog artifact includes catalog shards, locale/search assets, image metadata, and supported-filter metadata that all pass manifest checksum and Cloudflare-safe size/file-count validation.
- Web Edition shows only backed Species Catalog Filters and hides unsupported desktop-only filters.
- Web Edition preserves the current Web catalog data scope and reduced Plant Detail payload.
- Localized Common Name display and search continue to work for the supported UI languages.
- Catalog load and query failures produce visible Workbench error/retry behavior.
- Before/after performance evidence is recorded for browse, two-character active search, a backed strip filter, and locale switching.
- The Canopi website can publish the verified Web Edition artifact unchanged and serve catalog assets directly under the app route.

## User Stories

1. As a Web Edition designer, I want Species Catalog search and backed filters to respond quickly, so that I can choose Species without waiting on browser-side full-catalog scans.
2. As a Web Edition designer, I want the Plant Database filter area to follow the familiar desktop Workbench shape for backed fields, so that the browser app feels like the same Canopi workspace.
3. As a Web Edition designer, I want unsupported desktop-only filters hidden rather than disabled, so that I only see controls that can actually narrow results.
4. As a multilingual Web Edition user, I want Common Name display and search to use the selected app language, so that Web search matches desktop language behavior.
5. As a Web Edition designer, I want reduced Plant Detail to remain focused on current Web data, so that the browser catalog does not ship or imply unavailable desktop-only Species detail.
6. As a Web Edition designer, I want catalog load or query failures to produce visible error and retry behavior, so that missing assets do not look like an empty Species Catalog.
7. As a release engineer, I want generated catalog assets to stay below Cloudflare Pages size and file-count limits, so that the Web Edition can be published as a static artifact.
8. As a website implementer, I want the Canopi website to publish the verified Web Edition artifact unchanged, so that catalog behavior remains owned and testable in the Canopi app repository.
9. As a Canopi maintainer, I want backed Web filters to come from generated metadata, so that changing Web catalog data scope later does not require hardcoded UI edits.

## Implementation Decisions

- Treat the Web Edition Species Catalog storage engine as an adapter behind the existing Species Catalog Workbench and Species Catalog Read Projection seams.
- Generate Parquet shards as the primary Web catalog artifact. Expanded NDJSON may remain for fixtures or transitional tests, but it is not the browser performance path.
- Keep the current Web Edition data scope for this PRD: climate zone, habit or growth form, life cycle, selected-locale Common Name/search data, and one hero image metadata row.
- Do not export hardiness, height, stratum, edibility, risk, or other desktop-only Species attributes in this migration.
- Generate a Web-supported filter projection in catalog metadata or manifest assets. The Web UI and adapter consume this projection instead of hardcoding supported filters.
- Hide unsupported desktop Species Catalog Filters in Web Edition. Do not render them as disabled controls.
- Keep the shared Species search request shape stable unless a later bead explicitly changes the frontend/backend contract.
- Keep DuckDB-WASM alive as the Web catalog query engine for the catalog reader lifetime. Avoid the current load-everything-into-JavaScript pattern.
- Register or query catalog asset URLs through DuckDB and let queries fetch needed Parquet columns and row groups.
- Load or query locale-specific Common Name/search assets lazily for the active request locale. Do not eagerly fetch all 11 locale shards, all image metadata, or all Species rows on startup.
- Preserve the existing Species Catalog Search policy: empty text browses, one normalized character stays local/too-short, and active text search starts at two normalized characters with first-page exact counts omitted.
- Surface manifest, initialization, and query failures through Workbench error and retry behavior. Do not silently return an empty catalog or hide the Plant Database panel.
- Keep Web Edition Plant Detail reduced and separate from the desktop Plant Detail payload.
- Keep Web Edition source and catalog generation in the Canopi app repository. The Canopi website publishes the built artifact only.
- The website install flow must verify manifest checksums, per-asset byte limits, file-count limits, catalog asset presence, and supported-filter metadata asset presence.
- Keep the Web Edition static artifact within Cloudflare Pages constraints, with a conservative 25 MiB per-asset limit and 20,000-file fallback limit unless the app manifest records stricter values.
- Continue to load DuckDB-WASM through CDN-selected bundles rather than self-hosting raw DuckDB WASM files in the Web Edition artifact unless a later release explicitly changes that and still passes asset-size gates.

## Testing Decisions

- Test behavior through the generator, Web catalog adapter, Species Catalog Workbench, and Web panel seams rather than testing DuckDB internals or UI implementation details.
- Add generator tests that prove the manifest lists Parquet catalog assets, locale/search assets, supported-filter metadata, byte counts, checksums, and Cloudflare-safe size/file-count guardrails.
- Add adapter tests for manifest parsing, supported-filter projection, backed strip filtering, localized Common Name matching, pagination, favorite/recent hydration, reduced detail hydration, and query failure handling.
- Add Workbench or Web panel tests that verify unsupported filters are absent, backed filters are visible, active chips work for backed filters, and catalog errors surface with retry behavior.
- Add search-session or adapter coverage that preserves the short-query policy: empty browse, one normalized character local/too-short, two normalized characters active search.
- Add performance evidence before landing: record before/after timings for current Web catalog browse, two-character active search, a backed strip filter, and a locale switch.
- Add packaging tests that reject missing catalog metadata, missing supported-filter metadata, oversized assets, excessive file counts, raw bundled DuckDB WASM files, and browser chunks containing desktop-only runtime markers.
- Extend website integration smoke checks to verify catalog assets are served directly, not through the SPA fallback, and that Web Plant Database search/filter interactions work against the published artifact.

## Out of Scope

- Expanding the Web Edition Species data scope beyond current fields.
- Adding desktop-only dynamic filters that require hardiness, height, stratum, edibility, risk, soil, ecology, propagation, or extended taxonomy data.
- Recreating the full desktop Plant Detail payload in Web Edition.
- Reintroducing Site Adaptation, compatibility checks, or replacement suggestions.
- Moving desktop away from SQLite.
- Adding a backend, Pages Function, Worker search route, R2, KV, D1, or website-side generated index for Species Catalog behavior.
- Adding a service worker, PWA install prompt, app-managed precache, or offline-first catalog behavior.
- Importing Canopi app source into the website repository.
- Changing the Web Edition Location, Browser Drafts, Design Notebook, Problem Report, or export scope.

## Further Notes

- The current Web catalog generator and adapter still use a reduced NDJSON load path today; this PRD describes the target migration for future implementation beads.
- A later product/data-scope decision can expand the Web catalog to back more desktop Species Catalog Filters, but that should be sliced separately and rechecked against Cloudflare limits.
- The main implementation seam should stay deep: a small Workbench-shaped Web catalog adapter interface should hide DuckDB registration, Parquet query construction, manifest parsing, supported-filter projection, locale shard selection, and error mapping from UI callers.
- The Canopi website documentation has already been updated to preserve the artifact boundary and catalog asset verification expectations.
close_reason: Epic complete: Web Edition Species Catalog now uses generated Parquet-backed catalog assets with DuckDB-WASM query path, localized search, reduced detail/image hydration, generated supported-filter metadata, desktop-style backed filter UI, Cloudflare-safe package gates, NDJSON production retirement with performance evidence, and website artifact publish smoke. Closed after all child beads completed and verified.

title: PRD: Canopi coherence cleanup
description:
## Problem Statement

Canopi's current app and operating documentation have drifted in several places. Some documentation describes older shell chrome, older Web Edition routing assumptions, or superseded report/display behavior. The codebase also contains dormant or shallow surfaces that are not mounted by the current desktop app or Web Edition, including legacy chrome, a Learning stub, compatibility reexports, prototype-only UI, and a Site Adaptation slice that conflicts with the current Design Template import behavior.

This makes the project harder to reason about. Future agents and developers can waste time preserving code that no longer participates in the product, can follow stale docs, or can accidentally route new work through obsolete seams. The user wants the project to be coherent overall: the documentation should describe the app that actually ships, production code should map to active product surfaces or explicit decisions, and obsolete code should be removed when the issue is real.

## Solution

Deliver a coherence cleanup program that aligns Canopi's docs, app entries, domain language, and reachable code with the current product. High-confidence obsolete surfaces should be deleted with focused guardrails. Ambiguous surfaces should be resolved through an explicit decision bead before implementation.

The outcome should be a smaller and easier-to-navigate codebase where desktop and Web Edition boundaries remain clear, current Design workflows are documented accurately, shared contracts are regenerated when removed concepts disappear, and tests verify behavior at the app seams rather than preserving dead implementation details.

## Success Criteria

- Agent-facing docs describe the current mounted desktop app, current Web Edition shell, current panel composition, and current quality gates without stale app-entry names or contradictory Web Edition guidance.
- High-confidence obsolete frontend chrome and shallow compatibility modules are removed, and remaining boundary tests protect active app behavior rather than dead files.
- The Learning stub is removed across frontend, backend, shared contracts, translations, command registration, and generated bindings.
- Site Adaptation no longer remains dormant: it is either retired through a documented decision or intentionally integrated into the desktop Design Template import workflow with behavior-level tests.
- Web Edition still builds and tests against browser-safe boundaries, including no desktop-native chrome, native IPC, desktop document lifecycle, visible Location Workbench, Problem Report, Design Notebook, or native-style export flows.
- Superseded Design Report and plant display-mode language is corrected so the remaining PDF export path is clearly the canvas snapshot export.
- Prototype-only Saved Object Stamp entry points are removed or folded into the documented Saved Object Stamp workbench model.

## User Stories

1. As a Canopi maintainer, I want agent-facing documentation to match the current desktop and Web Edition app, so that future changes start from correct architecture assumptions.
2. As a Canopi maintainer, I want legacy shell chrome that is no longer mounted to be removed, so that developers do not mistake obsolete components for supported navigation.
3. As a Canopi maintainer, I want shallow compatibility modules to be deleted when their only behavior is pass-through reexporting, so that callers use the real module seam.
4. As a Canopi maintainer, I want the unmounted Learning stub removed end to end, so that the product does not carry abandoned content, commands, contracts, or translations.
5. As a Canopi maintainer, I want Site Adaptation to be either intentionally integrated or intentionally retired, so that Design Template import behavior is coherent and not split between dormant code and real workflows.
6. As a Canopi maintainer, I want Web Edition guidance and tests to agree on browser-safe shell seams, so that desktop-only command graph, IPC, native chrome, Location Workbench, Problem Report, Design Notebook, and export flows do not leak into the browser build.
7. As a Canopi maintainer, I want superseded report/display documentation and comments to be corrected, so that removed Design Report and plant display-mode concepts do not re-enter through stale language.
8. As a Canopi maintainer, I want prototype-only Saved Object Stamp surfaces resolved, so that personal reuse-library work is represented by the current Saved Object Stamp model instead of dev-only entry points.

## Implementation Decisions

- Use the domain language already defined by the project: Design, Design Session, Web Edition, Browser App Shell, Design Template, Site Adaptation, Compatibility Check, Replacement Suggestion, Species Catalog Workbench, Location Workbench, App Command Graph, Canvas Runtime Surface, Target Presentation, and Saved Object Stamp.
- Treat the mounted desktop app entry and Web Edition entry as the authority for reachability. Documentation should be corrected when it references old app-entry names, old chrome, or old panel composition.
- Preserve the split between desktop shell behavior and the Web Edition Browser App Shell. Browser behavior should continue to use browser-safe caller-shaped seams and compile-time adapters, not desktop-native IPC, native file chrome, or desktop-only command surfaces.
- Remove legacy activity/status chrome and its unused styling tokens once verified that current app entries do not mount them. Update source-boundary tests so they protect active architecture instead of naming removed files.
- Remove pass-through compatibility modules that provide no independent interface depth. Tests and callers should target the module that owns the real presentation behavior.
- Remove stale unmounted Location entry points when the current Location Workbench already owns desktop location behavior and Web Edition v1 intentionally omits visible Location editing.
- Remove the Learning stub end to end because it has no mounted user workflow, no current domain model term, and contains placeholder backend behavior. This includes frontend content, translation keys, backend command/service registration, shared contracts, and regenerated TypeScript bindings.
- Resolve Site Adaptation before editing its implementation. The default cleanup path is retirement because current Web Edition decisions omit Site Adaptation and current Design Template imports open templates as-is. If a decision keeps Site Adaptation, it must be intentionally mounted into the desktop Design Template import workflow as a real sibling Design workflow rather than left dormant.
- Keep the Species Catalog Workbench separate from Site Adaptation. Site Adaptation may consume Species Catalog read behavior, but it should not depend on Workbench UI state.
- Correct documentation drift around structured Design Report export and plant display modes. The remaining PDF behavior is the canvas snapshot export path; removed Design Report modules and general display-mode controls should remain out unless a new decision record reopens them.
- Resolve duplicate or confusing ADR history without losing the historical decision trail. Superseded decisions should stay clearly marked as superseded, and links should point at the accepted replacement decision.
- Resolve prototype-only Saved Object Stamp UI by deleting the dev-only route or folding any still-useful behavior into the real Saved Object Stamp workbench model. Do not rename the Favorites surface or conflate Saved Object Stamps with Design Templates or Species favorites.
- Use bd beads for delivery slices and decisions. Keep each implementation slice narrow enough to review, regenerate shared bindings in the same slice as contract removals, and update agent docs in the same slice as architecture changes.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should verify external behavior at app seams: what the desktop entry mounts, what the Web Edition entry can import, what commands or panels are available, and which contracts remain exposed. Avoid tests that preserve deleted files as implementation details.
- Documentation-only slices do not require runtime tests, but they should be reviewed against the current code and ADRs before completion.
- Frontend cleanup slices should run the TypeScript check and focused Vitest coverage for app shell, Web Edition boundaries, canvas workspace behavior, panel routing, and any source-boundary guardrails touched by the removal.
- Web Edition slices should keep the existing browser-boundary expectations: no desktop chrome, no native IPC, no desktop document lifecycle, no visible Location Workbench, no Problem Report, no Design Notebook, and no native-style exports beyond `.canopi` download/export.
- Shared contract removals should regenerate TypeScript bindings and verify that generated bindings are committed. Backend command/service removals should run Rust formatting, lint, workspace check, and relevant Rust tests.
- Site Adaptation cleanup should have a decision-backed test strategy. If retired, tests should prove the Design Template import workflow no longer references adaptation code and Web Edition still imports static templates as-is. If integrated, tests should cover the desktop import workflow's Compatibility Check and Replacement Suggestion behavior through the workflow seam.
- Learning removal should be verified across frontend, backend, shared contracts, and generated bindings so no registered command, exported type, translation namespace, or route points to the removed concept.

## Out of Scope

- Rebuilding Site Adaptation as a new user-facing feature without an explicit decision bead.
- Adding Web Edition Site Adaptation, compatibility fields, hardiness filters, replacement suggestions, or expanded reduced Species Catalog data.
- Reintroducing structured Design Report export, report-specific PDF rendering, or general plant display-mode controls.
- Adding a new Learning product surface or content strategy.
- Reworking the desktop shell or Web Edition shell for visual redesign beyond removing obsolete code and aligning docs.
- Replacing the current Species Catalog storage strategy or changing the Design file format except where shared contracts are intentionally removed.
- Changing Saved Object Stamp product scope beyond removing prototype-only entry points or aligning with the documented workbench model.

## Further Notes

The strongest ordering is: documentation drift first, high-confidence dead-code deletion second, shallow compatibility cleanup third, Learning removal fourth, Site Adaptation decision and cleanup fifth, and prototype debt last. Contract-removal slices should be isolated because they require regenerated bindings and Rust gates.

Site Adaptation is the only major item that should not be silently deleted as a mere reachability cleanup. The issue is real because dormant code and active Design Template import behavior disagree, but deletion versus integration is a product decision. The current ADR set supports removing or parking the dormant slice unless the product wants template hardiness review soon.

The audit report that motivated this PRD was generated at `/tmp/architecture-review-20260705-215604.html` and can be used as supporting context, but the bd epic should remain the durable source for delivery planning.
close_reason: Completed the coherence cleanup program: all child cleanup and decision beads are closed, final source-reachability scans found only intentional guardrail/retirement references, full frontend and Rust gates passed, and the requested session review found no new issues requiring follow-up beads.

title: Fix Web Edition website handoff preview command
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Follow the handoff's recommended website scripts, where `preview` runs `build:with-web` before starting Wrangler.
2. Follow the old local preview flow that first ran `CANOPI_WEB_EDITION_ARCHIVE=... npm run build:with-web`.
3. Run the old second command, `npm run preview`, without repeating `CANOPI_WEB_EDITION_ARCHIVE`.

## Expected
The handoff's local preview flow can be copied and run as written, with the Web Edition artifact path available to the command that performs the preview build.

## Actual
The old local preview flow dropped the artifact environment variable before invoking the recommended `preview` script, so the script would rebuild without the artifact path.

## Slice Summary
The Web Edition website integration handoff had conflicting local preview instructions: it first ran the artifact-backed build with `CANOPI_WEB_EDITION_ARCHIVE`, then told the agent to run `npm run preview` even though the recommended preview script rebuilds and needs the same artifact environment variable.

## User Value
A website coding agent can follow the handoff exactly and get a working local preview of both the marketing site and `/app/` without inferring missing environment setup.

## Out of Scope
Do not implement the website integration in `canopi-website`. Do not change Web Edition app packaging behavior.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Correct the Web Edition website integration handoff so the local preview command preserves the artifact environment variable.

**Current behavior:**
The handoff recommends a `preview` script that runs the artifact-backed build, then its local preview section first runs `CANOPI_WEB_EDITION_ARCHIVE=... npm run build:with-web` and then runs `npm run preview`. Because the recommended `preview` script also runs `build:with-web`, the second command would rebuild without the artifact path unless the user repeats the environment variable.

**Desired behavior:**
The handoff should show a local preview flow that can be copied and run as written. The artifact environment variable should be present on the command that invokes the recommended `preview` script, or the instructions should bypass the script's rebuild and invoke Wrangler directly after the artifact-backed build.

**Key interfaces:**
- Website `package.json` script contract for `build:with-web` and `preview`
- `CANOPI_WEB_EDITION_ARCHIVE` environment variable used by the proposed install script
- Web Edition artifact installed under `/app/`

**Out of scope:**
- Implementing the website script itself
- Changing Web Edition packaging
- Adding release download automation

title: PRD: Web Edition desktop chrome parity
description:
## Problem Statement

Canopi Web Edition now delivers the core browser workflows, but its chrome does not feel like the desktop app. Users who know Canopi Desktop expect the same workspace muscle memory in the browser, especially the top bar/menu area and the right-side panel navigation. The current Web Edition shell presents a browser-specific button strip and sidebar layout, which makes the Web Edition feel like a separate product even though it edits real Designs.

The problem is not missing Web Edition features. The current Web Edition feature scope should remain intact: browser-local Drafts, explicit `.canopi` import/download, canvas workspace, Location within web scope, optional static Design Templates, Species Catalog, and Favorites. The problem is that the visible Browser App Shell does not preserve desktop chrome structure, command placement, or right-side PanelBar behavior closely enough.

## Solution

Align the Web Edition Browser App Shell with the desktop workspace UX while keeping web-safe command availability. The Web Edition should use desktop-like top bar structure, menu/dropdown interaction, centered Design identity and dirty state, language/theme controls, and the desktop right-side PanelBar pattern. The command set remains the Web Edition command set; unavailable desktop features are omitted rather than shown as broken or misleading controls.

The target behavior is desktop chrome parity with web-safe commands. Users should recognize the same Canopi workspace structure in both desktop and browser, while the Web Edition remains honest about browser-local Drafts, explicit `.canopi` download/export, static hosting, and omitted desktop-only surfaces.

## Success Criteria

- A desktop Canopi user recognizes the Web Edition top bar and right-side panel navigation as the same workspace chrome pattern as desktop.
- The Web Edition top bar uses desktop-like menu/dropdown interaction for web-safe commands instead of a separate browser-only button strip.
- The Web Edition shows current Design identity and unsaved state in the top bar consistently with desktop presentation.
- The Web Edition right side uses the desktop PanelBar pattern with only web-safe panel entries.
- The Web Edition command set remains unchanged in scope and does not expose desktop-only or deferred v1 surfaces.
- Web Edition build-boundary checks continue to prove that native/Tauri imports and desktop-only command implementations are absent from browser chunks.
- Focused shell and navigation tests pass, and the packaged `/app/` artifact still builds successfully.

## User Stories

1. As a desktop Canopi user, I want the Web Edition top bar to look and behave like the desktop workspace top bar, so that I can use the browser version without relearning app navigation.
2. As a Web Edition user, I want browser-safe commands to appear in familiar desktop-style menu/dropdown groups, so that I can find New, Open `.canopi`, Download `.canopi`, Drafts, panel navigation, language, and theme controls where I expect them.
3. As a Web Edition user, I want the active Design name and unsaved state to appear in the top bar like the desktop app, so that I can tell what Design I am editing and whether browser changes need attention.
4. As a Web Edition user, I want the right-side panel navigation to match the desktop PanelBar, so that Canvas, Location, optional Templates, Species Catalog, and Favorites use the same navigation pattern as desktop.
5. As a Web Edition user, I want unavailable desktop-only commands to be absent, so that I am not offered save paths, file reveal actions, update/report flows, or planning surfaces that the browser app cannot support.
6. As a maintainer, I want the Web Edition shell to reuse or follow platform-neutral desktop chrome seams where possible, so that the web and desktop chrome stay visually consistent without importing Tauri/native behavior into the browser bundle.
7. As a maintainer, I want tests to guard both chrome parity and web-safety boundaries, so that future desktop shell changes do not silently break the Web Edition or leak native-only imports.

## Implementation Decisions

- The canonical product shape is still the Web Edition Browser App Shell. This PRD refines its visual and interaction target; it does not replace it with native desktop chrome.
- The Browser App Shell should match the desktop workspace chrome structure as closely as practical: desktop-style top bar, menu/dropdown interaction, centered Design identity, language/theme controls, and right-side PanelBar pattern.
- The Web Edition command set remains limited to current web scope: New, Open `.canopi`, Download `.canopi`, Browser Drafts, language/theme, Canvas, Location, optional static Design Templates, Species Catalog, and Favorites.
- Desktop-only commands should be omitted from the Web Edition shell rather than shown as disabled placeholders. This includes native save/save-as, direct save-back, Recent Design path menus, reveal-in-file-manager, updater, Problem Report, Design Notebook, Timeline, Budget, Consortium, broad exports, geocoding, Site Adaptation, Display by, and Color by.
- Web Edition menu/dropdown groups should mirror desktop command placement where the underlying command exists in web scope. For example, Design lifecycle commands should live in a desktop-like file/project menu group, while panel navigation should follow the desktop right-side PanelBar pattern.
- The right-side panel navigation should use the desktop PanelBar UX pattern with web-safe panel entries only. Side-panel content remains the reduced Web Edition content for Species Catalog and Favorites.
- The top bar should show Design identity and dirty state consistently with desktop. If a desktop interaction depends on a non-web Design Session capability that is not already part of Web Edition scope, the first implementation should avoid adding that feature and should preserve display parity instead.
- Browser Drafts remain distinct from the Design Notebook. They may be reachable from a desktop-like menu group, but they must not gain Notebook Sections, saved filesystem paths, file reveal actions, notebook ordering, or desktop Recent Design semantics.
- Web Edition shell code should route through the App Command Graph, Design Session actions, settings seams, browser file/storage adapters, and panel chrome projections. Generic chrome should not import browser storage APIs, Tauri IPC, native file APIs, or desktop-only command implementations directly.
- Platform differences should be represented through command projections, adapters, and availability rules rather than through a visually separate browser shell model.
- Source-boundary and build-boundary checks should continue to prevent Tauri/native imports and desktop-only command surfaces from entering Web Edition chunks.
- The PRD is inspired by GeoLibre's cross-platform shell approach: preserve one workspace UX across desktop and browser while adapting command behavior to platform capability. Canopi should apply that principle through existing Canopi seams and Web Edition constraints, not by copying GeoLibre's implementation.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should verify behavior through public shell and command surfaces, not by asserting private component implementation details.
- Browser App Shell tests should cover desktop-like top bar structure, menu/dropdown command availability, Design identity/dirty presentation, language/theme controls, and Browser Draft access.
- Panel navigation tests should verify that the Web Edition uses the right-side PanelBar pattern for web-safe panels and that opening/toggling side panels preserves the expected active panel behavior.
- Omitted-surface tests should verify that desktop-only commands and panels are absent from Web Edition chrome, including native save/save-as, direct save-back, Recent Design paths, reveal-in-file-manager, updater, Problem Report, Design Notebook, Timeline, Budget, Consortium, broad exports, geocoding, Site Adaptation, Display by, and Color by.
- Boundary tests should verify that any shared desktop chrome reuse does not import Tauri-only adapters, desktop IPC, native file paths, or desktop-only command implementations into the Web Edition bundle.
- Build/package checks should continue to run for the Web Edition static artifact so chrome changes do not break the `/app/` bundle, Cloudflare Pages asset constraints, or browser adapter selection.
- Visual/regression coverage should include at least one desktop-width browser rendering of the Web Edition shell with top bar, PanelBar, and side-panel content visible. If the existing test stack has screenshot coverage, use it for this shell parity surface.

## Out of Scope

- Adding new Web Edition product features beyond the current web scope.
- Reintroducing native window controls, native file management, direct save-back, desktop Recent Design paths, reveal-in-file-manager, updater flows, Problem Report, diagnostic bundle generation, or desktop export formats.
- Adding Design Notebook behavior to Web Edition.
- Adding Timeline, Budget, Consortium, broad exports, geocoding, Site Adaptation, Display by, Color by, offline/PWA behavior, accounts, backend persistence, sync, or cloud libraries.
- Changing the desktop app chrome as part of this PRD, except for extracting platform-neutral seams when that is the safest way to make Web Edition match desktop.
- Reopening the Web Edition static artifact, Cloudflare Pages, DuckDB-WASM catalog, or browser-local app data product decisions.

## Further Notes

- The highest-risk design issue is accidentally sharing too much desktop chrome and pulling native-only commands or Tauri imports into the web bundle. The useful seam is a web-safe command projection behind desktop-like chrome, not direct desktop shell reuse at any cost.
- The highest-risk UX issue is creating a near-match that still feels like a separate product. The top bar and right-side PanelBar should be treated as the first acceptance surface.
- Implementation should likely be sliced into separate work for command/menu projection, top bar/Design identity, PanelBar/right-side layout, omitted-surface hardening, and visual/package verification.
- Existing local worktree changes already touch Web Edition shell files; implementation slices should read and preserve that work rather than overwriting it.
close_reason: Delivered Web Edition desktop chrome parity: all child and review-follow-up beads are closed, Web Edition shell matches desktop-like top bar/menu and right PanelBar patterns within web-safe scope, and final verification passed npm test, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build:web, and npm run package:web with artifact dist-web-artifacts/canopi-web-edition-v0.9.1-585bf8e66c09.tar.gz.

title: Disable Web Edition download when no Design is loaded
description:

design:

title: Resolve Web Edition open command when file picker is cancelled
description:

title: Contain async recently viewed persistence failures
description:

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Workbench `selectSpecies`
- Web Edition reduced Species Catalog recently viewed persistence

**Out of scope:**
- New visible error UI for recently viewed writes
- Redesigning favorite or recents storage
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A focused Workbench test covers a rejecting async `onSpeciesSelected` callback.
- [ ] Species detail loading still starts when recents persistence fails.
- [ ] No new user-visible error surface is added for recents write failures.
close_reason: Contained async recently viewed persistence failures during Species selection while preserving detail loading. Tests: cd desktop/web && npx vitest run src/__tests__/web-species-catalog-adapter.test.ts; cd desktop/web && npm test; cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit; cd desktop/web && npm run build:web; cd desktop/web && npm run package:web.

title: Fix canvas runtime localized common-name hydration
description:
## Problem
The frontend full test suite currently fails in desktop canvas runtime localized Common Name tests. Running `cd desktop/web && npm test -- scene-runtime.test.ts` fails three tests around renderer snapshot localizedCommonNames, pinned plant labels after locale changes, and selected plant presentation contexts.

## Observed Failure
- `refreshes localized common names in renderer snapshots when the active locale changes` receives no cached Apple label.
- `keeps pinned plant name labels visible and localized in renderer snapshots` remains Apple after switching to fr instead of Pommier.
- `uses localized common names in selected plant presentation contexts` does not call `getCommonNames(['Malus domestica'], 'fr')`.

## Notes
The app-adapter path currently constructs SceneCanvasRuntime without a CanvasPlantLabelResolver, while the detached/default label source is no-op. Do not fix by importing desktop IPC into browser-safe canvas construction; preserve the Web Edition native-import boundary.
acceptance_criteria: `cd desktop/web && npm test -- scene-runtime.test.ts` passes without introducing IPC into the Web Edition bundle boundary checks.
close_reason: Fixed by routing runtime Species presentation sources through CanvasRuntimeAppAdapter.presentationData: desktop app adapters now provide the IPC-backed CanvasPlantLabelResolver and CanvasSpeciesCache, while shared runtime construction stays browser-safe and still accepts explicit test overrides. Verified with scene-runtime.test.ts, frontend-boundaries-sources.test.ts, full npm test, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run package:web, and git diff --check.

title: Integrate DuckDB-WASM Species Catalog Workbench
description:
## Slice Summary

## User Value
A designer can search and filter Species in the Web Edition with Canonical Name/Common Name text, climate zone, habit or growth form, life cycle, and localized Common Name display/search.

## Out of Scope
Do not add desktop-only detail fields, edibility, hardiness, height, stratum, Site Adaptation, or desktop DuckDB migration.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Integrate the DuckDB-WASM Species Catalog adapter with the shared Species Catalog Workbench.

**Current behavior:**
Species Catalog Workbench behavior currently reads through desktop storage and IPC-shaped adapters. Web Edition needs a browser-native read adapter over reduced DuckDB-WASM assets.

**Desired behavior:**
The Web Edition Species Catalog Workbench can browse, search, filter, paginate, favorite, and show recently viewed Species using the browser DuckDB-WASM read adapter. Search supports Canonical Name/Common Name text and selected-language Common Name display/search for all 11 UI languages. Filters are limited to climate zone, habit or growth form, and life cycle.

- Species Catalog Workbench

- Browser-local favorites and recently viewed app data
- Species search/filter request behavior

**Out of scope:**
- Edibility, hardiness, height, stratum, Site Adaptation, or replacement suggestions

acceptance_criteria:

close_reason: Implemented DuckDB-WASM-backed reduced Web Edition Species Catalog workbench, browser-local favorites/recently viewed, web-safe Species panels, and Cloudflare/Tauri artifact guards. Verified with focused Vitest suites, TypeScript, package:web, artifact scan, and git diff --check.

title: Add Browser Drafts and browser-local app data
description:

title: Package Web Edition static artifact for website handoff
description:
## Slice Summary
Produce a versioned static Web Edition artifact with the correct `/app/` base path, SPA fallback expectations, and Cloudflare Pages asset-limit checks.

## User Value
The website can publish Web Edition as static assets without importing app source or committing generated `/app` output long term.

## Out of Scope
Do not build feature-complete browser app behavior beyond what is needed to prove artifact handoff and guardrails.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** chore
**Summary:** Package the Web Edition as a versioned static artifact for website handoff.

**Current behavior:**
The accepted architecture says the Canopi app repository owns Web Edition source and the website publishes a built artifact under `/app/`, but the artifact packaging and handoff checks are not implemented.

**Desired behavior:**
The Web Edition build produces a versioned static artifact with a `/app/`-compatible base path, documented SPA fallback expectations, and automated Cloudflare Pages per-asset limit checks. The website handoff follows the selected artifact source decision and does not require importing Canopi app source or committing generated `/app` assets long term.

**Key interfaces:**
- Web Edition build artifact
- Website `/app/` route contract
- Cloudflare Pages asset-limit check
- Release artifact metadata

**Out of scope:**
- Feature-complete Web Edition behavior
- Changing the website into an app source consumer
- Adding service workers, PWA install, or offline-first cache behavior
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A command or workflow produces a versioned static Web Edition artifact.
- [ ] The artifact is built with a `/app/`-compatible base path.
- [ ] The expected website SPA fallback for `/app/*` is documented or implemented in the relevant handoff.
- [ ] Asset-size checks cover app chunks, workers, WASM, catalog shards, templates, and image-metadata assets.
- [ ] The handoff does not require committed generated `/app` assets in the website repository.
- [ ] No service worker, PWA install flow, or app-managed precache is introduced.
close_reason: Added npm run package:web to build the Web Edition at /app/, scan browser chunks, package a versioned artifact directory plus tar.gz, write manifest/checksums and SPA fallback metadata, enforce Cloudflare Pages asset/file limits, ignore generated outputs, and document the handoff. Verified with npm test -- web-edition-packaging.test.ts frontend-boundaries-sources.test.ts, npm run package:web, npm run build, and git diff --check.

title: Verify Web Edition v1 end-to-end release readiness
description:

title: PRD: Web Edition v1
description:
## Problem Statement

Canopi needs a lightweight Web Edition that users can open from the public website without installing the desktop app or relying on a backend. The website is hosted as a static Cloudflare Pages site, so the Web Edition must fit static asset limits, avoid server-side persistence, and not turn the website into an account-backed application.

The current desktop app already has the real Canopi Design model, canvas runtime, Species Catalog Workbench, Location and map flows, favorites, Saved Object Stamps, and `.canopi` save/load behavior. The problem is to make a browser-accessible Canopi experience that reuses those proven seams while removing desktop-only promises such as native windows, filesystem paths, native save dialogs, broad export surfaces, desktop user databases, and full bundled Species Catalog data.

## Solution

Build Web Edition v1 as a real Canopi app delivered as a static browser bundle under the website's `/app/` route. Users can create, open, edit, draft, and download real `.canopi` Designs in the browser. The Web Edition uses a Browser App Shell around the shared Canopi app core, browser-local Drafts and personal app data, a reduced DuckDB-WASM Species Catalog, and explicit `.canopi` download/export as the durable portable boundary.

The Canopi app repository owns the Web Edition source and build. The website publishes a versioned static artifact only; it does not import app modules or commit generated `/app` assets long term. The Web Edition remains compatible with Cloudflare Pages by keeping all app, worker, WASM, catalog, template, and image-metadata assets under the per-asset limit and by avoiding backend services, service workers, PWA install flows, and offline-first cache promises in v1.

## Success Criteria

- A user can launch Web Edition v1 from the static website, create a Design, edit the canvas, use the reduced Species Catalog, save a Browser Draft, reopen it in the same browser profile, and download a valid `.canopi` file.
- A user can open a `.canopi` file from desktop or another browser session, preserve unsupported loaded Design sections where possible, and download a valid `.canopi` file after web edits.
- The Web Edition bundle is served as static assets under `/app/` without a backend, accounts, sync, server-side persistence, service worker, PWA install flow, or app-managed offline cache.
- The website deployment consumes a versioned Web Edition build artifact and does not import Canopi app source or commit generated `/app` assets long term.
- The web build uses browser adapters selected at compile time and has automated checks that prevent Tauri/native adapters or desktop-only command surfaces from entering web chunks.
- All generated app, WASM, worker, catalog, template, and image-metadata assets stay within Cloudflare Pages per-asset limits.
- The reduced DuckDB-WASM Species Catalog supports the v1 filters, 11-language Common Name display/search, reduced Plant Detail, and lazy hero image metadata without bundling image binaries.
- Web Edition v1 clearly omits desktop-only and deferred surfaces: Design Notebook, native file management, direct save-back, broad export formats, Problem Report, geocoding, Site Adaptation, satellite/terrain/offline maps, Timeline, Budget, Consortium, Display by, and Color by.

## User Stories

1. As a website visitor, I want to launch Canopi in my browser, so that I can try real design workflows without installing the desktop app.
2. As a designer, I want to create a new Design in the Web Edition, so that I can start planning directly from the website.
3. As a designer, I want to open an existing `.canopi` Design in the browser, so that I can inspect or continue work created elsewhere.
4. As a designer, I want to download my current Design as a `.canopi` file, so that I own a durable portable artifact that can move to the desktop app.
5. As a designer, I want browser-local Drafts and autosave, so that I can resume recent browser work on the same device/profile without manually downloading after every edit.
6. As a designer, I want the Web Edition to make the difference between a browser draft and a downloaded `.canopi` file clear, so that I do not mistake convenience storage for durable cloud sync.
7. As a designer, I want to place plants, zones, annotations, measurement guides, groups, locks, Plant Colors, and Plant Symbols in the browser, so that the Web Edition feels like Canopi rather than a static catalog demo.
8. As a designer, I want the Species Catalog to support text search by Canonical Name and Common Name, plus climate zone, habit or growth form, and life cycle filters, so that I can find usable plants from the lightweight catalog.
9. As a multilingual user, I want Common Name display and search in the current 11 UI languages, so that the Web Edition works consistently with the existing localized app experience.
10. As a designer, I want a reduced Species detail view with a hero image when available, Canonical Name, Common Names, climate zone, habit or growth form, and life cycle, so that I get the essential planning information quickly.
11. As a designer, I want Species favorites, recently viewed Species, and Saved Object Stamps to persist in my browser, so that my web workspace remains useful across visits without an account.
12. As a designer, I want Location to work through manual latitude/longitude and map click or pin placement, so that I can set a site without relying on a geocoding backend.
13. As a designer, I want the Web Edition map to show a street basemap where network access is available, so that location context remains useful in the browser.
14. As a designer, I want static Design Templates to open as real Designs when bundled for web, so that I can start from examples without arbitrary remote downloads.
15. As a website maintainer, I want the website to publish a versioned Web Edition artifact, so that the website stays a static Astro/Cloudflare site and does not own app internals.
16. As a maintainer, I want the web build to fail when browser chunks import desktop-only adapters or exceed Cloudflare Pages asset limits, so that static deployment problems are caught before release.

## Implementation Decisions

- Web Edition v1 is a real Canopi app, not a static catalog, sketch format, iframe widget, or website-only demo.
- The Web Edition creates, opens, edits, drafts, and exports real `.canopi` Designs. Unsupported web UI sections must be omitted while preserving loaded Design data where possible and emitting valid empty sections for new web-created Designs.
- The Browser App Shell replaces the desktop title bar, desktop menu bar, native window controls, native file menu, native Recent Design path menus, reveal-in-file-manager actions, updater affordances, Problem Report entry points, native save/save-as flows, direct save-back, and desktop-style export commands.
- The Browser App Shell v1 command set is New, Open `.canopi`, Download `.canopi`, Drafts, language/theme, and panel toggles.
- Web Edition source stays in the Canopi app repository as a browser Vite entry/build that shares platform-neutral app modules with desktop. The website publishes the built artifact only.
- The website should not import Canopi app source as an Astro component package, workspace dependency, package import, submodule, or copied component tree.
- Generated `/app` assets should not be committed to the website repository long term. Deployment should copy or download a versioned Web Edition build artifact; local development may copy from a sibling checkout for preview only.
- Desktop and Web Edition entries select platform adapters at compile time. Shared modules must not use runtime `isWeb` or `isTauri` branches to choose IPC, browser storage, file, catalog, or shell behavior.
- Shared app modules should depend on small caller-shaped interfaces for Design Session persistence, settings, personal app data, Species Catalog reads, shell commands, and file import/export.
- CI or build checks should reject Web Edition chunks that import Tauri-only adapters, desktop IPC modules, native file path behavior, or desktop-only command surfaces.
- Web Edition build checks should fail when any generated app, WASM, worker, catalog, template, or image-metadata asset exceeds the Cloudflare Pages per-asset limit.
- Web Edition v1 uses DuckDB-WASM with generated reduced catalog assets from canopi-data export lineage. The reduced catalog is not hand-maintained in the website repository.
- The reduced catalog includes the v1 search/filter fields: Canonical Name/Common Name text search, climate zone, habit or growth form, and life cycle.
- The reduced catalog excludes edibility, hardiness, height, and stratum in v1. Web v1 Placed Plant presentation uses explicit design colors/symbols and generic fallbacks, not stratum metadata.
- Common Name display and search should support the current 11 UI languages with language-specific reduced/search shards and Canonical Name plus English fallback data where needed.
- Web Edition image support is metadata-only and lazy: at most one remote hero image per Species when available, with source/credit/license fields. It must not bundle image binaries, prefetch galleries, add a backend image proxy, or port the desktop native image cache.
- Plant detail in Web Edition v1 is reduced to hero image, Canonical Name, Common Names, climate zone, habit or growth form, and life cycle.
- Browser Drafts and autosave are the active browser save target. Explicit `.canopi` download/export remains the durable portable save path.
- The Drafts list is not the Design Notebook. It has no Notebook Sections, saved filesystem paths, file reveal actions, notebook ordering model, or notebook-style organization.
- Browser-local app data may include Design drafts and autosave state, Drafts list, settings, favorites, recently viewed Species, and Saved Object Stamps. It is convenience state that can be lost if site data is cleared or evicted.
- Web Edition v1 keeps Saved Object Stamps browser-local only and does not expose stamp import/export.
- Web Edition v1 exports `.canopi` only. PNG, SVG, PDF, CSV, report, diagnostic bundle, native-style exports, and Saved Object Stamp import/export are out of scope.
- Web Edition v1 omits Problem Report, Diagnostic Bundle generation, native report-folder creation, and folder reveal behavior.
- Web Edition v1 omits address search/geocoding. Location remains editable through manual latitude/longitude entry and map click or pin placement.
- Web Edition v1 keeps street basemap behavior only. It omits satellite basemaps, terrain contours, hillshade, offline tile download, service-worker tile precache, and offline map promises.
- Web Edition v1 may keep the Community/Design Template world map only for templates shipped as known static `.canopi` assets. If no static template set is prepared, the template map should be hidden.
- Static web templates import as Designs without Site Adaptation review, compatibility checks, or replacement suggestions.
- Web Edition v1 is not offline-first. It should not add service workers, PWA install prompts, offline-first caches, or app-managed precache behavior.
- The deepest module seams to preserve are Design Session, Canvas Runtime Surface, Canvas Runtime App Adapter, App Command Graph, Species Catalog Workbench, Species Catalog Read Projection, Design Edit, MapLibre Host, MapLibre Surface Adapter, Location Workbench, Canvas Layer Presentation, settings projection, and browser/desktop platform adapters.
- Delivery should be sliced so the static build/adapter boundary lands before the full catalog and app-data work. The reduced DuckDB-WASM catalog and browser document persistence are independent prerequisites for a useful Web Edition but can be validated separately.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should verify behavior through the same seams production callers use, not by reaching around module interfaces or asserting implementation details.
- Add build-boundary tests that prove the Web Edition bundle imports browser adapters only and does not include Tauri-only imports, desktop IPC modules, native file-path behavior, or desktop-only command surfaces.
- Add artifact-size checks for Web Edition build outputs, DuckDB-WASM worker/WASM files, reduced catalog shards, static templates, and image-metadata assets against Cloudflare Pages per-asset limits.
- Add Design Session adapter tests for browser create/open/edit/draft/download flows using the normal Design Session lifecycle and save-composition seams.
- Add `.canopi` round-trip tests proving Web-created Designs are valid, loaded unsupported sections are preserved where possible, and new web-created Designs emit valid empty unsupported sections.
- Add Browser Draft tests that cover autosave, reopening a draft, distinguishing browser-local draft state from downloaded `.canopi`, and avoiding Design Notebook semantics.
- Add browser-local app-data adapter tests for settings, favorites, recently viewed Species, and Saved Object Stamps, including storage unavailable or eviction-like failure handling where practical.
- Add Species Catalog read adapter tests for the reduced DuckDB-WASM catalog: browse/search, Canonical Name/Common Name matching, locale-specific Common Name display/search, v1 filters, pagination/cursors, and reduced Plant Detail hydration.
- Add catalog generator tests that prove the generated assets contain only approved v1 fields, exclude hardiness/height/stratum/edibility, include image metadata shape, and produce deterministic asset names with size checks.
- Add Plant Detail UI tests for missing/failed remote hero images, attribution/source display, and hiding desktop-only detail sections.
- Add Browser App Shell tests for visible command set, absence of desktop/native commands, and correct routing through command/document/settings seams.
- Add Location and map tests for manual coordinates, map click/pin placement, street-basemap-only scope, geocoding absence, and graceful behavior when map resources fail.
- Add static Design Template tests for known static asset import through normal Design Session template-open flow and hiding the template map when no static template set is configured.
- Add boundary tests comparable to the existing frontend boundary/source tests, command registry tests, document session tests, MapLibre Host tests, Species Catalog search/session tests, settings projection tests, and file-format round-trip tests.

## Out of Scope

- Backend services, accounts, sync, cloud libraries, server-side persistence, or any requirement that turns the website into an account-backed app.
- Importing Canopi app source into the website repository or committing generated `/app` assets to the website repository long term.
- Direct save-back to an originally imported file.
- Desktop title bar, desktop menu bar, native window controls, native File menu, desktop Recent Design path menus, saved path references, reveal-in-file-manager actions, native save/save-as flows, and desktop updater/reporting affordances.
- Design Notebook, Notebook Sections, notebook-style Design organization, and desktop Recent Design behavior in the Web Edition.
- Timeline, Budget, Consortium, Display by, Color by, Design Report PDF export, and native-style export surfaces in Web Edition v1.
- PNG, SVG, PDF, CSV, report, diagnostic bundle, Saved Object Stamp import/export, or other browser export formats beyond `.canopi`.
- Problem Report, Diagnostic Bundle generation, native report-folder creation, and folder reveal behavior.
- Address search/geocoding.
- Site Adaptation, compatibility checks, replacement suggestions, and reduced-catalog fields needed only for those workflows.
- Edibility, hardiness, height, and stratum fields or filters in the Web Edition v1 catalog.
- Satellite basemaps, terrain contours, hillshade, offline tile download, offline maps, service-worker tile precache, and offline map/image promises.
- Bundled image binaries, image galleries, backend image proxying, and desktop native image caching in the Web Edition.
- Desktop migration from SQLite to DuckDB-WASM. Desktop storage migration requires separate measured evidence.
- Service worker, PWA install flow, offline-first cache, or app-managed precache strategy in v1.

## Further Notes

- Major delivery slices likely include: static web build and artifact handoff; compile-time adapter seams and boundary checks; Browser App Shell; browser file/draft/settings/app-data adapters; reduced DuckDB-WASM catalog generator and adapter; reduced Plant Detail with hero image metadata; canvas/design workflow pruning for web; Location/map web scope; optional static Design Templates; and CI/deployment checks.
- Cloudflare Pages compatibility is a hard constraint. Current documented limit is 25 MiB per single asset, and the generated build should keep file count conservative.
- Web Edition v1 should tolerate network failures for map tiles and remote Species hero images without implying offline support.
- The reduced catalog measurements from the grill session suggest the v1 data shape is feasible when compressed/sharded: core reduced Species fields were roughly 6.8 MiB gzipped, all 11-language Common Names roughly 8.4 MiB gzipped, and first-image-per-species metadata roughly 4.6 MiB gzipped. Implementation should remeasure using the actual generator output.
- The website deployment handoff still needs an exact implementation plan: whether it downloads an artifact from CI/release storage or copies from a local sibling checkout for preview. The PRD decision is artifact handoff, not the final release automation mechanism.
- Later enhancements such as geocoding, offline/PWA behavior, additional export formats, Site Adaptation, satellite/terrain maps, stamp import/export, or desktop DuckDB migration require separate product/architecture decisions.
close_reason: All 13 Web Edition v1 child beads are complete. Final release verification passed for the targeted web suite, static package artifact, adapter boundary checks, and Cloudflare Pages asset/file constraints; follow-up canopi-t1ma tracks the unrelated canvas runtime localized-label test failure found during full frontend-suite verification.

title: Deduplicate prefix Common Name relevance rows
description:
## Slice Summary
Fix Species Catalog Search so selected-language Common Name prefix relevance joins cannot emit duplicate Species rows when one Species has multiple matching tokens for the same query prefix.

## User Value
Users see each Species once in active relevance search results, and pagination does not skip or underfill pages because duplicate rows consumed result slots.

## Out of Scope
Do not change the selected-language-only search policy, add fuzzy matching, or change the user-facing ranking tiers beyond preserving the existing first-token-position ordering without duplicates.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Prevent duplicate Species rows during selected-language Common Name prefix relevance search.

**Current behavior:**
Active Species Catalog Search relevance joins selected-language Common Name tokens by query prefix. If one Species has multiple token rows in the selected language that match the same prefix, the list query can emit that Species more than once before LIMIT/OFFSET pagination is applied.

**Desired behavior:**
Each Species appears at most once in active relevance search results. Prefix token ranking should still use the best first token position for each query token, and pagination should continue to operate on unique Species rows.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Search list query planning
- selected-language Common Name token relevance joins
- active text search pagination

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the selected-language-only Common Name search policy
- Adding fuzzy typo tolerance
- Reworking the public search request contract
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A Species with multiple selected-language token rows matching the same query prefix appears only once in search results.
- [ ] Prefix relevance still orders by the earliest matching token position for each query token.
- [ ] Active text search pagination works over unique Species rows.
- [ ] Regression tests cover duplicate-token prefix behavior.
close_reason: Implemented grouped selected-language Common Name token relevance joins so prefix searches return each Species once; covered by focused regression, query-builder tests, workspace tests, bundled relevance examples, and latency harness.

title: Suppress detail English Common Name fallback
description:
## Slice Summary
Fix Species detail hydration so a non-English selected language with no localized Common Name does not fall back to the English storage Common Name.

## User Value
Detail pages stay coherent with list, favorites, and recently viewed surfaces: untranslated Species show Canonical Name rather than an unexplained English Common Name.

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Keep Species detail Common Name display selected-language-only.

**Current behavior:**
List-style Species Catalog surfaces no longer fall back to English Common Names in non-English locales, but Species detail hydration can still use the storage Common Name when the selected language has no localized Common Name.

**Desired behavior:**
Species detail should return no Common Name for a non-English locale when the selected language has no Common Name, letting callers display Canonical Name consistently with list, favorites, and recently viewed rows. English locale behavior may continue to use the English storage Common Name fallback.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog detail read projection
- Common Name lookup service
- Species detail caller contract

**Out of scope:**
- Hiding untranslated Species
- Adding machine-translated or synthetic Common Names
- Changing English-locale detail behavior
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A non-English Species detail request with no selected-language Common Name returns no Common Name instead of the English storage Common Name.
- [ ] English Species detail requests still return the available English Common Name.
- [ ] List-style selected-language Common Name behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the detail fallback behavior.
close_reason: Removed detail English storage Common Name fallback for non-English locales while preserving English locale behavior; covered by focused detail regression, species catalog read tests, workspace tests, and review grep.

title: Explain alternate Common Name search matches
description:
## Slice Summary
Expose and render a selected-language Matched Common Name when an active Species Catalog Search result matched an alternate Common Name that is not already displayed.

## User Value
Rows such as Clochette d'Irlande can explain why they appeared for mélisse by showing the matched alternate name without making every result row show extra names.

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Show a selected-language Matched Common Name when it explains an active search result.

**Current behavior:**
Rows can appear because of an alternate Common Name that is not displayed, making results feel strange. The existing secondary Common Name display is not explicitly query-aware.

**Desired behavior:**
Search results may include an optional Matched Common Name that explains why the row matched the active query. The UI should show it coherently as secondary/explanatory text only when it is useful and selected-language-local. Browse rows should remain compact and should not permanently show three Common Names.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species list item shared contract
- Species Catalog Search result projection
- Species Catalog row/card rendering
- Locale-aware result display tests

**Out of scope:**
