acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Search results can carry an optional selected-language Matched Common Name distinct from the displayed Common Name.
- [ ] When a row matched an alternate selected-language Common Name, the Species Catalog row/card displays that matched name as search explanation.
- [ ] Browse mode and non-search lists do not show extra matched-name explanations.
- [ ] The UI does not show duplicate names when the matched name is already the displayed Common Name or existing secondary name.
- [ ] Shared type bindings and frontend/backend tests are updated for the new result contract.
close_reason: Added matched_common_name to SpeciesListItem, populated it from selected-language alternate Common Names only when the displayed name does not already explain the active search, and rendered it coherently in list/card results while browse/favorites stay compact. Verified with backend and frontend regressions plus generated bindings and full gates.

title: Rank displayed Common Name prefixes first
description:
## Slice Summary
Improve relevance ordering so exact and prefix matches on the displayed selected-language Common Name outrank weaker Common Name, alternate-name, and broader text matches.

## User Value
Searches such as apple/appl in English and mélisse/melis in French return the species users expect at the top of the list.

## Out of Scope
Do not introduce fuzzy typo tolerance or substring-first behavior for incomplete tokens.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Rank exact and prefix matches on displayed selected-language Common Names ahead of weaker matches.

**Current behavior:**
Common Name token matches can tie many rows together, so BM25 may rank longer or hidden-name matches above the expected displayed Common Name result. Incomplete prefixes such as appl and melis do not receive the same Common Name priority as full tokens.

**Desired behavior:**
Relevance ordering should prioritize selected-language displayed Common Names before weaker matches. Exact displayed Common Name matches rank first. Displayed Common Names whose tokens start with the query tokens rank before displayed names containing the query later. Alternate selected-language Common Name matches rank below displayed-name matches. Broader BM25 matches for Canonical Name, taxonomy, uses, or other text follow after Common Name tiers.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog relevance ordering
- Common Name token normalization and prefix matching
- Species list projection for displayed Common Name
- Active text search pagination

**Out of scope:**
- Substring-first ranking inside tokens
- Typo correction or fuzzy search
- Ranking English Common Names in non-English locales
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] English apple and appl searches rank Malus domestica first.
- [ ] French mélisse and melis searches rank the displayed Mélisse result first and rank Mélisse alpine / Mélisse des champs ahead of weaker or hidden-name matches.
- [ ] Violette à feuilles de mélisse ranks below displayed names starting with Mélisse but above broader non-Common-Name matches.
- [ ] Alternate-name matches such as Clochette d'Irlande via Mélisse des Moluques do not outrank displayed-name matches.
- [ ] Backend regression tests assert the ordered examples and prefix behavior.
close_reason: Implemented selected-language Common Name relevance tiers with exact/displayed prefix/displayed contains/alternate match ordering, prefix token matching, and short-name tie breaking. Added apple/appl and melis/melisse regression coverage and verified against the bundled DB ordering harness plus full gates.

title: Verify bundled DB asset supports selected-language search
description:
## Slice Summary
Validate whether the existing bundled Species Catalog database asset supports the new selected-language relevance behavior without regeneration, and document any required asset work if it does not.

## User Value
Release preparation has a clear answer on whether the next release is code-only or requires regenerating and uploading the plant database asset.

## Out of Scope
Do not regenerate or upload a new database asset unless verification proves it is necessary and the release workflow is explicitly invoked.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** chore
**Summary:** Verify whether the current bundled Species Catalog DB asset supports the selected-language search implementation.

**Current behavior:**
The planned search behavior appears likely to be implementable with existing Common Name and token tables, but release risk remains unless this is checked against the bundled database and representative latency.

**Desired behavior:**
After the selected-language matching and ranking changes land, verify the bundled database asset has the tables and indexes needed for correctness and acceptable first-page latency. Record whether the next release can ship code-only or whether a database asset regeneration/upload is required.

**Key interfaces:**
- Bundled Species Catalog database schema version
- Common Name token indexes and selected-language query plans
- Species Catalog latency harness or equivalent release-facing validation
- Build/release agent guidance

**Out of scope:**
- Regenerating, uploading, or promoting a new database asset unless verification proves it is necessary and release work explicitly requests it
- Changing product search behavior
- Broad canopi-data import changes
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The bundled database schema/tables/indexes are checked against the selected-language search implementation.
- [ ] Representative searches such as apple, appl, mélisse, and melis are verified against the bundled database.
- [ ] First-page latency is measured or otherwise bounded using the repo's Species Catalog latency harness or an equivalent documented method.
- [ ] The bead records a clear release answer: code-only is sufficient, or a regenerated database asset is required.
- [ ] Agent/release docs are updated if the asset requirement or validation command changes.
close_reason: Verified the existing bundled canopi-core.db supports the selected-language search implementation without regeneration: the manual relevance harness shows Malus domestica first for apple/appl and French melisse/melis ordering as expected, including Moluccella matched_name; the latency harness ran against desktop/resources/canopi-core.db. Release answer: code-only is sufficient; no DB asset reupload required.

title: Restrict Common Name search to selected language
description:
## Slice Summary
Make Species Catalog Search match Common Names only in the selected app language while preserving language-neutral Canonical Name and botanical taxonomy search.

## User Value

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Restrict Species Catalog Common Name matching to the selected app language.

**Current behavior:**
Species Catalog Search can match against Common Names aggregated across languages or fall back to English Common Names for relevance. This can make non-English searches surface rows for language reasons users cannot see.

**Desired behavior:**
Common Name matching uses only Common Names in the selected app language. Canonical Name, genus, family, and other language-neutral botanical fields remain searchable. Non-English searches should not match a Species solely because of an English Common Name.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Search request contract
- Species Catalog Read Projection list/count planning
- Common Name token normalization and selected-language matching
- Search pagination and first-page/next-page behavior

**Out of scope:**
- Typo tolerance or fuzzy edit-distance search
- Removing Canonical Name or taxonomy search
- Database asset regeneration unless a follow-up verification bead proves it is needed
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] In French, an English-only Common Name does not cause a Species to match a Common Name search.
- [ ] Canonical Name, genus, and family searches still work regardless of selected UI language.
- [ ] Count and list queries use coherent selected-language search predicates.
- [ ] Pagination remains stable for active text search results.
- [ ] Regression tests cover selected-language-only matching and absence of English Common Name fallback matching.
close_reason: Restricted Common Name search predicates and relevance joins to the selected language while keeping Canonical Name, genus, family, and other FTS fields language-neutral. Verified selected-language-only and no-English-fallback regressions plus full frontend/Rust gates.

title: Use selected-language Common Names only
description:

title: Remove Species Catalog sort controls
description:

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Remove user-facing Species Catalog sort controls while keeping deterministic browse and relevance search behavior.

The Species Catalog has internal support for multiple sort modes, and stale UI/test surfaces still model explicit sort selection. Active text search can be overridden away from relevance.

**Desired behavior:**
The Species Catalog Workbench should not expose sort controls. Empty browse requests use deterministic Canonical Name ordering. Active text searches always request relevance ordering. Existing backend sort variants may remain for compatibility, but the user-facing workflow should not offer them.

close_reason: Removed the Species Catalog sort selector and set browse to Canonical Name order while active text search always requests relevance. Verified with focused Vitest, full npm test, TypeScript, Rust query/search tests, cargo fmt/check/clippy, cargo test --workspace, and git diff --check.

design:

title: Align Measurement Guide labels using drafting convention
description:
## Slice Summary
Make Measurement Guide distance values follow architectural drafting dimension conventions: centered on the guide, aligned with the guide direction, upright for readability, and spaced cleanly away from the dashed dimension line.

## User Value
A designer placing Measurement Guides at any angle can read the distance immediately without awkward horizontal labels, visual crowding, or inconsistent spacing between interactive canvas and print/export renderers.

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Render Measurement Guide distance labels using drafting-style aligned dimension placement.

**Current behavior:**
Measurement Guide distance values are always horizontal and positioned near the midpoint with a small fixed perpendicular offset. At angled guide orientations this does not match drafting conventions and the text can feel visually crowded against the guide.

**Desired behavior:**
Measurement Guide distance values should behave like architectural drafting dimension text. The value is centered on the Measurement Guide, aligned parallel to the guide direction, flipped when necessary so it remains upright/readable, and offset from the dashed line by a consistent screen-space clearance that accounts for label height. The same placement model should drive interactive canvas rendering and print/export rendering paths so Measurement Guides look coherent across renderers.

**Key interfaces:**
- Measurement Guide presentation model
- Canvas renderer Measurement Guide drawing
- Print/export Measurement Guide drawing path
- Renderer geometry and visual regression tests for Measurement Guides

**Out of scope:**
- Label collision avoidance between multiple Measurement Guides
- User-configurable label orientation or spacing
- Changes to Measurement Guide endpoint marks, dash style, layer behavior, selection behavior, or persistence
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Measurement Guide distance labels are centered at the guide midpoint and rotate parallel to the guide direction.
- [ ] Labels are flipped as needed so text is never upside down for ordinary left-to-right reading.
- [ ] Label spacing uses a stable screen-space clearance from the dashed guide line after accounting for label height, instead of crowding the line with a small center offset.
- [ ] Pixi and Canvas2D Measurement Guide renderers consume the same placement model and produce matching orientation/spacing behavior.
- [ ] Print/export canvas output uses the same aligned label convention as the interactive canvas.
- [ ] Focused tests cover horizontal, vertical, diagonal, and reversed-angle Measurement Guides, including upright flipping and spacing invariants.
- [ ] Existing Measurement Guide creation, selection, endpoint editing, layer visibility, and persistence behavior remain unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented drafting-style Measurement Guide labels: shared presentation now centers labels at the guide midpoint, rotates them parallel to the guide, flips reversed angles upright, and spaces labels by font height plus clearance; Canvas2D and Pixi renderers both consume that placement. Verified with npm test -- --run src/canvas/runtime/measurement-guides.test.ts src/__tests__/canvas2d-scene.test.ts src/__tests__/pixi-scene.test.ts, npm test, and npx tsc --noEmit.

Creating a Measurement Guide by dragging adds the guide to the scene, but any previous canvas selection can remain active. Follow-up delete or toolbar actions may still target the stale selected object, and the newly created guide is not immediately ready for Select-tool endpoint editing.

**Desired behavior:**
When a Measurement Guide creation drag commits a real guide, the new guide becomes the active Design Object selection. If the drag is too small, blocked by Layer state, or otherwise produces no guide, selection should not change.

**Key interfaces:**
- Measurement Guide creation tool and Scene Edit transaction boundary
- Scene selection model for Design Objects
- Selection Action Toolbar and Measurement Guide endpoint-control presentation
- Undo/redo and dirty-state behavior for creation edits

**Out of scope:**
- Adding new Measurement Guide editing gestures
- Changing Measurement Guide persistence or layer semantics
- Changing selection behavior for other creation tools unless required for consistency tests
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Creating a Measurement Guide by drag selects the newly created guide after commit.
- [ ] If another object was selected before the drag, that stale selection is replaced only when a guide is actually created.
- [ ] No-op or blocked Measurement Guide creation attempts do not clear or replace selection.
- [ ] Delete and Selection Action Toolbar behavior after creation targets the new guide.
- [ ] Focused tests cover creation over an existing selection and the no-op/blocked creation path.
close_reason: Fixed Measurement Guide creation selection: created guides become the active selection only when a valid guide is committed; no-op and blocked attempts preserve the existing selection. Verified with npm test -- --run src/canvas/runtime/scene-runtime.test.ts -t 'Measurement Guide', npm test -- --run src/canvas/runtime/scene-runtime.test.ts, and npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Add artifact-based PDF visual checks for Design Report polish
description:
## Slice Summary
Add representative artifact-based regression checks for Design Report output so frame, scale, table, Unicode, page-density, and language invariants are protected across supported operating systems and computers.

## User Value
Future report changes are less likely to regress printing, localization, or layout polish on another platform.

## Out of Scope
Do not replace focused unit tests with full-page golden snapshots or require absolute paths to local user downloads.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** chore
**Summary:** Add durable Design Report PDF output checks for cross-platform, multilingual polish.

**Current behavior:**
Several report regressions were only found by inspecting a generated artifact: broken frame border, tiny canvas content, pipe-delimited Timeline text, sparse pages, awkward Consortium wrapping, and prior mojibake risk.

**Desired behavior:**
The test suite should include representative artifact-style checks that protect Design Report layout, Unicode text, all-locale labels, and page-density invariants across supported operating systems and computers without relying on brittle full-page golden snapshots or absolute local paths.

**Key interfaces:**
- Design Report export service and test fixtures.
- PDF text extraction or structured PDF inspection.
- PDF rasterization or bounded pixel/geometry checks where visual invariants are required.
- Locale coverage for supported UI languages.

**Out of scope:**
- Replacing all focused report unit tests.
- Requiring `/home/daylon/Downloads` fixtures or user-specific paths.
- Introducing broad new runtime dependencies unless justified by CI-portable report testing needs.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Tests inspect or rasterize generated PDFs using tooling available in normal CI or a clearly documented CI subset.
- [ ] Checks cover first-page border continuity, white background, canvas content fill, and absence of excessive empty margins.
- [ ] Checks cover absence of pipe-delimited Timeline or Consortium table text.
- [ ] Checks cover absence of mojibake, replacement characters, raw translation keys, raw UUIDs, and raw hex color text in user-visible report sections.
- [ ] Checks cover page-density invariants so representative sparse sections do not create mostly blank generated pages.
- [ ] Coverage includes all supported UI locales or combines all-locale frontend input coverage with backend Unicode/render invariants and documents the rationale.
- [ ] The representative fixture is checked into the test suite or generated deterministically, without relying on absolute paths in a user's Downloads directory.
- [ ] Failure messages identify the broken invariant and report page or section.
close_reason: Added deterministic PDF artifact regression checks for Design Report polish: parsed PDF page density, first-page frame/image geometry, white-background no full-page paint, section text, pipe-dump absence, mojibake/raw-key/raw-color leaks, and page-specific failure messages. Tests: CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo test -p canopi-desktop services::design_report::tests::renderer_preserves_representative_pdf_artifact_invariants_without_snapshots -- --nocapture; CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo test -p canopi-desktop services::design_report::tests::renderer_ -- --nocapture; cargo fmt --all -- --check; CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo check --workspace; CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo test --workspace.

title: Polish sparse Budget report pages

design:

acceptance_criteria:

title: Add cross-platform all-locale Design Report regression coverage
description:
## Slice Summary
Add regression coverage for representative Design Reports across all supported UI locales and platform-independent rendering invariants.

## User Value
Future report changes catch mojibake, missing glyphs, clipped text, blank pages, missing sections, and non-deterministic report resources before release.

## Out of Scope
Building a visual design-review approval workflow or adding screenshot baselines that cannot run reliably in CI.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** chore
**Summary:** Add cross-platform-oriented regression coverage for representative Design Reports across all supported UI languages.

**Current behavior:**
Existing report tests do not fully exercise the real failure modes seen in a dense multilingual Design Report: mojibake, missing glyphs, unreadable first-page canvas output, raw implementation values, sparse planning rows, and dense section pagination.

**Desired behavior:**
The test suite should include representative report fixtures and assertions that are portable in CI and meaningful across Linux, macOS, and Windows. Coverage should run through all supported UI languages and detect text corruption, missing report sections, internal-value leaks, blank pages, non-white first-page background, and layout regressions that can be checked deterministically.

**Key interfaces:**
- Design Report read model generation
- Shared Rust Design Report renderer
- Locale resources for all supported UI languages
- Representative dense Design fixture
- Portable PDF validation helpers

**Out of scope:**
- Pixel-perfect visual snapshot approval
- Manual human review workflow
- OS-specific renderer implementations
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A representative dense Design Report fixture exercises metadata, canvas image, legends, Timeline, Budget, Consortium, visible Layers, hidden Layers, and sparse planning data.
- [ ] Regression coverage runs against every supported UI language.
- [ ] Tests detect mojibake, missing glyphs, internal IDs/keys in user-facing output, blank pages, missing sections, and page-number failures.
- [ ] Tests verify first-page white-background behavior and absence of app chrome using deterministic assertions suitable for CI.
- [ ] Tests avoid brittle pixel-perfect snapshots unless they are stable across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
- [ ] The coverage runs in normal project gates or is clearly documented if a narrower CI-compatible subset is required.
close_reason: Added representative all-locale Design Report input coverage and backend PDF invariant coverage for nonblank pages, page numbers, embedded first-page canvas image, section presence, Unicode/mojibake checks, internal-value leaks, and non-snapshot chart/table rendering. description:

## User Value

## Out of Scope
Core report command creation and planning-section report layouts.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Include persistent canvas aids and legends in Design Report canvas output.

**Current behavior:**

- Adding export-time layer or legend override controls.
- Timeline, Budget, and Consortium sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Design Report canvas output includes visible Pinned Plant Names.
- [ ] Design Report canvas output includes visible Measurement Guides with distance labels.
- [ ] The report includes the pinned-name legend under the same conditions as the canvas.
- [ ] The report uses the Color by legend instead of the pinned-name legend when Color by is active.
- [ ] Legend and plant-name text uses the active app locale at export time.
- [ ] Focused tests cover pinned labels, Measurement Guides, legend selection rules, locale snapshot behavior, and visible-layer interaction.
close_reason: Shipped Design Report canvas aids: localized pinned plant labels, visible Measurement Guides with distance labels, pinned-name legend selection, Color by legend precedence, locale snapshot behavior, and visible-layer filtering. title: Add Consortium section to Design Report
description:
## Slice Summary
Render Consortium information in the Design Report only when the user has changed entries from auto-created defaults, using a chart and complete table.

## User Value
A designer can print meaningful Consortium planning without noisy untouched defaults.

## Out of Scope
Timeline, Budget, Consortium editing changes, and changing auto-sync behavior.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Add a print-native Consortium section to Design Reports.

**Current behavior:**
Consortium entries are auto-created for active species without marking the Design dirty. Untouched defaults should not make a report section appear.

**Desired behavior:**
The Design Report includes a Consortium section only when at least one active Consortium Entry differs from the default auto-created state. When included, the section shows the complete current active Consortium: a readable chart by Stratum and Succession Phase plus a complete table of active entries. The table includes localized plant name, canonical name where helpful, Stratum, start Succession Phase, end Succession Phase, and count where available. Labels use the active app locale. Untouched auto-created defaults do not count as user input, but once the section is included, all active entries are represented.

**Key interfaces:**
- Consortium Entry contract and Consortium Time Model.
- Consortium auto-sync defaults.
- Planning Projection for active entries, localized names, species colors, Strata, and Succession Phases.
- Design Report chart/table layout and pagination.

**Out of scope:**
- Changing Consortium editing or auto-sync behavior.
- Budget and Timeline report sections.
- Adding user-managed Consortium lanes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The Consortium section is omitted when all active entries are untouched auto-created defaults.
- [ ] The Consortium section appears when at least one active entry differs from the default state.
- [ ] When included, the section represents all active Consortium Entries, not only changed entries.
- [ ] The section includes a readable chart by Stratum and Succession Phase.
- [ ] The section includes a complete table with localized name, canonical name where helpful, Stratum, start/end phases, and counts where available.
- [ ] Labels use the active app locale.
- [ ] Focused tests cover default omission, changed-entry inclusion, complete active-entry coverage, chart/table data, and localization.
close_reason: Implemented Consortium Design Report section with default omission, complete active-entry chart/table payload, localized labels, PDF pagination, and focused frontend/Rust tests. title: Polish complete Design Report output
description:

## User Value

Adding new report sections or changing the already-approved feature scope.
design:

**Category:** task

design:

title: Export Design Report foundation
description:
## Slice Summary
Add the File menu Design Report PDF export path with a fitted canvas page, metadata, white page/background, visible layers respected, and current in-memory Design Session state.

## User Value
A designer can export a printable Design Report even when there are unsaved edits, without losing visible canvas information.

## Out of Scope
Timeline, Budget, Consortium, pinned-name legend, and Measurement Guide report refinements.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Add the foundational File menu Design Report PDF export.

**Current behavior:**
The app has file actions and a platform-shaped canvas PDF export path, but there is no user-facing Design Report export that uses current Design Session state and structured report output.

**Desired behavior:**
The File menu exposes an Export Design Report PDF action. Export uses the current in-memory Design Session, including unsaved edits, and does not mutate or mark the Design clean. The initial report includes a fitted canvas page and compact metadata: Design name always, plus description and location when present. The first page orientation adapts to the fitted design bounds. The canvas page forces the page/background to white, suppresses UI chrome such as rulers, grid, editing handles, selections, hover states, and toolbars, and respects visible design and map layers. The report has section headings and quiet page numbers.

**Key interfaces:**
- App Command Graph and File menu.
- Design Session current-state composition.
- Structured Design Report read model.
- Chosen cross-platform PDF renderer boundary.
- Canvas export snapshot or print-render surface.

**Out of scope:**
- Timeline, Budget, and Consortium report sections.
- Pinned-name legend and Measurement Guide-specific report refinements.
- Export-time layer override controls.
- Saving the Design before export.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The File menu exposes an Export Design Report PDF action only when a Design can be exported.
- [ ] Export uses current in-memory Design Session state, including unsaved edits, without clearing dirty state.
- [ ] The report includes Design name and includes description/location only when present.
- [ ] The canvas page is fitted to the whole visible Design and chooses portrait or landscape based on design bounds.
- [ ] The canvas page has a white page/background, suppresses UI chrome, and respects visible design/map layers.
- [ ] The report includes section headings and page numbers.
- [ ] Focused tests cover command availability, current-state export input, metadata omission, orientation choice, visible-layer behavior, and dirty-state preservation.
close_reason: Shipped File menu Design Report PDF export using current Design Session state, structured report input, printpdf renderer, white fitted canvas page, visible-layer handling, metadata omission, headings/page numbers, and focused frontend/Rust coverage. title: Add Timeline section to Design Report
description:

design:

acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] The section includes a compact overview chart grouped by action type.
- [ ] The section includes a complete table with every Timeline Action.
- [ ] Description, target, recurrence, dependency, and status text wraps without clipping.
- [ ] Date and action-type labels use the active app locale.
- [ ] Repeated table headers and page breaks preserve readability.

title: Edit and operate on Measurement Guides
description:
## Slice Summary
Make Measurement Guides behave as practical design objects for editing, layer visibility, locking, duplicate, and copy/paste.

## User Value
A designer can adjust and reuse Measurement Guides after creation while keeping them out of planning targets and stamp workflows.

## Out of Scope
Grouping, Object Stamp, Saved Object Stamp, Timeline targets, Budget targets, and Consortium participation.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Make Measurement Guides editable and reusable as ordinary measuring aids.

**Current behavior:**
After the creation slice, Measurement Guides can be created and saved, but advanced post-creation operations are not yet complete.

**Desired behavior:**
Users can select a visible editable Measurement Guide, move the whole guide, drag either endpoint, delete it, duplicate it, and copy/paste it. Endpoint drags update the distance label live using snapped preview geometry when snapping is enabled. Layer visibility and locking block selection and mutation consistently with other design objects. Measurement Guides do not show a rotation handle in this slice because endpoint dragging provides the needed orientation control. They do not participate in Object Groups, Object Stamp, Saved Object Stamps, Timeline targets, Budget targets, or Consortium planning.

**Key interfaces:**
- Canvas selection and hit testing for design objects.
- Scene edit transactions, history, and mutation eligibility.
- Endpoint handle overlay and measurement-label rendering.
- Clipboard, duplicate, delete, and layer-lock behavior.

**Out of scope:**
- Grouping, stamping, saved stamp thumbnails, or planning targets for Measurement Guides.
- Design Report export.
- Adding rotation-handle support.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Users can select, move, delete, duplicate, and copy/paste Measurement Guides.
- [ ] Users can drag either endpoint, and the distance label updates live during the drag.
- [ ] Endpoint and move edits are undoable, abort cleanly, and avoid history entries for no-op gestures.
- [ ] Measurement Guide selection and mutation respect layer visibility, layer lock, and direct lock rules.
- [ ] Measurement Guides do not appear in Object Group, Object Stamp, Saved Object Stamp, Timeline, Budget, or Consortium workflows.
- [ ] Focused tests cover hit testing, move, endpoint drag, duplicate, copy/paste, deletion, locks, and out-of-scope workflow exclusion.
close_reason: Implemented Measurement Guide editing: select, move, endpoint drag with live labels, duplicate, copy/paste, delete, direct/layer lock handling, renderer selection/hover projection, and exclusion from grouping/object stamp/saved stamp affordances. Verified with npm test, npx tsc --noEmit, focused runtime/interaction/renderer/saved-stamp suites, and git diff --check.

title: Pin placed plant names on canvas
description:
## Slice Summary
Let users pin selected placed plant names so those names stay visible on the canvas and in saved designs.

## User Value
A designer can make important placed plant names persistently readable without turning them into Annotations or Design Object Locks.

## Out of Scope
Pinned-name legend behavior, Design Report export, and Measurement Guides.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Add Pinned Plant Names for selected placed plants.

**Current behavior:**
Plant names can appear transiently through selection or hover presentation, but there is no persisted per-placed-plant presentation state that keeps names visible.

**Desired behavior:**
Users can use a Selection Action Toolbar button to pin or unpin the names of selected placed plants. The pinned state belongs to each individual placed plant and is saved with the Design. Pinned names remain visible during ordinary canvas use, update when the active language changes, and do not imply a Design Object Lock. If a selection includes plants plus other design objects, the action affects only the selected placed plants. If any selected placed plant is not pinned, the action pins all selected placed plants; if all selected placed plants are pinned, it unpins them. Duplicate preserves the pinned state; copy/paste, Object Stamp, Saved Object Stamp placement, and Plant Spacing create unpinned placed plants.

**Key interfaces:**
- Placed Plant persisted contract and file-format migration.
- Canvas selection and Selection Action Toolbar command surface.
- Canvas renderer and localized plant-name presentation cache.
- Duplicate, clipboard, Object Stamp, Saved Object Stamp, and Plant Spacing creation semantics.

**Out of scope:**
- Pinned-name legend behavior.
- Design Report export.
- Changing Design Object Lock behavior.
- Turning pinned names into Annotations or Timeline/Budget/Consortium targets.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A selected placed plant can be pinned and unpinned from the Selection Action Toolbar.
- [ ] Pinned Plant Name state is saved and reloaded with the Design.
- [ ] Pinned labels remain visible on the canvas and update after changing the app language.
- [ ] Mixed selections affect only selected placed plants and leave other selected design objects unchanged.
- [ ] The toggle pins all selected plants when any are unpinned and unpins all when all are already pinned.
- [ ] Duplicate preserves pinned-name state, while copy/paste, Object Stamp, Saved Object Stamp placement, and Plant Spacing create unpinned plants.
- [ ] Focused tests cover persistence, toggle behavior, locale refresh, and copy/duplicate/stamp/spacing semantics.
close_reason: Implemented pinned placed plant names with persisted v4 pinned_name state, Selection Action Toolbar toggle, localized always-visible labels, and copy/duplicate/stamp/spacing semantics. Tests: npm test; npx tsc --noEmit; npm run check:types; cargo fmt --all -- --check; CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo check --workspace; CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace.

title: Choose Design Report PDF renderer
description:
## Slice Summary
Choose the cross-platform renderer strategy for structured Design Report PDF export.

## User Value
Future implementation beads can build a consistent File menu export path instead of extending the current platform-stubbed canvas-snapshot PDF export.

## Out of Scope
Implementing the renderer, report UI, or report sections.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** decision
**Summary:** Choose the cross-platform PDF rendering strategy for structured Design Reports.

**Current behavior:**
Canopi has a native PDF export path shaped around a canvas snapshot and small layout metadata. That path is not a full structured Design Report, and platform support is uneven.

**Desired behavior:**
A human should choose the implementation strategy for generating structured, paginated Design Report PDFs consistently across supported desktop platforms. The decision should preserve the product rule that the report is built from structured report data: the canvas contributes a fitted white-background image that respects visible layers, while metadata, legends, Timeline, Budget, and Consortium content are structured PDF content with wrapping and pagination.

**Key interfaces:**
- Design Report export command boundary from the File menu.
- Cross-platform PDF rendering dependency or platform service boundary.
- Structured report read model and canvas image input.
- Desktop packaging and build/release constraints.

**Out of scope:**
- Implementing the renderer or export command.
- Designing report section layouts beyond preserving the already-settled product decisions.
- Adding export-time layer override options.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A renderer strategy is selected and documented in the bead or a durable ADR.
- [ ] The decision explicitly covers Linux, macOS, and Windows behavior.
- [ ] The decision explains how structured text/tables and a fitted canvas image will be composed into one PDF.
- [ ] The decision states any accepted dependency, platform, packaging, or testing tradeoffs.
- [ ] Downstream implementation beads can proceed without another product or architecture decision about PDF generation.
notes: Historical renderer decision: ADR 0011 retired the former structured Design Report implementation and the printpdf choice in ADR 0007. ADR 0024 (docs/adr/0024-shared-canvas-pdf-export.md) is the current approved direction for planned Canvas PDF export across desktop and Web Edition; it leaves the new PDF library selection open and defers Timeline, Budget, and Consortium PDF sections. Documentation reconciled in canopi-fwmf.
close_reason: Selected printpdf as the shared Rust Design Report PDF renderer and documented the cross-platform strategy, rejected alternatives, structured composition boundary, font embedding requirement, and testing/packaging tradeoffs in docs/adr/0007-design-report-pdf-renderer.md. Tests skipped: docs-only decision.

title: Create persistent Measurement Guides
description:

Add a left-toolbar tool that creates saved Measurement Guides with dotted lines, end ticks, and always-visible distance labels.

## User Value

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Add a left-toolbar tool for creating persistent Measurement Guides.

**Current behavior:**
Canopi has Zone Measurements and temporary spacing/distance guides, but no saved straight measuring aid that is separate from Linear Zones.

**Desired behavior:**
Users can choose a left-toolbar Measurement Guide tool and drag from a start point to an endpoint to create a saved Measurement Guide. A Measurement Guide is a Design Object with two endpoints, a dotted line, small end ticks, and an always-visible distance label. It lives on its own fixed Measurement Guides layer, respects layer visibility and locking, participates in undo/redo and dirty state, and is saved/reloaded with the Design. Its distance label uses the same compact unit formatting rules as Zone Measurements and updates live while creating. Measurement Guides are not Zones, Spacing Guides, Annotations, planning targets, or ecological boundaries.

**Key interfaces:**
- Design file contract, generated bindings, and file-format migration.
- Scene state, history, dirty state, layers, and save/load composition.
- Canvas toolbar command graph and interaction tool modules.
- Renderer and measurement-label overlay behavior.

**Out of scope:**
- Post-creation endpoint editing and copy/duplicate/paste operations.
- Grouping, Object Stamp, Saved Object Stamp, Timeline/Budget/Consortium targeting.
- Design Report export.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A left-toolbar Measurement Guide tool creates a saved guide by dragging start to endpoint.
- [ ] Created guides render as dotted lines with end ticks and always-visible distance labels.
- [ ] Guide labels use the same distance unit formatting rules as Zone Measurements.
- [ ] Measurement Guides live on a fixed Measurement Guides layer and respect that layer's visibility and locking.
- [ ] Measurement Guides persist through save/load and migrate older Designs safely.
- [ ] Creation is undoable/redoable and marks the Design dirty only when a guide is actually created.
- [ ] Focused tests cover creation, rendering data, layer behavior, persistence, migration, and undo/redo.
close_reason: Implemented persistent Measurement Guides with toolbar command, scene persistence and v5 migration, Measurement Guides layer behavior, live and rendered distance labels, Canvas2D/Pixi rendering, undo/redo creation, generated bindings, and localized labels. Tests: npm test; npx tsc --noEmit; npm run check:types after staging; cargo fmt --all -- --check; CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo check --workspace; CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace.

title: Pack Consortium Entries into derived Consortium Lanes
description:
## Slice Summary
Make the Consortium tab pack Consortium Entries into derived Consortium Lanes so entries in the same Stratum can share a lane when their inclusive Succession Phase spans do not overlap.

## User Value
Designers can see more consortium planning in the same vertical space and can move a species-level Consortium Entry to a later phase without being forced into a separate lane when there is temporal room.

## Out of Scope
Do not persist lane numbers, add manual lane management, change the Consortium Time Model phase or Stratum definitions, or split Consortium Entries by individual Placed Plant.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Pack Consortium Entries into derived Consortium Lanes based on inclusive Succession Phase overlap.

**Current behavior:**
Consortium Entries in the same Stratum are presented as separate visual lanes even when their Succession Phase spans do not overlap. The visual lane effectively follows saved entry order, and same-Stratum vertical dragging can behave like manual lane reordering.

**Desired behavior:**
The Consortium tab should present derived Consortium Lanes. Within each Stratum, entries should use the fewest lanes that fit their inclusive Succession Phase spans. Entries whose spans do not overlap can share one lane. Entries whose spans overlap are presented in separate lanes. Saved consortium order remains a deterministic tie-breaker when multiple lane packings are possible, but lane numbers are not saved Design state and are not directly managed by designers.

Dragging a Consortium Entry vertically should choose the target Stratum, not a manual lane. Dragging or resizing should repack lanes during preview and after commit. Body dragging should preserve the entry phase-span length; resizing remains the way to change span length.

**Key interfaces:**
- Consortium planning projection: derives Consortium Entry presentation from Design consortiums, placed plants, localized names, and species colors.
- Consortium drag and resize interaction: previews non-canvas Design edits and commits them through Design Edit transactions.
- Consortium renderer and hit testing: consume derived lane layout without owning the Consortium Time Model or saved Design state.
- Consortium Time Model: owns Succession Phase order, Stratum order, clamping, and default entry timing.

**Out of scope:**
- Persisting lane IDs, lane indexes, or manual lane ordering in `.canopi` files.
- Changing Succession Phase labels, durations, Stratum order, or default Consortium Entry timing.
- Splitting Consortium Entries by individual Placed Plant.
- Adding a new list UI, popover, keyboard interaction, or explicit lane-management control.
- Changing unrelated Timeline, Budget, Target Presentation, or canvas scene behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Non-overlapping Consortium Entries in the same Stratum share a derived Consortium Lane.
- [ ] Overlapping Consortium Entries in the same Stratum appear in separate derived Consortium Lanes.
- [ ] Phase-span overlap is treated as inclusive of both the start and end Succession Phase.
- [ ] Lane packing uses the fewest lanes per Stratum and uses saved consortium order only as a deterministic tie-breaker.
- [ ] Drag preview and commit repack lanes when a Consortium Entry moves between phases or Strata.
- [ ] Resize preview and commit repack lanes when a Consortium Entry span changes.
- [ ] Dragging vertically within the same Stratum no longer creates or preserves a manual lane assignment.
- [ ] No lane IDs, lane indexes, or manual lane ordering are added to saved Design state or shared contract types.
- [ ] Focused frontend tests cover projection packing, renderer row height or hit-test behavior where affected, and drag/resize repacking behavior.
- [ ] Required frontend gates pass: `cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit` plus focused Vitest coverage for the changed Consortium behavior.
close_reason: Implemented derived Consortium Lane packing in Planning Projection, removed manual same-Stratum lane reordering from Consortium drag previews, and added focused coverage for non-overlap sharing, inclusive overlap separation, deterministic tie-breaking, and drag/resize repacking. Tests: cd desktop/web && npm test -- --run src/__tests__/consortium-renderer.test.ts src/__tests__/consortium-interaction.test.ts src/__tests__/frontend-boundaries-sources.test.ts; cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit; cd desktop/web && npm test; git diff --check.

title: Make Plant Symbol menu a true two-row grid
description:

## User Value

## Out of Scope

design:

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Symbol menu presentation and keyboard/pointer selection behavior.

- Changing canvas renderer behavior.
- Changing Species Catalog fields or filtering.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The Plant Symbol menu renders exactly two visual symbol rows: five Plant Habit Symbols on the first row and five abstract Plant Symbols on the second row.
- [ ] The popover width, preview area, spacing, and focus states remain coherent with the existing Canopi field-notebook UI.
- [ ] Existing symbol selection behavior still works for both placed-plant overrides and species default symbol updates.

close_reason: Implemented the true two-row Plant Symbol menu layout with five habit symbols and five abstract symbols, updated frontend agent docs, and verified with focused PlantSymbolMenu Vitest plus TypeScript check.

title: Land the chosen shrub and groundcover Plant Symbols
description:
## Slice Summary
Replace the shrub and groundcover Plant Symbol artwork with the agreed prototype direction: a filled puffy three-lobe shrub with a bottom line, and a groundcover made from three low curved runners from one bottom-center origin.

## User Value
A designer can choose shrub and groundcover symbols that are more recognizable on the canvas and coherent with the built-in Plant Symbol set.

## Out of Scope
Adding user-uploaded icons, changing placed-plant hit testing, changing the Visual Footprint boundary, changing plant-size behavior, or adding Species Catalog-derived symbol inference.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Replace shrub and groundcover built-in Plant Symbol artwork with the chosen prototype direction.

**Current behavior:**
The shrub symbol is an angular outline with a bottom line, and the groundcover symbol is a jagged low stroke. The symbols are functional but do not feel as coherent or recognizable as the rest of the built-in Plant Symbol set when shown at canvas scale.

**Desired behavior:**
The shrub symbol renders as a filled puffy three-lobe canopy with a bottom horizontal line, using fill behavior consistent with the tree symbol. The groundcover symbol renders as three low curved runners that start from the same bottom-center origin and spread left, slightly right/up, and right. Both symbols remain renderer-native Plant Symbol recipes inside the placed plant Visual Footprint.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Symbol recipe command contract.
- Plant Symbol glyph preview rendering.
- Pixi and Canvas2D canvas renderers for placed-plant Plant Symbols.
- Recipe bounds and renderer tests for Plant Symbols.
- ADR-0003: built-in Plant Symbols must remain renderer-native primitives without runtime SVG parsing, image textures, uploaded artwork, or a new icon dependency.

**Out of scope:**
- Runtime SVG parsing or storing raw SVG artwork in design data.
- Changing the stable Plant Symbol IDs.
- Changing circular hit testing, selection rings, stacking, bounds, zoom-to-fit behavior, or the Visual Footprint boundary.
- Changing Plant Symbol menu layout; that is tracked separately.
- Adding Species Catalog-derived symbol inference.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Shrub renders as the agreed filled puffy three-lobe canopy with a bottom horizontal line in the Plant Symbol menu, glyph preview, Pixi renderer, and Canvas2D renderer.
- [ ] Groundcover renders as three low curved runners from one bottom-center origin in the Plant Symbol menu, glyph preview, Pixi renderer, and Canvas2D renderer.
- [ ] The implementation uses renderer-native primitives and does not introduce runtime SVG parsing, image textures, uploaded icon support, or a new icon dependency.
- [ ] Plant Symbol recipe bounds stay within the approved Visual Footprint optical limit.
- [ ] Focused tests cover the updated recipes and any new recipe command support across SVG preview, Pixi, and Canvas2D behavior where local test seams exist.
- [ ] Required frontend checks are run, including `cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit` and focused Vitest coverage.
close_reason: Implemented the chosen shrub and groundcover Plant Symbol recipes with native curve-path rendering in SVG preview, Canvas2D, and Pixi, kept recipes inside the Visual Footprint, and verified with focused Plant Symbol tests, TypeScript check, and full frontend Vitest.

title: Make the Design name editable in the title bar
description:
## Slice Summary
Expose the Design name as editable title-bar text with localized fallback copy and standard text-edit confirmation behavior.

## User Value
A designer can double-click the title-bar Design name, get the whole visible name selected, type a new name, and confirm with Enter or by clicking elsewhere without seeing extra buttons.

## Out of Scope
This slice does not change main Design open/save flows, file picker labels, recent file behavior, or document schema beyond the existing Design name value.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Make the Design name editable directly from the title bar.

**Current behavior:**
The title bar displays a non-editable name only for named Designs, hides the default name, and double-clicking the drag region can trigger window maximize behavior.

**Desired behavior:**
The title bar shows a localized visible fallback Design name when no user-owned name exists: English "Untitled Design" and French "Planche sans titre", with equivalent locale keys for all supported languages. Double-clicking the title text enters text edit mode and selects the complete visible name. Enter or blur confirms, Escape cancels, and no confirm/cancel buttons are shown. Confirming an unchanged fallback should not persist placeholder text or dirty the Design. Confirming a real changed name updates the Design name through the app-owned Design edit/session seam and marks the Design dirty as a normal non-canvas Design edit. Title text double-click must not trigger window maximize or drag behavior.

**Key interfaces:**
- Title bar Design name presentation
- Design Session name state
- Design dirty-state behavior
- Locale strings for visible fallback names

**Out of scope:**
- File picker behavior
- Recent files
- Main Design open/save command flow
- Native window title integration unless already owned by the existing title-bar seam
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The title bar shows a localized fallback Design name when no user-owned name is present.
- [ ] Double-clicking the title text enters edit mode and selects the full visible name.
- [ ] Enter and blur confirm; Escape cancels; no title-bar confirm/cancel buttons are shown.
- [ ] Confirming unchanged fallback text does not persist placeholder copy or dirty the Design.
- [ ] Confirming a changed real name updates the Design name and marks the Design dirty.
- [ ] Editing the Design name does not trigger title-bar drag or double-click maximize behavior.
- [ ] All user-visible fallback/edit labels are localized.
close_reason: Implemented editable title-bar Design name with localized fallback, select-all edit mode, no-button confirmation, unchanged fallback no-op, dirty real renames, and regression coverage in title-bar.test.tsx.

title: Polish Saved Object Stamp rename mode
description:
## Slice Summary
Improve Saved Object Stamp inline rename so it behaves like a focused edit mode rather than a full row with every action still visible.

## User Value
A designer can rename a saved arrangement quickly: the current name is selected automatically, only confirm and cancel actions are shown during editing, blur or Enter confirms, Escape or cancel reverts, and the row spacing feels balanced with the reorder grip.

## Out of Scope
This slice does not change Saved Object Stamp placement, export, import, delete confirmation, thumbnail previews, or Species favorites.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Make Saved Object Stamp rename mode feel focused and coherent with the Favorites side panel.

**Current behavior:**
Saved Object Stamp rename starts in place, but the user must manually select the existing name and row actions such as Place and Export remain visible while the name is being edited. The row spacing between the reorder grip and stamp name feels slightly loose.

**Desired behavior:**
When the designer starts renaming a Saved Object Stamp, the full current stamp name is selected automatically. During rename mode the row shows only confirm and cancel actions. Blur or Enter confirms a non-empty name, Escape or cancel reverts, and empty names still revert rather than persisting blank text. Confirm uses the approved localized green action affordance and cancel uses the approved localized red action affordance for this inline edit exception. The stamp name sits slightly closer to the six-dot reorder grip.

**Key interfaces:**
- Favorites side panel Saved Object Stamp rows
- Saved Object Stamp Workbench inline rename command
- User-visible Saved Object Stamp action strings

**Out of scope:**
- Saved Object Stamp placement behavior
- Saved Object Stamp import/export behavior
- Saved Object Stamp delete confirmation behavior
- Species favorites
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Starting rename selects the complete visible Saved Object Stamp name.
- [ ] Rename mode hides Place and Export and shows only confirm and cancel actions.
- [ ] Enter and blur confirm a non-empty rename; Escape and cancel revert.
- [ ] Confirm and cancel use the approved green/red inline-edit exception without changing unrelated UI chrome colors.
- [ ] Empty rename input reverts rather than saving a blank name.
- [ ] The stamp name/reorder grip spacing is visibly tighter and covered by a focused regression where practical.
close_reason: Implemented focused Saved Object Stamp rename mode: full-name auto-selection, rename-only confirm/cancel actions, green/red inline edit affordances, tighter grip spacing, and regression coverage in favorites-panel.test.tsx.

title: Make Saved Object Stamp dragging reorder live
description:
## Slice Summary
Make Saved Object Stamp manual ordering update visually while the designer drags the reorder grip, while committing persistence once when the drag completes.

## Out of Scope
This slice does not change stamp body drag-to-place, canvas placement ghosts, import/export order semantics, or cross-panel drag behavior.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Make Saved Object Stamp reorder dragging update visibly during the drag.

**Current behavior:**
Manual Saved Object Stamp ordering is only reflected after the drag completes, making the future drop position harder to read while the designer is dragging.

**Desired behavior:**
Dragging the reorder grip updates the visible Saved Object Stamp row order dynamically as the pointer moves across rows. The durable library order is committed once when the drag completes. Cancelling the drag or ending it outside a valid reorder target leaves the durable order unchanged or restored to its original order.

- Saved Object Stamp reorder grip interaction

- Favorites side panel visual row order

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Dragging a Saved Object Stamp reorder grip updates the visible row order before pointer release.
- [ ] The persistent Saved Object Stamp order is committed once when the drag completes.
- [ ] Cancelling or abandoning a reorder drag does not corrupt the saved order.
- [ ] Reorder behavior remains separate from stamp body drag-to-place behavior.

title: Keep Cancel from committing Saved Stamp rename drafts
description:
## Slice Summary
Fix the Saved Stamp inline rename flow so the Cancel rename action discards the current draft instead of letting input blur commit it.

## User Value
Designers can abandon an accidental Saved Stamp rename with the visible Cancel action without changing their library.

## Out of Scope

The rename input confirms on blur. When the dirty input has focus and the user activates the visible Cancel rename action, focus can leave the input first and the blur handler can send the draft to the rename command before the Cancel action runs.

**Desired behavior:**
Activating Cancel rename should discard the draft and keep the existing Saved Stamp name. Blur should still confirm ordinary non-empty edits, and Confirm/Enter should still save intentional edits.

title: Clamp Saved Stamps frame after panel measurement changes
description:
## Slice Summary

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Keep the Saved Stamps frame clamped to the measured Favorites panel height.

**Current behavior:**
The Saved Stamps frame height is resolved during render. On the initial render the panel element may not be available yet, and later panel height changes do not necessarily force a re-render. In those cases a persisted or default frame height can exceed the usable panel space and leave too little room for Plant favorites.

**Desired behavior:**
The Favorites panel should recompute the visible Saved Stamps frame height after the panel can be measured and whenever the panel size changes. The committed user preference should remain the user's requested frame height, while the rendered height is clamped so Plant favorites and Saved Stamps each keep their minimum usable height.

**Key interfaces:**
- Saved Stamps frame height preference in app settings state

**Out of scope:**
- Changing Saved Object Stamp placement, import/export, rename, delete, or reorder behavior

acceptance_criteria:

title: Implement Saved Stamp spatial-signature thumbnail renderer
description:
## Slice Summary
Implement the recognition-thumbnail renderer that turns Saved Object Stamp payloads into compact spatial signatures optimized for recognition rather than literal downscaling.

## User Value
Dense Saved Stamps remain visually recognizable in the hover thumbnail without collapsing into unreadable dots.

## Out of Scope
Do not change exact placement ghost rendering or Saved Object Stamp payload persistence in this slice.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** task
**Summary:** Render Saved Stamp recognition thumbnails as spatial signatures.

**Current behavior:** There is no reusable renderer that minifies Saved Object Stamp payloads into recognition-focused thumbnails.

**Desired behavior:** The renderer consumes a Saved Object Stamp payload and draws a compact spatial signature optimized for recognition, not literal downscaling. It preserves overall bounds and empty space, draws the largest two or three Zones, represents up to about 24 Plants as representative individual marks or clusters using dominant visual identity, and draws up to four Annotation strokes.

**Key interfaces:**
- Saved Object Stamp payload parser/types
- Zone geometry helpers for oriented Zone shapes
- Plant symbol/color presentation helpers where practical
- Favorites thumbnail overlay from the blocker slice

**Out of scope:**
- Exact placement ghost rendering
- Saved Object Stamp payload persistence changes
- Storing precomputed thumbnail data
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Renderer derives thumbnails from Saved Object Stamp payload data at runtime; no persisted thumbnail data is introduced.
- [ ] Overall payload bounds and empty space are preserved in the thumbnail coordinate mapping.
- [ ] Largest two or three Zones are represented with rough shape/orientation.
- [ ] Dense Plant sets are capped at about 24 representative marks or cluster marks while preserving spatial spread and dominant visual identity.
- [ ] Annotations render as capped label strokes, not readable text.
- [ ] Sparse stamps still render individual objects recognizably.
- [ ] Focused tests cover dense plant payloads, sparse payloads, rotated Zones, annotation caps, and empty/invalid payload fallback.
- [ ] Frontend typecheck passes.
close_reason: Implemented runtime Saved Stamp spatial-signature thumbnails with tested sparse, dense, rotated-zone, annotation-cap, and fallback behavior. Checks: npm test -- saved-object-stamp-thumbnail-renderer.test.ts favorites-panel.test.tsx; npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Implement dense Saved Stamp ledger rows
description:

Replace the existing Saved Stamp row/card layout with dense ledger rows that prioritize user-owned stamp names, use a six-dot reorder grip, and keep right-side icon actions visible.

## User Value

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature

**Current behavior:** Saved Stamp rows use text buttons and a layout that does not give enough priority to the stamp name or feel fully integrated with the Favorites panel.

**Desired behavior:** Saved Stamps render as dense ledger rows. The left affordance is a compact six-dot reorder grip that only reorders the library. The row body prioritizes the user-owned stamp name and puts composition counts in the secondary summary. Right-side icon actions are always visible in this order: Place, Export, Rename, Delete. Plain row clicks are inert; body drag starts drag/drop placement; the Place icon arms click-to-place mode.

**Key interfaces:**
- `FavoritesPanel`
- Saved Object Stamp Workbench commands
- Saved Object Stamp drag/drop source
- Existing rename/delete/reorder behaviors

**Out of scope:**
- Recognition thumbnail overlay
- Spatial-signature renderer

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Saved Stamp rows use a left six-dot reorder grip instead of generated codes such as `ST-01`.
- [ ] Reorder grip drag only reorders the library; row-body drag starts Saved Object Stamp drag/drop placement.
- [ ] Row name gets the dominant flexible track; composition counts appear in the secondary summary, not fixed metric columns.
- [ ] Right-side icon actions are always visible in order: Place, Export, Rename, Delete.
- [ ] Plain row click does not arm placement, select a stamp, or open details.
- [ ] Rename uses an in-place input; while renaming, Place and Export remain available, Rename becomes Confirm, Delete becomes Cancel, Enter confirms, Escape cancels, blur confirms non-empty names, and empty names revert.
- [ ] Delete uses inline two-step confirmation; while confirming, the row shows concise danger copy and only Confirm Delete / Cancel actions.
- [ ] Focused tests cover row actions, inert row click, drag/reorder separation, rename, delete confirmation, and export visibility.
- [ ] Frontend typecheck passes.
close_reason: Implemented dense Saved Stamp ledger rows with six-dot reorder grip, body-only placement drag, right-side icon actions, rename mode, and inline delete confirmation; covered behavior in Favorites panel tests and typecheck.

## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Persist the Saved Stamps frame height as a user setting.

**Current behavior:** The Saved Stamps section uses a fixed max-height inside the Favorites panel and does not remember a user-adjusted split between Species favorites and Saved Stamps.

title: Preserve effective Plant Symbols in Saved Object Stamps
description:
## Slice Summary
Saved Object Stamps should capture the Plant Symbol a designer actually sees, including symbols inherited from Design-level species defaults, so later placement/import/export does not depend on the target Design's defaults.

## User Value
Designers can reuse saved arrangements without Plant Symbols changing or falling back when the source used species-level Plant Symbol defaults.

## Out of Scope
Do not change Plant Symbol editing semantics, the Saved Object Stamp payload schema shape beyond stored values, or Species Catalog data.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Saved Object Stamps must preserve effective Plant Symbols, including species defaults.

**Current behavior:** Saved Object Stamp payloads store only a placed plant's explicit Plant Symbol. If the visible symbol comes from a Design-level species default, saving/importing/exporting the stamp stores `null`, so later placement can fall back to `round` or inherit a different target Design default.

**Desired behavior:** Saving or importing a Saved Object Stamp should capture the effective Plant Symbol visible on the source placed plant. Later placement should use that captured symbol explicitly so Saved Object Stamps are portable across Designs with different species defaults.

**Key interfaces:**
- Saved Object Stamp Workbench payload normalization
- Saved Object Stamp `.canopi` import path
- Plant Symbol resolution between placed-plant explicit symbols and species defaults

**Out of scope:**
- Changing Plant Symbol edit commands or default-clearing semantics
- Changing Species Catalog data
- Adding new custom/uploaded symbols
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Saving a selected placed plant with no explicit symbol but a species default captures the effective Plant Symbol.
- [ ] Importing a `.canopi` file as a Saved Object Stamp captures effective Plant Symbols from `plant_species_symbols` when placed plants omit explicit symbols.
- [ ] Captured symbols remain explicit on later stamp placement/export.
- [ ] Focused regression tests cover selection save and `.canopi` import behavior.
close_reason: Fixed Saved Object Stamp payload normalization to preserve effective Plant Symbols inherited from species defaults during selection save and .canopi import. Verified with focused Saved Object Stamp tests, TypeScript, Rust cargo check, and related Rust unit tests.

title: Import Saved Object Stamp anchors from Elliptical Zone bounds
description:
## Slice Summary
Importing a `.canopi` file as a Saved Object Stamp should derive the stamp anchor from visible design object geometry, treating an Elliptical Zone's second point as radii rather than a world coordinate.

## User Value
Designers can import arrangements containing Elliptical Zones and place them at the expected cursor/drop location.

## Out of Scope
Do not change Zone rendering, Zone editing, or the persisted Zone data format.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Saved Object Stamp import must derive anchors from visible design object geometry for Elliptical Zones.

**Current behavior:** Importing a `.canopi` file as a Saved Object Stamp flattens all Zone points into anchor calculation. For Elliptical Zones, the second point represents radii, not a world point, so the anchor can be pulled away from the visible geometry.

**Desired behavior:** Imported Saved Object Stamp anchors should be based on visible geometry bounds. Elliptical Zones should contribute their actual world-space bounds or center/radii-derived bounds, so placing the imported stamp aligns the visible arrangement with the cursor/drop anchor.

**Key interfaces:**
- Saved Object Stamp import from `.canopi`
- Zone geometry semantics for Elliptical Zones
- Saved Object Stamp placement delta calculation

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the persisted Zone representation
- Changing Zone rendering or editing tools
- Changing Object Stamp sampling behavior
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Importing a stamp with only an Elliptical Zone derives an anchor from the ellipse's visible bounds, not its radii point as a coordinate.
- [ ] Mixed imports with plants, annotations, and Elliptical Zones derive an anchor from combined visible geometry.
- [ ] Existing non-elliptical Zone import behavior remains intact.
- [ ] Focused regression tests cover Elliptical Zone import anchor behavior.
close_reason: Fixed Saved Object Stamp .canopi import anchors for Elliptical Zones by deriving anchors from visible Zone bounds instead of treating radii as coordinates. Verified with focused Saved Object Stamp file tests, TypeScript, Rust cargo check, and related Rust unit tests.

title: Export Saved Object Stamp groups with valid zone member ids
description:
## Slice Summary
Exported Saved Object Stamp `.canopi` files must contain Object Groups whose typed Zone members point at the exported Zone names used by the file schema.

## User Value
Designers can export and re-import grouped Saved Object Stamps without losing Zone membership or creating stale Object Group references.

## Out of Scope
Do not change the Saved Object Stamp payload schema or Object Group semantics outside export composition.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Saved Object Stamp export must write Object Group Zone members using the Zone identifiers valid in the exported `.canopi` file.

**Current behavior:** Saved Object Stamp payloads carry an internal Zone id separate from the Zone display/name. Export composition writes Zones under their `name` field but leaves Object Group members pointing at the payload-internal Zone id. The resulting `.canopi` file can contain stale Object Group references.

**Desired behavior:** Exported Object Groups should preserve only members that resolve to exported objects, and Zone members should reference the exported Zone name used by the `.canopi` schema. A Saved Object Stamp exported and imported again should preserve valid captured Object Groups involving Zones.

**Key interfaces:**
- Saved Object Stamp `.canopi` file composition
- Typed Object Group member contract for Placed Plants, Zones, and Annotations
- Saved Object Stamp import path from `.canopi`

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the Saved Object Stamp payload schema
- Changing Object Group flat typed membership semantics
- Changing normal Design save/load behavior
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Exported `.canopi` Object Group Zone members reference exported Zone names, not payload-internal Zone ids.
- [ ] Exporting and importing a grouped Saved Object Stamp involving a Zone preserves valid Object Group membership.
- [ ] Invalid or missing members are still dropped rather than written as stale references.
- [ ] Focused regression tests cover grouped Zone export/import round-tripping.
close_reason: Fixed Saved Object Stamp .canopi export so Object Group Zone members reference exported Zone names and round-trip through import. Verified with focused Saved Object Stamp file tests, TypeScript, Rust cargo check, and related Rust unit tests.

description:
## Slice Summary

## User Value

description:

description:

## User Value

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Create the first end-to-end Saved Object Stamp save path and panel section.

**Current behavior:**
Canopi has Species favorites in the right Favorites side panel and transient Object Stamp/clipboard reuse on the canvas, but there is no personal library entry for saving a selected visible canvas arrangement for later reuse.

**Desired behavior:**
A designer can save an eligible canvas selection as a named Saved Object Stamp and see it in a Saved Stamps section below Species favorites. Directly locked selected Design Objects may be captured, but structural blockers such as hidden Layers, locked Layers, missing targets, and grouped members selected outside their Object Group are not eligible.

Default names are generated once at save time. Use the three most frequent selected plant species names at most, using localized Common Name with Canonical Name fallback; ties follow first appearance in the saved arrangement. If there are no plants, use Zone and Annotation counts.

**Key interfaces:**
- Saved Object Stamp domain term and ADR for personal user DB storage plus `.canopi` portability.

**Out of scope:**
- Inline rename, delete, manual reorder, import/export, click placement, drag/drop placement.
- Adding a new PanelBar route.
- Embedding Saved Object Stamps into normal `.canopi` Design save composition.

- [ ] Frontend can save the current eligible selection into the Saved Stamps section below Species favorites.

- [ ] Default names follow the agreed plant-name/count rules and do not auto-change after creation.
- [ ] Focused Rust and frontend tests cover persistence, eligibility, payload normalization, default naming, and panel rendering.

title: Keep Elliptical Zone boundary hit tolerance screen-stable
description:
## Slice Summary
Fix Elliptical Zone boundary hit testing so the selectable and hoverable boundary remains within the intended screen-space tolerance across large ellipse sizes and high viewport scales.

## User Value
Users can reliably select, hover, and drag large Elliptical Zone boundaries at high zoom without boundary clicks missing because of a coarse polygon approximation.

## Out of Scope
Do not change rendered ellipse geometry, Zone selection priority, filled-interior selection behavior, or broad non-ellipse hit-testing semantics.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Keep Elliptical Zone boundary hit testing screen-space stable for large high-zoom ellipses.

**Current behavior:**
Elliptical Zone boundary hit testing approximates the ellipse with a fixed number of polygon segments. For large Elliptical Zones at high viewport scale, the approximation can drift farther from the rendered boundary than the intended screen-space hit tolerance, so clicks on visible boundary arcs can miss selection, hover, or whole-Zone drag start.

**Desired behavior:**
Elliptical Zone boundary hits should honor the same screen-space-stable tolerance as other Zone boundary hits regardless of ellipse size or zoom. A click on or near the rendered Elliptical Zone boundary should be considered a boundary hit within the configured tolerance, while interior clicks away from the boundary should continue to pass through according to existing Zone selection rules.

**Key interfaces:**
- Zone boundary hit testing
- Elliptical Zone geometry and rotation semantics
- Selection, hover, and whole-Zone drag intent that consume boundary hit results

**Out of scope:**
- Changing rendered ellipse geometry
- Changing the 6 px-style boundary tolerance contract for non-ellipse Zones
- Reintroducing filled-interior Elliptical Zone selection
- Broad hit-testing priority changes between Plants, Annotations, and Zones
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Large Elliptical Zone boundary hits at high viewport scale succeed for points on visible boundary arcs between coarse fixed polygon sample vertices.
- [ ] Elliptical Zone interior clicks away from the boundary do not become Zone hits.
- [ ] Rotated Elliptical Zone boundary hits continue to respect the ellipse orientation.
- [ ] Existing Plant and Annotation priority over Zone boundary hits is preserved.
- [ ] Focused regression coverage exercises the large high-zoom Elliptical Zone boundary miss through the public hit-testing or scene interaction path.
close_reason: Fixed Elliptical Zone boundary hit testing by adapting ellipse boundary polygon density to viewport scale and radius so chord sag stays under the screen-space tolerance. Added high-zoom large-ellipse regression coverage. Gates: cd desktop/web && npm test -- hit-testing.test.ts; cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit; cd desktop/web && npm test.

title: Prevent no-op Zone Control Point taps from mutating zones
description:
## Slice Summary
Ensure pressing and releasing a Zone Control Point without meaningful drag movement does not reshape the Zone, update measurements, or create an undoable edit.

## User Value
Users can inspect or tap Zone Control Points without accidentally changing Zone geometry, even when snapping is enabled or the pointer lands inside the handle hit target rather than exactly on the visual mark.

## Out of Scope
Do not redesign Zone Control Point affordances, snapping behavior during real drags, or Zone geometry editing beyond preserving no-op tap semantics.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Preserve no-op semantics when a user taps a Zone Control Point without dragging.

**Current behavior:**
A Zone Control Point press followed by release can apply the pointer-up position as a shape edit even when the pointer never moved past the drag threshold. With snapping enabled, or when the pointer lands inside the handle hit target but away from the visual point, the Zone can resize or move and an undoable edit can be committed from what should be a no-op tap.

**Desired behavior:**
Zone geometry, live measurements, and the undo stack must remain unchanged unless the pointer movement crosses the drag threshold for an actual Zone Control Point drag. Once a real drag starts, existing dynamic geometry and measurement updates should continue to work.

**Key interfaces:**
- Zone Control Point pointer gesture lifecycle
- Zone geometry mutation and commit behavior
- Dynamic Zone measurements during control-point drags
- Undoable scene edit transaction boundary

**Out of scope:**
- Changing which Zone Control Points are shown
- Changing snapping behavior for real drags
- Broad Zone editing architecture refactors
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Pressing and releasing a Zone Control Point without crossing the drag threshold leaves Zone geometry unchanged.
- [ ] A no-op Zone Control Point tap does not create an undoable scene edit.
- [ ] The no-op behavior holds when snapping is enabled and when the pointer starts inside the handle hit target but away from the visual mark.
- [ ] Real Zone Control Point drags still update geometry and measurements dynamically and still commit one undoable edit.
- [ ] Focused regression coverage exercises no-op taps through the public scene interaction path.
close_reason: Fixed Zone Control Point no-op taps by applying final geometry only after pointer movement crosses the drag threshold. Added public scene interaction regression coverage. Gates: cd desktop/web && npm test -- scene-interaction.test.ts; cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit; cd desktop/web && npm test.

title: Add Elliptical Zone radius-handle dragging
description:
## Slice Summary
Single selected editable Elliptical Zones should expose four oriented cardinal Zone Control Points that resize width or height while preserving ellipse semantics.

## User Value

## Out of Scope
