title: PRD: Canvas Selection Actions and Rotation
description:
## Problem Statement

Permaculture designers need to rotate selected Design Objects on the canvas so they can orient beds, paths, annotations, groups, and plant arrangements to match real site conditions. Today the canvas has movement, selection, grouping, locking, layer visibility, and hidden shortcut commands, but the transform UX is fragmented: rotation is not exposed, selection highlights are too subtle, Design Object Locks and Object Groups are difficult to discover, Layer locks exist in the model but are not clearly controlled, and selecting all placed plants of the same Species requires manual multi-selection.

The result is that users cannot confidently manipulate a selected arrangement, and they cannot reliably understand why some visible objects are editable while others are locked, grouped, hidden by Layers, or unavailable for transformation.

## Solution

Add a coherent canvas selection UX centered on editable Design Object selections. Users can rotate visible editable Design Objects with an on-canvas Rotation Handle, use a compact Selection Action Toolbar for common object commands, see stronger selection highlights, discover and manage Design Object Locks and Layer locks, use visible Group/Ungroup affordances, and double-click a Placed Plant to select visible editable Placed Plants of the same Species.

Rotation uses a shared Rotation Pivot for multi-selection and preserves shape intent for Rectangular Zones and Elliptical Zones. The UX follows the field-notebook design system: ochre canvas affordances, precise icon controls, fixed screen-space overlay sizing, no green UI chrome, no bulky floating cards, and no automatic focus changes.

## Success Criteria

- Users can rotate supported editable Design Object selections with a discoverable on-canvas Rotation Handle, including single annotations, single zones, Object Groups, and multi-object arrangements.
- Rotation preserves shape intent for Rectangular Zones and Elliptical Zones, creates one undoable Scene Edit per committed drag, and does not dirty the document for no-op drags or selection-only gestures.
- Selection highlights, Rotation Handle placement, live angle readout, and Selection Action Toolbar are clear in light and dark themes without violating the field-notebook design system.
- Design Object Locks, Layer locks, and Object Groups are discoverable through visible canvas or panel affordances, while preserving the invariant that editable selection excludes locked or hidden objects.
- Species Selection lets users double-click a Placed Plant in Select tool mode to select all visible editable top-level Placed Plants with the same Canonical Name.
- Existing canvas authority boundaries remain intact: SceneStore stays the canvas state authority, Scene Edits own canvas mutations, and renderers remain projections rather than interaction owners.

## User Stories

1. As a designer, I want to rotate one selected annotation, zone, or linear feature, so that labels, beds, paths, and boundaries can match the orientation of my site.
2. As a designer, I want to rotate multiple selected Design Objects around one shared Rotation Pivot, so that a whole arrangement keeps its relative layout while turning together.
3. As a designer, I want Object Groups to rotate like one arrangement, so that grouped clusters and stamped patterns remain easy to manipulate.
4. As a designer, I want Rectangular Zones and Elliptical Zones to remain their original Zone kinds after rotation, so that shape-specific editing and Zone Measurements still make sense.
5. As a designer, I want selection highlights and rotation affordances to be clearly visible, so that I can tell what will be transformed before I drag.
6. As a designer, I want Shift-drag rotation snapping and a live angle readout, so that I can make precise turns without opening a separate panel.
7. As a designer, I want rotation drags to behave like other canvas drags, so that Escape cancels, pointer-up commits, and off-canvas movement remains predictable.
8. As a designer, I want a Selection Action Toolbar for common commands, so that Delete, Duplicate, ordering, Lock/Unlock, Group/Ungroup, and Select Same Species are discoverable without memorizing shortcuts.
9. As a designer, I want locked Design Objects to be visible and discoverable without becoming editable selections, so that I understand why an object cannot be moved, rotated, deleted, grouped, or stamped.
10. As a designer, I want an obvious way to unlock a locked Design Object from the canvas, so that I do not need to know a hidden shortcut.
11. As a designer, I want Layer locks to be visible in the Layer Panel and reflected on canvas hover, so that I can distinguish object-level locks from Layer-level edit restrictions.
12. As a designer, I want Object Group commands to be visible when valid, so that grouping is a coherent canvas feature rather than a hidden shortcut.
13. As a designer, I want double-clicking a Placed Plant to select all visible editable Placed Plants of the same Species, so that I can quickly recolor, duplicate, delete, group, or inspect a species placement pattern.
14. As a keyboard user, I want toolbar actions to be keyboard-accessible only when I intentionally focus the toolbar, so that visual highlights on canvas do not unexpectedly become keyboard targets.

## Implementation Decisions

- Use the project term Design Object, not element, shape, or canvas object, for placed plants, zones, annotations, and object groups.
- Treat rotation as a Scene Edit because it mutates canvas-owned Design state and must participate in undo/redo, dirty state, serialization, and render invalidation.
- The primary rotation affordance is an on-canvas Rotation Handle shown when rotation has visible meaning. It appears above the combined selection bounds, with the Rotation Pivot at the center of those same bounds.
- Do not show the Rotation Handle for a single selected Placed Plant, because its current circular symbol has no visible orientation. Show it for multi-plant selections, mixed selections, annotations, linear zones, rectangular zones, elliptical zones, polygonal zones, and object groups.
- Compute multi-selection Rotation Pivot and Rotation Handle placement from combined axis-aligned visual bounds. Plant bounds use current Visual Footprint. Annotation bounds use readable text bounds. Zone bounds use current visible geometry.
- Rotation Handle, live rotation readout, lock badges, and Selection Action Toolbar are runtime-owned DOM overlays coordinated by scene interaction behavior. They are not renderer-owned projections and not outer Preact chrome reaching into runtime internals.
- Rotation overlays use fixed screen-space sizing and follow the interface design system: ochre selection color, thin ruled outlines/stems, compact icon controls, fixed readable stroke weights, tokenized sizes, no green chrome, and no decorative card treatment.
- Rotation starts on pointer-down on the Rotation Handle, updates live during pointer movement, commits as one undoable Scene Edit on pointer-up if the final delta crosses a small angular threshold, and aborts without history when the delta is effectively zero.
- Escape during rotation aborts the active rotation transaction, restores starting geometry, hides the live angle readout, and leaves selection unchanged.
- Pointer release outside the canvas commits rotation, and off-canvas movement is edge-clamped consistently with existing canvas drawing and movement expectations.
- Shift during rotation snaps to 15-degree increments. Rotation does not snap to grid or guides in this scope.
- The drag readout shows signed clockwise delta degrees normalized to `-180` through `180`. Stored orientation values use degrees and are normalized to `0 <= degrees < 360` where orientation fields exist.
- Add optional Zone orientation support for file compatibility. Missing orientation means `0` degrees. The optional field may exist on Zone records for schema simplicity, but only Rectangular Zones and Elliptical Zones interpret it.
- Preserve shaped Zone kind during rotation. Rectangular Zones and Elliptical Zones keep explicit orientation instead of being converted to Polygonal Zones. This follows the accepted architecture decision for shaped-zone rotation.
- Rotate Rectangular Zones and Elliptical Zones by moving their centers around the active Rotation Pivot and incrementing orientation while preserving intrinsic size. Rotate Linear Zones and Polygonal Zones by directly rotating their saved points.
- Placed Plants rotate by moving their positions around the Rotation Pivot. Do not assign individual plant orientation until plant symbols have visible direction.
- Annotations rotate by moving their positions and rotating visible text orientation.
- Object Group rotation mutates member geometry as the visible source of truth. The group wrapper is not a hidden transform surface. Mixed selections containing groups and standalone Design Objects rotate as one selected arrangement.
- Rotation respects Design Object Locks and Layer locks. Locked objects and objects on locked Layers are not editable selections and cannot be transformed. If lock state changes during an active rotation, the gesture should abort rather than partially commit.
- Hidden Layers suppress object hit testing, selection, hover discovery, lock badges, Rotation Handles, and toolbar actions for those objects.
- Strengthen selection highlights as part of this work. Selected state should be visibly stronger than hover state across plants, zones, annotations, light/dark themes, and renderer backends.
- Locked Design Objects remain hover-discoverable but not selectable. Hover can show a lock badge/action. Clicking a locked object must not create a special locked selection.
- Layer-locked objects show a distinct locked-Layer cue that points users toward the Layer Panel, not an object-level unlock.
- `Cmd/Ctrl+L` should affect the current editable selection only. Legacy unlock-all-when-no-selection behavior should not be preserved. Any unlock-all command must be explicit and clearly labeled.
- Keep fixed Layers as a long-term product concept. Improve Layer Panel discoverability and add visible lock controls for scene Layers. Do not add arbitrary user-created Layer management in this scope.
- Keep Object Groups as a long-term product concept. Expose Group/Ungroup affordances, while preserving current same-Layer Object Group semantics unless a future model change deliberately revisits group layering.
- The Selection Action Toolbar appears automatically for editable selections, does not take focus automatically, and avoids covering selected geometry or the Rotation Handle.
- The Selection Action Toolbar uses icon-only buttons with tooltips and shortcuts. Mostly hide invalid commands rather than rendering a disabled command set. Show disabled states only when a command is conceptually relevant but blocked by a clear condition.
- Include common existing object commands in the Selection Action Toolbar: Delete, Duplicate, Bring Forward, Send Back, Lock/Unlock, Group/Ungroup, and Select Same Species when applicable. Precision rotation may be added there later.
- Keep the existing plant color affordance for now. It may eventually move into selection actions, but that is not required for the first coherent rotation/lock/group pass.
- Selection Action Toolbar buttons remain keyboard-focusable and activatable with Enter/Space only when users explicitly tab or focus into the toolbar. Canvas selection must not auto-focus the toolbar.
- The Rotation Handle itself is not keyboard-focusable in the first version. Keyboard rotation should come through explicit shortcuts or future numeric rotation input.
- Disable native context menu behavior on canvas interaction surfaces and selection overlays only. Do not suppress normal defaults in inputs, textareas, menus, dropdowns, dialogs, Species Catalog surfaces, or other non-canvas UI.
- Species Selection is a Select-tool gesture. Plain double-click on a visible editable top-level Placed Plant selects all visible editable top-level Placed Plants with the same Canonical Name across the whole design. Shift+double-click toggles that Species set against the current selection.
- Species Selection excludes grouped members, locked Design Objects, hidden Layers, and locked Layers. It uses Canonical Name identity, not Common Name. It does not apply in Plant Stamp, Object Stamp, Plant Spacing, Zone drawing, Text, or other non-Select tools.
- Species Selection does not create document history or dirty state. Selection highlights, selection labels, and Selection Action Toolbar placement update immediately after the selection changes.
- Double-click behavior for zones, annotations, and Object Groups is out of scope for this first pass.

## Testing Decisions

- Test behavior through public runtime interaction seams and user-equivalent pointer/keyboard events, not by calling private handlers.
- Add focused geometry tests for rotation math as a deep module: pivot calculation from visual bounds, degree normalization, Shift snapping, threshold handling, point rotation, shaped-zone orientation updates, group member transforms, and annotation orientation changes.
- Add file-format and contract tests for optional Zone orientation, including old files loading with `0` degree orientation and new saves preserving shaped-zone orientation.
- Add renderer/backend behavior tests or visual snapshot-oriented assertions for stronger selection highlights and oriented Rectangular/Elliptical Zone rendering where existing renderer tests already cover scene projections.
- Add hit-testing tests for oriented Rectangular Zones and Elliptical Zones, locked Design Object hover discovery, locked Layer hover cues, and hidden Layer non-interactivity.
- Add interaction-frame tests for Rotation Handle drag lifecycle: live update, Shift snapping, Escape abort, pointer-up commit, off-canvas commit, edge-clamped movement, no-op threshold abort, and one Scene Edit per drag.
- Add toolbar interaction tests for Selection Action Toolbar visibility, valid command filtering, non-autofocus behavior, explicit keyboard activation, and command dispatch through the app command graph.
- Add Layer Panel tests for visible Layer lock controls and authority-correct lock writes through Canvas Layer Presentation.
- Add lock UX tests for object-level lock badges/actions, no special locked selection state, and removal of legacy unlock-all shortcut behavior.
- Add Object Group command tests showing Group/Ungroup affordances are available only when valid and preserve same-Layer semantics.
- Add Species Selection tests for plain double-click replacement selection, Shift+double-click toggling, Canonical Name identity, whole-design selection, grouped member exclusion, lock/Layer exclusion, Select-tool-only behavior, and no dirty/history mutation.
- Existing prior art includes scene interaction tests, runtime mutation tests, hit-testing tests, renderer tests, command shortcut tests, canvas layer presentation tests, file-format round-trip tests, and frontend boundary tests.

## Out of Scope

- Arbitrary user-created Layers or a full Layer management system.
- Custom Rotation Pivot editing or persistent pivot placement.
- Multi-touch two-finger rotation.
- Custom right-click context menus.
- Group editing, nested group editing, or selecting individual members inside Object Groups.
- Per-plant orientation until plant symbols have visible direction.
- Moving plant color into the Selection Action Toolbar unless a later slice deliberately includes it.
- Numeric rotation inspector, absolute orientation inspector, or keyboard rotation shortcuts beyond the existing shortcut architecture.
- Equivalent double-click "select same" behavior for zones, annotations, or Object Groups.
- Broad global suppression of browser/OS defaults outside canvas interaction surfaces.

## Further Notes

- This PRD is intentionally broad enough to become an epic. Delivery should be split into slices with clear dependencies: selection highlight tuning, shaped-zone orientation schema/geometry, rotation interaction overlays, Selection Action Toolbar, lock/layer UX, Object Group command discoverability, and Species Selection.
- The shaped-zone orientation decision is recorded in the architecture decision record for preserving Rectangular Zones and Elliptical Zones during rotation. Implementation should not replace those shaped zones with polygon approximations.
- Runtime ownership of selection transform overlays is deliberate. Adding outer component seams before the runtime exposes stable read models would likely create leaky authority boundaries.
- Layer lock and Design Object Lock cues must remain visually related but semantically distinct.
- The first implementation should prefer deep geometry and selection-command modules with narrow, testable interfaces so renderer and interaction code can call shared behavior instead of duplicating rotation math or selection eligibility rules.
close_reason: Closed after all 10 child beads shipped: selection read model, oriented shaped Zones, stronger highlights, toolbar, groups, object locks, layer locks, species selection, single-selection rotation, and multi-selection/Object Group rotation. Final child gates included focused interaction/read-model tests, full frontend npm test, TypeScript check, generated binding check on the stack, and whitespace checks.

title: Clear Polygonal Zone draft redo after redo-only cancellation
description:
## Slice Summary
Fix the Polygonal Zone Zone Draft cancellation path where Undo of the only draft vertex leaves redoable draft state even though the visible draft is gone. Pressing Escape after that redo-only state should cancel the draft redo state so Redo cannot restore the cancelled vertex.

## User Value
A user who starts a Polygonal Zone, undoes the only draft vertex, and then cancels with Escape gets a truly cancelled Zone Draft instead of stale Redo restoring the old vertex.

## Out of Scope
Do not change committed Scene Edit history semantics. Do not remove the intentional ability to Redo the one undone draft vertex before explicit cancellation. Do not add transient redo support for other tools.

## Source
Follow-up review finding from canopi-kjxk.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Clear Polygonal Zone Zone Draft redo state when a redo-only draft is explicitly cancelled.

**Current behavior:**
After a user places one Polygonal Zone draft vertex and runs Undo, the visible Zone Draft is cleared but the transient draft redo stack can still hold the undone vertex. Because some cancellation paths treat an empty draft vertex list as no active draft, pressing Escape in that redo-only state can fail to clear the redo stack. Redo can then restore a vertex after the user tried to cancel the draft.

**Desired behavior:**
A redo-only Polygonal Zone Zone Draft state is still cancellable transient tool state. After placing one draft vertex, running Undo, and pressing Escape, draft Redo must no longer be available and must not restore the cancelled vertex. Before Escape or another explicit cancellation path, Redo should still restore the one undone draft vertex.

**Key interfaces:**
- Polygonal Zone Zone Draft transient Undo/Redo behavior
- Scene Interaction Frame keyboard cancellation handling
- Canvas Runtime Surface history command availability

**Out of scope:**
- Changing committed Scene Edit history behavior

title: Make Polygonal Zone draft Undo/Redo step through vertices
description:
## Slice Summary
When a user is drawing a Polygonal Zone, Undo and Redo should operate on the active Zone Draft before falling through to committed Scene Edit history. Undo removes the most recent placed draft vertex; Redo restores draft vertices while the same unbranched draft remains active.

## User Value
A user can correct the latest Zone Edge while building a Polygonal Zone without losing the whole draft, and can restore an accidentally undone draft edge. Toolbar, menu, command palette, and keyboard command availability should match the actual draft/history state.

## Out of Scope
Do not add redo support for other transient tool drafts. Do not change persisted Zone geometry or Scene Edit history semantics after a Polygonal Zone is committed. Do not introduce a generalized app-wide transient history framework unless the local canvas seams require it.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Make active Polygonal Zone Zone Draft Undo/Redo step through draft vertices before committed Scene Edit history.

**Current behavior:**
While drawing a Polygonal Zone, Backspace can remove the most recent draft vertex, but Undo is routed to committed Scene Edit history. If the latest committed edit is a completed Polygonal Zone, Undo removes the whole committed Zone rather than stepping back through the active Zone Draft. Command availability is tied to committed history only, so toolbar/menu/palette Undo may be disabled even when a Zone Draft has vertices that can be undone.

**Desired behavior:**
When a Polygonal Zone Zone Draft is active, every Undo entry point should first remove the most recent placed draft vertex. If the draft has one vertex, Undo clears the draft. Redo should restore draft vertices while the same unbranched draft remains active. If no draft undo/redo is available, Undo/Redo should fall through to committed Scene Edit history. Undo/Redo command availability should include draft undo/redo availability. Native text undo/redo must continue to win when focus is inside editable text controls.

Draft Redo should clear whenever the user branches the draft by placing a new vertex after undoing, commits/closes the Polygonal Zone, cancels the draft, switches tools, disposes/replaces the design, or otherwise clears transient tool state. Committing after draft Undo should create the Polygonal Zone from only the currently visible draft vertices.

**Key interfaces:**
- App Command Graph Undo/Redo commands and their disabled-state projections
- Canvas Runtime Surface history command surface
- Scene Interaction Frame and Polygonal Zone tool state
- Scene Edit history for committed canvas changes

**Out of scope:**
- Redo behavior for other transient tools
- Persisting Zone Draft history into the design
- Changing committed Scene Edit undo/redo semantics
- Changing native editable-field undo/redo behavior
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] While drawing a Polygonal Zone with multiple draft vertices, Undo removes only the most recent draft vertex and does not commit or undo a Scene Edit.
- [ ] Undo with one draft vertex clears the Zone Draft without dirtying the design or creating a Zone.
- [ ] Redo restores draft vertices after draft Undo while the same unbranched Zone Draft remains active.
- [ ] Placing a new draft vertex after draft Undo clears the draft Redo stack.
- [ ] Closing/committing a Polygonal Zone after draft Undo uses only the currently visible draft vertices.
- [ ] Escape cancellation, tool switching, disposal, and transient cleanup clear draft undo/redo state.
- [ ] Toolbar, menu, command palette, and keyboard Undo/Redo route through draft state before committed Scene Edit history.
- [ ] Undo/Redo disabled states are enabled when draft undo/redo is available, even if committed Scene Edit history is empty.
- [ ] Editable text controls keep native Undo/Redo behavior.
- [ ] Focused frontend tests cover draft Undo, draft Redo, command availability, and fallthrough to committed Scene Edit history.
- [ ] Relevant agent docs remain aligned with the final behavior.
close_reason: Implemented Polygonal Zone Zone Draft Undo/Redo through transient draft vertices before committed Scene Edit history. Passing checks: cd desktop/web && npm test -- scene-interaction.test.ts canvas/runtime/scene-runtime.test.ts commands-registry.test.ts; cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit. description:

## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Stabilize Timeline Action Canvas geometry and render dependencies so tooltip-only pointer movement does not repaint the canvas.

**Current behavior:**
Timeline hover updates can re-render the host model for tooltip coordinate changes even when the hovered Timeline Action identity has not changed. The canvas renderer dependency set observes a freshly-created geometry object, so overlay-only renders can schedule a full Timeline canvas redraw at mousemove frequency.

**Desired behavior:**
The Timeline canvas should redraw only when canvas-visible inputs change, such as rows, layout, origin, zoom, scroll, selection, hovered action identity, locale/theme, or species colors. Pointer movement that only changes tooltip overlay coordinates for the same hovered Timeline Action should update the overlay without creating new renderer dependencies or redrawing the canvas.

**Key interfaces:**
- Timeline Action Canvas host model renderer dependency contract.
- Timeline Action Canvas geometry snapshot used by rendering and interaction hit testing.
- Shared Canvas2D renderer hook dependency behavior.

**Out of scope:**
- Changing Timeline Action drag, resize, add, edit, or delete behavior.
- Reintroducing hidden Timeline ruler-control hit testing.
- Changing Planning Projection grouping or lane assignment.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Tooltip-only mouse moves over the same Timeline Action do not create a new canvas renderer dependency or force a Timeline canvas redraw.

- [ ] Focused tests cover the tooltip-only no-redraw behavior through the public Timeline Action Canvas host/render seam or the closest stable app seam.
- [ ] Existing Timeline Action Canvas interaction-frame tests and frontend typecheck pass.

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Guard Problem Report submission state against stale async completions after close, reset, or reopen.

**Current behavior:**
Problem Report submission state is held in a persistent frontend module. A submit command awaits report creation and then writes result, error, show-folder state, and submitting state into shared signals. If the dialog is closed and reopened while an older report creation is still pending, the older completion can write into the fresh dialog state.

**Desired behavior:**
Only the currently active submission attempt may update submission result, error, show-folder, or submitting state. Closing, resetting, or reopening the dialog invalidates any older in-flight submission. Late success or failure from an invalidated attempt is ignored. Existing default privacy behavior remains unchanged: current Design contents are excluded unless the user explicitly opts in.

**Key interfaces:**
- Problem Report frontend submission module
- Problem Report dialog view model
- Diagnostic Bundle IPC adapter
- Current Design attachment opt-in seam

**Out of scope:**
- Changing Diagnostic Bundle contents or privacy exclusions
- Adding upload, telemetry, external issue creation, or support-channel behavior
- Changing Rust Problem Report assembly or folder reveal validation
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A regression test covers a pending Problem Report submission that completes after the dialog is closed and reopened.
- [ ] Late success from an invalidated submit does not populate a fresh dialog's result or clear its current state.
- [ ] Late failure from an invalidated submit does not populate a fresh dialog's error or clear its current state.
- [ ] The active submit path still sets submitting state, handles success and failure, and preserves current Design explicit opt-in behavior.
- [ ] Focused Problem Report frontend tests and TypeScript checks pass.
close_reason: Guarded Problem Report submission state with a monotonic generation token so close, reset, reopen, and newer submits invalidate older async completions. Added regression coverage for stale success and stale failure after close/reopen, plus active failure behavior. Verified with focused Problem Report Vitest coverage and TypeScript check.

title: Move Problem Report submission behind one frontend module
description:
## Slice Summary
Move frontend Problem Report submission state and request assembly behind a dedicated module so the dialog renders state and invokes commands instead of assembling diagnostics, sensitive attachments, and IPC calls itself.

## User Value
Problem Reports keep their local-first Diagnostic Bundle behavior while privacy-sensitive request assembly becomes easier to verify and harder to bypass from UI code.

## Out of Scope
Do not add automatic upload, telemetry, external issue creation, new Diagnostic Bundle contents, or changes to Rust privacy filtering in this slice.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** task
**Summary:** Move frontend Problem Report submission state and request assembly behind one module.

**Current behavior:**
The Problem Report dialog owns UI state and also assembles the Problem Report request. It reads recent frontend diagnostics, decides whether to build a current Design attachment, constructs sensitive attachment payloads, calls the IPC adapter, handles copy behavior, and reveals the generated folder. This gives the view too much knowledge of the local-first privacy interface.

**Desired behavior:**
The frontend Problem Report module owns submission state, request assembly, diagnostics capture, optional current Design attachment assembly, IPC submission, copy summary behavior, and generated-folder reveal behavior. The dialog consumes a view model and calls module commands. Current Design attachment assembly uses the Design Session document surface or injected equivalent so persisted content is composed the same way as a save. Rust remains the authoritative Diagnostic Bundle assembly and privacy-filtering module.

**Key interfaces:**
- Problem Report frontend module
- Problem Report request contract
- Diagnostic Bundle IPC adapter
- Frontend diagnostic recorder
- Design Session document surface
- Rust Problem Report assembly module

**Out of scope:**
- Adding automatic upload, telemetry, email drafts, or external issue creation
- Changing Rust Diagnostic Bundle privacy filtering or default exclusions
- Adding new sensitive attachment kinds
- Changing Design persistence semantics
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The Problem Report dialog no longer directly assembles Problem Report request objects, frontend diagnostics, sensitive attachment payloads, or IPC calls.
- [ ] A frontend Problem Report module exposes state and commands for description edits, current Design opt-in, submit, copy summary, reveal folder, error handling, and close/reset behavior.
- [ ] Current Design attachment assembly remains explicit opt-in and is composed through the Design Session document surface or an injected equivalent.
- [ ] Default Diagnostic Bundles still exclude Design contents, precise Location, screenshots, and raw filesystem paths unless the current Design attachment is explicitly selected.
- [ ] Frontend tests cover dialog behavior through the public Problem Report module behavior rather than internal component state.
- [ ] Relevant agent docs are updated if Problem Report frontend seams or privacy invariants change.
close_reason: Moved frontend Problem Report submission state and request assembly into app/problem-report/submission, made the dialog render module state and call module commands, kept current Design attachment opt-in through the existing Design Session persistence attachment seam, updated Problem Reporting docs, and verified with focused Problem Report tests, full frontend Vitest, and TypeScript check.

title: Narrow Design Session operations to intent-shaped commands
description:
## Slice Summary
Make Design Session callers use intent-shaped operations instead of constructing low-level transition recipes with source strings, dirty guard modes, load callbacks, queue behavior, and attached session facts.

## User Value
Opening, saving, autosaving, mounting, and tearing down a Design Session keep the same behavior while replacement policy gains locality behind one interface.

## Out of Scope
Do not redesign the Design file format, dirty-state model, canvas scene authority, or persistence composition rules in this slice.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** task
**Summary:** Narrow Design Session callers to intent-shaped operations instead of low-level transition recipes.

**Current behavior:**
Design Session replacement behavior is centralized, but production callers can still construct low-level transition requests that include source identifiers, dirty guard modes, load callbacks, queue deferral behavior, attached session selection, and cancellation checks. This makes callers know policy details that should live behind the Design Session seam.

**Desired behavior:**
Production callers express Design Session intent through narrow operations such as creating a new Design, opening a Design from a known path, opening a template as an unsaved Design, mounting an attached Design Session, consuming queued loads, saving, autosaving, and tearing down. Low-level transition request construction becomes internal to the Design Session module or only a focused internal test surface. Existing attached and detached behavior, dirty guard ordering, queued load behavior, autosave behavior, workflow installation, and persistence composition remain unchanged.

**Key interfaces:**
- Design Session operation interface
- Design Session state machine
- Dirty replacement guard
- Design Session persistence composition
- Canvas document surface
- Queued Design load behavior

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the Design file format or migration behavior
- Changing which Design fields are canvas-owned or document-owned
- Changing autosave interval settings
- Changing current Problem Report submission behavior
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Production callers no longer construct low-level Design transition request objects.
- [ ] User-facing open, new, template import, save, save-as, autosave, queued-load, mount, and teardown behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] Low-level transition source, dirty guard, attached/detached branching, queue restoration, and load callback ordering are local to the Design Session module.
- [ ] Tests cover the public intent-shaped operations and preserve existing dirty guard, queued load, attached mount, detached transition, save, autosave, and teardown behavior.
- [ ] No Design file ownership or persistence composition rules are weakened.
- [ ] Relevant agent docs are updated if Design Session operation names or caller conventions change.
close_reason: Moved open/new/template Design replacement recipes behind intent-shaped Design Session operations, removed low-level transition request construction from public document actions, kept state-machine transition details internal to the Design Session module and tests, updated document lifecycle docs, and verified with focused Design Session tests, full frontend Vitest, and TypeScript check.

title: Make canvas runtime surfaces real adapters
description:
## Slice Summary
Make the canvas runtime public seam consist of explicit command, query, and document adapters instead of exposing one mounted runtime that satisfies every canvas interface.

## User Value
App features that command, query, or persist canvas state can depend on a narrower interface, making future canvas and Design Session work safer to change and easier to test.

## Out of Scope
Do not change canvas user behavior, renderer behavior, scene edit semantics, Design Session policy, or Problem Report submission behavior in this slice.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** task
**Summary:** Make the canvas runtime public seam consist of real command, query, and document adapters.

**Current behavior:**
The canvas public seam is documented as separate command, query, and document surfaces, but the mounted runtime still satisfies all three interfaces directly. The published surfaces mostly forward to that single object, and compatibility paths allow tests or callers to publish a mounted runtime or narrow fake surface directly.

**Desired behavior:**
Production code publishes explicit canvas runtime surfaces, and each surface is a concrete adapter over the private runtime implementation. The runtime implementation no longer needs to satisfy the combined mounted-runtime interface directly. App callers and broad tests consume command, query, or document surfaces according to their role. Any compatibility path that accepts a combined runtime is removed from production code or confined to narrow test helper behavior.

**Key interfaces:**
- Canvas command surface
- Canvas query surface
- Canvas document surface
- Canvas runtime surface publication seam
- Scene runtime implementation
- Design Session lifecycle canvas attachment

**Out of scope:**
- Changing renderer behavior, fallback behavior, or scene rendering output
- Changing Scene Edit semantics, undo/redo behavior, or dirty-state semantics
- Changing Design Session replacement policy
- Changing Problem Report behavior
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Production canvas session publication accepts explicit command/query/document surfaces rather than relying on a mounted runtime object satisfying every surface.
- [ ] The scene runtime implementation is wrapped by concrete command, query, and document adapters with no app caller receiving the combined runtime as its public interface.
- [ ] Test helpers that need fake canvas surfaces publish role-specific surfaces or explicit surface bundles.
- [ ] Existing canvas toolbar, Design Session lifecycle, Planning Projection, MapLibre, and plant color behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] Focused tests cover surface separation and prevent query consumers from issuing commands or document lifecycle calls.
- [ ] Relevant agent docs are updated if canvas runtime publication or test-helper conventions change.
close_reason: Implemented explicit CanvasRuntimeSurfaces publication with concrete SceneCanvasRuntime command/query/document adapters, removed MountedCanvasRuntime publication compatibility, migrated test helpers to publish explicit surface bundles, updated canvas runtime agent docs, and verified with focused Vitest, full frontend Vitest, and TypeScript check.

title: Enforce Design Object Locks through Object Group membership
description:
## Slice Summary
Enforce the agreed invariant that an Object Group containing a locked Design Object cannot be moved, deleted, stamped, ungrouped, or otherwise edited in a way that mutates the locked member.

## User Value
A Design Object Lock consistently protects the object even when the user interacts with an Object Group that contains it.

## Out of Scope
This slice should not change the persistence contract created by the direct lock slice, and should not add visual lock indicators.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Enforce Design Object Locks when editing Object Groups that contain locked members.

**Current behavior:**
Lock checks are centered on direct object identity. Object Group operations can be reasoned about separately from member lock state, which leaves room for indirect mutation of a locked Design Object through its group.

**Desired behavior:**
A Design Object Lock protects the object even when the user interacts with an Object Group that contains it. If an Object Group contains any locked member, editing operations that would mutate that group or its members are blocked. Read-only presentation such as rendering and hover may continue as long as it does not mutate the locked member.

**Key interfaces:**
- SceneStore lock lookup for Design Objects and Object Groups
- Scene interaction hit testing and band selection
- Scene Edit transactions for drag, delete, ungroup, reorder, and stamp operations
- Object Stamp and Plant Spacing source validation
- Target and selection behavior for grouped Design Objects

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the embedded persistence contract for Design Object Locks
- Adding visual lock indicators
- Changing Layer lock semantics
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A group containing a locked placed plant, zone, or annotation cannot be selected for editing through ordinary hit testing or band selection.
- [ ] Drag, delete, ungroup, reorder, Object Stamp, and other mutating group operations reject Object Groups that contain locked members.
- [ ] Object Groups with no locked members keep existing behavior.
- [ ] A directly locked Object Group remains protected even when its members are unlocked.
- [ ] Regression tests cover locked members across all grouped Design Object types and verify no false positives for missing or unlocked members.
- [ ] Agent docs are updated if the implementation adds or changes lock-related SceneStore or Scene Edit rules.
close_reason: Enforced effective group locks when any existing member Design Object is locked, covering selection, select-all, Object Stamp, duplicate, delete, ungroup, and reorder with focused tests plus full frontend gates.

title: Persist direct Design Object Locks through SceneStore
description:
## Slice Summary
Persist direct Design Object Lock state by embedding a lock field on every Design Object and moving direct lock/unlock behavior behind SceneStore and Scene Edit. A directly locked Design Object should save, reopen, undo, redo, and block direct canvas editing operations.

## User Value
A user can lock a placed plant, zone, annotation, or object group and trust that the lock survives normal Design save/load behavior instead of being a transient runtime mirror.

## Out of Scope
Indirect Object Group member lock invariants are handled by a follow-up slice. This slice should not add new lock UI chrome or redesign layer locking.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Persist direct Design Object Locks as embedded Design Object state owned by SceneStore.

**Current behavior:**
Design Object lock state is represented as transient runtime mirror state. It participates in parts of Scene Edit and history behavior, but it is not embedded in the saved Design Object data and does not have one SceneStore-owned authority.

**Desired behavior:**
Every Design Object carries a saved `locked` boolean. Older Designs load with all Design Objects unlocked. New saves write explicit lock state. Direct lock and unlock commands update Design Object state through Scene Edit so dirty state, undo, redo, save, and load all observe the same authority. Direct selection, transformation, deletion, select-all, band selection, Object Stamp source selection, and Plant Spacing source selection respect direct Design Object Locks.

**Key interfaces:**
- Shared Design file contract for placed plants, zones, annotations, and object groups
- SceneStore hydration, serialization, snapshots, and restore behavior
- Scene Edit transactions and Scene History commands
- Canvas command, query, and document surfaces
- File-format round-trip behavior for old and new Designs

**Out of scope:**
- Indirect Object Group member lock invariants
- New visual lock indicators or lock-management UI
- Changes to Layer lock semantics
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The shared Design contract exposes a required `locked: boolean` field for placed plants, zones, annotations, and object groups in generated frontend types.
- [ ] Rust deserialization defaults missing Design Object lock fields to `false` so old `.canopi` files load without migration errors.
- [ ] SceneStore hydrates, clones, snapshots, restores, and serializes embedded Design Object lock state for all Design Object types.
- [ ] Direct lock and unlock commands write through Scene Edit and participate in dirty state, undo, redo, save, and reopen behavior.
- [ ] Direct selection, band selection, select-all, deletion, Object Stamp source selection, and Plant Spacing source selection respect directly locked Design Objects.
- [ ] Production code no longer depends on a global `lockedObjectIds` runtime mirror for Design Object lock authority.
- [ ] Required generated-contract and frontend quality gates pass, including focused SceneStore, Scene Edit, and interaction regression tests.
close_reason: Moved Design Object lock state into SceneStore persisted entities, removed the lockedObjectIds production mirror, regenerated shared bindings, and verified with frontend/Rust gates.

title: Collapse Timeline Action canvas into a host-model seam
description:
## Slice Summary
Deepen the Timeline Action canvas module so the canvas host consumes one compact host model for rendering, events, and overlays while interaction ordering, document mutation, and Target Presentation writes stay internal.

## User Value
Timeline Action behavior stays the same, but future timeline maintenance has one narrow interface instead of a wide set of caller-visible implementation details.

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** task
**Summary:** Deepen the Timeline Action canvas module behind a compact host-model interface.

**Current behavior:**
The Timeline Action canvas host consumes a wide surface: planning rows, layout, row offsets, render dependencies, cached geometry, event handlers, tooltip and popover state, cleanup behavior, and document mutation callbacks are exposed separately. The implementation has useful internal seams, but the caller-facing interface is still close to the implementation.

**Desired behavior:**
The Timeline Action canvas module exposes a compact host model for the canvas host: canvas wiring, container wiring, render inputs, event wiring, and overlay state. Interaction ordering, document listeners, popover lifecycle, Target Presentation writes, selection cleanup, and document mutation orchestration stay internal to the Timeline Action canvas module. - Timeline Action document editing and popover orchestration

- Canvas2D Timeline renderer

**Out of scope:**
- Timeline Action behavior changes
- Timeline visual redesign
- Planning Projection semantic changes
- Replacing the existing Canvas2D renderer
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The Timeline Action canvas host consumes one compact host model instead of independently wiring render dependencies, geometry cache, event handlers, tooltip state, popover state, and cleanup behavior.
- [ ] Timeline Action interaction ordering, document listeners, popover lifecycle, Target Presentation writes, selection cleanup, and document mutation orchestration stay internal to the Timeline Action canvas module.
- [ ] Existing Timeline Action add, edit, delete, hover, select, drag, resize, pan, zoom, auto-scroll, and popover behavior is preserved.

Gates: focused Timeline Vitest, full npm test, npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false.

title: Apply Visual Footprint curve to Placed Plant dots
description:
## Slice Summary
Apply the resolved Visual Footprint policy to symbolic Placed Plant markers in default Plant Size Mode.

## User Value
Designers see default Placed Plant markers scale smoothly with zoom, stay visible when zoomed out, and become slightly smaller than today at close zoom.

## Out of Scope
Do not change persisted Design data, canopy spread geometry for known canopy data, Zone geometry, Annotation text behavior, stack badge grouping semantics, or general renderer stroke normalization.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Apply a smooth Visual Footprint curve to symbolic Placed Plant dots.

**Current behavior:**
Default Plant Size Mode represents Placed Plants with a hybrid symbolic dot whose screen size uses hard floor and cap behavior. This can make zooming feel mechanical, and close zoom markers are larger than the resolved target. Canopy spread mode is physically meaningful when canopy spread data is known, while missing canopy data currently falls back through legacy symbolic sizing.

**Desired behavior:**
Default Plant Size Mode dots use one shared Visual Footprint calculation based on absolute viewport scale in pixels per meter. The curve should be smooth with soft screen-readable limits: about 2px minimum, about 6.75px asymptotic maximum, roughly 2.2px at 1 px/m, and roughly 6.3px at 200 px/m. Rendering, hit testing, band selection bounds, grouping bounds, zoom-to-fit bounds, and missing-canopy fallback should consume the same computed footprint. Known canopy spread remains physical geometry and bypasses the symbolic curve.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Size Mode presentation state
- Plant presentation context and entries
- Scene-side hit testing and bounds
- Scene zoom-to-fit bounds
- Renderer snapshots for Placed Plants

**Out of scope:**
- Changing persisted Design data or adding migrations
- Changing known canopy spread geometry
- Changing Zone geometry or Annotation text behavior
- Changing stack badge grouping semantics or badge placement
- Normalizing general renderer strokes and outlines
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Default Plant Size Mode dot radius follows a smooth absolute-scale Visual Footprint curve with about 2px minimum and about 6.75px asymptotic maximum.
- [ ] At representative scales, focused tests cover approximate radius targets around 1 px/m, 5 px/m, 10 px/m, 50 px/m, and 200 px/m.
- [ ] Rendering, hit testing, band selection bounds, grouping bounds, and zoom-to-fit bounds all consume the same symbolic plant footprint.
- [ ] Known canopy spread mode remains physical geometry and does not use the symbolic curve.
- [ ] Missing canopy spread fallback uses the symbolic Visual Footprint curve.
- [ ] No persisted Design schema, generated bindings, or migration changes are introduced.
- [ ] Focused frontend tests and `cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit` pass.
close_reason: Applied smooth absolute-scale Visual Footprint sizing for default Placed Plant dots and missing-canopy fallback while preserving known canopy geometry. Added focused coverage for representative radii, hit bounds, scene bounds, band selection, and Plant Spacing ghost sizing. Verified with npm test -- --run src/__tests__/plant-presentation.test.ts src/__tests__/camera-controller.test.ts src/__tests__/hit-testing.test.ts; npm test; npx tsc --noEmit; git diff --check.

title: Normalize screen-readable canvas presentation aids
description:
## Slice Summary
Align canvas presentation aids so strokes, outlines, labels, badges, and annotation selection affordances stay screen-readable across zoom and renderer backends.

## User Value
Designers see consistent visual weight for presentation aids while zooming, without physical Design Object geometry being distorted.

## Out of Scope
Do not change symbolic plant dot sizing, stack badge grouping semantics, persisted Design data, map projection behavior, grid/ruler chrome, or Zone physical geometry.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** feature
**Summary:** Normalize screen-readable canvas presentation aids across zoom and renderer backends.

**Current behavior:**
Some canvas presentation aids are already screen-readable, while others can scale as world geometry depending on renderer or object type. This creates inconsistent visual weight when zooming and can make Pixi and Canvas2D diverge for equivalent Design Objects.

**Desired behavior:**
Presentation aids remain screen-readable across zoom without changing physical Design Object geometry. Zone strokes, selected and highlighted outlines, plant strokes and highlight rings, annotation selection rectangles, labels, stack badge visuals, handles if present, and Zone Measurement text should keep stable screen-readable visual weight. Zones and known canopy spread remain physical geometry; Annotation text remains readable presentation anchored to a design position.

**Key interfaces:**
- Renderer snapshots and renderer backend parity
- Zone rendering and highlighting
- Plant stroke and highlight rendering
- Annotation text bounds and selection outlines
- Selection labels and Zone Measurement overlays

**Out of scope:**
- Changing symbolic Placed Plant dot sizing or Visual Footprint curve
- Changing stack badge grouping semantics
- Changing persisted Design data, map projection behavior, grid/ruler chrome, or Zone physical geometry
- Redesigning colors, typography, or general canvas visual style
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Zone strokes and selected/highlighted outlines maintain stable screen-readable widths across zoom in both renderer backends.
- [ ] Plant strokes and highlight rings maintain stable screen-readable widths around the computed plant footprint.
- [ ] Annotation selection rectangles use the same visible text bounds as rendering, hit testing, band selection, grouping, and zoom-to-fit.
- [ ] Labels, stack badge visuals, handles if present, and Zone Measurement text remain screen-readable and do not scale as physical geometry.
- [ ] Physical geometry for Zones and known canopy spread remains unchanged.
- [ ] Focused renderer or presentation tests cover backend parity for the changed presentation aids.
- [ ] Focused frontend tests and `cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit` pass.
close_reason: Normalized Pixi Zone and Placed Plant stroke widths to screen-readable pixel weights across viewport scale, including viewport-only updates. Added Pixi renderer coverage for zone and plant stroke widths at multiple zoom levels. Verified with npm test -- --run src/__tests__/pixi-scene.test.ts; npm test; npx tsc --noEmit; git diff --check.

title: Keep stack badges anchored to current plant footprint
description:
## Slice Summary
Keep stack badges attached to Placed Plant markers after symbolic marker sizing becomes zoom-aware.

## User Value
Designers still get count badges for Placed Plants whose centers collapse together, and badges stay visually attached to the current marker size.

## Out of Scope
Do not badge ordinary Visual Footprint overlap, change the center-collapse threshold unless tests show it must be restored, or redesign badge styling.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** task
**Summary:** Keep stack badges anchored to the current Placed Plant Visual Footprint.

**Current behavior:**
Stack badge offsets are tied to legacy fixed dot-size assumptions. Once symbolic Placed Plant dots use a zoom-aware Visual Footprint curve, badge placement can drift from the marker size even if center-collapse grouping still behaves correctly.

**Desired behavior:**
Stack badges continue to indicate Placed Plants whose centers collapse to nearly the same screen position. Badge placement should derive from the current plant visual radius so the badge remains visually attached to the marker across zoom levels and Plant Size Mode fallback cases. Ordinary overlap between symbolic Visual Footprints should not create stack badges by itself.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant presentation entries
- Stack badge decision model
- Renderer badge drawing for Placed Plants
- Scene-side plant presentation tests

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the meaning of stack badges from center collapse to visual overlap
- Redesigning badge styling, text, color, or count formatting
- Changing the Visual Footprint curve itself
- Changing selection labels or hover tooltips
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Stack badges still appear for Placed Plants whose centers collapse within the existing screen-space proximity rule.
- [ ] Stack badges do not appear merely because two symbolic plant Visual Footprints overlap at ordinary dense spacing.
- [ ] Badge center offsets are derived from the current plant visual radius, not a fixed legacy dot radius.
- [ ] Badge placement remains correct at representative low, normal, and high zoom scales.
- [ ] Pixi and Canvas2D badge drawing remain visually consistent with the shared badge decision data.
- [ ] Focused frontend tests and `cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit` pass.
close_reason: Updated stack badge placement to derive badge offsets from the current Placed Plant Visual Footprint while preserving center-collapse grouping semantics. Added coverage for footprint-derived badge centers and ordinary Visual Footprint overlap not creating badges. Verified with npm test -- --run src/__tests__/plant-presentation.test.ts; npm test; npx tsc --noEmit; git diff --check.

title: Remember bottom panel height per tab
description: Bottom Panel Tab heights should be remembered independently for Timeline, Budget, and Consortium. First-use defaults should fit the base Timeline and Consortium rows, while legacy 200px defaults should be treated as unset rather than as a user-resized preference.
acceptance_criteria: Timeline, Budget, and Consortium each have independent persisted heights after manual resize. Tabs with no explicit height use compact first-use defaults. Existing single bottom_panel_height values migrate so 200px is treated as unset and other values seed all tabs. Focused settings projection tests cover hydration, snapshotting, and legacy normalization.
close_reason: Implemented per-tab Bottom Panel Tab height preferences with nullable first-use defaults, legacy bottom_panel_height migration, regenerated settings bindings, focused frontend coverage, Rust migration tests, and agent docs updates. Verified with focused Vitest, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run check:types, cargo fmt --all -- --check, CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo check --workspace, CANOPI_SKIP_BUNDLED_DB=1 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, and git diff --check.

title: Fix Species Catalog filter row height reservation
description:
## Slice Summary
Fix the always-visible Species Catalog Filter rows so wrapped choice ribbons reserve vertical space in their own row instead of painting behind the next filter row.

## User Value
Users resizing the Species Catalog Workbench sidebar can see every Climate Zone ribbon, including Boreal, without wrapped ribbons overlapping Habit or any following filter row.

## Out of Scope
Do not change Species Catalog filter semantics, option ordering, backend filtering behavior, sidebar width persistence, or redesign the More Filters panel.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Make always-visible Species Catalog Filter rows reserve height for wrapped choice ribbons.

**Current behavior:**
At very narrow Species Catalog Workbench sidebar widths, Climate Zone choice ribbons wrap, but the Climate Zone row does not reserve enough vertical space for every wrapped line. The final ribbon, such as Boreal, can paint behind the following Habit row instead of forcing Climate Zone to become taller.

**Desired behavior:**
Each always-visible choice filter row participates in normal vertical flow and reserves enough height for every wrapped ribbon. Climate Zone may become three or more ribbon lines at narrow widths, then shrink as width increases. Wrapped ribbons must never overlap following filter rows. More Filters should remain the reference behavior: chip groups wrap naturally and their parent content grows around them.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Workbench sidebar
- Always-visible Species Catalog Filter strip
- Choice filter row and ribbon/chip presentation
- Filter region height cap and scrolling behavior
- Frontend regression coverage for filter-row overlap

**Out of scope:**
- Changing Species Catalog request or backend filter contracts
- Changing Climate Zone values, translations, or option ordering
- Changing saved sidebar width persistence
- Redesigning More Filters
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] At narrow Species Catalog Workbench sidebar widths, Climate Zone reserves enough height for all wrapped ribbons, including Boreal.
- [ ] No wrapped choice ribbon paints behind Habit or any following always-visible filter row.
- [ ] Other always-visible choice filter rows keep natural wrapping behavior and reserve their wrapped height.
- [ ] The combined filter region remains the only capped/scrollable filter container; individual choice rows do not rely on visible overflow to expose wrapped content.
- [ ] Existing sidebar default width and saved width persistence behavior remain unchanged.
- [ ] More Filters chip wrapping behavior is not regressed.
- [ ] Focused frontend regression coverage protects the row-height reservation behavior, preferably through rendered geometry; if the local test environment cannot compute layout, the test must explicitly guard against the layout combination that allowed wrapped ribbons to escape their row.
- [ ] Required frontend checks are run, including focused Vitest coverage and `cd desktop/web && npx tsc --noEmit`.
close_reason: Implemented flex-based Species Catalog filter rows so wrapped choice ribbons reserve row height; verified with focused filter-strip Vitest coverage and npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Fix Species Catalog filter strip row wrapping
description:
## Slice Summary
Fix the always-visible Species Catalog Filter strip so choice rows grow and shrink naturally as the Species Catalog Workbench sidebar width changes.

## User Value
Users resizing the Species Catalog Workbench can see all visible Climate Zone and other choice ribbons without rows appearing fixed at one or two lines.

## Out of Scope
Do not change Species Catalog request contracts, filter semantics, filter option ordering, sidebar width persistence, or the More Filters panel behavior except as needed to preserve shared wrapping expectations.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Make always-visible Species Catalog Filter choice rows resize naturally with the Species Catalog Workbench sidebar.

**Current behavior:**
The always-visible Species Catalog Filter strip appears to keep Climate Zone at a fixed two-row height across practical sidebar width changes. Other choice rows can also appear locked to a single row. The implementation relies on a parent strip layout that does not behave like the natural wrapping chip groups used in More Filters, so row-height changes are not reliably visible when the panel width changes.

**Desired behavior:**
Each always-visible Species Catalog Filter row owns its own height. Choice rows wrap like More Filters chip groups: narrower sidebars may produce more ribbon rows, wider sidebars may produce fewer rows, and all visible ribbons remain available. The combined filter region may remain capped and scrollable, but individual choice rows must not clip or force a fixed row count.

**Key interfaces:**
- Species Catalog Workbench filter strip projection
- Always-visible Species Catalog Filter rows
- Shared filter chip/ribbon presentation

title: Ignore Plant Spacing HUD pointer moves
description:
## Slice Summary
Prevent pointer movement that originates inside the Plant Spacing HUD from updating the active spacing guide or generated count.

## User Value
A designer can edit the Plant Spacing Interval and move over HUD controls without the canvas guide jumping to HUD coordinates.

## Out of Scope
Do not change Plant Spacing sequence math, interval parsing, pointerdown handling, shortcut behavior, or non-Plant Spacing tool interactions.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Prevent Plant Spacing HUD-origin pointer movement from changing the active spacing guide.

**Current behavior:**
After a Plant Spacing source is selected, the interaction controller updates the spacing preview from window-level pointer movement. Pointer movement over HUD controls can therefore be interpreted as a canvas endpoint, making the guide and generated count jump while the user is editing the interval or moving across controls.

**Desired behavior:**
Pointer movement that originates inside the Plant Spacing HUD or its controls is treated as HUD interaction only. It must not update the spacing guide endpoint, generated count, ghost preview, or pending commit endpoint. Pointer movement outside the HUD continues to update Plant Spacing previews normally, including click-hold drag previews.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Spacing HUD control surface
- Scene interaction pointer movement handling
- Plant Spacing preview endpoint and generated count
- Plant Spacing click-hold drag preview

**Out of scope:**
- Changing Plant Spacing sequence math
- Changing interval parsing or formatting
- Changing pointerdown or keyboard shortcut behavior beyond what is necessary to ignore HUD-origin pointer movement
- Reworking non-Plant Spacing canvas interactions
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Moving the pointer over the Plant Spacing HUD after a source is selected does not update the guide endpoint, length label, generated count, or ghost positions.
- [ ] Moving the pointer over the Plant Spacing interval input does not alter the active spacing guide while the user is editing.
- [ ] Canvas pointer movement outside the HUD still updates Plant Spacing preview geometry normally.
- [ ] Click-hold Plant Spacing drag behavior outside the HUD still previews and commits as before.
- [ ] Focused regression tests cover HUD-origin pointermove events and normal canvas pointermove behavior.
close_reason: Fixed Plant Spacing HUD pointermove handling by consuming HUD-origin pointer movement before it reaches the window canvas interaction listener, so interval input/HUD movement no longer changes the active spacing guide while normal canvas movement still works. Tests: npm test -- --run src/__tests__/scene-interaction.test.ts -t 'HUD pointermoves'; npm test -- --run src/__tests__/scene-interaction.test.ts -t 'Plant Spacing'.

title: Stabilize Plant Spacing HUD event boundaries
description:
## Slice Summary
Codify the Plant Spacing HUD as a control surface rather than canvas input by auditing HUD-origin pointer and keyboard events after the known pointermove leak is fixed.

## User Value

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Audit and test the Plant Spacing HUD/canvas event boundary as a single invariant.

**Current behavior:**
Recent Plant Spacing fixes have addressed individual HUD/canvas event leaks one at a time, including HUD pointerdowns, interval input keyboard handling, focus behavior, and now HUD pointer movement. This pattern makes it easy for another HUD-origin event to slip through and affect canvas interaction state.

**Desired behavior:**
The Plant Spacing HUD is explicitly protected as a control surface. HUD-origin events that belong to controls must not be interpreted as canvas source sampling, endpoint previewing, endpoint committing, or generated plant creation. Events outside the HUD continue to drive Plant Spacing normally. Existing interval input behavior remains intact: Enter and Escape are handled by the tool, while unrelated global shortcuts can still bubble according to the app command policy.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Spacing HUD pointer and keyboard event handling
- Scene interaction pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup, and keyboard handling
- Plant Spacing interval input focus, blur, Enter, Escape, and shortcut bubbling behavior
- Plant Spacing preview and commit endpoint lifecycle

**Out of scope:**
- Redesigning HUD layout or visual styling
- Changing shortcut assignments
- Changing Plant Spacing sequence math, density thresholds, or hard caps
- Refactoring unrelated canvas tools
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Tests or implementation-level guards cover HUD-origin pointerdown, pointermove, and relevant control clicks as non-canvas input.
- [ ] Tests preserve interval input keyboard behavior: Enter commits interval input, Escape cancels Plant Spacing, and unrelated global shortcut keydowns can bubble.
- [ ] Tests preserve interval input focus/blur behavior without stealing focus from other controls.
- [ ] Normal canvas-origin source sampling, previewing, two-click commits, and click-hold drag commits still work.
- [ ] Any newly discovered HUD/canvas boundary gaps are fixed in this bead or split into concrete follow-up beads if they exceed this scope.

title: Refresh Plant Spacing drag endpoint on release
description:
## Slice Summary
Ensure click-hold Plant Spacing drag commits use the pointerup release coordinate when the release represents a newer endpoint than the last pointermove, while still preserving an intentionally Shift-constrained preview.

## User Value
A designer can release a Plant Spacing drag at the intended endpoint and trust the generated plants will follow the final release position instead of stopping at a stale preview.

## Out of Scope
Do not change Plant Spacing sequence math, interval parsing, zero-length guide label formatting, two-click endpoint placement, or non-Plant Spacing drag behavior.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Refresh Plant Spacing drag commit endpoints from pointerup when the release coordinate is newer than the latest preview.

**Current behavior:**
During click-hold Plant Spacing drag, commit can reuse the last preview endpoint unconditionally. If the pointer is released at a different coordinate than the last pointermove, the generated plants stop at the stale preview endpoint rather than the final release position.

**Desired behavior:**
Plant Spacing drag commit should use the final pointerup coordinate when it represents a newer unconstrained endpoint. If the latest visible preview was intentionally Shift-constrained and the only difference is that Shift was released before pointerup, commit must preserve the constrained preview so generated plants match what the user saw. Normal unconstrained click-hold drag, Shift-constrained click-hold drag, and two-click endpoint placement should keep their existing behavior.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Spacing click-hold drag preview
- Plant Spacing pointerup endpoint commit
- Shift direction constraint behavior
- Plant Spacing generated plant placement

**Out of scope:**
- Changing generated plant spacing math
- Changing interval parsing, warnings, hard caps, or zero-length label formatting
- Changing keyboard shortcut behavior
- Changing drag behavior for other canvas tools
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Releasing a Plant Spacing click-hold drag at a coordinate that differs from the last pointermove commits plants along the release endpoint.
- [ ] Releasing Shift before pointerup after a Shift-constrained preview still commits plants along the latest visible constrained guide.
- [ ] Unconstrained Plant Spacing click-hold drag still commits the previewed unconstrained guide when pointerup does not move.
- [ ] The normal two-click Plant Spacing endpoint flow still works.
- [ ] Focused regression tests cover both stale release-coordinate refresh and Shift-constrained preservation.
close_reason: Fixed Plant Spacing click-hold drag commits to refresh from the pointerup endpoint when the release coordinate is newer than the preview, while preserving Shift-constrained preview commits when Shift is released at the same coordinate. title: Preserve Shift-constrained Plant Spacing endpoint on commit
description:
## Slice Summary

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Preserve the last previewed Shift-constrained Plant Spacing endpoint when committing a drag.

**Current behavior:**
During Plant Spacing click-hold drag, the live preview endpoint can be constrained by Shift. If the user releases Shift before pointerup without moving the pointer again, the commit path can recompute the endpoint from the pointerup event without Shift. The generated plants then follow a different line than the guide the user saw.

**Desired behavior:**
Plant Spacing drag commit should use the same endpoint represented by the latest visible preview. Modifier changes between the last preview update and pointerup must not make the committed generated plants diverge from the visible guide. Normal unconstrained drag, Shift-constrained drag, and two-click endpoint placement should keep their existing behavior.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Spacing click-hold drag preview
- Plant Spacing endpoint commit on pointerup
- Shift direction constraint behavior
- Plant Spacing generated plant placement

**Out of scope:**
- Changing generated plant spacing math
- Changing interval parsing, warnings, or hard cap behavior
- Changing keyboard shortcut behavior
- Changing drag behavior for other canvas tools
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Releasing Shift before pointerup after a Shift-constrained Plant Spacing drag commits plants along the same guide shown in the preview.
- [ ] The latest previewed endpoint is preserved for Plant Spacing drag commit instead of recomputing from stale modifier state.
- [ ] Unconstrained Plant Spacing drag still commits the previewed unconstrained guide.
- [ ] The normal two-click Plant Spacing endpoint flow still works.
- [ ] Focused regression tests cover Shift held during preview then released before pointerup.

title: Let Plant Spacing interval input pass global shortcuts
description:
## Slice Summary

## User Value

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Let global app shortcuts pass through the Plant Spacing interval input unless the input is handling Enter or Escape.

**Current behavior:**
The Plant Spacing interval input stops propagation for every keydown. That prevents app-level shortcut handling from seeing global shortcuts while the input has focus, including shortcuts that are intentionally allowed from editable targets.

**Desired behavior:**
The interval input should consume only keys it owns, specifically Enter for interval commit and Escape for Plant Spacing cancellation. Other keydown events, including Ctrl/Cmd and command-palette shortcuts, should be allowed to bubble so the app command registry can handle them according to its existing editable-target policy.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Spacing interval input keyboard handling
- App command registry global shortcut handling
- Editable-target shortcut policy

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the global shortcut registry
- Changing interval parsing or commit behavior
- Changing keyboard behavior for non-Plant Spacing inputs
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Enter in the Plant Spacing interval input still commits the interval and does not leak to unrelated canvas keyboard behavior.
- [ ] Escape in the Plant Spacing interval input still cancels the Plant Spacing source/flow.
- [ ] Non-Enter/Escape keydown events in the interval input are not stopped by the HUD input handler.
- [ ] A focused regression test proves a representative global shortcut keydown can bubble from the interval input.
- [ ] Existing Plant Spacing interval input tests continue to pass.

title: Require intentional Plant Spacing drag before fast-path commit
description:
## Slice Summary

## User Value

## Out of Scope

design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Require a real intentional Plant Spacing click-hold drag before using the pointerup fast-path commit.

**Current behavior:**
After a source placed plant is sampled, a very small pointer movement can enter the Plant Spacing drag state. On pointerup, that drag state can commit generated plants if the jittered world endpoint is at least one interval away, which can happen at low zoom or with small intervals.

**Desired behavior:**
Plant Spacing should only use the click-hold drag commit path after an intentional drag gesture. Minor pointer jitter after a source-sampling click should not create generated plants. The normal two-click flow, where the user samples a source and then clicks an endpoint, should keep working.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Spacing source sampling
- Plant Spacing click-hold drag gesture detection
- Plant Spacing endpoint commit on pointerup
- Canvas pointer slop/drag threshold behavior

**Out of scope:**
- Changing generated plant spacing math
- Changing the two-click endpoint placement flow
- Changing drag thresholds for unrelated canvas tools unless a shared helper already owns the policy
- Changing interval validity or commit safety cap behavior
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A source-sampling click followed by minor pointer jitter does not create generated plants on pointerup.
- [ ] Intentional click-hold Plant Spacing drag still previews and commits generated plants.
- [ ] The normal two-click Plant Spacing flow still samples a source on the first click and commits an endpoint on the second click.
- [ ] Focused regression tests cover minor pointer jitter and intentional drag behavior.
- [ ] Existing Plant Spacing interaction tests continue to pass.

title: Bound Plant Spacing commits before materializing
description:
## Slice Summary
Prevent Plant Spacing from materializing an unbounded number of generated plants when committing a line with a very small but physically valid interval.

## User Value
Users can still enter small agroecological spacing intervals, but a single commit cannot hang the app by allocating hundreds of thousands or millions of plants.

## Out of Scope
Do not change interval validity rules, preview styling, warning threshold color behavior, or unrelated Plant Spacing interaction flows.
design:
## Agent Brief
**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Add a hard Plant Spacing commit safety cap before generated positions are materialized.

**Current behavior:**
Plant Spacing preview generation is capped, but the final commit path recomputes and materializes the full generated position list. With a tiny but valid interval over a normal-length line, the app can allocate a very large plant list and hang during the scene edit.

**Desired behavior:**
Before committing Plant Spacing output, compute or otherwise bound the generated count without materializing an unsafe number of positions. If the count exceeds the hard safety cap, do not create plants and show a clear message that the line is too dense to commit. Physically valid intervals should remain valid inputs; the safety cap protects only the one-shot commit size.

Use a hard cap of 5,000 generated plants per Plant Spacing commit. Keep the existing 100-plant warning threshold as warning-only behavior. Counts from 101 through 5,000 remain allowed; counts above 5,000 are blocked from commit.

**Key interfaces:**
- Plant Spacing line endpoint commit flow
- Plant Spacing generated-count calculation
- Plant Spacing HUD status or error messaging
- Scene edit transaction that appends generated plants

**Out of scope:**
- Changing interval parsing or the 50 cm fallback
- Reintroducing confirmation UX for dense spacing
- Changing the 100-plant warning threshold behavior except as needed to distinguish it from the hard safety cap
- Changing generated plant placement math for safe counts
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Plant Spacing commits never materialize more than 5,000 generated plants in one operation.
- [ ] Counts from 101 through 5,000 remain physically valid and commit without a confirmation dialog.
- [ ] Counts above 5,000 are blocked with a clear HUD-visible safety message instead of creating plants.

title: Do not steal focus on Plant Spacing interval blur
description:
## Slice Summary
Prevent the Plant Spacing Interval input from moving focus back to the canvas during ordinary blur.

## User Value

## Out of Scope
